events.report_summary:
**Document:** Certificate/statement taken 30 July 1947 in Portland, Oregon from Richard Rankin, 834 N.E. Simpson Street, Portland, Oregon.

**Witness:** Richard Rankin, age 47, experienced aviator and air show stunt pilot. Soloed at age 19 in 1919. Flew over western U.S. for U.S. Forest Service, mapped all western states. Brother was "Tex" Rankin, a well-known figure in civilian and military flying circles who ran primary training schools for thousands of cadets during WWII and logged over 7,000 hours in the air. Witness states he is "well acquainted with most articles that one would see in the air and feel that I am well qualified to say when I see articles flying through the air."

**Sighting:** At approximately 1200 noon on 14 June 1947, witness was lying in the front yard of his home at 130 South "I" Street, Bakersfield, California. A lad was mowing the lawn nearby. Looking up into the sky, witness saw ten articles flying from south to north at what he judged to be 6,500 ft altitude. Objects were flying at approximately 350 miles per hour, he estimated.

**Object:** Witness distinctly remembers telling the lad mowing the lawn at the time that the objects were probably Army or Navy test planes from nearby test centers in the deserts of Southern California. However, upon reflection, the objects resembled pictures he had seen of the so-called "Flying Flapjack" that the Navy was testing. After the objects disappeared proceeding north, witness went back into the yard to sit in the shade. At this time the objects reappeared going from east to south, though this time there were only seven of the articles. When first saw the original ten objects they were flying in a "V" formation with one object seemingly staying in the rear of the formation. On the second time they appeared, the seven objects were still in the "V" formation although there was only seven objects at this time. Witness told the lad mowing the lawn that the objects had proceeded back to their base on a different course. Witness thought the case was that the other three objects had probably gone back to their base on the other side of the mountains from Bakersfield. Armstrong has been interviewed by headquarters personnel and requests that a copy of the MOIC be furnished to Randolph Field headquarters. The document references an earlier MOIC dated 15 July 1947 and a withdrawn MOIC dated 7 July 1947.

**Provenance:** The memo was issued by Colonel S.H. Morrow (GSC, Assistant Chief of Staff, A-2) from Headquarters Tenth Air Force, Office of the Assistant Chief of Staff, A-2, at Brooks Field, San Antonio, Texas. One enclosure (the actual MOIC) was included but is not visible on this page.

The room layout appears to be a simple rectangular space with furniture placement marked.

**Context:** This memorandum is the first page of what appears to be a longer report documenting a flying saucer sighting or related phenomenon experienced by the witness at his Arlington residence.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Summary of information from Headquarters Fifteenth Air Force, Colorado Springs, Colorado, dated 2 July 1947, regarding supersonic platters observed by railroad employees.

**Witnesses:** Three employees of the Pikes Peak Railway, Manitou Springs, Colorado: Mr. W. A. Hauser (24 North Chestnut Street, Colorado Springs), Mr. F. J. Smit (24 Fairview, Manitou Springs), and Mr. L. D. Jamison (2410 West Kiowa, Colorado Springs). Counter Intelligence Corps personnel interviewed these men at Fifteenth Air Force Headquarters on 27 June 1947.

**Sighting:** On or about 19 May 1947 during their lunch period (12:1-13:1:), a member of the train crew called attention to a silver object in the sky proceeding from the north east. It appeared to be travelling at great speed. All three men stated the altitude of the object was very difficult to determine because of its apparent smallness. They stated that because of this it was difficult to view the object as being large and having high altitude, or small and being at a relatively low altitude. They did say though that it appeared to be nearer than the top of Manitou Mountain which is over 1000 feet higher than the shops which are situated at its base.

**Object characteristics:** No definite shape could be determined and even with the aid of binoculars it still could not be brought into focus. The binoculars used were of about 6 power. The men stated they were certain that the object did not have any of the physical characteristics of modern conventional aircraft. The object remained in the immediate area for several minutes during which time it was seen to execute manuvers such as climbing, diving, and reversal of direction of flight, happening every few seconds. The distance and location between views prompted two of the men to think that there were more of the unidentified objects in the sky. At times the object seemed to hover in the air and then start on another path of flight. When last seen the silver object was climbing very fast towards the west almost directly into the wind.

**Weather:** The day was described as being clear and sunny with not a cloud in the sky and no ground wind.

**Evaluation:** Source rated E, information rated O.

**Document:** 来自科罗拉多州科罗拉多泉市第十五航空队司令部的信息摘要,日期为1947年7月2日,关于铁路员工观察到的超音速飞盘。

**Witnesses:** 科罗拉多州马尼托泉市派克峰铁路公司的三名员工:W. A. Hauser先生(科罗拉多泉市北栗树街24号)、F. J. Smit先生(马尼托泉市费尔维尤24号)和L. D. Jamison先生(科罗拉多泉市西基奥瓦街2410号)。反情报部队人员于1947年6月27日在第十五航空队司令部对这些人进行了访谈。

**Sighting:** 1947年5月19日左右,在他们的午餐时间(12:1-13:1)期间,列车组的一名成员注意到天空中有一个从东北方向飞来的银色物体。它似乎以极快的速度飞行。三名男子都表示,由于物体明显很小,很难确定其高度。他们表示,正因为如此,很难判断该物体是大型且位于高空,还是小型且位于相对较低的高度。不过他们确实说过,它似乎比马尼托山的山顶更近,而马尼托山比位于其山脚的车间高出1000多英尺。

**Object characteristics:** 无法确定明确的形状,即使借助双筒望远镜也仍然无法对焦。所使用的双筒望远镜大约是6倍放大率。这些男子表示,他们确信该物体不具有现代常规飞机的任何物理特征。该物体在附近区域停留了数分钟,在此期间可以看到它执行诸如爬升、俯冲和飞行方向反转等机动动作,每隔几秒钟就会发生一次。观测之间的距离和位置促使其中两人认为天空中有更多不明物体。有时物体似乎悬停在空中,然后开始另一条飞行路径。最后一次看到时,这个银色物体正以非常快的速度向西爬升,几乎是直接逆风飞行。

**Weather:** 当天被描述为晴朗且阳光明媚,天空中没有一片云,地面也没有风。

**Evaluation:** 来源评级为E,信息评级为O。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Memorandum to Security Officer, Oklahoma City Air Materiel Area (OCAMA), Tinker Field, dated 24 July 1947, regarding interview of Byron E. Savage conducted 23 July 1947.

**Witness:** Byron E. Savage, age 38, Field Engineer for Radio Corporation of America, Dallas, Texas, residing at 416 N.W. 29th Street, Oklahoma City. Married with one child. Private Pilot's License No. 39101 (signed Empire Land). Extensively studied electronics, sound engineering, and aeronautics. Present occupation involves installing theater sound equipment.

**Sighting:** Between 17-21 May 1947, just after dusk (8:30 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.), Savage and his wife observed an object while entering their car at their residence. The moon had not yet risen. City lights from Oklahoma City appeared to be shining on the object when first observed.

**Object:** Initially appeared as small aircraft approximately 100° south. As it moved closer toward the witness, Savage remarked to his wife "a big white plane was coming over." When object reached 45° angle, realized it was not conventional aircraft. Appeared elliptical at first, then perfectly round and flat as it approached. Disc-shaped with no appearance of spherical form. Ratio of diameter to thickness approximately 10:1, appearing thicker in center (could not be positively ascertained). Altitude estimated between 10,000 and 18,000 feet, leaving no trailing effects. Bulk comparable to six B-29s at same altitude. Visible approximately 15-20 seconds, traveling at speed judged to be three times that of jet-propelled aircraft.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Memorandum for the Officer in Charge, dated 16 July 1947, Incident LAP 1206 I, regarding an interview with Kenneth Arnold of Boise, Idaho, Box 387, concerning strange objects flying over the Cascade Mountain Range of Washington State on July 25th.

**Witness:** Kenneth Arnold, 32 years old, married with two children. Arnold is described as well thought of in his community, living in Boise, Idaho, and working as a fire equipment salesman. He is considered a very good provider for his family and had recently purchased a home on the outskirts of Boise and a $5,000 airplane. The interviewer's notes express skepticism about Arnold's character and integrity, suggesting he writes reports to gain attention rather than because he actually witnessed anomalous objects.

**Interview Context:** Arnold was interviewed in regard to his report about seeing strange objects flying over the Cascade Range. He voluntarily agreed to provide a written report of what he had seen, which is attached to this memorandum as Exhibit A.

**Agent's Assessment:** The agent expresses strong doubt about Arnold's credibility, stating "It is difficult to believe that a man of Mr. Arnold's character and apparent integrity and right that he saw objects and write up a report to the extent that he did if he did not see something." However, the agent concludes that if Arnold can write reports without actually having seen the objects, "it is the opinion of the interviewer that Mr. Arnold is in the wrong business, that he should be writing Buck Rogers fiction." The agent is very outspoken and generally bitter in his opinion of the leaders of the U.S. Army Air Forces and the Federal Bureau of Investigation for not investigating the matter sooner.

**Verification Attempts:** After checking an aeronautical map of the area over which Arnold claimed to have seen objects, it was determined that all statements made by Arnold regarding the distances involved, size of objects, and number of objects could very possibly be facts. However, distances mentioned are within a short distance of known aeronautical installations. Despite this, Arnold has never consulted aeronautical charts of the type the Army uses.

**Business Impact:** Arnold stated his business had suffered greatly since his report on July 25 became fact, with people stopping him at every stop on his business routes and large crowds gathering to question him. He stated that if he saw anything in the sky in the future, he would "quote Mr. Arnold, literally, 'If I saw a ten story building...'" [text appears cut off]

**Document:** 备忘录致负责官员，日期1947年7月16日，事件编号LAP 1206 I，关于对爱达荷州博伊西(Boise, Idaho)387信箱的肯尼斯·阿诺德(Kenneth Arnold)的访谈，涉及7月25日在华盛顿州喀斯喀特山脉(Cascade Mountain Range)上空飞行的奇异物体。

**Witness:** 肯尼斯·阿诺德(Kenneth Arnold)，32岁，已婚，育有两个孩子。阿诺德在其社区内被描述为备受尊重的人物，居住在爱达荷州博伊西，从事消防设备销售工作。他被认为是一位非常称职的家庭供养者，最近在博伊西郊区购买了一套住宅和一架价值5,000美元的飞机。访谈者的记录对阿诺德的品格和诚信表示怀疑，暗示他撰写报告是为了获取关注，而非因为他真正目击了异常物体。

**Interview Context:** 阿诺德接受访谈是关于他报告在喀斯喀特山脉上空看到奇异飞行物体一事。他自愿同意提供一份关于所见情况的书面报告，该报告作为附件A附于本备忘录。

**Agent's Assessment:** 调查员对阿诺德的可信度表示强烈怀疑，称"很难相信一个具有阿诺德先生这样品格、明显诚信和权利的人，如果他没有看到什么东西，会看到物体并撰写如此详尽的报告。"然而，调查员总结道，如果阿诺德能够在实际上未曾看到这些物体的情况下撰写报告，"访谈者认为阿诺德先生入错了行，他应该去写巴克·罗杰斯(Buck Rogers)科幻小说。"该调查员对美国陆军航空队(U.S. Army Air Forces)和联邦调查局(Federal Bureau of Investigation)的领导层未能更早调查此事直言不讳且普遍持批评态度。

**Verification Attempts:** 在查阅了阿诺德声称看到物体的区域的航空地图后，确定阿诺德关于涉及的距离、物体大小和物体数量的所有陈述很可能是事实。然而，提到的距离都在已知航空设施的短距离范围内。尽管如此，阿诺德从未查阅过陆军使用的那类航空图。

**Business Impact:** 阿诺德表示，自从他7月25日的报告成为事实以来，他的生意遭受了巨大损失，人们在他业务路线的每一站都拦住他，大群人聚集向他提问。他表示，如果将来在天空中看到任何东西，他会"引用阿诺德先生的原话，'如果我看到一栋十层楼的建筑……'"[文本似乎被截断]

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Naval Research Laboratory memorandum dated 18 July 1947, forwarding interview of C. H. Zohn regarding an unidentified aerial object he reported to the press.

**Witness:** Mr. C. H. Zohn, Administrative Assistant in the Rocket Sonde Section at Naval Research Laboratory (NRL). Zohn had previously released information to the press about an aerial object he observed on 29 June 1947 at White Sands, New Mexico. The interview was conducted at the request of Lt. Col. G. D. Garrett, AAF A-2.

**Sighting:** Between 1100 and 1130 p.m. on Sunday, 29 June 1947, Mr. Zohn was traveling along Highway 17 in a North-Easterly direction from Las Cruces, New Mexico to White Sands V-2 firing grounds. He was accompanied by Mr. J. E. Kauke (NRL Rocket Sonde Section telemetering supervisor), Mr. G. C. Rockwood (NRL Rocket Sonde high altitude spectrograph scientist), and Mrs. Nancy Rockwood. The automobile was driven by Mr. Kauke.

**Object:** At some point between the specified times and approximately one-third the distance from Las Cruces, Mr. Kauke noticed the object and called attention to the other occupants. Mr. Zohn opened the window nearest him and observed the object moving at an unknown rapid velocity at an unknown altitude, estimated at about 10,000 feet (though Mr. Kauke, who also observed it through an open window, estimated between 8,000 and 10,000 feet, with the former estimate given little credence).

When first sighted, the object was to the right and forward of the automobile at an unstated elevation, apparently moving horizontally in a Northerly direction from right to left across the highway. The object was observed by all persons in the automobile. Mr. Zohn stated he could not observe any details other than that its shape was uniform, with no protuberances such as the wings of an airplane. It was too distant to enable stereoscopic visualization.

There was apparently some solar specular reflection which seemed to change in intensity as the object receded until it was lost from sight after an estimated 30 seconds from the time first noticed. Mr. Zohn could not explain how it disappeared except perhaps that the reflection angle may have changed abruptly. There were apparently no clouds or visibility obstructions at the time. The sun was to the rear of the automobile. Mr. Kauke thought that at one time he saw vapor trails.

events.report_summary_zh:
**文件:** 海军研究实验室备忘录,日期为1947年7月18日,转发对C. H. Zohn的访谈,内容涉及他向媒体报告的一个不明空中物体。

**证人:** C. H. Zohn先生,海军研究实验室(NRL)火箭探空科的行政助理。Zohn此前曾向媒体透露他于1947年6月29日在新墨西哥州白沙观察到的一个空中物体。此次访谈是应陆军航空队情报处G. D. Garrett中校的要求进行的。

**目击事件:** 1947年6月29日星期日下午11:00至11:30之间,Zohn先生沿17号公路从新墨西哥州拉斯克鲁塞斯(Las Cruces, New Mexico)向东北方向前往白沙V-2导弹发射场。与他同行的有J. E. Kauke先生(NRL火箭探空科遥测主管)、G. C. Rockwood先生(NRL火箭探空科高空光谱学科学家)和Nancy Rockwood夫人。汽车由Kauke先生驾驶。

**物体:** 在指定时间段内的某一时刻,距离拉斯克鲁塞斯约三分之一路程处,Kauke先生注意到该物体并引起其他乘员的注意。Zohn先生打开离他最近的车窗,观察到该物体以未知的高速在未知的高度移动,估计约10,000英尺(尽管同样通过打开的车窗观察的Kauke先生估计在8,000至10,000英尺之间,且前一个估计几乎不可信)。

首次发现时,该物体位于汽车的右前方,高度未说明,显然在横向地从右向左穿过公路向北方向移动。汽车内所有人都观察到该物体。Zohn先生表示他无法观察到任何细节,只知道其形状是均匀的,没有像飞机机翼那样的突出物。距离太远无法进行立体视觉观测。

显然有一些太阳镜面反射,似乎随着物体远去而改变强度,直到从首次注意到后约30秒后从视野中消失。Zohn先生无法解释它如何消失,只是推测可能是反射角度突然改变。当时显然没有云层或能见度障碍。太阳在汽车后方。Kauke先生认为他曾一度看到了蒸汽尾迹。

**Interview Details:** This interview was conducted in the presence of Dr. H. E. Newell, Acting Rocket Sonde Section Head. The witness, Mr. Zohn, had recently been in the Navy and was described as familiar with the appearance of the majority of aircraft types and with meteorological balloons.

events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Ralph Stevens, co-pilot of a DC-3 aircraft, interviewed at 2130 hours on 9 July 1947. Stevens corroborated statements made by pilot Smith regarding a UFO sighting.

**Sighting:** On 4 July 1947, eight minutes after departing from Boise, Idaho, Stevens spotted the first object at 2012 hours. While flying at approximately 8,000 feet altitude, he thought it was an oncoming aircraft similar to their DC-3 about five miles away. He turned on landing lights to signal the other plane, then mentioned this to Smith. Both pilots watched as four more objects appeared at the same altitude as the first.

**Objects:** The objects seemed to be at the same altitude as their plane, about 6,000 feet, heading about 290 degrees magnetic North. Stevens turned to follow them and watched for four or five minutes as all five objects merged as one and disappeared. He could not determine whether they merged in line of flight, went beyond vision range, or dissipated. Two minutes later, the large object reappeared with three smaller ones on its left and one smaller one at a great distance to the right. This second group remained in sight for about twelve minutes in that formation before disappearing into the sunset. When last seen, the objects appeared to have continued climbing after the plane leveled off at nine or ten thousand feet.

**Conditions:** Weather was clear and unlimited with no clouds. Wind was 230-10 (out of Southwest at 10 mph). Air speed approximately 135 MPH. Sun was below the horizon; objects were silhouetted against the sky with no distinguishable color or reflection. A bright red glow from the sunset was visible above the horizon.

**Additional Details:** Stevens stated there was a big difference in size between the large objects and smaller ones, and it was hard to distinguish their shape. He confirmed the objects were at the same altitude as their climbing plane. The crew radioed ahead to Ontario, Oregon weather station (about thirty miles distant) asking them to look outside and observe. The weather station radioed back confirming they could see the objects.

events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** Ralph Stevens,一架DC-3飞机的副驾驶员,于1947年7月9日2130时接受访谈。Stevens证实了飞行员Smith关于UFO目击事件的陈述。

**Sighting:** 1947年7月4日,从爱达荷州博伊西(Boise, Idaho)起飞八分钟后,Stevens于2012时发现了第一个物体。当时飞行高度约为8,000英尺,他认为那是一架迎面而来的飞机,类似于他们的DC-3,距离约五英里。他打开着陆灯向另一架飞机发出信号,然后向Smith提及此事。两名飞行员一起观察时,又有四个物体出现在与第一个物体相同的高度上。

**Objects:** 这些物体似乎与他们的飞机处于同一高度,约6,000英尺,航向约为磁北290度。Stevens转向跟随它们,观察了四到五分钟,看到所有五个物体合并为一个并消失了。他无法确定它们是在飞行路线上合并、超出视野范围,还是消散了。两分钟后,那个大型物体重新出现,左侧有三个较小的物体,右侧远处有一个较小的物体。第二组物体保持该编队约十二分钟后消失在日落中。最后看到时,在飞机于九千或一万英尺高度平飞后,这些物体似乎继续爬升。

**Conditions:** 天气晴朗,能见度无限制,无云。风向风速为230-10(西南风,时速10英里)。空速约135英里/小时。太阳位于地平线以下;物体在天空中呈剪影状,无法辨别颜色或反光。地平线上方可见日落产生的明亮红色光芒。

**Additional Details:** Stevens表示大型物体与小型物体之间的尺寸差异很大,很难辨别它们的形状。他确认这些物体与他们正在爬升的飞机处于同一高度。机组人员通过无线电向前方约三十英里处的俄勒冈州安大略(Ontario, Oregon)气象站呼叫,要求他们到外面观察。气象站回复无线电确认他们能看到这些物体。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Memorandum for the Officer in Charge, Incident 44F 120B I, dated 16 July 1947, from Frank M. Brown, S/A, CIG 4th AF.

**Witness:** Captain Smith of United Airlines was interviewed at the Boise Municipal Airport, Boise, Idaho, on 12 July 1947. He was passing through Boise on a schedule flight at the time and had a 20-minute stop-over.

**Sighting:** Captain Smith reiterated statements originally made by him to the press regarding what he had seen in the late evening of July 4th, when 8 minutes out of Boise on the route to Seattle, Washington.

**Assessment:** The interviewer's opinion states that due to the position Captain Smith occupies, he (Captain Smith) would have to be very strongly convinced that he actually saw flying disks before he would open himself for the ridicule attached to a report of this type. The memorandum emphasizes the witness's credibility based on his professional position as an airline captain.

**Provenance:** Internal military intelligence memorandum documenting follow-up interview with commercial airline pilot regarding one of the numerous flying disk reports from July 1947.

**Sighting:** Smith机长重申了他此前向新闻界所做的陈述，内容涉及他在7月4日傍晚时分、在从博伊西飞往华盛顿州西雅图(Seattle, Washington)航线上起飞8分钟后所看到的情况。

**Assessment:** 访谈人员的意见指出，鉴于Smith机长所处的职位，他(Smith机长)必须非常确信自己确实看到了飞碟，才会冒着因报告此类事件而遭受嘲笑的风险。备忘录强调了该证人作为航空公司机长的职业身份所具有的可信度。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Sworn statement from Major Archie B. Browning, Air Corps, dated 16 July 1947, filed with Headquarters, Army Air Forces, Washington. Received at AFDIR-CO on 16 July 47. Handwritten notes indicate officer was assigned to ACIAS-1, Pentagon, phone 73852, with attached diagram referenced.

**Witness:** Major Archie B. Browning, AC (Air Corps), piloting a B-25 aircraft at 10,000 feet altitude on a flight from Ogden, Utah to Kansas City, Missouri.

**Sighting:** On 6 July 1947 at 1:45 P.M., approximately 100 miles west of Kansas City, Major Browning observed a very bright object low and to his left, approximately 10 miles away. After verifying his position on the map, he looked again (later time not specified in seconds). The object was described as a round, disc-shaped object, very bright and silvery colored, appearing to be flying one to two miles off his left wing at 11 o'clock position at 10,000 feet.

**Object Characteristics:** The brightness of the object was very great. Major Browning estimated it at 30-50 feet in diameter. The object traveled in the same direction at the same rate of speed (210 MPH) until it started to turn into the sun, then completely disappeared. Weather conditions at the time were CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited).

**Document Notes:** Handwritten annotation states "This officer is assigned to ACIAS-1, Pentagon, Phone 73852" and references an attached diagram (see attached diagram). Marked as document #9 in series.

**Sighting:** 1947年7月6日下午1:45，在堪萨斯城以西约100英里处，布朗宁少校观察到一个非常明亮的物体，位于他左侧低处，距离约10英里。在地图上确认自己的位置后，他再次观察(具体间隔秒数未在报告中说明)。该物体被描述为圆形、碟状物体，非常明亮，呈银色，看起来在他左翼1至2英里处飞行，位于11点钟方向，高度10,000英尺。

events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** Official Air Force directive establishing intelligence collection procedures

**Issuing Authority:** Department of the Air Force, Headquarters United States Air Force, Directorate of Intelligence, Washington 25, D.C.

**Classification:** RESTRICTED

**Purpose:** This memorandum establishes twofold requirements: (a) to enunciate continuing Air Force requirements for information pertaining to sightings of unconventional aircraft and unidentified flying objects, including the so-called "Flying Discs," and (b) to establish procedures for reporting such information.

**Administrative Action:** The document rescinds Department of the Army Collection Memorandum Number 7 (dated 21 January 1948) and letter CSGID 425.1 (dated 25 March 1948), transferring responsibility from Army to Air Force agencies.

**Reporting Procedures:** Establishes that complete answers should be dispatched by electrical transmission immediately after sightings, with supplementary reports forwarded by most expeditious means. Major Air Commands (Overseas) and Air Attaches are to transmit initial and supplementary cabled reports to the Director of Intelligence, USAF, with the phase "Pass to COMGENAMC WRIGHT-PATTERSON AFB, DAYTON, OHIO, ATTN: MCIAXO-3."

**Significance:** This directive formalizes Air Force UFO reporting channels during the early years of official investigation, establishing Wright-Patterson AFB as the central collection point for unidentified flying object reports.

events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** Administrative document with attached newspaper clipping discussing classification marking confusion.

**Incident:** A newspaper article titled "Glen Burnie 'Saucer' Clips 'Confidential,' but They Aren't" reports on a classification discrepancy involving "flying saucers" materials found in a Glen Burnie barn that were sent to Washington marked "Classified-Confidential."

**Classification Issue:** The article explains that as part of an OSI report containing other data, the clips were stamped into a folder marked "Confidential." However, the classification doesn't actually apply to the saucer materials themselves. An Air Force spokesman is quoted: "You can take that file and pull those clippings out and show them to anybody." He adds: "But if a folder is marked 'Confidential,' a fellow wants to look out because he knows some of the other stuff in there is a lot more important."

**Document Details:** The page contains multiple handwritten signatures and notations including "Killin'" and "Flying Discs!" The document is stamped "NOT RECORDED" dated "45 SEP 14 1949" with reference number "64-53594-A". Source is listed as "WASHINGTON DAILY NEWS FINAL EDITION" dated 9/13/47 (though the stamp shows 1949, suggesting a typographical error in the newspaper date line).

**Administrative Routing:** The page appears to be part of an internal routing system with multiple names listed on the right margin including Tolson, Ladd, Clegg, Glavin, Nichols, Rosen, Tracy, Harbo, Mohr, Tele. Room, Nease, and Gandy.

events.report_summary:
**Publication:** This is Issue No. 24 of Flying Saucers International, the official journal of the Amalgamated Flying Saucer Clubs of America, Inc. (AFSCA), published quarterly from headquarters at 2004 N. Hoover St., Los Angeles, California 90027. Gabriel Green served as Editor; Helen Green as Assistant Editor.

**Special Message:** The issue opens with a special message received by Master Kato-Helo on May 1, 1966, via a special directional short-wave radio from "Space Ship #1" orbiting at 15,000 feet. The message describes a remarkable ship capable of initial radio contact in 1961, monitoring Earth on special screens while the crew performs multi-hour watches. The entity claims their race has undersea and underground bases on our planet and many spaceships. They state they allowed pilots to observe their craft in a short sighting.

**Political Commentary:** The message warns that "Your government is a military puppet, a mere parrot of the monstrosity that is the Military-Industrial complex" and criticizes senators who are "robots" following the rule of 2%. It specifically critiques the Vietnam War as bringing "some degree of affluence" to the United States while questioning if ending the war would be good for the economy. The text suggests the U.S. economy has been "brainwashed into you by the Military-Industrial complex."

**AFSCA Activities:** The newsletter announces upcoming wedding bells for Gabriel Green and Helen Onken (June 4, 1966), a ceremonial meeting in Hollenbeck Park, Los Angeles with Sophia's parents from Mexico City present. Lists available publications including books by George Van Tassel, Bryant Reeve, Paul Thomas, George Hunt Williamson, and others. Membership information provided at $5.00/year.

**Convention News:** Announces AFSCA's 4th Annual Giant Space Ship Convention held June 18-19, 1966, with various speakers including Daniel W. Fry and Buck Nelson. Notes the International UFO Congress scheduled for February 5-6, 1966 in Hollywood.

**Guest Speakers:** Reports that Mr. Noel Scott, former Air Force lieutenant and airline pilot, spoke at the June 11 meeting about his Flying Saucer experiences and the Holloman AFB landing. He appeared on Louis Lomax TV Show and was invited by Mexican government group to speak. Also mentions Mrs. Dorothy Forrester of Inglewood speaking about a two-hour space craft experience in Los Angeles.

**Administrative Notes:** Emphasizes importance of ZIP codes for mailing, announces price increases on some publications from England, and notes back issues #6 and #11 are out of print. Requests members not to order unavailable materials.

events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** FBI memorandum from SAC Miami to Director, FBI, dated 6/8/67, regarding information provided by Paul L. Peyerl concerning unidentified flying objects.

**Witness Background:** Paul L. Peyerl appeared at the Miami FBI Office on July 24, 1959, volunteering to return to Austria as an intelligence agent. His expressed motivation was to repay a debt he felt he owed the United States. He was afforded a Washington, D.C. address at CIA Headquarters and told his inquiry should be directed there.

**Prior Contact:** On July 4, 1961, Peyerl appeared at the Miami Office again and gave an incoherent story of recently meeting an individual who asked him to kill his mother. Peyerl appeared to be somewhat bewildered and continuously gazed away from the interviewing agent during this visit.

**UFO Claim:** During his most recent visit to the Miami Office, Peyerl seemed genuinely concerned about the existence of an object he allegedly photographed during November 1944. He exhibited no emotional nor mental disorder and appeared to be rational.

**Disposition:** In view of recent publicity afforded UFO sightings, some apparently by responsible sources, this information is submitted to the Bureau for consideration of transmittal to the U.S. Air Force.

**Note:** The document shows various routing stamps and classification markings, including "FLYING SAUCERS" notation and reference number 62-83794-460.

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 220

**Witness:** Mr. Robert Tretcer, an AF Veteran, currently employed as a Science teacher at Francisco Jr High School.

**Sighting:** On the night of 29 November 1948 at approximately 2113 hours (9:13 PM), the witness called Headquarters 4th Air Force to report a yellow light flash he observed crossing the sky. The light was headed due North, then turned Northwest and disappeared.

**Object Characteristics:** The object appeared as a yellow light flash that lasted for about 7 seconds. The witness noted it was traveling too fast for a plane, but did not appear to be a comet or shooting star.

**Assessment:** The brief duration (7 seconds), high speed, and change of direction from due North to Northwest suggest an object with maneuverability. The witness's background as an AF Veteran and his profession as a Science teacher lend credibility to the observation and his ability to distinguish the object from conventional aircraft or astronomical phenomena.

**Document:** This appears to be an incident report card or summary, numbered 220, documenting the sighting report made to military authorities.

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 223a

**Date & Time:** 5 December 1948, approximately 2135 hours (initial report stated 2120 hours)

**Witnesses:** Captain VAN LLOYD, pilot of Pioneer Flight #65, and co-pilot James L. Smith

**Aircraft:** C-47 type plane operated by Frontier Airline Operations, Kirtland AF Base, at altitude of 9,000 ft (possibly heading of 270°)

**Sighting:** While approaching Las Vegas, Nevada, Captain VAN LLOYD initially reported seeing a green light approximately 40 miles west of Las Vegas. Pilot at first believed the light was a shooting star, but upon questioning thought it was too near the ground. He initially stated a very high altitude - about 500 ft. When he first observed the object, it appeared to be coming straight toward the plane and he attempted to swerve to avoid the light; however, it then trailed off to the ground. The light was pale green and had a pale green trail, like that on a rocket.

**Object Description:** Described as a bright white flash that came into view, then appeared as a yellowish orange color. Object first appeared to be coming directly toward their plane, then arched downward and disappeared from sight. Visible for a few seconds; no estimate could be made of size or distance.

**Discrepancy:** A discrepancy in color (time in the altitude) was noted between the initial telephone report to Kirtland AF Base Control Tower and the subsequent personal interview with S/A ELKIN, FBI. In the second report the object was described as higher than their plane (which was flying at 9,000 ft).

**Report Sources:** First report made to Kirtland AF Base Control Tower; second report obtained by S/A ELKIN, FBI in a personal interview. Reference made to Report No. 223 for surrounding data.
events.title_ocr_original: Sighting near Kirtland AFB, Albuquerque, New Mexico — Box 7 Incident Summary p.0119
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 223a

**Date & Time:** 1948年12月5日，大约2135时（初始报告称2120时）

**Witnesses:** VAN LLOYD上尉，先锋航班#65的飞行员，以及副驾驶James L. Smith

**Aircraft:** C-47型飞机，由边境航空公司运营，隶属于柯特兰空军基地(Kirtland AF Base)，飞行高度9,000英尺（航向可能为270°）

**Sighting:** 在接近内华达州拉斯维加斯(Las Vegas, Nevada)时，VAN LLOYD上尉最初报告在拉斯维加斯以西约40英里处看到一个绿色光体。飞行员起初认为该光体是流星，但经询问后认为它离地面太近。他最初陈述的高度非常高——约500英尺。当他首次观察到该物体时，它似乎正径直朝飞机飞来，他试图转向以避开该光体；然而，它随后拖曳着光迹坠向地面。该光体呈淡绿色，并带有淡绿色尾迹，类似火箭的尾迹。

**Object Description:** 被描述为一道明亮的白色闪光进入视野，随后呈现黄橙色。物体最初似乎正径直朝他们的飞机飞来，然后向下呈弧形运动并从视线中消失。可见时间仅几秒钟；无法估计其大小或距离。

**Discrepancy:** 在向柯特兰空军基地控制塔的初始电话报告与随后FBI特工ELKIN进行的面谈之间，发现了颜色（高度时间）方面的差异。在第二份报告中，该物体被描述为高于他们的飞机（当时飞行高度为9,000英尺）。

**Report Sources:** 第一份报告向柯特兰空军基地控制塔提交；第二份报告由FBI特工ELKIN通过面谈获得。参考第223号报告以获取相关背景数据。

events.title: Lt. McHenry: 2 silver discs, 300 MPH, Muroc AAFld, CA (8 Jul 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** Check-list report for unidentified flying objects, marked CONFIDENTIAL, Incident #1.

**Witness:** 1st Lt. Joseph C. McHenry, Billeting Officer in Charge at Muroc Army Air Field, California. Observation made from ground level at Muroc AAFld.

**Date & Time:** 8 July 1947 at 0930 hours.

**Number of Objects:** Two objects initially observed, with one appearing sometime later.

**Object Characteristics:** Color described as silver; shape reported as disc-like or spherical. Apparent construction appeared metallic (N/S - not specified, but apparently metallic). Size not specified.

**Flight Characteristics:** Objects flying at approximately 8,000 feet altitude at estimated speed of 300 MPH. Direction of flight: 320° due north heading. Tactics: performed a tight circle. Distance from observer and time in sight not specified (N/S).

**Additional Details:** No sound detected. No odor detected. No exhaust trails observed. Weather conditions not specified. No effect on clouds noted. No sketches or photographs available. Manner of disappearance: objects disappeared in the distance.

**Remarks:** At approximately 0900 hours, Lt. McHenry left Post Exchange (note appears incomplete at page bottom, marked CONFIDENTIAL).

**Document Status:** This appears to be a standardized military UFO reporting form from the early days of the 1947 flying disc wave.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document Type:** 不明飞行物核查清单报告,标记为机密,事件编号#1。

**Witness:** 约瑟夫·C·麦克亨利(Joseph C. McHenry)一级中尉,加利福尼亚州穆罗克陆军航空基地(Muroc Army Air Field, California)宿舍主管。观察地点为穆罗克陆军航空基地地面。

**Date & Time:** 1947年7月8日0930时。

**Number of Objects:** 最初观察到两个物体,稍后又出现一个。

**Object Characteristics:** 颜色描述为银色;形状报告为碟状或球形。外观构造似为金属(N/S - 未明确说明,但显然为金属)。尺寸未说明。

**Flight Characteristics:** 物体在约8,000英尺高度飞行,估计速度为300英里/小时。飞行方向:正北320°航向。飞行动作:进行了紧密盘旋。与观察者的距离及可见时间未说明(N/S)。

**Additional Details:** 未检测到声音。未检测到气味。未观察到尾迹。天气状况未说明。未注意到对云层的影响。无草图或照片。消失方式:物体在远处消失。

**Remarks:** 约0900时,麦克亨利中尉离开军人服务社(注释在页面底部似不完整,标记为机密)。

**Document Status:** 这似乎是1947年飞碟浪潮早期的标准化军方UFO报告表格。

events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 3

**Date & Time:** 7 July 1947 at 10:10

**Witness:** Major J. C. Wise, Test Pilot stationed at Muroc Army Air Field, Muroc, California

**Location:** Ground observation at Muroc AAF, Muroc, California

**Object Description:** One spherical object, 5 to 10 feet in diameter, yellowish-white in color. The object was located off to the north at an altitude of 10,000 to 12,000 feet.

**Flight Characteristics:** Speed estimated at 200 to 225 MPH, heading from west to east. Tactics described as "oscillating in a forward whirling movement without losing altitude." Time in sight was not stated.

**Distance:** Object was approximately 10,000 to 12,000 feet altitude from the observer.

**Sound & Physical Effects:** No sound detected. No exhaust trails observed. Effect on clouds not stated.

**Initial Assessment:** The apparent construction was assumed at first to be a weather balloon.

**Weather & Other Conditions:** Weather conditions not stated. No sketches or photographs were obtained.

**Manner of Disappearance:** Not stated.

**Document Classification:** This is a confidential military checklist for unidentified flying objects, cataloging detailed observation parameters in standardized format.

events.title: Mr & Mrs Norman Hall: formation of flying objects, Logan, UT (8 Sep 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** RESTRICTED check-list report on unidentified flying objects, Incident #61a.

**Witnesses:** Mr. & Mrs. Norman Hall of Logan, Utah. Occupation listed as N/S (not stated).

**Sighting Details:** On September 8, 1947, at approximately 10:30 P.M., the witnesses observed unidentified flying objects from Logan, Utah (coordinates 40° 45' N, 111° 54' W). The number of objects, distance from observer, time in sight, and altitude were all not stated in the report.

**Object Characteristics:** Speed described as "Much faster than birds." Direction of flight was clockwise above the city. Size approximated as "that of sta5" (likely star5 or similar reference). Tactics included changed formation during observation. Color, shape, odor, apparent construction, and exhaust trails were all marked N/S (not stated).

**Environmental Conditions:** Weather conditions were cloudy. Effect on clouds not stated. No sketches or photographs were available.

**Remarks:** The observers noted seeing "a group of flying objects similar in appearance to a group of moving stars which traveled clockwise above the city." The comparison to moving stars suggests luminous objects visible against the night sky, moving in coordinated formation.

**Document Status:** Marked RESTRICTED with "(over)" notation indicating continuation on reverse page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document Type:** 关于不明飞行物的限制级核查清单报告，事件编号#61a。

**Witnesses:** 犹他州洛根(Logan, Utah)的诺曼·霍尔(Norman Hall)先生和夫人。职业列为N/S(未说明)。

**Sighting Details:** 1947年9月8日晚上约10:30，目击者在犹他州洛根(坐标北纬40° 45'，西经111° 54')观察到不明飞行物。报告中未说明物体数量、与观察者的距离、可见时间和飞行高度。

**Object Characteristics:** 速度描述为"比鸟类快得多"。飞行方向为在城市上空顺时针方向。大小约为"sta5的大小"(可能是star5或类似参照物)。战术包括在观察期间改变编队。颜色、形状、气味、明显构造和尾迹均标记为N/S(未说明)。

**Environmental Conditions:** 天气状况为多云。对云层的影响未说明。无草图或照片可用。

**Remarks:** 观察者注意到看见"一组飞行物体，外观类似于一组移动的星星，在城市上空顺时针方向移动"。与移动星星的比较表明这些是在夜空中可见的发光物体,以协调编队移动。

**Document Status:** 标记为限制级，带有"(over)"标注，表示在背面有续页。

events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** RESTRICTED checklist for Unidentified Flying Objects, Incident #71.

**Witness:** Thomas L. Moore, Captain, USAAF, Ex-pilot.

**Date & Location:** 8 or 9 October 1947, outskirts of Las Vegas, Nevada.

**Sighting Details:** Observer witnessed one object at a distance of 4 to 5 miles. Time in sight and altitude were not specified (marked N/S).

**Object Characteristics:**
- **Speed:** 700 to 800 MPH
- **Direction of Flight:** East, then circled to west
- **Tactics:** Flew straight, turned, flew straight again
- **Sound:** Not specified
- **Size:** Not specified
- **Color:** Not specified
- **Shape:** Not specified
- **Odor:** None detected
- **Apparent Construction:** Not specified

**Exhaust Trails:** Trail described as "almost white and of cumulus cloud density which lasted some 15-20 minutes, almost cloudless."

**Weather Conditions:** Almost cloudless.

**Effect on Clouds:** Not specified.

**Documentation:** Sketch of course of object mentioned but not included on this page.

**Manner of Disappearance:** Not specified.

**Remarks:** Document indicates "(over)" suggesting additional information on reverse page. This standardized Air Force checklist format was used to systematically collect UFO observation data during the early investigative period.

events.title: Capt. E. A. Prehn: 3-6 chromium discs over Portland, OR (4 Jul 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** Incident #9 in a classified U.S. government checklist of unidentified flying objects.

**Witness:** Capt. E. A. Prehn, Harbor Pilot, residing at Ft. NW Irving St., Portland, Oregon. Observation made from the same location.

**Date & Time:** July 4, 1947, at 1305 hours.

**Object Description:** Observer reported 3 to 6 objects but was unable to ascertain the exact number. Objects were described as chromium in color and shiny. Shape was reported as "full disc, half-moon shape, then nothing," suggesting a changing or rotating appearance. Distance from observer not stated (N/S). Size not specified (N/S).

**Flight Characteristics:** Objects flew at high altitude at "terrific" speed, heading south over the Globe Hills. Tactics included oscillating, wobbling, disappearing and reappearing. Time in sight not specified (N/S). No sound detected, no odor detected, no exhaust trails observed.

**Manner of Disappearance:** Objects disappeared and reappeared during the sighting.

**Additional Details:** Weather conditions not specified. Effect on clouds not specified. No sketches or photographs available. Apparent construction and other technical details not stated.

**Document Classification:** This checklist bears "RESTRICTED" classification markings at top and bottom of page.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Date & Time:** 1947年7月4日，1305时。

events.title: Coast Guardsman Frank Ryman: white saucer over Lake Washington (4 July 1947)

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #11 in the RESTRICTED CHECK-LIST of UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS.

**Witness:** Frank Ryman, Coast Guardsman, residing in Lake City, Seattle, Washington. The observer's occupation as Coast Guardsman lends credibility to the report.

**Sighting Details:** On the evening of 4 July 1947, Ryman observed a single unidentified flying object from ground level in Lake City. The object was visible for approximately 10 minutes. The sighting occurred over the north end of Lake Washington.

**Object Description:** The object was described as **white** in color and **saucer or ball shaped**. Distance from observer, altitude, speed, size, sound, odor, apparent construction, exhaust trails, weather conditions, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance were all marked as "N/S" (not stated or not specified).

**Flight Characteristics:** The object executed **horizontal flight** traveling over the north end of Lake Washington.

**Documentation:** The form indicates "1 news photographs" were available as sketches or photographs. Additional remarks are noted as "(over)" suggesting continuation on reverse side.

**Provenance:** This is a standardized military intelligence checklist form stamped RESTRICTED, indicating official documentation and classification of the incident during the 1947 UFO wave.

events.title: Kenneth Arnold: 9 disc-shaped objects near Mt. Rainier, WA (24 Jun 1947)

events.report_summary:
**Incident #17 - Kenneth Arnold Sighting**

**Date & Time:** 24 June 1947 at 1500 hours

**Witness:** Kenneth Arnold, a dealer in fire control supplies who holds a private pilot's license. Address: Box 387, Boise, Idaho.

**Location:** Near Mineral, Washington, in the Mt. Ranier area.

**Sighting Details:** Arnold observed 9 unidentified flying objects at an altitude of 9,500 feet. The objects were in sight for 2-1/2 to 3 minutes and were at a distance of approximately 20 to 25 miles from the observer. They traveled at an estimated speed of 150 MPH, flying in horizontal flight from North to South at 170 degrees.

**Object Characteristics:** The objects were approximately circular in shape, with size estimated at 45 to 50 feet (roughly comparable to a DC-4 aircraft). Color described as "mirror like." No sound was detected (N/S). No odor detected (N/S). Apparent construction not specified (N/S). No exhaust trails observed (N/S).

**Weather & Documentation:** Weather conditions were CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited). Effect on clouds: N/S. Arnold produced drawings as documentation of the sighting. Manner of disappearance: N/S.

**Document Note:** This is a confidential checklist form for unidentified flying objects. Additional remarks indicated as "(over)" but continuation page not shown.

**地点:** 华盛顿州米纳勒尔(Mineral, Washington)附近,雷尼尔山(Mt. Ranier)地区。

**Sighting:** On 30 June 1947 at approximately 5:45 PM, while traveling west from Boise, Idaho toward Plantation Golf Course, the observer witnessed one unidentified object. **Object Characteristics:** The object was stationary (no speed or directional flight) and appeared bright and silvery in color. Its shape was described as half-circled. The apparent construction "looked like a mirror in the sun." Size and sound were not stated. No tactics were observed, and no odor was detected.

**Additional Details:** The object seemed to be clinging to a large cloud. No exhaust trails were observed. Weather conditions were not stated. No sketches or photographs were taken, and the manner of disappearance was not stated.

events.title: Capt. Charles E. McGee: hovering light near Lockbourne AAB, Ohio (7 Jan 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #30 in restricted UFO checklist series.

**Witness:** Captain Charles E. McGee, USAF, Assistant Operations Officer (Pilot), Airdrome Operations, Lockbourne AAB, Columbus, Ohio.

**Sighting:** On 7 January 1948 at 1925 EST, Capt. McGee observed one unidentified flying object during a Runway 23 overhead approach at Lockbourne Army Air Base. The object was first spotted approximately 1-5 miles southwest of the base, then observed a second time 6-7 miles west, moving westerly in a hovering manner. Altitude was approximately 3000 feet. Time in sight was not stated.

**Object characteristics:** Large size, comparable to a flood light. Shape described as oval, "as if looking at spot light." Color changed from white to yellowish to orange. Speed was slow, direction of flight westward. **Tactics:** Flashed on and off, appeared to be fading and descending on westward flight. **Sound:** No noise detected. **Apparent construction:** Like a spot light. **Exhaust trails:** Not stated initially, but whitish streaks like jet effect observed from right, according to Mr. Boudreaux on "squawk" box.

**Weather conditions:** Sky solid overcast. Effect on clouds not stated. No sketches or photographs obtained.

**Manner of disappearance:** Descending and burning out.

**Document classification:** RESTRICTED.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 限制级UFO核查清单系列第30号事件。

**Witness:** Charles E. McGee上尉，美国空军(USAF)，作战助理官(飞行员)，机场作战部门，俄亥俄州哥伦布市洛克伯恩陆军航空基地(Lockbourne AAB)。

**Sighting:** 1948年1月7日东部标准时间19时25分，McGee上尉在洛克伯恩陆军航空基地23号跑道上空进场时观测到一个不明飞行物体。该物体首次被发现时位于基地西南方约1-5英里处，第二次观测时在西侧6-7英里处，以悬停方式向西移动。高度约为3000英尺。目击持续时间未说明。

**Object characteristics:** 体积大，可比作泛光灯。形状描述为椭圆形，"如同看着聚光灯一样"。颜色从白色变为黄色再变为橙色。速度缓慢，飞行方向向西。**Tactics:** 闪烁明灭，在向西飞行时似乎逐渐变暗并下降。**Sound:** 未探测到噪音。**Apparent construction:** 像聚光灯一样。**Exhaust trails:** 初始未说明，但根据Boudreaux先生在"squawk"通话盒上的报告，从右侧观察到类似喷气效应的白色条纹。

**Weather conditions:** 天空完全被云层覆盖。对云层的影响未说明。未获得素描图或照片。

**Manner of disappearance:** 下降并熄灭。

**Document classification:** 限制级。

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #32

**Witness:** Lt. C. W. Thomas, pilot on Flight AF 99144 from Dayton to Washington.

**Sighting:** On 7 January 1948 at 1953 hours, during a cross-country flight from Dayton to Washington, the witness observed an unidentified flying object near Columbus Airways, to the west of his position. The observation occurred at an altitude of 3000 feet.

**Object Description:** The object appeared as a large, bright amber light positioned off to the west. It was described as "like a large star or planet" in shape and size. The witness estimated the object was approximately 15 miles away from their aircraft and located below them at about 3000 feet altitude. The object appeared stationary with no maneuvers observed.

**Flight Conditions:** Weather conditions were dark and overcast. Distance from observer was approximately 15 miles. Time in sight was not stated.

**Physical Characteristics:** Speed appeared stationary; direction of flight was stationary; no exhaust trails were observed; no odor detected; apparent construction not stated; no sound noted; no effect on clouds stated.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Manner of disappearance not stated. This is a restricted military checklist document for unidentified flying objects.

**Sighting:** 1948年1月7日19时53分,在执行从代顿飞往华盛顿的越野飞行期间,目击者在哥伦布航路(Columbus Airways)附近、其位置以西观察到一个不明飞行物。观察发生时的高度为3000英尺。

**Object Description:** 该物体呈现为一个巨大、明亮的琥珀色光体,位于西侧方向。其形状和大小被描述为"像一颗大星星或行星"。目击者估计该物体距离他们的飞机约15英里,位于他们下方约3000英尺高度处。该物体看起来静止不动,未观察到任何机动动作。

**Flight Conditions:** 天气条件为黑暗且多云。距离观察者约15英里。目击持续时间未说明。

**Physical Characteristics:** 速度表现为静止;飞行方向为静止;未观察到尾气轨迹;未探测到气味;表观结构未说明;未记录到声音;对云层的影响未说明。

**Documentation:** 未获得草图或照片。消失方式未说明。这是一份关于不明飞行物的军方机密核查清单文件。

events.location: Between Everett, Massachusetts and Bedford Radio Beacon
events.title: Pan American Airways crew: two elliptical objects near Boston, MA (4 Aug 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** Incident #73, a confidential UFO report filed with the U.S. government regarding unidentified flying objects observed near Boston, Massachusetts.

**Witnesses:** Alphonse D. Powell (Captain, PA Airways, Inc.) and Walter I. White (Navigator), crew members of a Pan American Constitution aircraft. Observer address: 28 Redwood Road, New Hyde Park, Long Island.

**Date & Time:** 4 August 1947 at 1600 hours (4:00 PM).

**Location:** Approximately midway between Everett, Massachusetts and Bedford Radio Beacon.

**Sighting Details:** Two objects observed at a distance of 1 mile from the aircraft for approximately 30 seconds. The aircraft was flying at 7,800 feet altitude at 175 MPH.

**Object Characteristics:** Each object was 15 feet long and approximately 2-3 feet in depth. Deep gold in color with an elliptical shape. Direction of flight was easterly, approximately 110° magnetic. No sound detected (N/S), no exhaust trails observed ("None"), no odor detected (N/S), and apparent construction not determined (N/S).

**Weather Conditions:** 5/10 scattered cumulus clouds with tops at 1000 feet; visibility 10 miles.

**Disappearance:** The objects were lost in clouds.

**Additional Notes:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Effect on clouds not specified (N/S). The document is marked "CONFIDENTIAL" and appears to be part of an official military or government investigation into unexplained aerial phenomena during the 1947 UFO wave.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 事件 #73，一份提交给美国政府的机密UFO报告，涉及在马萨诸塞州波士顿(Boston, Massachusetts)附近观测到的不明飞行物。

**Witnesses:** Alphonse D. Powell（机长，PA Airways, Inc.）和Walter I. White（领航员），泛美宪法号(Pan American Constitution)航班机组成员。观察者地址：长岛新海德公园(New Hyde Park, Long Island)红木路(Redwood Road) 28号。

**Date & Time:** 1947年8月4日 1600时（下午4:00）。

**Location:** 大约位于马萨诸塞州埃弗里特(Everett, Massachusetts)和贝德福德无线电信标台(Bedford Radio Beacon)之间的中点位置。

**Sighting Details:** 在距离飞机1英里处观测到两个物体，持续时间约30秒。飞机当时飞行高度为7,800英尺，速度175 MPH。

**Object Characteristics:** 每个物体长15英尺，厚度约2-3英尺。深金色，呈椭圆形状。飞行方向为向东，约磁方位角110°。未探测到声音(N/S)，未观察到尾迹("None")，未探测到气味(N/S)，明显构造无法确定(N/S)。

**Weather Conditions:** 5/10散积云，云顶高度1000英尺；能见度10英里。

**Disappearance:** 这些物体消失在云层中。

**Additional Notes:** 未获得草图或照片。对云层的影响未说明(N/S)。该文件标注为"CONFIDENTIAL"（机密），似乎是1947年UFO浪潮期间军方或政府对无法解释的空中现象进行正式调查的一部分。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Restricted check-list for unidentified flying objects, Incident #35, excerpted from the Oregon Journal dated 13 Nov 1947.

**Witness:** Second Officer Claude Lee Williamson observed the objects at sea, 20 miles offshore and 40 miles south of Cape Blanco, Oregon.

**Date & Time:** 12 November 1947, early morning hours.

**Object Count:** 2 objects observed.

**Duration:** 45 seconds in sight.

**Speed & Direction:** Traveling at 700 to 900 MPH from the north horizon in a westerly direction.

**Maneuvers:** The objects performed a long, low arc.

**Appearance:** Ball-shaped objects with apparent construction of fire. Size, color, and sound not specified (N/S). Exhaust trails described as "jet-like streams of fire."

**Altitude & Distance:** Not specified.

**Physical Evidence:** No sketches or photographs obtained. Weather conditions and effect on clouds not specified. Manner of disappearance not specified. No odor detected.

**Context:** This restricted military document catalogues the sighting systematically, noting the high velocity and fiery appearance of the objects witnessed by a maritime officer in the early post-war UFO wave period.

events.title: Constable Eric Kearsey: 5 phosphorescent objects, Grand Falls, NL (9 Jul 1947)

events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 39

**Date & Time:** 9 July 1947, between 11:15 and 11:40

**Witness:** Eric Kearsey, Constable with the Newfoundland Constabulary, Grand Falls

**Location:** Grand Falls, Newfoundland

**Sighting:** Observer witnessed initially 4 objects, then 1 additional object later, for a total of 5. The sighting lasted for a brief period.

**Object Characteristics:** Objects were described as round, approximately the size of a barrel head. They appeared phosphorescent with a glowing quality. The first four objects flew in an easterly direction while maintaining formation, flying side by side. The last object flew in a rocking motion. Speed was described as "terrific." There appeared to be a phosphorescent glow about the objects, though exhaust trails were not clearly observed.

**Flight Behavior:** The first four objects maintained tight formation and flew side by side. Direction of flight was easterly. Distance from observer, altitude, and manner of disappearance were not specified (N/S).

**Additional Details:** No sound was detected. No odor was detected. Weather conditions not specified. No effect on clouds observed. No sketches or photographs were taken. This is a restricted government document cataloging unidentified flying objects as part of official investigation procedures.

**Flight Behavior:** 前四个物体保持紧密编队并排飞行。飞行方向为向东。与观察者的距离、高度以及消失方式未予说明(N/S)。

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #43

**Witness:** Dale Bays, a former bus driver residing at Box 12, Crocker, Missouri, observed unidentified flying objects approximately 7 miles out of Clarion, Iowa in the direction of Mason City, Iowa (coordinates: 42° 43' N - 93° 44' W).

**Date/Time:** 29 June 1947 at 1645 hours (4:45 P.M.)

**Objects:** Two groups of objects were observed - 5 in the first group and 13 in the second group, totaling 18 objects. The objects were observed in single file formation.

**Physical Characteristics:** Each object measured from 175 to 250 feet in diameter and 12 feet in thickness. Shape described as between a circle and an oval - "inverted saucer." Color was "dirty" white. Distance from observer was not specified (N/S).

**Flight Characteristics:** Objects flew at an altitude of 1200 feet at an estimated speed of 300 MPH. Direction of flight was South by Southeast and North Northwest. Time in sight: several minutes.

**Sound:** Described as sounding like that of an electric motor or dynamo.

**Additional Details:** No odor detected, no exhaust trails observed, weather conditions not specified. Apparent construction, effect on clouds, sketches/photographs, and manner of disappearance were not recorded (N/S).

**Document:** This is a restricted U.S. government check-list form for unidentified flying objects, part of the official investigative record.

**Date/Time:** 1947年6月29日16时45分（下午4:45）

**Objects:** 观察到两组物体——第一组5个，第二组13个，总计18个物体。物体呈单列队形。

**Physical Characteristics:** 每个物体直径约175至250英尺，厚度12英尺。形状介于圆形和椭圆形之间——"倒置的碟状"。颜色为"暗淡的"白色。与观察者的距离未说明（N/S）。

**Flight Characteristics:** 物体在1200英尺高度飞行，估计速度为300英里/小时。飞行方向为东南偏南和西北偏北。视野停留时间：数分钟。

**Sound:** 描述为类似电动机或发电机的声音。

**Additional Details:** 未检测到气味，未观察到尾迹，天气状况未说明。明显的构造、对云层的影响、草图/照片以及消失方式均未记录（N/S）。

**Document:** 这是一份美国政府关于不明飞行物的受限核查清单表格，是官方调查记录的一部分。

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #45 in a restricted checklist series tracking unidentified flying objects.

**Date & Location:** Afternoon of 28 June 1947, Illinois. The specific location within Illinois is not specified.

**Witness:** Observer details marked "N/S" (not specified), though remarks indicate the information was taken from "The Latest News" radio broadcast at 8:00 to 8:15 A.M. with Charles Sebastin.

**Objects:** 7 to 10 objects were observed. The checklist form provides fields for comprehensive details including distance, time in sight, altitude, speed, direction of flight, tactics, sound, size, color, shape, odor detected, apparent construction, exhaust trails, weather conditions, effect on clouds, sketches/photographs, and manner of disappearance—but none of these fields are filled in on this page.

**Document Details:** This is a standardized "RESTRICTED" classification checklist form for UFO incidents. The form indicates "(over)" at the bottom, suggesting additional information on a reverse page. The remarks section notes the information was broadcast on 29 June 1947 at 8:00 A.M. over WGN "The Latest News" with announcer Charles Sebastin.

**Assessment:** This appears to be an administrative record capturing a radio news report of a UFO sighting, with minimal details recorded on this page.

events.title: Ward L. Stewart: 2 milk-white objects at 750 MPH, Hamilton Field, CA (29 Jul 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 52A

**Witness:** Ward L. Stewart, 1st Lieutenant, Air Reserve, former B-29 pilot. Address: Hearst Mining Building, University of California.

**Sighting:** On 29 July 1947 after 1200 hours near Hamilton Field, California, Lt. Stewart observed 2 unidentified flying objects. The sighting lasted approximately 15 seconds. Coordinates given as 38° 03' N 122° 31' W.

**Object Characteristics:** The objects were described as milk-white in color. They traveled at an estimated altitude of 6,000 feet at approximately 750 MPH on a heading of 120°. The observer noted their tactics were "similar to fighter a/c when accompanying heavier ships." No sound was heard during the observation. Size, shape, odor, apparent construction, weather conditions, and effect on clouds are all marked N/S (not specified).

**Additional Details:** No exhaust trails were observed. No sketches or photographs were taken. The objects' manner of disappearance was that they "flew out of sight." Distance from observer not specified.

**Document Type:** This is a standard military checklist form for reporting unidentified flying objects, marked CONFIDENTIAL. The form indicates remarks continue overleaf.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Sighting:** 1947年7月29日1200时后，在加利福尼亚州汉密尔顿机场(Hamilton Field, California)附近，Stewart中尉观察到2个不明飞行物体。目击持续时间约15秒。坐标为北纬38° 03' 西经122° 31'。

**Object Characteristics:** 这些物体被描述为乳白色。它们以约6,000英尺的高度、约750英里/小时的速度飞行，航向120°。观察者注意到它们的战术"类似于伴随重型飞机的战斗机"。观察期间未听到任何声音。尺寸、形状、气味、明显构造、天气条件以及对云层的影响均标注为N/S(未说明)。

**Additional Details:** 未观察到尾迹。未绘制草图或拍摄照片。物体的消失方式为"飞出视线"。与观察者的距离未说明。

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #53

**Date/Time:** 26 June 1947 at 1515 GST

**Witness:** 1st Lt Eric B. Armstrong, Ferry Division, Brooks Field, San Antonio, Texas, 170th AF Base Unit

**Location:** 30 miles northwest of Lake Meade, Nevada, observed from air at 6,000 ft altitude

**Objects:** 5 or 6 unidentified flying objects observed in horizontal very close formation

**Characteristics:** Each object was circular in shape, white in color, and approximately 36 inches in diameter. The formation traveled at approximately 285 MPH on a heading of 120° (northwest). Distance from observer and time in sight not specified (N/S).

**Additional Details:** No sound was detected. No odor, exhaust trails, weather conditions, or effect on clouds reported. No sketches or photographs were taken. Apparent construction and manner of disappearance not specified.

**Document:** This is a RESTRICTED classified check-list for unidentified flying objects, part of the early systematic Air Force documentation of UFO sightings in June 1947, shortly after the Kenneth Arnold sighting that initiated widespread "flying saucer" reports.

events.title: Miss Patricia Abbott & Lt Hammaker: reddish flashes, Newfoundland (23 Jul 1947)

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #55 in a classified U.S. military check-list of unidentified flying objects.

**Witnesses:** Miss Patricia Abbott (government employee) and Lt Hammaker (Navigator & Public Relations Officer). Both observed from Harmon Field, Stephenville, Newfoundland at coordinates 48° 30' N 58° 33' W.

**Date/Time:** 23 July 1947 at 0345Z (0715 local time).

**Object(s):** Number undetermined, observed for approximately three minutes at an altitude of 10,000 feet. The object(s) exhibited **reddish flashes of light** and performed **abrupt darts** as tactical maneuvers. Direction of flight listed as NNE (north-northeast).

**Performance:** Described as traveling at **high velocity**, specifically stated to be **faster than conventional aircraft**. No sound was detected during the observation. Distance from observers not specified (N/S).

**Conditions:** Weather conditions featured high scattered clouds with visibility of 15 miles.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Shape, size, odor, apparent construction, exhaust trails, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance all listed as N/S (not specified). The document is marked RESTRICTED and indicates remarks continue on an additional page (over).

events.title: S/Sgt Ira L. Livingston: 7-10 round objects, Birmingham, AL (6 Jul 1947)

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Restricted checklist for unidentified flying objects, Incident #56, documenting a sighting by a military pilot/gunner.

**Witness:** Staff Sergeant Ira L. Livingston, S/Sgt with 250 hours as Pilot and Armorer Gunner, residing at 1354 Meadow Lane, Green Acres, Birmingham, Alabama.

**Sighting:** On 6 July 1947 at 2045 hours (8:45 PM), observer witnessed 7 to 10 objects near Birmingham, Alabama, at coordinates 33° 33'N 86° 52'W. The objects were at approximately 2000 feet above horizon at a 45° angle. Distance from observer was undetermined; time in sight not specified (N/S).

**Object Characteristics:** Round objects, 2 feet in diameter, traveling at 500 to 600 MPH in a southeast direction. The objects executed a vertical ascent and traveled in an arc formation. No sound was detected. Color, odor, apparent construction, and exhaust trails were not specified or not observed.

**Additional Details:** Weather conditions not specified. Effect on clouds not specified. One photograph was obtained. Manner of disappearance not specified. The document is marked RESTRICTED with incident tracking number 56.
events.report_summary_zh:

events.title: Capt. Jack Peck & Co-pilot Vince Daly: black saucer NW of Bethel, Alaska (4 Aug 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #58** – Unidentified Flying Object checklist report.

**Witnesses:** Capt. Jack Peck (pilot) and Co-pilot Vince Daly of Al Jones Flying Service observed the object during an evening flight northwest of Bethel, Alaska on 4 August 1947.

**Location & Coordinates:** The sighting occurred at 60° 57' N, 161° 48' W, northwest of Bethel, Alaska.

**Object Characteristics:** The object was described as black in color, saucer-shaped (like a C-54 from the rear view but without motors or flying wings). Size was reported as large or larger than a C-54 aircraft. The object maintained an altitude between 500 to 1,000 feet.

**Flight Characteristics:** Speed estimated at 520 MPH – approximately 3 times that of a C-54 aircraft. Direction of flight was northwest. The object was observed at a distance of 1200 feet from the aircraft and remained in sight for 4 minutes before flying rapidly out of sight.

**Weather & Conditions:** Brilliant evening sky conditions reported. No odor detected, no exhaust trails observed, and no effect on clouds noted.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Address of observer marked as N/S (not stated). Tactics, sound, apparent construction, and exhaust trails all marked N/S. Document marked as CONFIDENTIAL.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident #58** – 不明飞行物核查清单报告。

**Witnesses:** Al Jones飞行服务公司的Jack Peck机长(飞行员)和副驾驶Vince Daly于1947年8月4日傍晚在阿拉斯加州伯特利(Bethel, Alaska)西北方向飞行期间观察到该物体。

**Location & Coordinates:** 目击事件发生在阿拉斯加州伯特利西北方向,坐标为北纬60° 57',西经161° 48'。

**Object Characteristics:** 该物体被描述为黑色,碟形(从后视角看像C-54运输机,但没有发动机或飞翼)。据报告尺寸与C-54飞机一样大或更大。该物体保持在500至1,000英尺的高度。

**Flight Characteristics:** 速度估计为520英里/小时——约为C-54飞机速度的3倍。飞行方向为西北方向。该物体在距离飞机1200英尺处被观察到,持续可见4分钟后快速飞离视线。

**Weather & Conditions:** 报告称傍晚天空状况晴朗明亮。未探测到气味,未观察到尾迹,未注意到对云层的影响。

**Documentation:** 未获得草图或照片。观察者地址标注为N/S(未说明)。战术、声音、明显构造和尾迹均标注为N/S。文件标记为机密(CONFIDENTIAL)。

events.title: Albert Samme (12): bright reddish-yellow flying disc
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Albert Samme, a twelve-year-old boy who was alone when he observed the object.

**Sighting:** Albert saw an object flying at what appeared to be the height of a high-altitude plane, but noted it looked strange for an airplane because it was not carrying lights ("planes do have a light or two"). The object was described as being of a bright reddish-yellow color. The witness saw it only momentarily because of its tremendous speed, stating "I saw it only for a minute because it was traveling at a terrific speed."

**Mother's Assessment:** His mother, Mrs. Samme, is the Post Mistress of the town. After hearing her son's description, she felt that it answered the description of the "flying disc." She added that Albert didn't believe the object was a plane since "it wouldn't shoot down like that did" and "besides it was too 'lit up'."

**Cross-References:** The document references Legge account (Incident 60) and Evans' account (Incident 60a) for additional information.

**Document Classification:** This page is marked "RESTRICTED" at top and bottom, indicating it was part of classified U.S. government files on unidentified flying objects.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** Albert Samme，一名十二岁的男孩，在观察到该物体时独自一人。

**Sighting:** Albert看到一个物体在似乎是高空飞机的高度飞行，但他注意到它看起来不像普通飞机，因为它没有携带灯光（"飞机确实会有一两盏灯"）。该物体被描述为明亮的红黄色。目击者只是短暂地看到了它，因为它的速度极快，他说"我只看到了一分钟，因为它以极快的速度飞行。"

**Mother's Assessment:** 他的母亲Samme夫人是该镇的邮政局长。在听到儿子的描述后，她觉得这符合"飞碟"的描述。她补充说，Albert不相信这个物体是飞机，因为"它不会像那样俯冲下来"，而且"它太'亮'了"。

**Cross-References:** 该文件引用了Legge的报告（事件60）和Evans的报告（事件60a）以获取更多信息。

**Document Classification:** 本页在顶部和底部标有"RESTRICTED"（限制级），表明它是美国政府关于不明飞行物的机密档案的一部分。

events.title: Mr. and Mrs. Richard Anderson: approx. dozen white objects, Logan, UT (8 Sep 1947)

**Document Type:** RESTRICTED CHECK-LIST - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS, Incident # 61

**Witness:** Mr. and Mrs. Richard Anderson of Logan, Utah. Occupation: N/S (not specified).

**Sighting Details:** On 8 September 1947 at 2230 P.M. (10:30 PM), the witnesses observed approximately a dozen unidentified flying objects from Logan, Utah at coordinates 40° 45' N 111° 54' W. The objects remained in sight for one to two minutes.

**Object Characteristics:** The objects were described as about the size of pigeons, white and illuminated in color. They flew at an altitude of 2,000 to 3,000 feet at a speed described as "faster than birds" in a northward direction. Shape: N/S. Sound: N/S. Odor: N/S. Apparent construction: N/S. Exhaust trails: N/S.

**Behavior:** The objects employed specific tactics, circling the city in approximately one to two minutes while maintaining group formation. Distance from observers: N/S.

**Conditions:** Weather was cloudy. Effect on clouds: N/S. No sketches or photographs were obtained.

**Manner of Disappearance:** The objects flew away to the north.

**Additional Notes:** The document indicates remarks continue on another page (marked "over"). This is a standardized military checklist form used for documenting UFO incidents during the 1947 wave of sightings.

events.title: R. J. Madden et al: circular metallic object, 25 NE Helena, MT (29 Jul 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #63, a confidential UFO checklist documenting a sighting on 29 July 1947 at 12:05 P.M.

**Witness:** R. J. Madden et al, Division Plant Engineer for The Pacific Telephone & Telegraph Company, observed while traveling northwest from Canyon Ferry to York, approximately 25 miles northeast of Helena, Montana.

**Object:** Single circular object, 3 feet in diameter and 3-4 inches thick as seen from observers' viewpoint (apparently much larger given the distance). Color described as "like polished nickel" with apparent construction matching this metallic appearance. Shape: circular.

**Flight Characteristics:** Object observed at altitude of 3,000 feet, distance 2-3 miles from observers. Time in sight: 5+ seconds. Speed: tremendous. Direction: northeast. Tactics described as "hovering - rising and descending thru vertical distance of some 50-100 ft - then swooping to the NE at tremendous speed."

**Conditions:** Blue sky with scattered small clouds; bright sunshine causing disc to gleam and shimmer. No sound detected (N/S). No odor detected (N/S). No exhaust trails (N/S). No effect on clouds (N/S).

**Disappearance:** Object "melted into thin air" according to witnesses.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs obtained. Document marked CONFIDENTIAL, part of official USAF UFO investigation files.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #63号事件，一份机密UFO核查清单，记录了1947年7月29日下午12:05的目击事件。

**Witness:** R. J. Madden等人，太平洋电话电报公司(The Pacific Telephone & Telegraph Company)分部工厂工程师，在从Canyon Ferry向西北前往York的途中观察到，位置约在蒙大拿州海伦娜(Helena, Montana)东北25英里处。

**Object:** 单个圆形物体，从观察者视角看直径3英尺、厚3-4英寸(考虑到距离，实际尺寸显然要大得多)。颜色描述为"像抛光的镍"，外观结构与这种金属外观相符。形状:圆形。

**Flight Characteristics:** 物体在3,000英尺高度被观察到，距离观察者2-3英里。目击时长:5秒以上。速度:极快。方向:东北。战术动作描述为"悬停——在垂直距离约50-100英尺范围内上升和下降——然后以极快速度向东北方向俯冲"。

**Conditions:** 蓝天伴有零星小云;明亮的阳光使圆盘闪闪发光、闪烁不定。未探测到声音(N/S)。未探测到气味(N/S)。无尾迹(N/S)。对云层无影响(N/S)。

**Disappearance:** 根据目击者描述，物体"消融于空气中"。

**Documentation:** 未获得草图或照片。文件标注为机密(CONFIDENTIAL)，属于USAF UFO调查官方档案的一部分。

events.title: H.H. Hedstrom triangular formation sighting, Twin Falls, ID (19 Aug 1947)
