events.report_summary:
**Document:** RESTRICTED check-list for unidentified flying objects, Incident #64, documenting a sighting in Twin Falls, Idaho.

**Witness:** Mr. H. H. Hedstrom, his wife, and a neighbor. Hedstrom was identified as Detective Sergeant A. Frazier (or Frazier) of the Twin Falls Police Department and a member of the Twin Falls Police Dept. His occupation is listed as Executive Director of the Twin Falls Housing Authority. Observer address: 322 3rd Ave., North, Twin Falls, Idaho.

**Sighting:** Date and time: 19 August 1947 at 9:30 P.M. Location: Twin Falls, Idaho. Weather conditions noted as overcast sky at night.

**Objects:** Number of objects undetermined. Distance from observers could not be estimated. Time in sight was "few minutes at a time." Altitude could not be determined. Speed described as "terrific." Direction of flight was NE and came back toward the SW.

**Characteristics:** Tactics showed "observed triangular formation." No sound detected (N/S). Size could not be estimated. Color described as "seen only as a glow going thru the air similar to that of regular electric lights." Shape could not be estimated. No odor detected. Apparent construction not specified (N/S). No exhaust trails could be observed. Effect on clouds: N/S. No sketches or photographs were made. Manner of disappearance: N/S.

**Remarks:** Continued on additional page(s).
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 关于不明飞行物的限制级检查清单，事件#64，记录了在爱达荷州特温福尔斯(Twin Falls, Idaho)的一次目击事件。

**Witness:** H. H. Hedstrom先生、他的妻子以及一位邻居。Hedstrom被确认为特温福尔斯警察局的侦缉警长A. Frazier（或Frazier），特温福尔斯警察局成员。其职业列为特温福尔斯住房管理局执行主任。目击者地址：爱达荷州特温福尔斯北第三大道322号(322 3rd Ave., North, Twin Falls, Idaho)。

**Sighting:** 日期和时间：1947年8月19日晚上9:30。地点：爱达荷州特温福尔斯。天气状况记录为夜间多云天空。

**Objects:** 物体数量无法确定。与目击者的距离无法估计。可见时间为"每次几分钟"。高度无法确定。速度被描述为"极快"。飞行方向为东北方向，然后返回向西南方向。

**Characteristics:** 战术特征显示"观察到三角形编队"。未检测到声音(N/S)。尺寸无法估计。颜色被描述为"只能看到穿过空中的光芒，类似于普通电灯的光芒"。形状无法估计。未检测到气味。表观构造未说明(N/S)。无法观察到尾迹。对云层的影响：N/S。未制作草图或照片。消失方式：N/S。

**Remarks:** 在附加页面继续。

events.title: Lt Colonel Walker: orange glow flying north-south near Silver Springs, OH (10 Aug 47)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 66

**Witness:** Lt Colonel F. L. Walker Jr., GSC, Scientific Branch, Research Group, R&DD, WDGS. High-credibility military scientific observer.

**Date & Time:** 10 August 1947, 9 o'clock, well after dark.

**Location:** Near Silver Springs, Ohio.

**Sighting:** Observer witnessed one unidentified flying object for approximately 3-4 seconds. The object was described as low-flying, moving in a north to south direction with absolutely horizontal flight tactics. Distance from observer was not specified.

**Object Characteristics:** The object displayed a bright orange glow or flame appearance. Speed, size, shape, sound, odor, and apparent construction were all not specified (N/S). The object left long, straight, narrow white exhaust trails described as "similar to streak left by tracer bullet" which vanished very quickly.

**Disappearance:** The object simply vanished in mid-air.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Weather conditions were noted as N/S (well after dark). Effect on clouds was not specified. Additional remarks noted as continuing on subsequent page(s).

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED checklist for unidentified flying objects.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident #:** 66

**Witness:** F. L. Walker Jr. 中校，GSC，科学分部，研究组，R&DD，WDGS。高可信度军事科学观察员。

**Date & Time:** 1947年8月10日，9点钟，天黑很久之后。

**Location:** 俄亥俄州银泉市(Silver Springs, Ohio)附近。

**Sighting:** 观察员目击到一个不明飞行物体，持续时间约3-4秒。该物体被描述为低空飞行，以北向南方向移动，飞行姿态绝对水平。与观察员的距离未说明。

**Object Characteristics:** 该物体呈现明亮的橙色光芒或火焰外观。速度、大小、形状、声音、气味和明显结构均未说明(N/S)。该物体留下细长、笔直、狭窄的白色尾迹，被描述为"类似曳光弹留下的条纹"，消失得非常快。

**Disappearance:** 该物体在半空中直接消失。

**Documentation:** 未获得任何草图或照片。天气状况记录为N/S(天黑很久之后)。对云层的影响未说明。附加备注注明在后续页面继续。

**Document Classification:** 不明飞行物体限制级核查清单。

events.location: 5 miles southwest of Placerville, California (Cedar Ravine Road)
events.title: Mr. & Mrs. Roy A. Switzer: polished chromium object, Placerville, CA (14 Aug 47)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #67

**Date & Time:** 14 August 1947, 1600 hours

**Location:** Between 4 and 5 miles southwest from Placerville on Cedar Ravine Road, California. Coordinates: 38° 42' 45" N, Lat x 120° 47' 15" W. Long.

**Witness:** Mr. Roy A. Switzer and wife. Switzer is an Insurance Executive with the firm of McGuire & Wallis and is a graduate of the University of California. Address: Box 43, Auburn, Eldorado County, California.

**Object Characteristics:** The object appeared to be approximately 5 feet long by 12 to 14 inches in depth. Color was polished chromium. Shape seemed rectangular except for a short period when it appeared to have a slightly curved top surface. Seemed tilted in semi-circle, more rocket-shaped than disc-shaped. Apparent construction was metallic.

**Flight Details:** Altitude between 500 to 1,000 feet. Speed described as high rate of speed. Direction of flight was north to south. Tactics described as "in a very shallow dive." Number of objects: 1. Distance from observer: estimated about 750 feet. Time in sight: short period.

**Exhaust & Smoke:** A white smoke trail was first observed, later the object was enveloped in puff of dark gray smoke.

**Disappearance:** Object disappeared in puff of dark gray smoke.

**Other Details:** Sound: N/S. Effect on clouds: N/S. Weather conditions: fair with sunshine. Sketches or photographs: None.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #67

**Date & Time:** 1947年8月14日，1600时

**Location:** 加利福尼亚州普莱瑟维尔(Placerville)西南方向4至5英里处的雪松峡谷路(Cedar Ravine Road)。坐标：北纬38° 42' 45"，西经120° 47' 15"。

**Witness:** Roy A. Switzer先生及其妻子。Switzer先生是McGuire & Wallis公司的保险业务主管，加利福尼亚大学毕业生。地址：加利福尼亚州埃尔多拉多县奥本市43号信箱。

**Object Characteristics:** 该物体外观长度约5英尺，厚度约12至14英寸。颜色为抛光铬色。形状似乎呈矩形，但在短暂时间内顶部表面似乎略微弯曲。呈半圆形倾斜状，更像火箭形而非圆盘形。外观构造为金属材质。

**Flight Details:** 高度在500至1,000英尺之间。速度描述为高速。飞行方向为由北向南。飞行动态描述为"非常浅的俯冲"。物体数量：1个。距离观察者：估计约750英尺。可见时间：短暂时段。

**Exhaust & Smoke:** 最初观察到白色烟雾轨迹，随后该物体被一团深灰色烟雾包裹。

**Disappearance:** 物体消失于一团深灰色烟雾中。

**Other Details:** 声音：无记录。对云层的影响：无记录。天气状况：晴朗有阳光。草图或照片：无。

**Document Classification:** 限制级

events.title: Fred M. Johnson: 5-6 round objects over Cascade Mts., OR (24 Jun 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #68

**Witness:** Fred M. Johnson, prospector, staying at Globe Hotel, 106 N.W. 1st Ave, Portland, Oregon.

**Sighting:** On the afternoon of 24 June 1947, Johnson observed 5 or 6 unidentified flying objects from the Cascade Mountains near Portland, Oregon. The objects were overhead at approximately 1,000 feet altitude (6,000 feet above sea level) and remained in sight for 45-60 seconds.

**Object Characteristics:** The objects were round with tails, approximately 30 feet in diameter. They flew in a banking maneuver toward the SE direction. No sound was detected. Speed was not specified (marked N/S). Color and other visual details were not recorded.

**Weather & Other Details:** Weather conditions were clear. No odor was detected, and apparent construction, exhaust trails, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance were all marked N/S (not specified). No sketches or photographs were taken.

**Document Type:** This is a standardized USAF/military checklist form for unidentified flying object reports, marked CONFIDENTIAL. The incident occurred on the same date as the famous Kenneth Arnold sighting, also near the Cascade Mountains in the Pacific Northwest.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #68

**Witness:** 弗雷德·M·约翰逊(Fred M. Johnson),勘探者,住在俄勒冈州波特兰市西北第一大道106号环球酒店(Globe Hotel, 106 N.W. 1st Ave, Portland, Oregon)。

**Sighting:** 1947年6月24日下午,约翰逊在俄勒冈州波特兰附近的喀斯喀特山脉(Cascade Mountains)观察到5或6个不明飞行物体。这些物体在头顶上方约1,000英尺高度(海拔6,000英尺)处飞行,在视野中停留了45-60秒。

**Object Characteristics:** 这些物体呈圆形带尾部,直径约30英尺。它们以倾斜机动方式向东南方向飞行。未探测到声音。速度未标明(标记为N/S)。颜色和其他视觉细节未记录。

**Weather & Other Details:** 天气状况晴朗。未探测到气味,明显的构造、尾迹、对云层的影响以及消失方式均标记为N/S(未标明)。未绘制草图或拍摄照片。

**Document Type:** 这是一份标准化的USAF/军方不明飞行物报告核查表格式文件,标记为机密(CONFIDENTIAL)。该事件发生日期与著名的肯尼斯·阿诺德(Kenneth Arnold)目击事件相同,地点也都在太平洋西北地区的喀斯喀特山脉附近。

events.title: Eleanor Haddle: large white object flying south, Philadelphia, PA (6 Aug 47)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #69 - UFO Sighting Report**

**Date and Time:** August 6, 1947, between 2230-2245 hours (10:30-10:45 PM)

**Witness:** Eleanor Haddle, employed by Geo A. Greenwald Mfg. Co., residing at 2114 Hobart St., Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Observation made from observer's home.

**Object Characteristics:** Large, white object observed at an unspecified distance and altitude. Speed described as "very fast" traveling in a southward direction with apparently straight flight pattern. A thin streak of grayish smoke served as exhaust trails. After passage, a slight buzzing sound was detected.

**Details:** Single object sighting. Shape, odor, apparent construction, weather conditions, and effect on clouds all marked "N/S" (not stated/not specified). Size noted as "large" and color as "white." No sketches or photographs were obtained. Manner of disappearance not specified.

**Document Classification:** This checklist for unidentified flying objects is marked "RESTRICTED" and represents a standardized reporting format used during the early wave of UFO sightings in 1947. The document indicates additional remarks existed (marked "over") but are not visible on this page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**事件 #69 - UFO目击报告**

**日期和时间：** 1947年8月6日，2230-2245时之间（晚上10:30-10:45）

**目击者：** Eleanor Haddle，就职于Geo A. Greenwald制造公司，居住在宾夕法尼亚州费城(Philadelphia, Pennsylvania)霍巴特街(Hobart St.)2114号。观察地点为目击者家中。

**物体特征：** 在未明确说明的距离和高度观察到大型白色物体。速度被描述为"非常快"，向南方向行进，飞行模式明显呈直线。有细长的灰色烟雾作为尾迹排出。通过后，探测到轻微的嗡嗡声。

**详细信息：** 单一物体目击。形状、气味、明显构造、天气条件以及对云层的影响均标注为"N/S"（未说明/未明确）。尺寸标注为"大型"，颜色为"白色"。未获得草图或照片。消失方式未明确说明。

**文件密级：** 这份不明飞行物核查清单标记为"限制级"(RESTRICTED)，代表了1947年早期UFO目击浪潮期间使用的标准化报告格式。文件显示存在额外备注（标记为"翻页"），但在本页中不可见。

events.title: John Snyder: high-speed object over Philadelphia, PA (6 Aug 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 70

**Witness:** John Snyder, insurance agent and former B-24 pilot, residing at 1440 Vankir St., Philadelphia, Pa. The observation was made from this same address.

**Date & Time:** 6 August 1947, around 2245 hours (10:45 PM)

**Sighting:** The witness observed a single unidentified flying object traveling at high speed. The object flew from northeast to southwest at an estimated altitude between 1,000-3,000 feet. Speed was estimated between 400-500 MPH.

**Object Characteristics:** The object emitted a hissing sound and produced exhaust trails described as "smoke or condensation" that also emitted a "bluish white flame." Distance from observer, time in sight, size, color, shape, odor, tactics, apparent construction, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance were all marked "N/S" (not stated/specified).

**Weather Conditions:** Clear

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Additional remarks were noted as "(over)" suggesting continuation on a subsequent page not shown here.

**Document Classification:** This checklist is marked "RESTRICTED" and appears to be part of a systematic Air Force collection of unidentified flying object reports from the immediate post-Kenneth Arnold era of 1947.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident #:** 70

**Witness:** 约翰·斯奈德(John Snyder),保险代理人,前B-24飞行员,居住在宾夕法尼亚州费城(Philadelphia, Pa.)万基尔街(Vankir St.)1440号。观测地点与居住地址相同。

**Date & Time:** 1947年8月6日,约2245小时(晚上10:45)

**Sighting:** 目击者观察到一个单独的不明飞行物体高速飞行。该物体从东北向西南方向飞行,估计高度在1,000-3,000英尺之间。速度估计在400-500英里/小时之间。

**Object Characteristics:** 该物体发出嘶嘶声,并产生被描述为"烟雾或凝结物"的尾迹,同时发出"蓝白色火焰"。与观测者的距离、可见时间、大小、颜色、形状、气味、飞行方式、明显构造、对云层的影响以及消失方式均标注为"N/S"(未说明/未具体说明)。

**Weather Conditions:** 晴朗

**Documentation:** 未获得草图或照片。附加备注标注为"(over)",表明在此处未显示的后续页面上有延续内容。

**Document Classification:** 该核查清单标记为"RESTRICTED"(限制级),似乎是空军系统性收集1947年肯尼斯·阿诺德(Kenneth Arnold)事件后不明飞行物体报告的一部分。

events.title: County Commissioner Hawkins & J.R. Brown: 2 objects at Salmon Dam (13 Aug 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 76

**Witnesses:** County Commissioner Hawkins and J.R. Brown, both County Commissioners.

**Sighting:** On 13 August 1947 at Salmon Dam, Idaho, two county commissioners observed 2 unidentified flying objects. The objects were located several miles away from the observers at an estimated altitude of 4,000 to 6,000 feet. Time in sight was not specified.

**Object Characteristics:** The objects were circular in shape and traveled at great speed. Direction of flight was not specified. The objects reflected light. Witnesses reported hearing the echo of a motor sound. Size, color details, tactics, and construction were not specified or recorded as N/S (not specified).

**Conditions & Evidence:** Weather conditions were not specified. Effect on clouds was not specified. No sketches or photographs were obtained (marked "None"). Distance from observers was described as "several miles away."

**Document Details:** This is a RESTRICTED classification checklist for unidentified flying objects, part of the official Air Force UFO investigation records. The form is standardized with numbered fields for systematic data collection. Additional remarks are noted as being on a subsequent page (marked "over").
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident #:** 76

**Witnesses:** 县专员霍金斯(Hawkins)和J.R.布朗(J.R. Brown),两人均为县专员。

**Sighting:** 1947年8月13日,在爱达荷州萨蒙大坝(Salmon Dam, Idaho),两名县专员观察到2个不明飞行物体。这些物体距离观察者数英里远,估计高度为4,000至6,000英尺。目击持续时间未说明。

**Object Characteristics:** 物体呈圆形,以极快速度飞行。飞行方向未说明。物体会反射光线。目击者报告听到马达声的回音。尺寸、颜色细节、飞行方式和构造均未说明或记录为N/S(未说明)。

**Conditions & Evidence:** 天气状况未说明。对云层的影响未说明。未获得草图或照片(标注为"无")。与观察者的距离描述为"数英里远"。

**Document Details:** 这是一份关于不明飞行物体的限制级(RESTRICTED)分类核查表,属于空军UFO调查官方档案的一部分。该表格采用标准化格式,带有编号字段以进行系统化数据收集。附加说明标注在后续页面(标注为"翻页")。

events.title: Commissioner L. W. Hawkins: roar & circular objects, Twin Falls ID (Aug 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED memo regarding sighting by County Commissioner L. W. Hawkins and witness J. H. Brown near Twin Falls, Idaho.

**Witness:** County Commissioner L. W. Hawkins, accompanied by J. H. Brown. Agent could not initially locate Commissioner Hawkins but Brown provided details of their joint sighting.

**Sighting:** Hawkins and Brown reported hearing a roar and looking up to observe 2 objects at great height, possibly between 4,000 and 6,000 feet altitude. The objects were traveling at great speed and at higher altitude than most planes. Witnesses stated they had seen something and were very doubtful if the objects were planes. The objects could have been several miles away, and no estimate of size was provided.

**Newspaper Account:** From the Times News, Twin Falls, Idaho (Friday Aug 15, 1947): Commissioner Hawkins stated he had seen an unusual object in the air the same day as Drue's experience (Incident 75). The sighting involved a sound resembling the roar of a motor engine caused him to look upward, and he saw two circular objects which reflected light. They were traveling at a great speed and at higher altitude than most planes.

**Document Date:** Reference to incident contemporaneous with Incident 75, dated August 15, 1947.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED备忘录，关于县专员L. W. Hawkins和证人J. H. Brown在爱达荷州双瀑城(Twin Falls, Idaho)附近的目击事件。

**Witness:** 县专员L. W. Hawkins，由J. H. Brown陪同。特工最初无法找到Hawkins专员，但Brown提供了他们共同目击的详细信息。

**Sighting:** Hawkins和Brown报告称听到轰鸣声，抬头观察到2个物体在极高的高度，可能在4,000至6,000英尺高度之间。这些物体以极快的速度飞行，飞行高度比大多数飞机更高。目击者表示他们看到了某种东西，但非常怀疑这些物体是否为飞机。这些物体可能在数英里之外，未提供尺寸估计。

**Newspaper Account:** 摘自爱达荷州双瀑城《时代新闻报》(Times News, Twin Falls, Idaho)（1947年8月15日星期五）：Hawkins专员称，他在与Drue经历（事件75号）同一天在空中看到了一个不寻常的物体。目击涉及一种类似发动机轰鸣的声音促使他抬头观看，他看到两个反射光线的圆形物体。它们以极快的速度飞行，飞行高度比大多数飞机更高。

**Document Date:** 参考与事件75号同时发生的事件，日期为1947年8月15日。

events.location: Near Williams Field over Grand Canyon, Arizona
events.title: Lt William G. McGinty: 2 light gray circular objects, Grand Canyon, AZ (30 Jun 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 78

**Date & Time:** 30 June 1947 at 0910 MST

**Location:** Near Williams Field over Grand Canyon, Arizona

**Witness:** Lt William G. McGinty, USN. Observer was a P-80 student at Williams Field, Chandler, Arizona. Address: Williams Field, Chandler, Arizona.

**Place of Observation:** From plane

**Sighting Details:** Observer witnessed 2 unidentified flying objects while descending from 25,000 ft altitude. The objects' direction of flight was described as "straight down." The speed was characterized as "inconceivable." Time in sight and distance from observer were not specified (N/S).

**Object Characteristics:** Size: 5 ft in diameter. Color: Light gray (with something struck through, possibly indicating uncertainty). Shape: Circular. No odor detected (N/S). Apparent construction, exhaust trails, weather conditions, and effect on clouds all marked N/S (not specified). No sketches or photographs were available.

**Tactics:** Not specified (N/S)

**Sound:** Not specified (N/S)

**Manner of Disappearance:** Seemed to have hit ground some 25 miles South of the South Rim of Grand Canyon, Arizona.

**Remarks:** Document indicates "(over)" suggesting additional information on reverse page. This is a confidential U.S. military checklist for unidentified flying objects.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident #:** 78

**Date & Time:** 1947年6月30日 0910 MST(山地标准时间)

**Location:** 亚利桑那州大峡谷上空威廉姆斯机场附近

**Witness:** 美国海军中尉威廉·G·麦金蒂(Lt William G. McGinty, USN)。观察者是亚利桑那州钱德勒威廉姆斯机场的P-80飞行学员。地址:亚利桑那州钱德勒威廉姆斯机场。

**Place of Observation:** 从飞机上

**Sighting Details:** 观察者在从25,000英尺高度下降时目击到2个不明飞行物体。物体的飞行方向被描述为"垂直向下"。速度被描述为"难以想象"。目击时间长度和与观察者的距离未注明(N/S)。

**Object Characteristics:** 尺寸:直径5英尺。颜色:浅灰色(有内容被划掉,可能表示不确定)。形状:圆形。未检测到气味(N/S)。明显的构造、尾迹、天气状况以及对云层的影响均标注为N/S(未注明)。无素描或照片。

**Tactics:** 未注明(N/S)

**Sound:** 未注明(N/S)

**Manner of Disappearance:** 似乎撞击到亚利桑那州大峡谷南缘以南约25英里处的地面。

**Remarks:** 文件标注"(over)",表明背面有额外信息。这是一份美国军方关于不明飞行物体的机密核查清单。

events.title: Weather reporter Mr. Minozewski: 3-4 metallic objects, Richmond, VA (Apr 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #79

**Date & Time:** April 1947, 1100 hours Eastern time, during pibal (pilot balloon) observation

**Location:** W/S - presumably Richmond, Virginia (place of observation confirmed as Richmond, Va.)

**Witness:** Mr. Minozewski, occupation: Weather reporters. Address classified as W/S.

**Sighting:** Observer reported 3-4 separate sightings of unidentified flying objects at high altitude. Total time in sight: 15 seconds. Distance from observer: high altitude. Objects traveled east to west at rapid speed.

**Object Characteristics:** Color described as metallic grey or silver. Size: larger than pibal balloon when observed through a theodolite. Shape, tactics, sound, odor, apparent construction, and exhaust trails all marked W/S (not specified/withheld/unknown).

**Weather Conditions:** Clear skies. Effect on clouds marked W/S.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs available (marked "None"). Manner of disappearance marked W/S.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED checklist for unidentified flying objects. Additional remarks noted as "(over)" but continuation page not shown in this image.

events.title: Maj. Archie B. Browning: silvery disc 100 mi W of Kansas City (6 Jul 1947)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 89

**Witness:** Maj. Archie B. Browning, U.S. Air Corps, pilot of B-25 aircraft. Military observer with professional aviation credentials.

**Sighting:** On 6 July 1947 at 1:45 P.M., approximately 100 miles west of Kansas City, Missouri, Major Browning observed an unidentified flying object while airborne. The observation was made from the air at an altitude of 11,000 feet.

**Object Characteristics:** Single object, round/disc-shaped, 30-50 feet in diameter. Described as very bright and silvery colored. Speed estimated at 210 MPH traveling eastward. Observer noted horizontal flight tactics at a distance of approximately 10 miles from his aircraft.

**Manner of Disappearance:** Object disappeared when the pilot started to turn his aircraft toward it, suggesting possible evasive action or loss of visual contact during maneuver.

**Additional Details:** Weather conditions reported as CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited). No sound detected, no odor noted. Time in sight and other technical parameters marked N/S (not specified). No sketches or photographs obtained.

**Document Status:** Restricted classification checklist for unidentified flying objects, standard military reporting format from early UFO investigation period.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident #:** 89

**Witness:** 美国陆军航空兵少校阿奇·B·布朗宁(Maj. Archie B. Browning)，B-25飞机飞行员。具有专业航空资质的军事观察员。

**Sighting:** 1947年7月6日下午1:45，在密苏里州堪萨斯城(Kansas City, Missouri)以西约100英里处，布朗宁少校在空中观察到一个不明飞行物体。观察是在11,000英尺高度的空中进行的。

**Object Characteristics:** 单个物体，圆形/碟形，直径30-50英尺。描述为非常明亮的银色。速度估计为210英里/小时，向东飞行。观察员注意到该物体在距离其飞机约10英里处进行水平飞行。

**Manner of Disappearance:** 当飞行员开始转向该物体时，物体消失了，表明可能采取了规避动作或在机动过程中失去了视觉接触。

**Additional Details:** 天气状况报告为CAVU(无云能见度无限)。未探测到声音，未注意到气味。视野停留时间和其他技术参数标记为N/S(未说明)。未获得草图或照片。

**Document Status:** 不明飞行物体限制级分类核查清单，早期UFO调查期间的标准军事报告格式。

events.title: Two USAF Captains observe disc-shaped UFO, Hartford, CT (11 Jan 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 93

**Date & Time:** 11 January 1948 at 1630 hours

**Location:** Hartford, Connecticut

**Witnesses:** Kenneth M. Belton and James J. Fargoe, both Captains in the USAF (ATC). Address: Atlantic Division, ATC (Sq. "D" Air Evac.)

**Object Description:** The object appeared as a disc, resembling a shooting star though observers were not certain. It had a bluish center with red edges. The shape was described as disc-like. No sound was detected, and no odor was reported.

**Flight Characteristics:** The object was moving at unknown but very high velocity, shooting toward earth at a 45-degree angle. Direction of flight was observed shooting toward earth at 45°. No exhaust trails or tail were visible.

**Size & Distance:** Size resembled a shooting star, though observers expressed uncertainty. Distance from observer and altitude were not stated (N/S). Time in sight was not stated.

**Manner of Disappearance:** The object dropped out of sight on the north side of Mt. Tom, which is near Holyoke, Massachusetts.

**Additional Details:** Number of objects: 1. Tactics: N/S. Weather conditions: N/S. Effect on clouds: N/S. No sketches or photographs were obtained. Apparent construction: N/S.

**Document Status:** Marked CONFIDENTIAL, this is a standardized UFO check-list form used for systematic reporting of unidentified flying objects.

**Location:** 康涅狄格州哈特福德(Hartford, Connecticut)

**Object Description:** 该物体呈圆盘状，类似流星，但观察者不能确定。它有一个蓝色的中心和红色的边缘。形状被描述为碟状。未探测到声音，也未报告有气味。

**Flight Characteristics:** 该物体以未知但极高的速度移动，以45度角向地球俯冲。观察到的飞行方向是以45°角向地球俯冲。未见尾气或尾迹。

**Size & Distance:** 大小类似流星，但观察者表示不确定。与观察者的距离和高度未说明(N/S)。视野内时间未说明。

**Manner of Disappearance:** 该物体在汤姆山(Mt. Tom)北侧消失，该山位于马萨诸塞州霍利奥克(Holyoke, Massachusetts)附近。

**Additional Details:** 物体数量：1个。战术动作：N/S。天气条件：N/S。对云层的影响：N/S。未获得草图或照片。明显构造：N/S。

**Document Status:** 标记为机密(CONFIDENTIAL)，这是一份用于系统化报告不明飞行物的标准化UFO核查表格式。

events.title: Shining object with long tail observed near Vaasa, Finland (3 Jan 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #99

**Date and Location:** 3 January 1948, observed near Vaasa, Finland. Official source of information was a military attaché in Helsinki, Finland.

**Observer:** The Helsinki Press reported the observation on 10 January 1948. The document references Finland and the USMILATTACHE AMLEGATION Helsinki Finland and Burrill. Observer's occupation and address listed as Helsinki, Finland; observation location was Vaasa, Finland.

**Object Description:** One (1) object described as a brightly shining object with a long tail. The color was noted as "Shining" and it had exhaust trails characterized as a "Long tail." Size, shape, apparent construction, sound, and odor were not specified (N/S).

**Flight Characteristics:** The object moved west to east and was visible for 30 seconds. Distance from observer, altitude, speed, and tactics were not specified (N/S).

**Additional Details:** Weather conditions, effect on clouds, sketches/photographs, and manner of disappearance were not specified or reported. No odor was detected.

**Remarks:** The Helsinki press on 10 January reported observation of light phenomena in the vicinity of Vaasa on 3rd January—a brightly shining object with long tail moved west to east, visible for 30 seconds.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED, part of CHECK-LIST for UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #99

**Date and Location:** 1948年1月3日，在芬兰瓦萨(Vaasa)附近观测到。官方信息来源是芬兰赫尔辛基的一名武官。

**Observer:** 赫尔辛基(Helsinki)新闻界于1948年1月10日报道了这次观测。该文件提及芬兰以及美国驻赫尔辛基公使馆武官处(USMILATTACHE AMLEGATION Helsinki Finland)和Burrill。观测者职业和地址列为芬兰赫尔辛基；观测地点为芬兰瓦萨。

**Object Description:** 一(1)个物体，被描述为带有长尾的明亮发光物体。颜色记录为"发光"，并具有被描述为"长尾"的排气尾迹。大小、形状、明显结构、声音和气味均未说明(N/S)。

**Flight Characteristics:** 该物体从西向东移动，可见时间为30秒。与观测者的距离、高度、速度和战术机动均未说明(N/S)。

**Additional Details:** 天气状况、对云层的影响、草图/照片以及消失方式均未说明或报告。未检测到气味。

**Remarks:** 赫尔辛基新闻界于1月10日报道了1月3日在瓦萨附近观测到光现象——一个带长尾的明亮发光物体从西向东移动，可见时间为30秒。

**Document Classification:** 限制级(RESTRICTED),属于不明飞行物体核查清单(CHECK-LIST for UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS)的一部分。

events.title: Multi-colored fireball southeast of Limon, Colorado (18 Feb 1945)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Sighting:** A huge multi-colored ball of fire trailing a dense cloud of smoke was sighted at approximately 1500 hours MST on 18 February 1945, at coordinates 39° N-100° W, approximately 20,000 feet altitude. The object was observed by B-29 aircraft of the 28th Bombardment Group (VH) operating some 100 miles southeast of Limon, Colorado.

**Object characteristics:** The fireball was traveling at very high speed and heading southeast. Size was estimated as large, though accurate determination was deemed impossible due to the distance from the observers.

**Witnesses:** Four crew members from two B-29 bombers provided testimony:
- Capt Howard H. Berodt, AO-405504, 718th Bomb Sq, 28th Bomb Gp (VH), Pilot of 1st B-29
- Capt Maurice T. Ritenour, AO-450143, 718th Bomb Sq, 28 Bomb Gp (VH), Co-Pilot of 1st B-29
- 1st Lt Leonard P. Marchese, AO-748714, 77th Bomb Sq., 28th Bomb Gp (VH), Pilot of 2nd B-29
- 1st Lt. Carl W. Stucki, AO-785916, 77th Bomb Sq, 28th Bomb Gp (VH), Co-Pilot of 2nd B-29

**Cross-reference:** The document notes: "See Incident 101 - Worcatur Kansas" suggesting a possible related sighting or investigation.

**Document provenance:** This appears to be a military intelligence report documenting the sighting by experienced bomber crews during wartime operations.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Sighting:** 1945年2月18日山地标准时间约1500时,在坐标39° N-100° W、约20,000英尺高度处,目击到一个巨大的多色火球,拖曳着一团浓密的烟云。该物体由第28轰炸大队(VH)的B-29飞机观测到,当时飞机在科罗拉多州利蒙(Limon, Colorado)东南约100英里处执行任务。

**Object characteristics:** 该火球以极高速度向东南方向飞行。尺寸估计很大,但由于与观测者距离较远,无法进行准确测定。

**Witnesses:** 来自两架B-29轰炸机的四名机组人员提供了证词:
- Capt Howard H. Berodt, AO-405504, 第718轰炸中队,第28轰炸大队(VH),第1架B-29飞行员
- Capt Maurice T. Ritenour, AO-450143, 第718轰炸中队,第28轰炸大队(VH),第1架B-29副驾驶
- 1st Lt Leonard P. Marchese, AO-748714, 第77轰炸中队,第28轰炸大队(VH),第2架B-29飞行员
- 1st Lt. Carl W. Stucki, AO-785916, 第77轰炸中队,第28轰炸大队(VH),第2架B-29副驾驶

**Cross-reference:** 该文件注明:"参见事件101 - 堪萨斯州沃卡图尔(Worcatur Kansas)",表明可能存在相关目击事件或调查。

**Document provenance:** 这似乎是一份军事情报报告,记录了经验丰富的轰炸机机组人员在战时行动期间的目击事件。

events.title: B-29 Pilots sight huge multi-colored fireball near Green River, UT (18 Feb 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #102

**Date & Time:** 18 February 1948 at 1500 MST

**Witnesses:** Lenord F. Marchese, B-29 Pilot, Lt., 28 Bomber Group; Carl W. Stuckl, Lt., Co-Pilot; and other witnesses listed on reverse side. Both officers stationed at 77th Bomb Sq, 28th Bomb Gp (VH), Weaver AFB, South Dakota.

**Location:** Air near Green River, Utah (39° N - 100° W), approximately 100 miles from observers' aircraft.

**Flight Conditions:** Aircraft altitude 20,000 feet, clear weather conditions.

**Object Description:** Huge, multi-colored ball of fire described as having explosion rate tactics. The object was traveling at very high speed in a southeast direction from Limon, Colorado. Sound could not be determined due to B-29 engine noise. Size characterized as "Huge."

**Appearance:** Multi-colored ball of fire with a dense cloud of smoke. Exhaust trails described as vapor trail with ball of fire at head of trail.

**Duration:** Time in sight not specified (N/S).

**Additional Details:** No odor detected, apparent construction not specified, no effect on clouds noted, no sketches or photographs taken, manner of disappearance not specified. No remarks section marked "XXXXX Over" suggesting continuation on reverse page.

**Document Type:** CHECK-LIST - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS, standardized military reporting form.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #102

**Date & Time:** 1948年2月18日 1500 MST（山地标准时间）

**Witnesses:** Lenord F. Marchese，B-29飞行员，中尉，第28轰炸机大队；Carl W. Stuckl，中尉，副驾驶；以及背面列出的其他目击者。两名军官均驻扎于南达科他州韦弗AFB（空军基地）第28轰炸机大队（VH）第77轰炸机中队。

**Location:** 犹他州格林里弗（Green River, Utah）附近空域（北纬39° - 西经100°），距离观察者飞机约100英里。

**Flight Conditions:** 飞机高度20,000英尺，天气状况晴朗。

**Object Description:** 巨大的多色火球，被描述为具有爆炸速度战术特征。该物体以极高速度从科罗拉多州利蒙（Limon, Colorado）向东南方向移动。由于B-29发动机噪音无法确定声音。尺寸特征为"巨大"。

**Appearance:** 多色火球，伴有浓密烟云。尾迹被描述为蒸汽轨迹，火球位于轨迹前端。

**Duration:** 目击持续时间未说明（N/S）。

**Additional Details:** 未检测到气味，未说明明显的构造，未注意到对云层的影响，未拍摄草图或照片，消失方式未说明。备注部分标有"XXXXX Over"，表明在背面有续页。

**Document Type:** 检查清单 - 不明飞行物体，标准化军事报告表格。

events.title: Capt. Bergdt & Lt. Ritenour: huge multi-colored fireball, Green River UT (18 Feb 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #103

**Date & Time:** 18 February 1948, 1500 MST

**Witnesses:** Capt. Howard H. Bergdt and Capt. Maurice T. Ritenour (see Inc 102 for corroboration), both pilots assigned to 718th Bomb Squadron, 28th Bomb Group (VH), Weaver AFB, South Dakota.

**Location:** 39° N - 100° W, near Green River, Utah (approximately 100 miles from observer position).

**Object Description:** Huge multi-colored ball of fire followed by a dense cloud of smoke. Object appeared at 20,000 feet altitude and was described as having a vapor trail with a ball of fire at the head of the trail. Size was characterized as "Huge" when seen 100 miles west of the observers' B-29 aircraft.

**Flight Characteristics:** Speed was "Very high." Direction of flight was Southeast (of Limon, Colorado). Tactics described as "Explosion rate." Sound could not be determined due to B-29 engine noise. Time in sight not specified (N/S).

**Observation Details:** Object observed from aircraft at 20,000 feet altitude. Distance from observer was approximately 100 miles. Number of objects: one. Weather conditions were clear. No effect on clouds noted. No sketches or photographs were obtained.

**Remarks:** Document notes "Same as incident 102 which see," indicating corroboration with another sighting report.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #103

**Date & Time:** 1948年2月18日，山地标准时间1500时

**Witnesses:** Howard H. Bergdt上尉和Maurice T. Ritenour上尉（见事件102号以获取佐证），两人均为飞行员，隶属于南达科他州Weaver AFB第28轰炸大队(VH)第718轰炸中队。

**Location:** 北纬39° - 西经100°，犹他州格林河(Green River, Utah)附近（距观察者位置约100英里）。

**Object Description:** 巨大的多色火球，其后跟随着浓密的烟云。物体出现在20,000英尺高度，被描述为带有蒸汽尾迹，尾迹前端有一个火球。当在观察者B-29飞机以西100英里处观察时，其尺寸被描述为"巨大"。

**Flight Characteristics:** 速度"非常快"。飞行方向为东南方向（相对于科罗拉多州莱蒙(Limon, Colorado)）。战术特征被描述为"爆炸速度"。由于B-29发动机噪音无法确定声音。目击持续时间未说明(N/S)。

**Observation Details:** 从20,000英尺高度的飞机上观察到该物体。距观察者约100英里。物体数量：一个。天气状况晴朗。未发现对云层的影响。未获得草图或照片。

**Remarks:** 文件注明"与事件102号相同，参见该事件"，表明与另一份目击报告相互印证。

**Document Classification:** 限阅级

events.title: Smyrna AAF personnel observe yellow-orange oval UFO (7 Mar 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #104

**Date & Time:** 7 March 1948 at 2055 hours (Central time)

**Location:** Smyrna Army Air Force Base, Smyrna, Tennessee; observation made from ground approximately 6 miles from the base

**Witnesses:** Major Frank L. Tenn (USAF, CO Smyrna AF Base), Colonel Richard C. Pettingill, and Private Frank C. Johnson. All three were radio and tower operators at AACS Station, Smyrna AAF.

**Object Characteristics:** Single object described as oval-shaped, yellow-orange in color. Size unknown. The object appeared about 5° above the horizon at a distance of 6 miles from observers. Speed was described as "very slow." The apparent construction "seemed to be flare" (N/S noted). No exhaust trails were detected, no sound was heard, and no odor was detected (N/S).

**Flight Behavior:** Object moved in a WNW direction away from Smyrna. Tactics described as "N/S Faded away." The object was in sight for 45 minutes before it faded into the horizon.

**Weather & Conditions:** CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited) with 10 miles visibility. Effect on clouds noted as N/S.

**Documentation:** Two photographs or sketches (Figs 2) reportedly show a "yellow orange flame-like oval."

**Classification:** Document marked RESTRICTED at both top and bottom.
events.report_summary_zh:

events.title: J.E. Johnson & Callie Mason: orange-red flame, Bakersfield, CA (9 Mar 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #109, a restricted UFO checklist report dated 9 March 1948 at 0830 hours.

**Witnesses:** J.E. Johnson (Dentist) and Mrs. Callie R. Mason (Secretary) observed the object from the 5th floor of a business building in Bakersfield, California. Address is marked N/S (not specified).

**Object Description:** The object had the appearance of a very small airplane with an orange-red flame color. Its size and shape both suggested a very small aircraft. Only one object was observed.

**Flight Characteristics:** The object was located 7-10 miles from the observers at an altitude of approximately 1000 feet, flying due north of Bakersfield. It exhibited zig-zagging tactics. Speed is not specified. Time in sight is not recorded.

**Exhaust Trail:** Considerable black smoke trailing for 4000 to 5000 feet was observed behind the object.

**Additional Details:** No sound was detected. Weather conditions, effect on clouds, apparent construction, odor, and manner of disappearance are all marked N/S (not specified). No sketches or photographs were obtained.

**Document Note:** The remarks section references "See supplement to incident #106," suggesting this sighting may be related to or a continuation of a previous incident report.

**Object Description:** 该物体外观像一架非常小的飞机，呈橙红色火焰颜色。其尺寸和形状都表明是一架非常小的飞行器。仅观察到一个物体。

**Flight Characteristics:** 该物体距离观察者7-10英里，高度约1000英尺，位于贝克斯菲尔德(Bakersfield)正北方向飞行。它表现出Z字形飞行策略。速度未说明。视线内时间未记录。

**Document Note:** 备注部分提及"参见事件#106号补充材料"，表明此次目击可能与之前的事件报告相关或为其延续。

events.title: Wife of ex-serviceman reports foreign-sounding aircraft noises, Hamilton, Baltimore (Mar 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Document:** Restricted memorandum from HQ Strategic Air Command, Andrews Field, Washington D.C., dated 29 March 1948, forwarding a report to the Chief of Staff, United States Air Force, Director of Intelligence. Document marked as Incident #110.

**Source:** Letter from Baltimore Office, FBI, to the Director of Intelligence, Second Army, regarding an individual reporting unidentified aerial sounds.

**Witness:** An unidentified woman who contacted the FBI on March 23, 1948. She is the wife of a former member of the United States military forces and is presently active in American Legion activities. She emphasized she was "in no way hysterical or unduly apprehensive regarding present world conditions."

**Sighting:** On multiple occasions during the past six to eight weeks, between the hours of 3:00 and 5:00 A.M., the witness heard peculiar sounding noises in the sky. The sounds appeared to come from airplanes in the distance, but were not the type of airplane motor drones normally heard from American planes. The witness discussed the matter with her husband, who believed the sound was more like that of a foreign type airplane.

**Corroboration:** The witness also discussed the matter with an unidentified woman in her neighborhood in Hamilton, Baltimore, Maryland. This second woman confirmed she too had heard the noise in question. Her husband is also an ex-G.I., and he stated that the motors sounded like that of foreign planes.

**Action:** No action was contemplated by Strategic Air Command headquarters. Document signed by Alan Margeau, CWO, USAF, Asst Adj Gen, for the Commanding General.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 美国战略空军司令部总部（位于华盛顿特区安德鲁斯机场）的限制级备忘录，日期为1948年3月29日，向美国空军参谋长情报局长转呈的报告。文件标记为第110号事件。

**Source:** FBI巴尔的摩办事处致第二集团军情报局长的信函，内容涉及一名个人报告不明空中声响。

**Witness:** 一名身份不详的女性，于1948年3月23日联系FBI。她是美国军队前成员的妻子，目前积极参与美国退伍军人协会活动。她强调自己"绝非歇斯底里或对当前世界局势过度忧虑"。

**Sighting:** 在过去六至八周内的多个场合，于凌晨3:00至5:00之间，目击者听到天空中传来奇特的声响。这些声音似乎来自远处的飞机，但并非通常从美国飞机听到的那种飞机发动机嗡嗡声。目击者与丈夫讨论此事，其丈夫认为该声音更像是外国型号飞机的声音。

**Corroboration:** 目击者还与她在马里兰州巴尔的摩汉密尔顿社区的一名身份不详的女性邻居讨论此事。这第二名女性证实她也听到了所述噪音。她的丈夫也是一名退伍军人，他表示发动机声听起来像外国飞机的声音。

**Action:** 战略空军司令部总部未考虑采取任何行动。文件由USAF准尉Alan Margeau代表司令将军签署，职务为助理副官长。

events.title: 1st Lt. Robert W. Meyers: silver hull near Philippine Islands (1 Apr 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #111 Summary Sheet**

**Date/Time:** 1 April 1948 at 0955 hours

**Witness:** 1st Lt. Robert W. Meyers, 67th Fighter Squadron, 18th Fighter Group. Observer was a P-47 pilot sighting the object from his aircraft over the Philippine Islands.

**Location:** Approximately lat. 31° East, 13° 53' North (airspace over Philippine Islands region)

**Object Characteristics:** Single silver-colored object described as hull-shaped, closely resembling a flying wing type aircraft with turtle back and an indistinct dorsal fin. Wing span approximately 30 feet, length 20 feet.

**Flight Behavior:** Object initially appeared in line of sight during flight. Speed estimated at 200 MPH, then disappeared in 5 seconds indicating great acceleration. Made a 90° left turn, then level flight accelerating rapidly. Direction of flight: 270° (due west). No sound observed.

**Duration:** Approximately 60 seconds in sight.

**Distance:** Estimated 3 miles from observer.

**Weather Conditions:** Scattered cumulus clouds, base at 3000 feet, tops at 6000 feet.

**Peculiarities:** Object made a left turn, leveled out on a 270° heading, accelerated rapidly and disappeared from sight.

**Effect on Clouds:** None observed.

**Document Type:** Official USAF Incident Summary Sheet to be filed and retained in official files.
events.title_ocr_original: Incident 111 — USAF UAP Check-List (formerly tagged Incident 94 due to OCR error)
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 第67战斗机中队、第18战斗机大队一级中尉Robert W. Meyers。观察者是一名P-47飞行员，在菲律宾群岛上空从其飞机上目击到该物体。

**Location:** 大约位于东经31°，北纬13° 53'（菲律宾群岛地区上空）

**Object Characteristics:** 单个银色物体，被描述为船体状，非常类似飞翼型飞行器，带有龟背状结构和不明显的背鳍。翼展约30英尺，长度20英尺。

**Flight Behavior:** 物体最初在飞行期间出现在视线范围内。速度估计为200 MPH，然后在5秒内消失，表明加速度极大。进行了90°左转，然后水平飞行并快速加速。飞行方向：270°（正西）。未观察到声音。

**Duration:** 在视线内约60秒。

**Distance:** 距观察者估计3英里。

**Weather Conditions:** 零散积云，云底高度3000英尺，云顶高度6000英尺。

**Peculiarities:** 物体进行了左转，在270°航向上水平飞行，快速加速并从视线中消失。

**Effect on Clouds:** 未观察到影响。

**Document Type:** USAF官方事件摘要表，将归档并保存在官方文件中。

events.title: Rev. John H. Bergen: spherical white object, Delaware, OH (8 Apr 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #112e

**Witness:** Rev. John H. Bergen, Pastor, residing at 111 North Washington Street, Delaware, Ohio. Occupation suggests credible civilian observer.

**Sighting:** On 8 April 1948 at 1430 hours (2:30 PM), Rev. Bergen observed one unidentified flying object from the ground in Delaware, Ohio. The object remained in sight for approximately ten minutes before disappearing from view behind trees.

**Object Description:** The object was spherical in shape with a small protrusion above it, resembling vapor streaks. It was very white in color and estimated to be not less than 5 feet in width. The object traveled at an altitude of several thousand feet at a speed described as "not too fast," moving almost due west into the wind.

**Flight Characteristics:** The object exhibited no tactical maneuvers and produced no sound. No exhaust trails were observed. Distance from observer could not be determined.

**Environmental Conditions:** Weather conditions were clear at the time of observation. Effect on clouds marked as "N/S" (not stated/applicable).

**Physical Evidence:** No odor was detected, no sketches or photographs were taken.

**Remarks:** The reporting officer noted that "this object appeared like a concentrated bit of cloud except it was clearly outlined. The size could not be determined."

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED checklist for unidentified flying objects.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 约翰·H·伯根牧师(Rev. John H. Bergen)，牧师，居住在俄亥俄州特拉华市北华盛顿街111号。其职业表明该观察者为可信的平民目击者。

**Sighting:** 1948年4月8日14时30分(下午2:30)，伯根牧师在俄亥俄州特拉华市(Delaware, Ohio)从地面观察到一个不明飞行物体。该物体在视野中停留了约十分钟，随后消失在树木后方。

**Object Description:** 该物体呈球形，顶部有一个小突起，类似蒸汽条纹。颜色非常白，估计宽度不少于5英尺。物体在数千英尺的高度飞行，速度被描述为"不太快"，几乎正西方向逆风移动。

**Flight Characteristics:** 该物体未表现出任何战术机动，也未产生声音。未观察到尾气痕迹。无法确定与观察者的距离。

**Environmental Conditions:** 观察时天气状况晴朗。对云层的影响标记为"N/S"(未说明/不适用)。

**Physical Evidence:** 未检测到气味，未绘制草图或拍摄照片。

**Remarks:** 报告官员指出："该物体看起来像一团浓缩的云，但轮廓清晰。无法确定其大小。"

**Document Classification:** 不明飞行物体受限级(RESTRICTED)核查清单。

events.title: 1st Lt. Aytch Johnson: silvery disc over Fairbanks, Alaska (18 Apr 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 114

**Witness:** 1st Lt. Aytch Johnson, USAF (discharged as per authority Para 1, SO 60 dated 28 May 48). Address: Ft. Worth, Texas.

**Sighting:** On 18 April 1948 at 1306 hours, Lt. Johnson observed a single unidentified flying object approximately 1 mile north of Fairbanks, Alaska, while flying over the city. The object remained in sight for only a few minutes.

**Object Description:** The object was round and flat in shape, silvery in color, and approximately 8 inches in diameter. It was observed at an altitude of 2000-3000 feet, traveling at an estimated speed of 250-300 miles per hour (the object traveled 500 feet in 1 or 2 seconds). The object's direction of flight was northeast toward southwest.

**Behavior:** The object oscillated from a horizontal plane to a vertical plane at very rapid speed. No sound was detected. No exhaust trails of any kind were observed.

**Conditions:** Weather was clear with unrestricted visibility. Distance from observer: N/S (not stated). Odor detected: N/S. Apparent construction: N/S. Effect on clouds: N/S. Manner of disappearance: N/S.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were taken. This is a confidential USAF checklist for unidentified flying objects.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Object Characteristics:** Single object observed. Size described as approximately that of a football. Color noted as blue flame (with "N/S" also marked, possibly indicating "not stated" or uncertainty). Speed characterized as meteoric. Direction of flight was earthward. Shape not stated (N/S). No odor detected.

**Behavior:** The object traveled in an earthward direction at meteoric speed. Manner of disappearance: exploded. No sound was noted during the sighting. Tactics not stated. Apparent construction described as meteor.

**Observation Details:** Number of objects: 1. Distance from observer, time in sight, and altitude all marked N/S (not stated). Weather conditions noted as night. Effect on clouds: N/S. No exhaust trails reported (marked with strikethrough "orangelight" and N/S notation).

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were provided. Additional remarks are noted as continuing over to another page.

**Document Classification:** This checklist is marked RESTRICTED at top and bottom.

events.title: Dr. Ormens: white point, South to North, Berlin (28 Mar 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Document:** CHECK-LIST - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS, Incident #118, declassified report from U.S. military files documenting a UFO sighting in post-war Berlin.

**Witness:** Dr. Ormens, former guided missile expert at Exeinmetall Borsi, observing from Berlin Lichtenrade, Kirchbachstrasse 2. The witness's technical background in missile systems lends credibility to the observation.

**Sighting Details:** On 28 March 1948 at 1630 hours (4:30 PM), Dr. Ormens observed one unidentified flying object at an altitude of 14 kilometers (approximately 46,000 feet). The object was described as traveling "rather fast" on a trajectory from South to North. Weather conditions were clear at the time.

**Object Characteristics:** The object appeared as a "white point" in color white. Distance from observer could not be determined (N/S). Time in sight was not specified. No sound was reported during the observation. Shape, odor, and apparent construction details were not specified (N/S). The object's size description as a "white point" suggests it was at significant distance or was relatively small.

**Additional Information:** No exhaust trail was reported. No sketches or photographs were obtained. Tactics and manner of disappearance were not specified (N/S). Effect on clouds was not specified. The checklist indicates remarks continued on additional pages (over).
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 核查清单 - 不明飞行物，事件编号#118，来自美国军方档案的解密报告，记录了战后柏林的一次UFO目击事件。

**Witness:** Ormens博士，前Exeinmetall Borsi公司导弹专家，在柏林利希滕拉德(Berlin Lichtenrade)基希巴赫大街(Kirchbachstrasse)2号进行观测。该目击者在导弹系统方面的技术背景为其观测增添了可信度。

**Sighting Details:** 1948年3月28日1630时(下午4:30)，Ormens博士在14公里高度(约46,000英尺)观测到一个不明飞行物。该物体被描述为以"相当快"的速度沿从南向北的轨迹飞行。当时天气状况晴朗。

**Object Characteristics:** 该物体呈现为一个"白色光点"，颜色为白色。与观测者的距离无法确定(N/S)。视野停留时间未说明。观测期间未报告任何声音。形状、气味和明显的构造细节未说明(N/S)。该物体被描述为"白色光点"表明它距离相当远或体积相对较小。

**Additional Information:** 未报告有尾气轨迹。未获得草图或照片。飞行战术和消失方式未说明(N/S)。对云层的影响未说明。核查清单注明备注在附加页面继续(背面)。

**Observation Details:** Single object observed from ground. The witness was riding four miles north of Alton at approximately 11:30 A.M. on 11 April 1948 when he observed the creature/object. Distance from observer, time in sight, altitude, speed, direction of flight, sound, color, odor, apparent construction, exhaust trails, weather conditions, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance are all marked N/S (not stated).

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained.

events.title: W. A. Bonneville: ball-shaped object between Plevna and Miles City, MT (17 May 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #130

**Witness:** W. A. Bonneville, Territory Manager for B. F. Goodrich Company, residing at 415 W. Rosser Ave., Bismarck, N.D.

**Sighting:** On the night of 17 May 1948, observer was traveling west on Route #212, west of Plevna, Montana (between Plevna and Miles City), when he observed an unidentified flying object at ground level.

**Object Characteristics:** The object was described as ball-shaped, fairly large compared with an aircraft, and white in color (might have had slight bluish-white tinge). It was observed at closest approach at approximately 2500 feet distance. The object traveled at twice the speed of Northwest Airlines planes, moving west, slightly south, then west again.

**Duration & Behavior:** The object remained in sight for approximately twenty minutes. It performed arc tactics and exhibited a long bright light shooting from under it, described as exhaust trails. The object eventually flew into a dark cloud bank and disappeared.

**Physical Evidence:** No sound was detected. Apparent construction appeared meteor-like. Weather conditions were moonlight but cloudy, with no reported effect on clouds. No photographs or sketches were obtained, but a map was forwarded showing the location of the object.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED checklist for unidentified flying objects. Reference made to a supplement for additional remarks.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #130

**Witness:** W. A. Bonneville，B. F. Goodrich公司地区经理，居住在北达科他州俾斯麦(Bismarck, N.D.)西罗瑟大街(W. Rosser Ave.)415号。

**Sighting:** 1948年5月17日夜间，观察者在蒙大拿州普莱夫纳(Plevna, Montana)以西的212号公路(位于普莱夫纳和迈尔斯城之间)向西行驶时，在地面高度观察到一个不明飞行物。

**Object Characteristics:** 该物体被描述为球形，与飞机相比相当大，颜色为白色(可能带有轻微的蓝白色调)。在最近距离观察时，物体距离约为2500英尺。该物体以西北航空公司飞机两倍的速度移动，先向西飞行，略微向南，然后再次向西。

**Duration & Behavior:** 该物体在视线范围内停留了大约二十分钟。它进行了弧形战术机动，并展示出从其下方射出的明亮长光，被描述为排气尾迹。该物体最终飞入乌云层并消失。

**Physical Evidence:** 未检测到声音。外观构造似乎类似流星。天气状况为有月光但多云，未报告对云层产生影响。未获得照片或草图，但转送了一份显示物体位置的地图。

**Document Classification:** 不明飞行物限制级(RESTRICTED)核查清单。参考补充文件以获取额外备注。

events.title: Daughter of Col. Rasmussen: luminous object over Oslo, Norway (12 Dec 1947)

events.report_summary:
**Document:** CHECK-LIST for Unidentified Flying Objects, Incident 132, filed as RESTRICTED, Evaluation A-3.

**Witness:** Daughter of MA Kai E. Rasmussen, Col GSC. Occupation listed as N/S (not stated). Address: Same as MA, Oslo, Norway.

**Sighting:** On 12 December 1947 at 2205 and 2208 hours, the observer witnessed one object from ground level in Oslo, Norway. Time in sight: between two and three seconds. Number of objects: 1.

**Object Description:** Color described as luminous/white with greenish-yellow tail. Apparent construction: meteor-like. Exhaust trails: greenish-yellow trail. Shape and size: N/S (not stated). The object was apparently traveling fairly close to ground or would be visible to more people. Speed: Not quite as fast as a meteor. Direction of flight: SSE-SSW to NNW(?). Altitude: N/S.

**Maneuvers:** Performed arc of circle, purvature very great (likely "curvature").

**Other Details:** Sound: None. Odor detected: None. Distance from observer: N/S.

**Weather:** No fog, sky clear and star-lit. Effect on clouds: none.

**Disappearance:** Trees obscured vision.

**Remarks:** Office employee reports unusual number of falling stars night of 13 Dec. University Observatory has no record of incident. Sketches or photographs: none.

**Sighting:** 1947年12月12日2205时和2208时，观察者在挪威奥斯陆地面目击到一个物体。可见时间：2至3秒之间。物体数量：1个。

**Object Description:** 颜色描述为发光/白色，带有绿黄色尾迹。外观构造：类似流星。尾气痕迹：绿黄色尾迹。形状和大小：N/S（未说明）。该物体显然飞行高度较低，否则会有更多人看到。速度：不及流星快。飞行方向：SSE-SSW至NNW（?）。高度：N/S。

**Maneuvers:** 执行弧形圆周运动，曲率非常大（可能是"curvature"）。

events.title: Multiple UFOs over Norway, Denmark & Sweden (20-26 Feb 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** INCIDENT 133 - A restricted UFO checklist documenting multiple unidentified flying object sightings over Scandinavia during a week-long period from February 20-26, 1948.

**Location & Time:** Sightings occurred over Norway, Denmark, and Sweden, typically around 2130 hours (9:30 PM). The document notes "The trend of these objects to appear at 2130 hours might be significant."

**Observer Information:** Most observer details are listed as N/S (not specified), including name, occupation, address, and place of observation.

**Object Characteristics:** The objects exhibited extraordinary performance capabilities. **Altitude:** Ranged from tree-top level up to 20,000 feet. **Speed:** One to two miles per second (3,600-7,200 mph). **Direction:** Coming from the direction of Peenemünde (the former German V-2 rocket facility). **Color:** Green tail with green exhaust trails noted. **Size, Shape, Sound, Tactics:** All listed as N/S.

**Additional Details:** Number of objects not specified. Distance from observers and time in sight not recorded. No odor detected. Apparent construction described as N/S with a strikethrough of illegible text. Weather conditions and effect on clouds not specified. No sketches or photographs available. Manner of disappearance not specified.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED classification stamped on document.

**Additional Details:** 物体数量未说明。与观察者的距离和可见时间未记录。未检测到气味。表观构造描述为N/S，并有删除线划掉了难以辨认的文字。天气状况和对云层的影响未说明。无草图或照片。消失方式未说明。

**Incident:** Incident 154 - Unidentified Flying Objects checklist report.

**Witness:** 1st Lt. Mokolomis, Corps of Engineers, stationed at Selfridge Field. Observer was approximately 6 miles east of Monroe, Michigan at the time of sighting.

**Sighting:** On 28 May 1948 at 1500 hours EDST, the witness observed five objects from Selfridge Field, Mt. Clemens, Michigan (approx 6 miles east of Monroe). Initially three objects were visible, followed by two more. Objects were in sight for 10-15 seconds. Distance from observer: first three objects at 2 miles to left, two later objects at 2-1/2 miles to left.

**Object Characteristics:** Disc-shaped objects, silvery-gold in color. Size estimated at 300-400 ft approximately, comparable to lake freighters (500 ft). Objects flew at altitude of 8,000+ feet at speed over 500 MPH. Direction: seven o'clock position to 350° heading north, proceeding from MacDill to Selfridge, making abrupt turn to right (pilot's left).

**Behavior:** Objects maintained nose-up attitude and made abrupt turns. They maintained smooth track through sky and flew in line or storm stepped-up formation. In second sighting, the second object flew about 50 feet higher than the first. All objects had hazy or fuzzy outline.

**Conditions:** Weather clear with visibility 10-15 miles. High overcast at 18,000 ft with thin stratus layer very broken at 8,000 ft. No sound detected. No exhaust trails observed. No odor detected. Apparent construction: N/S.

**Disappearance:** Objects lost in haze at 7 o'clock position to pilot. Sketch showing approximate positions is referenced but not visible on this page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 事件154 - 不明飞行物核查清单报告。

**Witness:** 一等中尉Mokolomis，工兵部队，驻扎在塞尔弗里奇机场(Selfridge Field)。观察者在目击时位于密歇根州门罗市(Monroe, Michigan)以东约6英里处。

**Sighting:** 1948年5月28日东部夏令时1500时，目击者从密歇根州克莱门斯山塞尔弗里奇机场(Selfridge Field, Mt. Clemens, Michigan)(门罗以东约6英里)观察到五个物体。最初看到三个物体，随后又出现两个。物体在视线中停留了10-15秒。与观察者的距离：前三个物体在左侧2英里处，后两个物体在左侧2.5英里处。

**Object Characteristics:** 碟形物体，银金色。尺寸估计约为300-400英尺，相当于湖区货轮(500英尺)。物体在8,000英尺以上高度飞行，速度超过500英里/小时。方向：从七点钟方位飞向350°朝北方向，从麦克迪尔(MacDill)飞往塞尔弗里奇，突然向右转弯(飞行员的左侧)。

**Behavior:** 物体保持机头上仰姿态并做出突然转弯。它们在天空中保持平滑轨迹，以直线或风暴式阶梯上升编队飞行。在第二次目击中，第二个物体飞行高度比第一个高约50英尺。所有物体都有模糊或朦胧的轮廓。

**Conditions:** 天气晴朗,可见度10-15英里。18,000英尺处有高空密云,8,000英尺处有非常分散的薄层云。未检测到声音。未观察到尾气痕迹。未检测到气味。明显构造：无/南。

**Disappearance:** 物体在飞行员七点钟方位的雾霾中消失。参考了显示大致位置的草图,但本页不可见。

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 135 - CHECK-LIST for UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS

**Witness:** Major Elmer H. Hammer, Jr. (AO-460144), Intel Officer of the 28th Bombardment Group (VR), stationed at Rapid City Air Force Base, Weaver, South Dakota.

**Date/Time:** Between 15th and 20th August 1947, at 2130 MST (Mountain Standard Time).

**Location:** Weaver, South Dakota, near Rapid City Air Force Base.

**Sighting Details:** Approximately 12 objects observed at a distance of 4 miles from the observer. Objects were visible for an unspecified time (N/S). They approached initially from the northwest, then turned right and disappeared toward the southwest.

**Object Characteristics:** 
- **Altitude:** Between 10,000 ft and approximately 6,000 ft
- **Speed:** 500 MPH or greater
- **Size:** Estimated length of 100+ feet
- **Shape:** Elliptical
- **Color:** Yellowish-white, brilliant
- **Formation:** Tight diamond-shaped formation
- **Sound:** No noise heard
- **Exhaust trails:** None observed

**Weather Conditions:** Clear sky with no clouds, stars visible, wind calm, visibility 30+ miles. No effect on clouds noted.

**Documentation:** Sketches were made of the objects.

**Remarks:** The report notes minor discrepancies regarding speed and altitude compared to a verbal report given to Glasebrook and Lieutenant to Headquarters f/Maj Hammer. Document is marked RESTRICTED.

- **Altitude:** 介于10,000英尺至约6,000英尺之间
- **Speed:** 时速500英里或更快

- **Shape:** 椭圆形

events.title: Mrs. Whitehouse: orange ball UFO, South Knoxville, TN (30 Jun 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 136

**Date & Time:** 30 June 1948 at 2140 hours

**Witness:** Mrs. Whitehouse, wife of Major Harvey J. Whitehouse, Commanding Officer, ASU, 3319 Tennessee. Location: South Knoxville, Tennessee.

**Object Description:** Single orange-colored, ball-shaped object constructed of what appeared to be "fire." The object exhibited a "streamer of bluish color trailing" as exhaust trails.

**Flight Characteristics:** Altitude estimated at 30,000 feet, traveling at approximately 1,000 MPH in a westerly direction. The object was observed for 3 minutes according to Mrs. Whitehouse, though ORC instructors reported only 3 seconds of observation time. Distance from observer was not specified (N/S). The object disappeared over the horizon.

**Additional Details:** No sound was detected. Size was not specified (N/S). No odor was detected. Tactics were not specified (N/S). Weather conditions and effect on clouds were not specified (N/S). No sketches or photographs were obtained.

**Document Classification:** This is a RESTRICTED U.S. military document from the CHECK LIST - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS series, documenting official UFO investigations during the early Cold War period.

events.title: Lt. Clarence Glasebrook: luminous object near Osborn, Ohio (9 Jul 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #139

**Witness:** 1st Lt. Clarence Glasebrook, USAF, stationed at Hq AMC (MCIAXO-4). Lt. Glasebrook was a reconnaissance pilot in World War II.

**Date & Location:** 9 July 1948, 2147 hours, north end of Osborn, Ohio. Ground-level observation.

**Object Description:** Pale yellowish-white (luminous) object. Size could not be estimated. No sound detected. Made intermittent appearances at regulated intervals, appearing 3 times total, each appearance lasting 1-2 seconds duration.

**Flight Characteristics:** Altitude estimated between 3,000 to 4,000 feet. Speed estimated between 500 & 600 (units not specified, likely mph). Direction of flight was west (east to west).

**Tactics:** Made intermittent appearances at regulated intervals.

**Physical Evidence:** No exhaust trails observed. No shape could be determined. No odor detected. Apparent construction: N/S (not stated).

**Weather Conditions:** Clear with quarter moon in the East-Southeast.

**Manner of Disappearance:** Suddenly at angle of 80° rox., 70° to horizon in front of observer who was looking north.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs available. Distance from observer not stated.

**Source:** CHECK-LIST - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS, marked RESTRICTED

**Date & Location:** 1948年7月9日，21时47分，俄亥俄州奥斯本(Osborn, Ohio)北端。地面观测。

**Object Description:** 淡黄白色（发光）物体。无法估计尺寸。未探测到声音。以规律间隔断续出现，总共出现3次，每次持续1-2秒。

**Flight Characteristics:** 高度估计在3,000至4,000英尺之间。速度估计在500至600之间（未注明单位，可能为英里/小时）。飞行方向为向西（由东向西）。

**Tactics:** 以规律间隔断续出现。

**Physical Evidence:** 未观察到尾迹。无法确定形状。未探测到气味。明显构造：N/S（未说明）。

**Weather Conditions:** 晴朗，四分之一月相位于东南偏东方向。

**Manner of Disappearance:** 突然消失于观测者正北方视野前方，大约80°仰角，与地平线成70°角。

**Documentation:** 无草图或照片。未说明与观测者的距离。

**Source:** 检查清单 - 不明飞行物体，标记为"限制级"(RESTRICTED)

events.title: Eastern Air Lines pilots sight cigar-shaped UFO near Montgomery, AL (24 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #144

**Witnesses:** Pilot Clarence Snipe Chiles and Co-Pilot John B. Whitted of Eastern Air Lines (EAL), plus Mr. McKelvie (occupation N/S). Atlanta Office of EAL.

**Sighting:** On 24 July 1948 at 0245 hours, while flying 20 miles south of Montgomery, Alabama, the pilots observed an unidentified flying object for 5 to 10 seconds at an altitude of 5,000 feet.

**Object Description:** The object was approximately 100 feet long and about twice the diameter of a "B-29" bomber. It was cigar-shaped with no reported color. The object exhibited red-orange flame exhaust trails and a blue fluorescent glow running beneath it. No sound was detected. The object's speed was estimated at 500 to 700 MPH.

**Maneuvers:** The object pulled up sharply with a tremendous burst of flame, as referenced in the Atlanta Constitution of 25 July 1948. Direction of flight was southwest toward Mobile and New Orleans.

**Conditions:** Full moon, clear weather with broken cloud coverage of 4/10 at 6,000 feet. The object pulled up into a cloud and disappeared.

**Documentation:** Two sketches or photographs were included. The document references attached statements for additional details. Apparent construction, odor, and some other characteristics were not specified (N/S).
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #144

**Witnesses:** 东方航空公司(EAL)飞行员克拉伦斯·斯奈普·柴尔斯(Clarence Snipe Chiles)和副驾驶约翰·B·惠特德(John B. Whitted)，以及麦凯尔维先生(Mr. McKelvie)（职业未说明）。东方航空公司亚特兰大办事处。

**Sighting:** 1948年7月24日02时45分，在阿拉巴马州蒙哥马利以南20英里处飞行时，飞行员在5,000英尺高度观察到一个不明飞行物，持续5至10秒。

**Object Description:** 该物体长约100英尺，直径约为"B-29"轰炸机的两倍。呈雪茄形状，未报告颜色。该物体展现出橙红色火焰排气尾迹，底部有蓝色荧光发光。未检测到声音。物体速度估计为每小时500至700英里。

**Maneuvers:** 该物体以巨大的火焰爆发急剧向上拉升，参见1948年7月25日《亚特兰大宪法报》(Atlanta Constitution)。飞行方向为西南方，朝向莫比尔和新奥尔良。

**Conditions:** 满月，晴朗天气，6,000英尺处有4/10的碎云覆盖。该物体向上拉升进入云层后消失。

**Documentation:** 包含两幅草图或照片。文件引用了附加陈述以提供更多细节。外观构造、气味及其他一些特征未说明(N/S)。

events.title: Pilot Louis Feldwery: jet/rocket trail near Blackstone, VA (24 Jul 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 144a

**Witness:** Louis Feldwery, pilot. **Address:** LGA (LaGuardia Airport)

**Sighting:** At 0230 hours on 24 July 1948, while in the air near Blackstone, Virginia, enroute to Raleigh-Durham, the observer witnessed only a trail from an unidentified flying object. The actual object was not seen.

**Object Characteristics:** Only an exhaust trail was perceived, described as seeming to be a jet or rocket trail. The trail covered an 80° to 90° arc laterally. Distance from observer, time in sight, altitude, sound, size, color, shape, and odor were all marked N/S (not stated/not seen). Number of objects: only trail seen.

**Flight Characteristics:** The trail traveled at what was described as "terrific speed" in a direction of 230°. No apparent construction could be determined since the object itself was not visible.

**Weather Conditions:** At 0230 at Blackstone: 0/70 @ HGT 112/73/72/, wsw 5/987. Greensboro and Raleigh-Durham had 0/15 plus [handwritten notation: "German"].

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were available. Effect on clouds: N/S. Manner of disappearance: N/S. Remarks noted as "(over)" suggesting continuation on reverse page.

**Incident #:** 144a

**Witness:** Louis Feldwery，飞行员。**Address:** LGA (LaGuardia Airport 拉瓜迪亚机场)

**Sighting:** 1948年7月24日0230时，观察者在飞往Raleigh-Durham（罗利-达勒姆）途中，于Virginia（弗吉尼亚州）Blackstone（布莱克斯通）附近空中目击到一个不明飞行物留下的尾迹。未看到实际物体本身。

**Object Characteristics:** 仅观察到排气尾迹，描述为似乎是喷气式飞机或火箭的尾迹。尾迹横向覆盖80°至90°的弧度。距观察者的距离、可见时间、高度、声音、大小、颜色、形状和气味均标注为N/S（未说明/未看见）。物体数量：仅看到尾迹。

**Flight Characteristics:** 尾迹以被描述为"极快速度"朝230°方向移动。由于物体本身不可见，无法确定其明显构造。

**Weather Conditions:** 0230时Blackstone（布莱克斯通）的天气状况：0/70 @ HGT 112/73/72/, wsw 5/987。Greensboro（格林斯伯勒）和Raleigh-Durham（罗利-达勒姆）为0/15 plus [手写注释："German"]。

**Documentation:** 无素描图或照片。对云层的影响：N/S。消失方式：N/S。备注标注为"(over)"，表明在背面有续页。

events.location: Between Blackstone, Virginia and Greensboro, North Carolina
events.title: Capt Perry R. Mansfield: meteoric object, Blackstone VA–Greensboro NC (24 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 1144b

**Witness:** Captain Perry R. Mansfield, occupation listed as "Capt on 571/23 EAL" (Eastern Air Lines), address EAL.

**Sighting:** On 24 July 1948 at 0230 hours, Captain Mansfield observed one unidentified flying object while traveling between Blackstone, Virginia and Greensboro, North Carolina. The object was visible for approximately 3 seconds.

**Object characteristics:** The object traveled horizontally at meteoric speed in a southerly direction. Distance from observer: N/S (not specified). Altitude: N/S. Sound: N/S. Size, color, shape, odor: all N/S. Apparent construction: N/S. Exhaust trails: N/S. Effect on clouds: N/S.

**Weather conditions:** VFR (Visual Flight Rules) CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited).

**Disappearance:** The object "died out" in the distance.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. The document is marked "CONFIDENTIAL" and represents a standardized Air Force check-list format for reporting unidentified flying objects. Remarks are noted as continuing on an additional page (marked "over").

**Assessment:** The brief duration (3 seconds), meteoric speed, and manner of disappearance suggest a possible meteor or bolide, though the horizontal trajectory is noted.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Sighting:** 1948年7月24日0230时,曼斯菲尔德上尉在弗吉尼亚州布莱克斯通(Blackstone, Virginia)和北卡罗来纳州格林斯伯勒(Greensboro, North Carolina)之间飞行时观察到一个不明飞行物体。该物体可见时间约为3秒。

**Object characteristics:** 该物体以流星般的速度向南方向水平飞行。距离观察者:N/S(未说明)。高度:N/S。声音:N/S。大小、颜色、形状、气味:均为N/S。明显构造:N/S。尾迹:N/S。对云层的影响:N/S。

**Weather conditions:** VFR(目视飞行规则)CAVU(无云高限制且能见度无限)。

**Disappearance:** 该物体在远处"熄灭消失"。

events.location: San Acacia Dam, New Mexico (65 miles south of Albuquerque)
events.title: 7 metallic objects at 20,000 ft near San Acacia Dam, NM (17 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #146, classified CONFIDENTIAL checklist for unidentified flying objects.

**Date & Time:** 17 July 1948 at 1650 hours

**Location:** Vicinity of San Acacia Dam, 65 miles south of Albuquerque, New Mexico

**Witnesses:** M/Sgt Wm R. Carter (armament technician) and M/Sgt Bernard E. Harvey (experienced Air Force non-commissioned officer), both stationed at 428th AFSU, Kirtland Air Force Base

**Sighting Details:** Seven objects observed maintaining formation, traveling at an estimated speed of 1,500 MPH (if estimated altitude correct) at approximately 20,000 feet altitude. Direction of flight was northerly heading, between north and northwest. Time in sight and distance from observers not specified (N/S).

**Object Characteristics:** Metallic construction with color of aluminum aircraft at high altitude. When overhead, objects appeared circular in shape; after passing zenith, shape became indeterminate. Size not specified. No exhaust trails observed. No sound detected. Tactics included maintained formation throughout observation.

**Weather Conditions:** CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited) at 20,000 feet with wind velocity 8 to 10 miles per hour. Effect on clouds not specified.

**Disappearance:** Objects disappeared in northwest direction. No sketches or photographs obtained.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #146号事件,不明飞行物机密核查清单,密级为机密

**Date & Time:** 1948年7月17日16时50分

**Location:** 新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基(Albuquerque)以南65英里,圣阿卡西亚大坝(San Acacia Dam)附近

**Witnesses:** M/Sgt Wm R. Carter(军械技术员)和M/Sgt Bernard E. Harvey(经验丰富的空军士官),两人均驻扎于柯特兰空军基地(Kirtland Air Force Base)第428 AFSU

**Sighting Details:** 观察到七个物体保持编队飞行,在大约20,000英尺高度以估计1,500英里/小时的速度飞行(若估计高度正确)。飞行方向为向北,介于正北与西北之间。观察时长和与观察者的距离未明确(N/S)。

**Object Characteristics:** 金属结构,颜色类似高空中的铝制飞行器。当物体位于正上方时,呈圆形;通过天顶后,形状变得难以辨认。尺寸未明确。未观察到尾气轨迹。未探测到声音。战术特征包括在整个观察过程中保持编队。

**Weather Conditions:** 20,000英尺高度为CAVU(无云能见度无限),风速8至10英里/小时。对云层的影响未明确。

**Disappearance:** 物体向西北方向消失。未获得草图或照片。

events.title: Mrs. H. H. Gibson: round object resembling huge ball, Springfield, OH (27 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Document:** Confidential checklist for unidentified flying objects, Incident #147, documenting a sighting in Springfield, Ohio.

**Witness:** Mrs. H. H. Gibson, housewife, residing at 1217 East Main Street, Springfield, Ohio.

**Sighting:** On 27 July 1948 at 2200 hours (10:00 PM), Mrs. Gibson observed a single unidentified object from Springfield, Ohio. The object was visible for approximately 3 seconds before flying out of sight. Distance from observer was not specified (marked N/S).

**Object Description:** The witness described the object as resembling a "huge ball" that was round in shape. The object traveled in a straight line heading north at what the witness estimated was the speed of a jet plane, flying at great height/altitude. The object left a bright red tail of fire (exhaust trail) behind it. No sound was detected during the observation. Color of the main object was not specified.

**Conditions:** Weather conditions included some thunder and lightning at the time of the sighting. Effect on clouds was not specified.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were available. The document notes "See attached" in the remarks section, suggesting additional materials were part of the original file.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 机密文件,不明飞行物核查清单,事件编号#147,记录了俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德(Springfield, Ohio)的一次目击事件。

**Witness:** H. H. Gibson夫人,家庭主妇,居住在俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德东主街1217号(1217 East Main Street, Springfield, Ohio)。

**Sighting:** 1948年7月27日2200时(晚上10:00),Gibson夫人在俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德观察到一个不明物体。该物体在飞出视线之前可见时间约为3秒。与观察者的距离未明确说明(标记为N/S)。

**Object Description:** 目击者将该物体描述为类似"巨大的球体",呈圆形。该物体沿直线向北飞行,目击者估计其速度相当于喷气式飞机的速度,飞行高度/海拔极高。该物体身后留下明亮的红色火焰尾迹(尾气轨迹)。观察期间未探测到任何声音。主体物体的颜色未明确说明。

**Conditions:** 目击时的天气状况包括一些雷电。对云层的影响未明确说明。

**Documentation:** 无草图或照片。文件在备注部分注明"见附件",表明原始档案中包含额外材料。

events.title: Mrs. Rose Henry: hovering yellow sphere, Springfield, OH (28 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident Number:** 148

**Date and Time:** 28 July 1948 at 0400 hours (4:00 AM)

**Location:** Springfield, Ohio

**Witness:** Mrs. Rose Henry, housewife, residing at 826 Dibert Avenue, Springfield, Ohio. Observation made from her residence address.

**Object Description:** Single object described as round in shape, about the size of a basketball, and intense yellow in color. The object remained nearly stationary, hovering during the observation.

**Sighting Details:** The witness observed the object for a total of 15 minutes across two separate viewing periods: first sighting lasted 5 minutes, second sighting lasted 15 minutes. Distance from observer was not specified (N/S). The witness reported hearing the sound of a plane before sighting the object. Altitude, direction of flight, and speed details were not specified or not applicable given the hovering behavior.

**Physical Evidence:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Weather conditions, apparent construction, exhaust trails, odor detected, and effect on clouds were all listed as N/S (not specified).

**Manner of Disappearance:** The object faded away.

**Remarks:** Additional information noted as attached to the report.

**Document Classification:** This checklist is marked CONFIDENTIAL and represents a standard U.S. Air Force UFO investigation form from the late 1940s era.

**Object Description:** 单一物体，被描述为圆形，大约篮球大小，呈强烈的黄色。该物体在观察期间几乎静止不动，处于悬停状态。

**Physical Evidence:** 未获得草图或照片。天气状况、明显构造、尾迹排放、检测到的气味以及对云层的影响均列为N/S(未说明)。

**Manner of Disappearance:** 该物体逐渐消失。

**Remarks:** 附加信息注明附于报告中。

events.location: North Jutland (Hjerrin, Sæby and Hjerup), Denmark
events.title: North Jutland UFO: Three rocket-like objects explode (19 Jan 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 149

**Date & Time:** 19 January 1948, 7:30 AM

**Location:** North Jutland, Denmark (specifically Hjerrin, Sæby and Hjerup)

**Source:** Report taken from CMA R-34-48 (NAD 11796) as prepared by Lt Col Franklin E. Tomlinson

**Witness Information:** Name, occupation, and address marked N/S (not stated)

**Number of Objects:** Three

**Object Characteristics:** The objects displayed rocket-like characteristics with apparent rocket-like construction. Speed was described as "apparently rocket-like." Shape was noted as "ball - saucer." Objects had exhaust trails described as a "brilliant tail of green light."

**Flight Behavior:** Direction of flight was East to West. Tactics were dramatic: objects "suddenly stopped, exploded and disappeared." The manner of disappearance was specifically noted as "Exploded and disappeared."

**Observational Data:** Distance from observer, time in sight, altitude, sound, size, color, odor, weather conditions, and effect on clouds all marked N/S (not stated). No sketches or photographs were available.

**Document Classification:** This restricted checklist for unidentified flying objects represents an early systematic attempt to catalog UFO characteristics and behavior patterns in post-WWII Europe.

events.location: Swedish Coast (enroute Aalberg, Denmark to Oslo, Norway)
