events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 150

**Date & Time:** Approximately 1 March 1948, 0930 hours

**Location:** Swedish Coast, air enroute from Aalberg, Denmark to Oslo, Norway

**Witness:** Norwegian pilot (OML pilot), name not specified. Material taken from MA R-130-48 NAD 20560.

**Sighting:** The pilot observed a single unidentified flying object while at an altitude of 20,000 feet. The object was visible for approximately 4 seconds. Direction of flight was described as southeast, passing along the Swedish Coast and disappearing over Norway. The flight path followed the earth's surface.

**Object Characteristics:** The object emitted a bluish-green flame. No exhaust trails were observed. Size, shape, speed, distance from observer, sound, odor, and apparent construction were all marked as N/S (not specified). Weather conditions and effect on clouds were also not specified.

**Additional Details:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. The object disappeared over Norway. Most physical characteristics of the object could not be determined or were not recorded in the available material.

**Document Status:** RESTRICTED classification checklist for unidentified flying objects.

events.title: Mr. & Mrs Vernon Swigert: white cymbal-shaped object, Indianapolis, IN (31 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 152

**Witnesses:** Mr. & Mrs Vernon Swigert, residing at 2020 Boyd St., Indianapolis, Indiana. Mr. Swigert was an electrician; Mrs. Swigert a housewife.

**Sighting:** On 31 July 1948 at 0825 hours, the witnesses observed a single unidentified flying object from their address in the south-central part of Indianapolis. The object was visible for approximately 10 seconds.

**Object Description:** The object was described as cymbal-shaped (like a cymbal), white in color with no shine. Size estimates indicated approximately 20 feet in diameter and 6 to 8 feet in height at the center, with a ratio of about 3:1. The object traveled at an altitude of 2,000 feet at an estimated speed of 1800 MPH in a direction of 90° (due east). Distance from observers was not specified (N/S).

**Additional Details:** No sound was detected during the observation. No exhaust trails were observed. Weather conditions were reported as sky clear. The object's tactics, odor, apparent construction, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance were all marked as N/S (not specified). One sketch or photograph was noted as accompanying the report.

**Document Classification:** This checklist is marked CONFIDENTIAL and is part of the U.S. Air Force's systematic collection of unidentified flying object reports from 1948.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Object Description:** 该物体被描述为铙钹状（像铙钹），白色，无光泽。尺寸估计直径约20英尺，中心高度6至8英尺，比例约为3:1。该物体在2,000英尺高度飞行，估计速度为1800英里/小时，方向为90°（正东）。与观察者的距离未说明(N/S)。

events.title: Attorney Charles Saunders: grey-black object over Columbus, OH (2 Aug 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 154

**Witness:** Charles Saunders, attorney, residing at 265-1/2 South High St, Columbus, Ohio. Observation made from the yard of 1337 Clifton Ave., Columbus.

**Date & Time:** 2 August 1948 at 1945 hours (7:45 PM)

**Object Description:** Single object judged to be 20 to 30 ft in diameter. Perimeter appeared constant grey-black; center was transparent. Shape was changing: initially viewed as a parallelogram from the side, then assumed a circular/flattened form before reverting to original shape. No odor detected. Apparent construction not specified (N/S).

**Flight Characteristics:** Object observed for 10-15 minutes at altitude of 1,500 to 2,000 ft, traveling at approximately 15 MPH, moving south from the north. Maintained constant slow speed. At one point hesitated and emitted a thin trail of smoke from the opposite direction of travel, then changed position assuming different shapes. Distance from observer not stated (N/S).

**Environmental Conditions:** Weather was CAVU (ceiling and visibility unlimited). No clouds present; no effect on clouds noted.

**Sound & Exhaust:** No sound detected. Thin trail of smoke observed during the hesitation phase.

**Documentation:** 4 sketches were made by the witness.

**Document Type:** This is a confidential Air Force UFO checklist form for unidentified flying objects, marked page 95.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Object Description:** 单个物体，判断直径为20至30英尺。外围呈现恒定的灰黑色；中心部分透明。形状不断变化：最初从侧面看呈平行四边形，随后变为圆形/扁平形状，之后又恢复原状。未检测到气味。明显构造未说明（N/S）。

**Flight Characteristics:** 物体在1,500至2,000英尺高度被观察10-15分钟，以大约15英里/小时的速度从北向南移动。保持恒定的缓慢速度。在某一时刻停顿并从飞行方向的相反方向释放出一道细烟迹，随后改变位置并呈现不同形状。与观察者的距离未说明（N/S）。

**Environmental Conditions:** 天气为CAVU（云高和能见度无限制）。无云；未观察到对云层的影响。

events.title: Mrs. Edward G. Watson: 6-7 gold starlike objects, Columbus, OH (31 Jul 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #155, classified CONFIDENTIAL

**Witness:** Mrs. Edward G. Watson, housewife, residing at 480 N. Monroe Ave., Columbus, Ohio.

**Date/Time:** 31 July 1948 at 1630 hours (4:30 PM).

**Location:** Columbus, Ohio (observation made from 480 N. Monroe Ave.).

**Objects:** 6 or 7 unidentified flying objects observed at a very great distance away and at very great altitude. Objects were described as gold in color, starlike in shape, and approximately the size of an ash tray when viewed from the observer's position.

**Behavior:** The objects were hovering and hanging in the sky. Speed was listed as "Hovering." Direction of flight was not specified (N/S).

**Duration:** Time in sight not specified (N/S).

**Environmental Conditions:** Weather conditions were CAVU (Ceiling and Visibility Unlimited) with bright sunlight. Effect on clouds: N/S.

**Additional Details:** No sound detected (N/S). No odor detected (N/S). Apparent construction: N/S. No exhaust trails observed (N/S). No sketches or photographs were obtained. Manner of disappearance: N/S.

**Document:** This is a standard military UFO check-list form used to catalog unidentified flying object reports during the late 1940s, part of early Air Force investigation efforts. Remarks section indicates continuation (over).

events.title: Mrs. Price & Mrs. Rippetoe: Black oblong object, Columbus, OH (31 Jul 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** Case #156, documented on a restricted U.S. military checklist for unidentified flying objects.

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Merlin Price (housewife) and Mrs. Mary Rippetoe (mother of Mrs. Price), residing at 2186 Lemont Ave., Columbus, Ohio.

**Sighting Location:** Tremont Road near WOSU radio tower, located near University Golf Course, Columbus, Ohio.

**Date & Time:** 31 July 1948 at 8:00 P.M.

**Object Description:** Single black oblong object approximately the size of a gasoline drum (5' x 6'). The object traveled from west to east at an altitude of 250 feet, moving very slowly. Distance from observers was approximately 250 feet. The object made no noise and did not change course or altitude during observation. Black smoke was seen spouting from the top, leaving exhaust trails.

**Flight Characteristics:** Direction: West to East. Speed: Very slow. Altitude: 250 feet (constant). Tactics: No course or altitude changes observed.

**Environmental Conditions:** Weather was clear with no clouds present.

**Documentation:** No photographs or sketches were obtained. Time in sight and manner of disappearance not specified (N/S). Odor detection and apparent construction also not specified.

**Document Status:** Marked RESTRICTED at top and bottom of page, indicating military classification at time of filing.

**Document Status:** 页面顶部和底部标记为RESTRICTED（限制级），表明归档时属于军事机密级别。

**Object characteristics:** Silver in color, cylindrical in shape, traveling at very slow speed in a southwesterly direction. No tactics, sound, or exhaust trails were detected. Size, apparent construction, odor, and effect on clouds were all not specified. No sketches or photographs were taken.

**Conditions:** Weather was clear with high scattered clouds and good visibility.

**Disappearance:** Manner of disappearance not specified.

**Document notes:** This is a standardized military intelligence form used to catalog UFO sightings during Project Sign/Grudge era. The form indicates remarks continue on an additional page (noted as "over"). Multiple data fields remain incomplete (marked N/S), suggesting either incomplete reporting or witness inability to provide certain details.

events.title: John Jannicky, Jr.: star-like object, Dravasburg, PA (4 Jul 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #160

**Date & Time:** 4 July 1948, 11:15 P.M.

**Location:** Dravasburg, Pennsylvania

**Witness:** John Jannicky, Jr., residing at Box 227, Dravasburg, PA. Occupation listed as N/S (not stated).

**Object Description:** The witness observed a single object described as star-like in appearance. The object was reported to be the size of a star, the same color as a star, and shaped like a star. No sound was detected during the observation.

**Behavior & Characteristics:** The object was initially hovering, then moved across the sky at an undetermined speed. Its tactical movement was distinctive: it moved across the sky, stopping three times and resuming movement. The object remained in sight for 20 seconds or more. Direction of flight and altitude were not stated (N/S).

**Additional Details:** Distance from observer was not stated. No odor was detected, and no exhaust trails were visible. Weather conditions were not recorded. The object's effect on clouds was not stated. The manner of disappearance was not documented.

**Documentation:** A vague sketch was provided with the report. This appears to be a standard U.S. military check-list form for unidentified flying objects, marked RESTRICTED, documenting a brief star-like sighting during evening hours on Independence Day 1948.

events.title: S/Sgt Leroy H. Estes: silver V-2 rocket-shaped object, Los Angeles (30 Aug 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident Number:** 166

**Date and Time:** 30 August 1948, 20:00 hours (8:00 P.M.)

**Witness:** S/Sgt Leroy H. Estes, address 1301 W. Olympic Blvd., Los Angeles. Observation made from same location.

**Object Description:** Single object, silver in color, shaped like a V-2 rocket. Size described as larger than a B-29 aircraft. The object exhibited blue exhaust trails.

**Flight Characteristics:** Altitude estimated to be well over 20,000 feet. Speed thought to be well over 700 MPH. Direction of flight: West to East. Tactics described as "none - flew level course." No sound was detected during the observation.

**Weather and Conditions:** Weather conditions marked as "Clear" (handwritten notation). Effect on clouds: N/S (not specified). Distance from observer and time in sight both marked N/S.

**Additional Details:** No odor was detected. Apparent construction described as "rocket-like." No sketches or photographs were obtained. Manner of disappearance: N/S.

**Document Status:** This check-list form is marked "RESTRICTED" and appears to be a standardized U.S. military UFO incident report from the late 1940s, documenting a high-altitude, high-speed object over Los Angeles observed by military personnel.

**Flight Characteristics:** 估计高度远超20,000英尺。速度被认为远超700英里/小时。飞行方向：由西向东。战术特征描述为"无——水平飞行"。观测期间未探测到任何声音。

events.title: A. D. Otter: wingless aircraft at high speed, Arnhem, The Hague (20 Jul 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident #:** 168

**Date & Time:** 20 July 1948 at 1330 local

**Location:** Obrechstreet, Arnhem, The Hague. Coordinates: 52° 30' N, 4° 30' E

**Witness:** A. D. Otter, Chief Investigator of Court of Damage, residing in Arnheim, The Hague

**Object Characteristics:** The observer reported a wingless aircraft with two decks and no wings. The object traveled at very high altitude and high speed, comparable to a V-2 rocket. The sound produced was the same as a V-2. The object was described as traveling at very high altitude and was seen intermittently through clouds. It was traveling at very high speed.

**Sighting Details:** One object was observed. Distance from observer, time in sight, direction of flight, tactics, size, color, odor detected, apparent construction, and exhaust trails were all listed as N/S (not stated). The object appeared to be a wingless aircraft with 2 decks. Weather conditions at the time included unlimited visibility with scattered clouds. Effect on clouds was N/S.

**Documentation:** No sketches or photographs were taken. Manner of disappearance was N/S.

**Remarks:** The object appeared to be a wingless aircraft with two decks traveling at very high altitude and was seen four times intermittently through clouds. Visibility was unlimited.

**Document Classification:** RESTRICTED

**Documentation:** 未拍摄草图或照片。消失方式为N/S。

**Remarks:** 该物体似乎是一架带有两层甲板的无翼飞行器，在极高海拔飞行，透过云层间歇性地被观测到四次。能见度无限制。

events.title: Farmer Faby Niswonger: silver sphere, Maplewood, OH (29 Aug 1948)

**Date and Time:** 29 August 1948 at 0530 hours.

**Location:** Maplewood, Ohio.

**Object Description:** The witness observed one large, silver-colored spherical object. Size described as "large" with no specific dimensions provided.

**Sighting Details:** The object arose from behind woods and appeared to unravel a silver substance that floated earthward. The object left exhaust trails described as "silver substance" (with question mark notation). **Additional Information:** No sketches or photographs were obtained. Weather conditions and effect on clouds not stated. Apparent construction not determined. No odor detected.

events.title: American correspondent: narrow object near Moscow, USSR (3 Aug 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** #171

**Date & Time:** 3 August 1948, at sunset

**Location:** Approximately 25 km (13x20 miles) northwest of Moscow, USSR

**Witness:** An American newspaper correspondent based in Moscow, USSR. Observer's position was on the ground.

**Object Description:** One object sighted. The object shone brightly and came into the observer's line of sight. It was described as long and narrow in shape, with a bright metallic appearance ("shone brightly"). The object traveled at high speed but not excessively so, moving in a southwest to northwest direction.

**Characteristics:** The object appeared to be metallic in construction. No sound was reported. Weather conditions at the time were sunny. Peculiarities noted were described as "wingless, long and narrow."

**Documentation:** This is an Incident Summary Sheet, a standardized U.S. government form used to catalog unidentified aerial phenomena reports. The form indicates that a separate summary sheet is attached with additional details.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** #171

**Date & Time:** 1948年8月3日，日落时分

**Location:** 苏联莫斯科西北约25公里（13×20英里）

**Witness:** 一名驻苏联莫斯科的美国报社记者。观察者位置在地面。

**Object Description:** 目击到一个物体。该物体发出明亮的光芒并进入观察者的视线范围。物体被描述为狭长形状，具有明亮的金属外观（"发出明亮光芒"）。物体以高速移动但速度并非极快，运动方向为西南至西北。

**Characteristics:** 该物体似乎为金属结构。未报告有声音。当时天气状况为晴朗。注明的特异之处被描述为"无翼、狭长"。

**Documentation:** 这是一份事件摘要表，是美国政府用于记录不明空中现象报告的标准化表格。该表格注明另附有一份摘要表，其中包含更多细节。

events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 174

**Date and Time:** 1 October 1948, Friday morning, 0940 hours

**Location:** Ascension Parish, Township 10 South, Range 4 East, Louisiana, approximately 90 miles from New Orleans (ground observation)

**Witness:** B.B. Williams, President, United Lead Co., 219 Dryades St., New Orleans, RA 0515. Witness described as having considerable flying experience.

**Object Description:** Approximately the length of a passenger aircraft, white-hot in color, cone-shaped. The object appeared to be a white-hot cone that displayed no lights but seemed encased in flame. The object played no lights but seemed encased in flame and did not light up the surrounding area.

**Altitude and Distance:** Estimated 1500 to 2000 feet altitude, 3/4 miles away from observer

**Speed:** Approximately 200 MPH

**Duration:** Sufficiently long to enable Williams to make a fairly detailed observation, approximately 10 seconds

**Flight Characteristics:** Straight and level flight, traveling East. Soundless.

**Apparent Construction:** Described as "flame"

**Exhaust Trail:** Red flames

**Weather Conditions:** No clouds with wind fairly calm

**Peculiarities:** Object left no trail of any kind and did not light up the area (over).

**Document Classification:** SECRET

**Object Description:** 大约相当于一架客机的长度，白热色，锥形。该物体呈现为一个白热的锥体，没有显示任何灯光，但似乎被火焰包裹。该物体没有发光，但似乎被火焰包裹，并且没有照亮周围区域。

**Apparent Construction:** 被描述为"火焰"

**Exhaust Trail:** 红色火焰

**Weather Conditions:** 无云，风相当平静

**Peculiarities:** 物体没有留下任何类型的尾迹，也没有照亮区域（翻页）。

events.title: A. Rubio Angier: white disc, stationary, Santa Fe, NM (23 Sept 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 175

**Date and Time:** 23 September 1948, 0945 hours

**Location:** Santa Fe, New Mexico (observation made from ground, air, southwest from Plaza of Santa Fe, N.M.)

**Witness:** A. Rubio Angier, 2630 Proctor Street, Waco, Texas. Neon Sign Manufacturer and own employer. Experienced pilot since 1928 (not a hobby). Observer was watching another aircraft when attention was attracted to the object.

**Object Description:** White in color, perfectly flat in appearance compared to dime in sky. Size estimated at least 100 to 150 feet in diameter. Altitude estimated between 25,000 to 30,000 feet. Shape appeared perfectly flat.

**Sighting Details:** Object was stationary at time sighted. Witnessed in daylight. Time in sight: 15 or 20 minutes. Very little movement noticed, if any. No sound determined at time of sighting. No clouds present. No evidence of exhaust noticed. Weather conditions: CAVU (Ceiling and Visibility Unlimited).

**Object Behavior:** Stationary - seemed to move in a semi-circle, from S. to E. and finally to NE. May have been optical illusion. Still in view when observer left.

**Peculiarities:** Gave the appearance of being flat.

**Summary Note:** Document indicates "(over)" suggesting continuation on additional page(s).
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident No.:** 175

**Date and Time:** 1948年9月23日，0945时

**Location:** 新墨西哥州圣达菲（从地面和空中进行观测，位于新墨西哥州圣达菲市广场西南方向）

**Witness:** A. Rubio Angier，德克萨斯州韦科市普罗克特街2630号。霓虹灯标牌制造商及个体经营者。自1928年起即为有经验的飞行员（并非业余爱好）。观察者当时正在观察另一架飞机时，注意力被该物体吸引。

**Object Description:** 白色，外观呈完美的扁平状，与天空中的一角硬币相似。尺寸估计直径至少100至150英尺。高度估计在25,000至30,000英尺之间。形状呈现完美的扁平状。

**Sighting Details:** 物体在被观测时处于静止状态。在白天目击。视野内停留时间：15至20分钟。几乎未观察到移动迹象。观测时未确定有声音。无云层存在。未注意到排气痕迹。天气状况：CAVU（云高和能见度无限制）。

**Object Behavior:** 静止状态——似乎以半圆形轨迹移动，从南向东，最后到东北方向。可能是视觉错觉。观察者离开时物体仍在视野内。

**Peculiarities:** 呈现扁平状外观。

**Summary Note:** 文件标注"(翻页)"，表明内容在后续页面继续。

events.title: Col. Horace S. Balsan: translucent sphere near Castro's Ranch, CA (23 Sep 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 176

**Date and Time:** 23 September 1948, approximately 1200 hours

**Location:** Castro's Ranch, 4 miles due east of San Pablo, California, and 4½ miles south of Pinole, California

**Witness:** Col. Horace S. Balsan, U.S. Army (Ret.), 1024 Walther Drive, Walnut Creek, California. Retired Army colonel, formerly a veterinarian, presently employed as a meat inspector by California State Department of Agriculture.

**Observer Position:** On ground (air, control tower, etc.)

**Object Description:** Approximately the size of a 4-engine bomber, longer than wide. Main body translucent and of a dirty gray color. Shape described as undulating with center portion appearing spherical, having the shape and depth similar to a globe-like amoeba. Did not reflect or give off light of any type. Thought main part of object appeared like canvas. Appendages seemed to flap or oscillate while center portion remained stable.

**Flight Characteristics:** Altitude over a mile (estimated). Distance over a mile directly above observer. Very fast speed. Direction of flight nearly due east. Observer was observing an Army bomber when he observed an unknown object flying above the bomber. Time in sight could not be estimated. Object just disappeared from sight in a very short time.

**Sound:** No noise

**Effect on Clouds:** N/S

**Exhaust Trail Color:** No evidence of exhaust

**Weather Conditions:** Clear day, very few clouds in the sky at the time.

**Peculiarities:** See drawing attached
events.report_summary_zh:

**Date and Time:** 1948年9月23日,约1200时

**Location:** 加利福尼亚州圣巴勃罗(San Pablo)正东4英里的卡斯特罗牧场(Castro's Ranch),加利福尼亚州皮诺尔(Pinole)以南4½英里

**Witness:** 美国陆军退役上校霍勒斯·S·巴尔桑(Col. Horace S. Balsan),住址:加利福尼亚州核桃溪(Walnut Creek)沃尔瑟大道(Walther Drive)1024号。退役陆军上校,曾任兽医,目前受雇于加利福尼亚州农业部,担任肉类检查员。

**Observer Position:** 地面(空中、控制塔等)

**Object Description:** 大小约相当于一架四引擎轰炸机,长度大于宽度。主体呈半透明状,颜色为污灰色。形状描述为起伏波动状,中心部分呈球形,其形状和深度类似于球状变形虫。不反射光线,也不发出任何类型的光。认为物体主体部分看起来像帆布。附属部分似乎在拍打或摆动,而中心部分保持稳定。

**Flight Characteristics:** 高度超过一英里(估计)。距离在观察者正上方一英里以上。速度非常快。飞行方向几乎正东。观察者在观察一架陆军轰炸机时发现了一个不明物体在轰炸机上方飞行。无法估计目击时长。物体在极短时间内就从视野中消失了。

**Sound:** 无声音

**Effect on Clouds:** 无说明

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 182

**Date and Time:** 1 October 1948, 2230 GMT to 2310 GMT (approximately 40 minutes observation)

**Location:** North Atlantic Ocean, 40° North by 36° West

**Observer:** Ship's captain aboard the S/S Gulfport

**Object Characteristics:** The witness observed one bright, round object approximately 1/4 the size of a full moon. The object's luminosity was reported as N/S (not specified). The observer could not estimate the object's speed or distance. The object was sighted by means of N/S (not specified) visual observation.

**Behavior:** The object's direction of flight was described as "southwest." Time in sight was 30 minutes. The observer reported no tactics or evasive maneuvers. No sound was made by the object. The object had no apparent effect on clouds or exhaust trails.

**Weather Conditions:** Weather conditions existing at the time were N/S (not specified).

**Peculiarities:** The observer noted "Had distinct bright center" as a distinguishing characteristic.

**Additional Details:** The apparent construction or material of the object could not be determined (N/S). The summary of the incident is listed as "(over)," suggesting additional information may exist on a following page.

**Document Status:** This is a declassified "Incident Summary Sheet" to be filled out and retained in files, representing a standardized UFO reporting form from 1948.

events.title: Military personnel observe silver/gray disc, Mechtberg AF Base, Germany (11 Oct 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 190

**Date and Time:** 11 October 1948 at 1300 hours (1:00 PM)

**Location:** Mechtberg Air Base, Germany

**Witnesses:** Six military personnel of the 86th Fighter Wing, Mechtberg. Observers were ground-based.

**Object Description:** One object sighted, described as silver and gray in color with a shiny appearance. Size was difficult to determine but noted as an "40-60 craft flying between object and observer" with the object appearing small in relation to the size of the object. Shape was either round or unable to determine if disc or ball-like shaped.

**Flight Characteristics:** Object appeared at a 50° heading from Mechtberg Air Base. Estimated distance from observers was 40,000 feet altitude. Speed was noted as "Did not appear to move but got smaller - presumably because it continued to rise." Time in sight was approximately 45 minutes. Tactics described as "appeared stationary."

**Luminosity:** The object had reflected light characteristics.

**Weather Conditions:** Clouds at 20,000 feet with sunlight.

**Sound and Construction:** No sound made by the object. Apparent construction described as metallic.

**Effect on Environment:** Object disappeared behind clouds and/or exhaust trail.

**Peculiarities:** None noted.

**Document Type:** Incident Summary Sheet - a standardized U.S. Air Force reporting form to be filled out and retained in files.

events.title: Incident 196: Target tracked on GCA scope, 1 Nov 1945 (unidentified)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** Designated as Incident 196 in what appears to be a series of tracked unidentified aerial phenomena.

**Sighting:** Target was picked up on GCA (Ground Control Approach) scope at 2145Z on 1 November at 3-3/4 miles from station on a bearing of 103°. The object traveled on a heading of approximately 243° and disappeared at 7-1/2 miles on a bearing of 162° from the station.

**Object Characteristics:** Blip traveled the 4 miles in 4 minutes and 7 seconds, yielding a speed of approximately 60 MPH. The object was tracked with a stop watch. The operator stated the blip was too small at 7-1/2 miles to be an aircraft and too large to be a bird. Size of blip ranged from 270 to 300 and at 5 to 10 KPH.

**Observers:** Target witnessed by the GCA operators monitoring the scope.

**Document Context:** Brief typed incident report, appears to be part of a systematic cataloging of radar contacts with unidentified targets. The technical nature of the report (precise bearings, distances, timing) suggests military radar installation tracking. No specific base location is provided in this summary page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 在一系列被追踪的不明空中现象中，被指定为第196号事件。

**Sighting:** 目标于11月1日2145Z时在GCA(地面进场控制)雷达屏幕上被捕获，距离站点3又3/4英里，方位角103°。该物体以大约243°的航向飞行，并在距离站点7又1/2英里、方位角162°处从雷达上消失。

**Object Characteristics:** 光点在4分钟7秒内飞行了4英里，得出的速度约为每小时60英里。该物体使用秒表进行追踪。操作员表示，在7又1/2英里距离上，该光点太小而不像飞机，但又太大而不像鸟类。光点大小范围在270到300之间，速度为5到10 KPH。

events.title: Lt. Kuzman & Maj Morris: yellow egg-shaped objects near Grays Harbor (Incident 199)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 199

**Witnesses:** Lt. Kuzman (pilot) and Maj Morris (observer) flying in formation with another aircraft.

**Initial Sighting:** Objects first appeared as a very small compact group at 1:00 o'clock position relative to the aircraft. Later moved to 3:00 o'clock position. At that location they appeared to string out to an in-line formation. At first Kuzman could not identify anything. At the time there were clouds up and down in the craft but none in the observer's vicinity. The first color Kuzman noticed was yellow. At 1:00 position the color appeared white. Lt. Kuzman thought they were seagulls with an estimated quantity of 10 to 20 objects.

**Object Description:** At no time did Kuzman identify any object. He saw something and mentioned it to Maj Morris, the pilot who was buying at the time and didn't see the objects. Objects came around to a 3:00 o'clock position in approximately the same V-type formation in color, then made a turn back to a 2:30 position, paralleling the course of the aircraft and then disappeared. No exhaust fume from an airplane would appear much as an exhaust fume from an airplane would. At first the object appeared yellow then changed to white, seemed to change shape slightly. He thought that they looked egg-shaped. Few appeared rather translucent - immediately before the disappearance. In this respect it is pointed out that there was fog and smoke in the vicinity according to weather reports for the vicinity of Grays Harbor.

**Assessment:** No evasive action could be made as to size. Objects disappeared on a northerly course. No evidence of aggressive or evasive tactics. Speed could not be estimated.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 199

**Witnesses:** Kuzman中尉(飞行员)和Morris少校(观察员)与另一架飞机编队飞行。

**Initial Sighting:** 物体最初以非常小的紧密群组形式出现在相对于飞机1点钟方向的位置。后来移动到3点钟方向。在那个位置,它们似乎拉成一条直线队形。起初Kuzman无法识别任何东西。当时飞机上下都有云层,但观察员附近没有。Kuzman注意到的第一个颜色是黄色。在1点钟位置时,颜色呈现白色。Kuzman中尉认为它们是海鸥,估计数量为10到20个物体。

**Object Description:** Kuzman始终没有识别出任何物体。他看到了某些东西并向Morris少校提及,但当时正在驾驶的飞行员没有看到这些物体。物体移动到3点钟位置,大致保持相同的V型队形和颜色,然后转向2点30分位置,与飞机航线平行,之后消失。看起来很像飞机的尾气。起初物体呈现黄色,然后变为白色,似乎形状略有变化。他认为它们看起来像蛋形。在消失前的一刻,有几个显得相当半透明。在这方面需要指出的是,根据格雷斯港(Grays Harbor)附近的天气报告,该地区有雾和烟雾。

**Assessment:** 无法对大小做出任何规避性判断。物体向北方向消失。没有攻击性或规避性战术的证据。速度无法估计。

events.title: Dry cleaner observes metallic plane-like object, Crescent City, CA (17 Oct 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 206b

**Date and Time:** 17 October 1948, 1610 hours

**Location:** Crescent City, California

**Witness:** Ernest Haley, Box 446, Crescent City, California. Occupation: Dry Cleaner. Observer's position: ground.

**Sighting:** The witness's attention was attracted by a glint of light in the sky. He observed one object of unknown size and unknown color (listed as "Unknown Color"). The shape was described as resembling a small plane. The object's luminosity appeared to be reflected light (directed beam of light). The estimated altitude was between 20,000 and 25,000 feet.

**Object Characteristics:** The apparent construction was described as metallic. No sound was made by the object. The direction of flight was southerly. No exhaust trail was observed.

**Maneuvers:** The object made a 45° turn and banked to the right, then made a sharp turn to the south.

**Duration:** The sighting lasted 4 to 5 minutes.

**Disappearance:** The object gradually disappeared from view.

**Weather Conditions:** CAVU (Ceiling and Visibility Unlimited) at time of sighting.

**Additional Details:** Estimated distance from observer: N/S (not stated). Estimated speed: N/S. Effect on clouds: N/S. No peculiarities noted.

**Document Note:** This is an incident summary form with additional details noted as appearing on an attached page (over).

events.title: Sgt. Wright: white speck object near Clark AFB, Philippines (12 Nov 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 206

**Date and Time:** 12 November 1948 between 1300 and 1400 hours

**Location:** Northeast portion of Clark Air Force Base, Phillipine Islands

**Witness:** Sgt Fredrick M. Wright, 18th Maintenance Sq, 18th Main & Supply Gp, Clark AF Base, Sgt, USAF. Observer's position was on ground (air control tower, etc.)

**Object Characteristics:** Single object described as a "white speck." Estimated size: 100 ft / 35 ft body at wings; wings 47-1/2; width of wing 25 ft. Color: snow-white. Estimated altitude: 3 to 6 miles high. Distance from observer: 20 to 30 miles. Speed: Faster than jet plane.

**Observation Details:** Time in sight: W/S (weather station) observed intermittently thru cloud formation. Nature of luminosity: directed beam of light N/S. Flight characteristics: Flying around Clark AF Base - no definite heading, horizontal flight - apparently reconnaissance, single roar. Direction of flight: no definite heading - flew around Clark AF Base. Apparent construction: Similar to plane.

**Weather Conditions:** 4500 scattered, visibility 30 miles.

**Effect on Clouds:** W/S - entered and broke out of cloud six times.

**Exhaust Trail:** Appeared to leave an exhaust trail from tail-end of mentioned object - "it appeared to be sky writing."

**Peculiar Details:** Appeared to have no tail assembly - straight body tapering off from directly above the wings to small point (AFR). Attracted attention by white speck.

**Shape:** See attached (sketch referenced but not visible on this page).
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** Fredrick M. Wright中士，第18维修中队，第18主要与补给大队，克拉克空军基地，USAF中士。观察者位置在地面（空中管制塔等）

**Object Characteristics:** 单个物体，被描述为"白色斑点"。估计尺寸：100英尺/机翼处机身35英尺；翼展47.5英尺；机翼宽度25英尺。颜色：雪白色。估计高度：3至6英里高。距离观察者：20至30英里。速度：比喷气式飞机更快。

**Observation Details:** 视野内时长：W/S（气象站）通过云层间歇性观测到。发光性质：定向光束，方向为南北向。飞行特征：在克拉克空军基地周围飞行——无明确航向，水平飞行——显然是侦察，单一轰鸣声。飞行方向：无明确航向——在克拉克空军基地周围飞行。外观构造：类似飞机。

**Weather Conditions:** 4500英尺零星云层，能见度30英里。

**Effect on Clouds:** W/S——六次进入并穿出云层。

**Exhaust Trail:** 从所述物体尾部似乎留下排气尾迹——"看起来像是天空书写"。

events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 219

**Witness:** Doris Croke, age 14, a ninth grade student at North Junior High, Newburgh, N.Y.

**Sighting:** On the night of 23 November 1948 at precisely 8:00, the witness was standing with two young friends on the corner of Concord St & 1st Street when she observed a ball of fire with a long tail in the north of the sky. The object was visible from east to west for two seconds and then went below the horizon.

**Object:** She described the astral phenomenon as being "a large red ball spreading thru the heavens." She was convinced that she had seen a blue-tailed comet.

**Observations:** The witness stated that while she had seen many shooting stars, she had never seen anything like this. This represents a sighting by a young civilian witness of what appears to be a meteor or similar astronomical phenomenon, distinguished by its red color, long tail, and brief but dramatic visibility as it crossed the northern sky before disappearing below the horizon.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 219

**Witness:** Doris Croke，14岁，纽约州纽堡市(Newburgh, N.Y.)北初中(North Junior High)九年级学生。

**Sighting:** 1948年11月23日晚上8点整，目击者与两位年轻朋友站在康科德街(Concord St)与第一街(1st Street)的街角，观察到天空北方有一个带着长尾巴的火球。该物体从东向西可见约两秒钟，随后消失在地平线下方。

**Object:** 她将这一天文现象描述为"一个巨大的红色球体划过天际"。她确信自己看到的是一颗蓝尾彗星。

**Observations:** 目击者表示，虽然她见过许多流星，但从未见过这样的现象。这是一起年轻平民目击者的观测记录，所见似乎是流星或类似的天文现象，其特点是红色、长尾巴，以及在划过北方天空并消失在地平线下方之前短暂但引人注目的可见性。

events.date_raw: Night of December 12th (approximate 9h 2c plus or minus 30s)
events.location: West of L-Gynt (likely Laguna), New Mexico
events.title: Dr. La Paz: bright green fireball west of L-Gynt, NM (Incident 227)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 227

**Witness:** Dr. La Paz's attention was directed to an area approximately 15° west of L-Gynt when he observed a very bright green ball (apparent angular diameter 5°) to the right of his center field of view, moving from east to west very low on the horizon. Also present were companions including Dr. G. L. Phillips (AF-OSI Medical Officer), Kirtland Fld.; Lt. Allen Clark, Intel Officer; E. Mer. King CAF; and inspectors Jaffers and McQuigg, AFC Security Service (Los Alamos, N.M.).

**Object Description:** The path of the green ball was almost exactly horizontal (altitude estimated as only 3 or 4 degrees) until just a tenth of a second or so before it disappeared. During the last one or two tenths of a second of its visibility, a slight but definite curvature downward developed in its path. From the very beginning the ball was quite bright. Immediate comparison with Sirius (at a much greater altitude than the green fireball) indicates that during all but the last one or two tenths of a second of the fireball's visibility it was at least of apparent magnitude minus four. Just as curvature in its path developed, the magnitude of the fireball rose slightly and it broke up into three or four smaller but still bright green fragments which disappeared almost instantly. Although Lt. Clark stopped the car the moment the fireball disappeared and the occupants stood outside and listened for sonic detonations or rumblings, nothing was heard.

**Coordination:** Two light guards at Los Alamos had also witnessed the phenomenon simultaneously. The anomalous green fireball of December 12th, 9 h 2c plus or minus 30s appeared at latitude 35° 50' longitude 1-6° W' and disappeared near a point with coordinates latitude 35° N' longitude 107° 5', traversing a nearly or exactly horizontal path with a length of very nearly twenty-five (25) miles at an altitude at mid-surface of the earth of approximately 8 to 10 miles, depending on the estimate of angular altitude employed in the reduction.

**Analysis:** The velocity with respect to the earth works out at between 4 to 12 miles a second - depending on the duration estimate used. It should be observed that the above results are obtained under the assumption that the points of appearance and of disappearance of the fireball were seen simultaneously by both the Bernall and Los Alamos groups. If this assumption is not fulfilled, the real path could very easily be no more than 10 to 12 miles long, with a velocity with respect to the earth then working out at between 3 and 6 miles a second. While there is considerable uncertainty because of the lack of confirming azimuth observations from a third station, the discrepancies in the five (5) different estimates of angular elevation make it most unlikely that the linear height of the fireball was much less than 8 miles and much more than 10 miles.

**Context:** During the entire night of the 12th, meteors of all magnitudes from the first to the fifth and of various colors (with white and yellow predominating and with a wide swath of green usually emanating from the Geminid radiant). This radiant was well above the horizon even at the time of the Starvation Peak incident (near Bernal, N.M.).
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 227

**Witness:** 拉帕兹博士的注意力被引向L-Gynt以西约15°的区域，当时他在视野中心的右侧观察到一个非常明亮的绿色火球(视角直径5°)，在地平线很低的位置从东向西移动。在场的还有同伴包括G·L·菲利普斯博士(AF-OSI医疗官)，Kirtland Fld.(柯特兰基地)；艾伦·克拉克中尉，情报官；E·默·金CAF；以及检查员贾弗斯和麦奎格，AFC安全服务处(新墨西哥州洛斯阿拉莫斯)。

**Object Description:** 绿色火球的路径几乎完全水平(高度角估计仅为3或4度)，直到它消失前大约十分之一秒。在其可见的最后十分之一或十分之二秒期间，其路径出现了轻微但明确的向下弯曲。从一开始，火球就相当明亮。与天狼星(海拔高度远高于绿色火球)的即时比较表明，在火球可见的最后十分之一或十分之二秒之外的所有时间里，其视星等至少为负四等。就在其路径出现弯曲时，火球的亮度略有上升，并分裂成三到四个较小但仍然明亮的绿色碎片，这些碎片几乎立即消失。尽管克拉克中尉在火球消失的瞬间停下车，车上人员站在外面倾听音爆或隆隆声，但什么也没听到。

**Coordination:** 洛斯阿拉莫斯的两名光线警卫也同时目睹了这一现象。12月12日9时2分正负30秒的异常绿色火球出现在北纬35°50'、西经106°处，在坐标北纬35°、西经107°5'附近消失，沿几乎或完全水平的路径移动，距离地球中表面的长度非常接近二十五(25)英里，高度约为8至10英里，这取决于计算中使用的仰角估计值。

**Analysis:** 相对于地球的速度计算结果为每秒4至12英里——取决于所使用的持续时间估计。应该注意的是，上述结果是在假设伯纳尔和洛斯阿拉莫斯两组同时看到火球的出现点和消失点的情况下获得的。如果这一假设不成立，真实路径很容易不超过10至12英里，那么相对于地球的速度将在每秒3至6英里之间。虽然由于缺乏来自第三站的方位角确认观测而存在相当大的不确定性，但五(5)个不同仰角估计值的差异使得火球的线性高度不太可能远低于8英里或远高于10英里。

**Context:** 在12日整个夜晚，出现了从一等到五等、各种颜色(以白色和黄色为主，通常有大片绿色)的流星，通常从双子座辐射点发出。即使在饥饿峰事件(新墨西哥州伯纳尔附近)发生时，该辐射点也远在地平线以上。

events.location: Holloman Air Force Base, Alamogordo, New Mexico
events.title: Green fireball analysis: meteor shower observations (Incident 227)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** This page (numbered 3) discusses Incident 227 and provides analytical notes on green fireball observations, comparing them with normal meteor showers and genuine meteorite falls.

**Green Fireball Characteristics:** The document notes that meteor showers normally produce extremely bright green fireballs like those recently observed. Examples cited include Mr. Monnig's observation (Incident 231) near the Quadrantid shower maximum in early January, Mr. McCullough's observation of August near the Perseid shower (Incident 290), and December observations (223, 223a, 224, 226, 227) falling in the interval covered by the Geminid shower. This relationship **might indicate** an attempt to render the green fireballs less conspicuous by causing them to appear only when there is considerable meteoric activity.

**Color Analysis:** The remarkably vivid green color reported for most December fireballs is rarely observed in genuine meteors. Laboratory tests indicate this popular color is identical with that given off by copper salts in blowpipe flames. If this identification is correct, the wavelength of radiation from the green fireballs is near λ = 5216 Å.

**Duration:** Duration estimates of between 2 and 3 seconds reported for the green fireballs are considerably longer than those (0.1 - 0.5 seconds) for ordinary visual meteors, but shorter than duration estimates invariably reported for genuine meteorite falls (5 to 30 seconds or even longer).

**Trailing Effects:** Many of the green fireballs seem to have a train of sparks or a dust cloud following, contrasting sharply with behavior noted in cases of meteoric fireballs, particularly those that penetrate to very low levels where the green fireball of December 12 was observed.

**NOTE:** Inquiry at Holloman AF Base, Alamogordo, N.M., revealed that research work at night and on Sundays does not involve the use of any lighting device or flares such as described in the various reports submitted.
events.report_summary_zh:
**事件：** 本页（编号3）讨论了事件227，并提供了关于绿色火球观测的分析说明，将其与正常流星雨和真正的陨石坠落进行比较。

**绿色火球特征：** 文件指出，流星雨通常会产生极其明亮的绿色火球，就像最近观测到的那样。引用的例子包括蒙尼格先生（Monnig）在1月初象限仪座流星雨极大期附近的观测（事件231）、麦卡洛先生（McCullough）8月在英仙座流星雨期间的观测（事件290），以及12月的观测（223、223a、224、226、227）落在双子座流星雨覆盖的时间区间内。这种关系**可能表明**有人试图通过使绿色火球仅在流星活动频繁时出现，来降低其显眼程度。

**颜色分析：** 12月大多数火球报告的极其鲜艳的绿色在真正的流星中很少观察到。实验室测试表明，这种流行的颜色与铜盐在吹管火焰中释放的颜色相同。如果这一识别是正确的，绿色火球辐射的波长接近λ = 5216 Å。

**持续时间：** 绿色火球报告的持续时间估计在2到3秒之间，比普通目视流星的持续时间（0.1 - 0.5秒）要长得多，但比真正陨石坠落时报告的持续时间估计（5到30秒甚至更长）要短。

**尾迹效应：** 许多绿色火球似乎有火花尾迹或尘埃云跟随，这与流星火球案例中观察到的行为形成鲜明对比，特别是那些穿透到很低高度的流星火球，12月12日观测到的绿色火球就是在这种高度观测到的。

**注意：** 在新墨西哥州阿拉莫戈多（Alamogordo, N.M.）的霍洛曼空军基地（Holloman AF Base）的询问显示，夜间和周日的研究工作不涉及使用各类报告中描述的任何照明装置或照明弹。

**Incident #:** 232

**Location:** Pomeret, New Jersey, approximately 5 miles NW NW. Observer was at Copster Hill, Pomeret, New Jersey.

**Object Description:** Three unidentified flying objects were observed. The objects were described as aluminum or silvery in color with dark color mixed in. Shape was reported as "Ball Like." The apparent construction was metallic.

**Flight Characteristics:** Objects were observed at an altitude of 1000 feet, traveling at an unspecified speed. Direction of flight was North to South. Time in sight was 1 minute. Distance from observer was not specified.

**Remarks:** The document notes that no further investigation was being made by this office due to the fact that only one person witnessed the phenomena. This is a checklist-style unidentified flying objects report form, standard for the period.

events.title: Tom Rush (pilot) & wife: cigar-shaped object, Jackson, MS (1 Jan 1949)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 233

**Witness:** Mr. Tom Rush, a pilot with Dixie Air Service, Jackson, Mississippi, and his wife (private pilot), signed an unidentified aerial object report for a sighting 2 miles east of Jackson at 1700 C on 1 January 1949 while coming in for a landing at Dixie Airport.

**Object Description:** The object was first described as being cigar-shaped with short stubby wings resembling a rocket. Rush stated in a signed letter that "as the object made its turn, it was then that I noticed the object **without stubby wings.**" The object was thought to be a large tow target, about 60 feet long and about 10 feet in diameter at one end and about 4 feet at the trailing end. The tail even fluttered a foot but there was nothing solid swaying and the object moved at greater speed than tow targets.

**Speed and Maneuvers:** When the object crossed in front of the plane, Rush estimated the speed to be about 200 MPH and stated that the object crossed some 500 feet in front of them. After the turn, the object was within 1,200 feet of the plane. Rush attempted to point out the object to the pilot, but the pilot did not understand and apparently did not see the object. As the object turned to the southwest it accelerated its speed and flew out of sight. Object was seen for some 10-12 seconds. Color was dark blue or black. Speed at first sighting approximately 200 miles per hour, later thought to have accelerated to between 400 to 600 mph.

**Additional Witness:** Object was sighted by the above persons who were passengers in a Stinson civilian aircraft. No photographs were taken since a camera was not available. The Stinson was flying at about 1,800 feet. Investigation of flight schedules of adjacent airfields could throw no light on the incident.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 233

**Witness:** Tom Rush先生，密西西比州杰克逊市Dixie航空服务公司的飞行员，及其妻子（私人飞行员），在1949年1月1日下午5时（中部时间）于杰克逊以东2英里处准备降落Dixie机场时，签署了一份不明飞行物体目击报告。

**Object Description:** 该物体最初被描述为雪茄状，带有短粗的机翼，类似火箭。Rush在一封签名信中陈述："当该物体转弯时，我注意到该物体**没有短粗机翼**。"该物体被认为是一个大型拖靶，长约60英尺，一端直径约10英尺，尾端直径约4英尺。尾部甚至有一英尺的摆动，但没有固体物质在晃动，且该物体移动速度比拖靶快得多。

**Speed and Maneuvers:** 当该物体从飞机前方穿过时，Rush估计速度约为200英里/小时，并表示该物体在他们前方约500英尺处穿过。转弯后，该物体距离飞机约1,200英尺。Rush试图向飞行员指出该物体，但飞行员没有理解，显然没有看到该物体。当该物体向西南方向转弯时，加速飞行并消失在视线中。该物体被观察了约10-12秒。颜色为深蓝色或黑色。首次目击时速度约为每小时200英里，后来被认为加速到每小时400至600英里。

**Additional Witness:** 该物体被上述人员目击，他们当时是Stinson民用飞机的乘客。由于没有相机，未能拍摄照片。该Stinson飞机当时飞行高度约为1,800英尺。对邻近机场航班时刻表的调查未能为该事件提供任何线索。

events.title: Mrs. Elma McDaniel & daughter: very high altitude object, Kentwood, LA (5 Sep 1948)

events.report_summary:
**Incident Summary Sheet No. 177**

**Date and Time:** 5 September 1948 between 3:00 and 3:30 P.M.

**Location:** Kentwood, Louisiana

**Witnesses:** Mrs. Elma McDaniel and her daughter Mildred, observing from ground level.

**Object Description:** The object was not clearly perceived and was described as being at "very high altitude." The witnesses found it "terrific" (likely referring to impressive or remarkable). The object was not seen clearly enough to determine specific characteristics—size, color, shape, number of luminosity, exhaust trail color, manner of disappearance, weather conditions at time of sighting, effect on clouds, and apparent construction are all marked "N/S" (not stated).

**Flight Characteristics:** Direction of flight was westward. The sound made by the object was described as "Unlike any made by known aircraft." An "Unusual sound" was noted as a peculiarity. Time in sight and motion were not recorded.

**Attention:** The incident attracted attention in Tangipahoe, Louisiana (neighboring parish).

**Summary:** The report notes that "Object was not perceived as it was too high and going (over)" indicating the continuation of details on an additional page. The extreme altitude prevented detailed observation of the object's characteristics.
events.report_summary_zh:
**事件摘要表第177号**

**日期和时间：** 1948年9月5日下午3:00至3:30之间

**地点：** Kentwood（肯特伍德），Louisiana（路易斯安那州）

**目击者：** Elma McDaniel夫人和她的女儿Mildred，从地面观察。

**物体描述：** 该物体未被清楚地观察到，被描述为处于"非常高的高度"。目击者认为它"很惊人"（likely referring to impressive or remarkable，可能指令人印象深刻或非凡）。该物体未被看清到足以确定具体特征——大小、颜色、形状、数量或亮度、尾迹颜色、消失方式、目击时的天气状况、对云层的影响以及明显的构造都标注为"N/S"（未说明）。

**飞行特征：** 飞行方向为向西。该物体发出的声音被描述为"不同于任何已知飞行器发出的声音"。一个"不寻常的声音"被记录为特殊之处。可见时间和运动情况未被记录。

**关注情况：** 该事件在Louisiana（路易斯安那州）Tangipahoe（坦吉帕霍，邻近教区）引起了关注。

**总结：** 报告指出"物体未被观察清楚，因为它太高并且正在（飞越）"，表明详细信息在附加页面上继续。极高的高度使得无法详细观察该物体的特征。

events.title: Incident 185: Fiery object with smoke trail, Minneapolis, MN (20 Oct 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 185

**Location:** Object sighted from 13th and Lake Street, Minneapolis at 4th & 7th Street and 4th Ave., Minneapolis.

**Witnesses:** Lawrence A. Hansen, teletype operator and Harold Oliver, mailman. Both witnesses submitted stories that conform in the object description throughout.

**Time:** Approximately 0550 hours (5:50 AM) on 20 October 1948.

**Object Description:** The object appeared blurred as if enveloped in smoke. The rear of the main body was a fiery orange color. The tail appeared to be boiling sheets of flame which carried on back at variable distances and broke off, dropping vertically for a short distance before becoming indistinguishable.

**Behavior:** The object was last seen by both witnesses entering the cloud bank to the north-northeast and disappearing.

**Document Type:** Brief incident report summarizing a UFO sighting in Minneapolis with multiple corroborating witnesses describing a fiery, smoke-trailing object in the early morning hours.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 185

**Location:** 物体目击地点为明尼阿波利斯第13街与湖街交叉口，物体位于明尼阿波利斯第4街与第7街交叉口及第4大道上空。

**Witnesses:** Lawrence A. Hansen，电传打字员，以及Harold Oliver，邮递员。两位目击者提交的陈述在物体描述方面完全一致。

**Time:** 1948年10月20日约0550时（上午5时50分）。

**Object Description:** 物体看起来模糊不清，仿佛笼罩在烟雾中。主体后部呈火橙色。尾部看起来像沸腾的火焰片，向后延伸的距离不定，并不断脱落，垂直下降一小段距离后变得无法辨认。

**Behavior:** 两位目击者最后看到该物体进入北-东北方向的云层并消失。

**Document Type:** 简要事件报告，总结了一起发生在明尼阿波利斯的UFO目击事件，有多名互相印证的目击者在清晨描述了一个冒火并拖着烟迹的物体。

events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 186

**Date and Time:** 16 October 1948, 1145 in the morning

**Location:** 1 mile south and 6 miles due east of Sterling, Utah. Observer's position was ground-based, from a mountain ridge at 9,000 feet elevation.

**Witness:** Mr. Fred Nash, 20 East Crystal, Salt Lake City, Utah. Occupation: Used car dealer and airplane mechanic. Member of Latter Day Saints Church (engaged in missionary work in Hawaii).

**Object Description:** The object was 9 inches long, 6 inches wide, and 3 inches thick. Color described as silver and black, with a silver stripe running down the center of the underside (see drawing referenced). Shape similar to a flat football.

**Flight Characteristics:** Estimated altitude 500 feet overhead. Estimated distance from observer 500 feet. Estimated speed 300 mph. Time in sight: 4 seconds or longer. Tactics: horizontal flight. Direction of flight: north and a little west (in general direction of Salt Lake City, Utah).

**Sound and Luminosity:** Object produced a throbbing noise or steady purr. Nature of luminosity: N/S (not stated or none observed). No visible exhaust trail; however, an opening could be seen in the center of the object from the rear.

**Weather Conditions:** Calm with no clouds in the sky at time of sighting.

**Attention Attracted By:** Sound of throbbing noise.

**Document Note:** Summary of incident continues on attached page (not shown).
events.report_summary_zh:

**Object Description:** 该物体长9英寸，宽6英寸，厚3英寸。颜色描述为银色和黑色，底部中央有一条银色条纹(见参考图示)。形状类似扁平的橄榄球。

**Flight Characteristics:** 估计高度为头顶上方500英尺。估计距观察者500英尺。估计速度300英里/小时。可见时间：4秒或更长。飞行策略：水平飞行。飞行方向：向北并略微偏西(大致朝向犹他州盐湖城方向)。

**Sound and Luminosity:** 物体发出脉动噪音或稳定的呼呼声。发光性质：N/S(未说明或未观察到)。无可见尾迹；但从后方可以看到物体中心有一个开口。

events.title: Unidentified flying object, Godman AFB, Kentucky (19 Aug 1948) - Incident 187
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 187

**Date & Time:** At 1050E on 19 August 1948, the Wright-Patterson Flight Service Center was notified by Lt Col John Waugh, Executive Officer at Godman Air Force Base, Kentucky, that an unidentified flying object was visible from the ground at Godman AFB.

**Object Description:** The object was ascertained to be at approximately 30,000 to 40,000 feet altitude, spherical in shape, bright silver color, and giving off a bright reflection from the sun.

**Investigation:** An F-51 was dispatched from Standiford AFB, Kentucky, to observe the object. At 1132E a message was received from Godman AFB stating that an elevation of the object due to sun reflection had changed, and reporting it seemed to be moving southwest from Godman AFB at approximately 232° at an elevation of 45° from Godman AFB. The F-51 was flying at 30,000 to 35,000 feet at the time and could not locate the object. However, the object was visible from the ground with the naked eye and azimuth and elevation readings were being taken by theodolite every minute, with the progress of the object being charted.

**Identification:** At 1219E on 19 August 1948, Major Blackwell, Operations Officer at Godman AFB, notified Wright-Patterson Flight Service Center that the unidentified object was ascertained to be the planet Venus. This information was given by the Commanding Officer at Godman AFB by Mr Moore, Head Astrologer at University of Louisville, Kentucky. This assumption was verified by MCI later the same day.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 187

**Date & Time:** 1948年8月19日1050E时，赖特-帕特森飞行服务中心接到肯塔基州戈德曼空军基地执行官约翰·沃中校的通知，称从戈德曼AFB地面可见一个不明飞行物。

**Object Description:** 经确定，该物体位于约30,000至40,000英尺高度，呈球形，明亮的银色，反射着太阳的强烈光芒。

**Investigation:** 一架F-51战斗机从肯塔基州斯坦迪福德AFB起飞以观察该物体。1132E时收到来自戈德曼AFB的消息，称该物体因太阳反射而改变了仰角，报告显示它似乎正以约232°方向从戈德曼AFB向西南方向移动,相对戈德曼AFB的仰角为45°。F-51当时在30,000至35,000英尺高度飞行,未能定位该物体。然而,该物体可从地面用肉眼看到,并且每分钟用经纬仪测量方位角和仰角读数,绘制该物体的运动轨迹。

**Identification:** 1948年8月19日1219E时,戈德曼AFB作战军官布莱克威尔少校通知赖特-帕特森飞行服务中心,经确定该不明物体为金星。此信息由肯塔基州路易斯维尔大学(University of Louisville, Kentucky)首席天文学家摩尔先生提供给戈德曼AFB指挥官。该结论于当日晚些时候得到MCI的证实。

events.title: Capt Glenn Baber: metallic object faster than aircraft, Junction City, KS
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident:** 191

**Date and Time:** At 1545 CST on 24 October 1948

**Witness:** Capt Glenn Baber, Base S-3 Officer, Ft Riley, Kansas

**Sighting:** Captain Baber sighted an unidentified metallic object proceeding in a general westerly direction. The object was viewed from a ground position 10 miles from Junction City, Kansas. Altitude appeared over 20,000 ft and it was traveling with the speed of a fast aircraft. It then turned north at a speed greater than any aircraft he had ever seen. Visibility was excellent. Wind south-southwest.

**Object Characteristics:** Described as metallic and moving at extraordinary speed, faster than any known aircraft. The object executed a turn to the north while maintaining its high velocity.

**Observer Credibility:** Military officer serving as Base S-3 Officer at Fort Riley, providing operational and planning expertise, suggesting trained observer capability.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident:** 191

**Date and Time:** 1948年10月24日中部标准时间1545时

**Witness:** 格伦·贝伯上尉(Capt Glenn Baber)，堪萨斯州莱利堡(Fort Riley, Kansas)基地S-3军官

**Sighting:** 贝伯上尉目击到一个不明金属物体，大致朝西方向行进。该物体是从距离堪萨斯州章克申城(Junction City, Kansas)10英里的地面位置观察到的。高度似乎超过20,000英尺，以快速飞行器的速度飞行。随后它转向北方，速度超过了他见过的任何飞行器。能见度极佳。风向西南偏南。

**Object Characteristics:** 描述为金属质地，以超常速度移动，快于任何已知飞行器。该物体在保持高速的同时完成了向北的转向。

**Observer Credibility:** 军官，在莱利堡担任基地S-3军官，负责作战和规划工作，表明其具备训练有素的观察能力。

events.title: Radarscope operator: 2 aircraft circling, Wakkanai, Japan (6 Nov 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident No:** 198

**Date and Time:** 6 November 1948, 1157 hours

**Location:** Immediately above radar site at Wakkanai, Japan

**Observer:** Ground-based radarscope operator (name and address listed as N/S). Observer's position was on the ground operating radarscope equipment at the radar site, including control tower.

**Occupation:** Radarscope operator

**Object Details:** Target initially appeared as a single craft on radarscope, then registered as 2 aircraft. The objects were described as normal for aircraft on radarscope. The object(s) were not observed visually at any time. Color, shape, nature of luminosity, and altitude are all listed as N/S (not stated) or unknown.

**Behavior:** The targets gave the impression of 2 fighter aircraft engaged in dog-fighting, continuously changing course in a circling pattern. Estimated speed varied from 160 miles to 240 miles per hour. The objects remained in sight on the radarscope continuously for one hour and 5 minutes.

**Weather Conditions:** Low and high cloud formation, forming very dense overcast at medium height.

**Additional Notes:** The radarscope operator's attention was attracted by a blip on the radarscope. At times the targets appeared single and at times gave appearance of 2 aircraft in vicinity. Sound made by objects and effect on clouds are listed as N/S. Exhaust trail color and number of passengers are also N/S. Direction of flight was circling. Apparent construction and estimated distance from observer could not be determined.

**Document Type:** Ancient Bakery Sheet incident report form (see attached page reference)
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident No:** 198

**Date and Time:** 1948年11月6日，1157时

**Location:** 日本稚内(Wakkanai)雷达站正上方

**Observer:** 地面雷达显示器操作员(姓名和地址列为N/S)。观察者位置为雷达站地面，操作雷达显示器设备，包括控制塔。

**Occupation:** 雷达显示器操作员

**Object Details:** 目标最初在雷达显示器上显示为单个飞行器，随后记录为2架飞机。这些物体在雷达显示器上显示为正常飞机特征。该物体在任何时候都未被目视观察到。颜色、形状、发光性质和高度均列为N/S(未说明)或未知。

**Behavior:** 目标给人的印象是2架战斗机正在进行空中格斗，以环形模式持续改变航向。估计速度从每小时160英里到240英里不等。这些物体在雷达显示器上持续可见时间为1小时5分钟。

**Weather Conditions:** 低云层和高云层形成，在中等高度形成非常浓密的阴天。

**Additional Notes:** 雷达显示器操作员的注意力被雷达显示器上的一个光点所吸引。目标有时显示为单个，有时显示为附近区域的2架飞机。物体发出的声音和对云层的影响列为N/S。尾气轨迹颜色和乘客数量也为N/S。飞行方向为环绕飞行。无法确定明显的构造和与观察者的估计距离。

**Document Type:** Ancient Bakery Sheet事件报告表格(见附页参考)

events.title: Two Air Force officers observe white object near Clark AF Base (17 Nov 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 208

**Date and Time:** 17 November 1948, 1430 hours

**Location:** Clark Air Force Base, Philippines - observed at stern edge of base

**Witnesses:** 1st Lt. Kenneth L. Chandler and 1st Lt. Max H. Fetholman, both pilots with the 4th Fighter Squadron (3rd) 18th Fighter Group (3d) 5th AF 74, U.S. Army. Observer position: ground.

**Object Description:** White in color, with an irregular mass appearance - described as looking "as if plane had exploded and left a white smoke column." Shape sketched as irregular if possible. Size and nature of luminosity both listed as "N/S" (not specified).

**Altitude and Distance:** Estimated altitude of 30,000 feet. Estimated distance from observer: 30,000 feet. Estimated speed of object: N/S.

**Duration:** Approximately 3 minutes with smoke trail visible.

**Object Behavior:** Object appeared to make a loop inasmuch as the smoke trail performed complete circle resembling a corkscrew. Direction of flight: Either 120° or 300° according to origin. Object appeared like burst of flak.

**Environmental Conditions:** Weather conditions at time of sighting: none - visibility was a cloudless sky. White exhaust trail extended some 1 to 10 miles. Manner of disappearance: trail evaporated after three minutes like smoke, scattering thinly throughout the atmosphere.

**Additional Notes:** Weather conditions at time of sighting show 1000 feet scattered clouds with visibility 50 miles and high overcast. The object had the peculiar appearance of flak burst sitting still in the atmosphere and connected to a curved trail of corkscrew appearance. Summary characterizes this as having "the appearance of a vapor trail."
events.report_summary_zh:
**Incident No.:** 208

**Date and Time:** 1948年11月17日，1430时

**Location:** 克拉克空军基地(Clark Air Force Base)，菲律宾 - 在基地后缘边界观测到

**Witnesses:** 肯尼斯·L·钱德勒一级中尉(1st Lt. Kenneth L. Chandler)和马克斯·H·费索尔曼一级中尉(1st Lt. Max H. Fetholman)，两人均为美国陆军第5航空队第18战斗机大队(第3)第4战斗机中队(第3)的飞行员。观察者位置：地面。

**Object Description:** 白色，呈不规则块状外观 - 描述为"看起来像飞机爆炸后留下的白色烟柱"。如有可能，形状草图绘制为不规则状。大小和发光性质均列为"N/S"(未说明)。

**Altitude and Distance:** 估计高度30,000英尺。距观察者估计距离：30,000英尺。物体估计速度：N/S。

**Duration:** 约3分钟，烟迹可见。

**Object Behavior:** 物体似乎做了一个环形运动，因为烟迹形成了完整的圆圈，类似螺旋开瓶器状。飞行方向：根据起源点，方位角为120°或300°。物体看起来像高射炮爆炸。

**Environmental Conditions:** 目击时的天气状况：无 - 能见度为无云晴空。白色尾迹延伸约1至10英里。消失方式：尾迹在三分钟后像烟雾一样蒸发，在大气中稀疏散开。

**Additional Notes:** 目击时的天气状况显示1000英尺处有零星云层，能见度50英里，高空多云。该物体具有特殊的外观，像高射炮爆炸后静止悬浮在大气中，并连接着一条弯曲的螺旋开瓶器状尾迹。总结将其描述为"具有凝结尾迹的外观"。

**Location:** North of Fairfield-Suisun Air Force Base, California

**Observer:** Control tower personnel at Fairfield-Suisun AF Base, observing from control tower using 8-power binoculars (ground, air, control tower position)

**Object Description:** Single object, 1 to 2 feet in diameter, bright light, circular shape. Color described as "bright light." Luminosity similar to a ramp flood light (directed beam of light). Apparent construction similar to a ramp floodlight.

**Behavior and Flight Characteristics:** Object began rapid climb but with erratic movement, described as "like change to pace." When first sighted at altitude of 1 to 2,000 feet, it climbed to estimated 20,000 feet. Direction of flight was toward southeast. Estimated speed: 400 to 500 MPH. No sound heard during observation.

**Observational Details:** Attention attracted by N/S (not specified). Time in sight: N/S. No exhaust trail observed. Effect on clouds: N/S. Manner of disappearance: N/S.

**Weather Conditions:** 15 miles visibility, wind west at 5 mph at time of sighting.

**Peculiarities Noted:** Intensity of the light was specifically remarked upon.

**Document Type:** This is an Incident Summary Sheet, a standardized USAF reporting form for unidentified aerial objects. A summary of the incident is noted as attached on a separate page (not shown).

events.location: 40 miles northwest of Martinsburg, West Virginia
events.title: AF 7974 crew: brilliant red flare object, 40 miles NW of Martinsburg, WV
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Pilot and crew of Air Force aircraft AF 7974.

**Sighting:** Approximately 40 miles northwest of Martinsburg, West Virginia, the crew sighted a brilliant red flare at an altitude of approximately 10,000 to 11,000 feet. The object appeared approximately 20 miles in front of the aircraft, which was on a heading of 125°. The shape of the object appeared similar to a parachute flare.

**Object:** The object's color was variable, changing from red to blue to red. It appeared to be stationary throughout the observation. No sound was heard and no exhaust trail was noticed. The flare lasted approximately 1 minute.

**Note:** No opinion was formed by any member of the crew as to the identity of the object. This incident is labeled as number 215 in what appears to be a series of UFO reports. The brief nature of the sighting (one minute duration) and the parachute flare-like appearance suggest a possible conventional explanation, though the crew did not confirm the object's identity.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 空军飞机AF 7974的飞行员和机组人员。

**Sighting:** 在西弗吉尼亚州马丁斯堡(Martinsburg, West Virginia)西北约40英里处,机组人员在大约10,000至11,000英尺的高度目击到一个明亮的红色火焰。该物体出现在飞机前方约20英里处,飞机当时的航向为125°。该物体的形状类似降落伞照明弹。

**Object:** 该物体的颜色会变化,从红色变为蓝色再变回红色。在整个观察过程中,它似乎是静止的。没有听到声音,也没有注意到尾气痕迹。火焰持续了大约1分钟。

**Note:** 机组成员中没有任何人对该物体的身份形成意见。此事件在一系列UFO报告中被标记为215号。考虑到目击时间较短(持续1分钟)以及类似降落伞照明弹的外观,这暗示可能存在常规解释,尽管机组人员并未确认该物体的身份。

events.title: Science teacher observes yellow light flash, San Francisco, CA (29 Nov 1948)
events.record_description: Each of these incident summaries includes a "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" that contains details about the incident. Many summaries also include witness lists or statements and other narrative reports or descriptions.
events.report_summary:
**Incident No.:** 220

**Date and Time:** 29 November 1948 at 2113 hours (9:13 PM)

**Location:** San Francisco, California

**Witness:** Mr. Robert Thatcher, 1729 38th Avenue, San Francisco, California. Occupation: Science Teacher at Francisco Junior High School. Observer's position was ground-based.

**Object Description:** A single yellow light described as a "flash of light" that flashed across the sky. Color was yellow. The object appeared as a flash of light rather than a solid craft.

**Observation Details:** The sighting lasted approximately 7 seconds. The object's initial heading was north, then turned to a north-northwest direction. Direction of flight was North Northwest. The witness described the object's attention-attracting feature as "yellow light flashing across the sky."

**Speed and Distance:** Estimated speed was noted as "too fast for plane." Distance from observer could not be estimated (marked N/S). Altitude also could not be estimated.

**Additional Notes:** No sound was made by the object. No exhaust trail color was observed - just a flash of light. No effect on clouds noted. Weather conditions at time of sighting were not specified. The witness noted the extreme speed was "too fast for plane but did not think it was a comet or shooting star."

**Apparent Construction:** Flash of light

**Document Status:** Under investigation. Summary of incident noted as attached on separate page.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Observation Details:** 目击持续时间约7秒。物体初始航向为北,随后转向北-西北方向。飞行方向为北西北。目击者描述该物体的引人注意特征为"黄色光芒划过天空"。

**Apparent Construction:** 闪光

**Document Status:** 调查中。事件摘要已附在单独页面上。

events.report_summary:
**Document Type:**
This is a blank INCIDENT SUMMARY SHEET template form (Incident No. 221) for documenting UFO sightings. The form indicates the sighting location as Midland, Michigan, with observer position noted as "Case under investigation."

**Form Structure:**
The standardized form contains 25 fields for systematic UFO incident documentation:

**Observation Details (Fields 1-7):** Date/time of observation, location sighted (Midland, Michigan), observer's position (ground, air, control tower, etc.), name and address of observer, occupation and/or hobbies, attention attracted by, and number of object(s) seen.

**Object Characteristics (Fields 8-14):** Size of object(s), color, shape (with space for sketch if possible), nature of luminosity (directed beam of light), altitude (estimated), estimated distance from observer, and estimated speed of object.

**Behavioral Data (Fields 15-20):** Time in sight, tactics, sound made by object(s), direction of flight, apparent construction, and effect on clouds.

**Additional Information (Fields 21-25):** Exhaust trail color, manner of disappearance, weather conditions at time of sighting, peculiarities noted, and summary of incident (see attached page).

**Status:**
This blank form was marked "Case under investigation" but contains no completed data fields. It represents the standardized documentation protocol used for UFO incident reporting during this period.
events.report_summary_zh:

**物体特征(字段8-14):** 物体尺寸、颜色、形状(如可能请附草图)、发光性质(定向光束)、高度(估计值)、与观察者的估计距离、物体估计速度。

events.title: Incident 173: Adams observes aluminum object near Shreveport LA (15 Sep 1948)
events.record_description: USAF Project SIGN/GRUDGE Incident Summary Sheet — declassified Box 7 file.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** George Adams of 256 Columbia Ave., Shreveport, Louisiana, observed an object from the ground 3 miles SE of Shreveport on 15 September 1948 at 1700 Central Standard Time. He was scanning the sky with binoculars when he detected the object.

**Object:** The object appeared aluminum in color and metallic in construction, with an estimated diameter of approximately 12 feet. Adams observed it at an angle of 40-60° above the horizon (the form gives conflicting values of 50° and 40-60°), at an estimated altitude of 20,000 feet and lateral distance of 2.5 miles. The object made no sound and left no exhaust trail.

**Sighting:** The object remained in sight for 10-15 seconds as it traveled southward in smooth horizontal flight at an estimated speed of 100-150 mph. Weather conditions were excellent: 1/10 cumulus clouds at 5,500 feet, visibility 15 miles, and winds of 20 mph at 20,000 feet.

**Tactics:** The object maintained smooth, level flight in a southerly direction with no unusual maneuvers.

**Note:** The investigating agent noted that a radiosonde (weather balloon) was released from Barksdale Field at 1600 CST, 15 minutes before Adams' sighting at 1700 CST. The radiosonde was similar in size to the reported object, at 15-18 feet at 20,000 feet altitude. The agent concluded it was possible that the radiosonde was the object Adams observed.
events.title_ocr_original: Incident 173: 1700 Central Standard Time 3 miles SE of Shreveport, La (1948-09-15)
events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 乔治·亚当斯(George Adams),住址为路易斯安那州什里夫波特(Shreveport, Louisiana)哥伦比亚大道256号,于1948年9月15日中部标准时间1700时在什里夫波特东南3英里处从地面观测到一个物体。他当时正在用双筒望远镜扫视天空时发现了该物体。

**Object:** 该物体呈铝色,具有金属结构特征,估计直径约12英尺。亚当斯观测到它位于地平线上方40-60°角(表格给出了50°和40-60°两个相互矛盾的数值),估计高度为20,000英尺,横向距离为2.5英里。该物体没有发出声音,也没有留下尾迹。

**Sighting:** 该物体在视野中停留了10-15秒,以平稳的水平飞行方式向南移动,估计速度为每小时100-150英里。天气条件极佳:5,500英尺高度处有1/10积云,可见度15英里,20,000英尺高度处风速为每小时20英里。

**Tactics:** 该物体保持平稳的水平飞行,朝南方向移动,没有异常机动动作。

**Note:** 调查人员注意到,中部标准时间1600时从巴克斯代尔机场(Barksdale Field)释放了一个无线电探空仪(气象气球),这比亚当斯在中部标准时间1700时的目击早15分钟。该无线电探空仪的尺寸与报告的物体相似,在20,000英尺高度时为15-18英尺。调查人员得出结论认为,亚当斯观测到的物体有可能就是该无线电探空仪。

events.title: Incident 178: Maj Drum observes silver disc near Honolulu HI (18 Oct 1948)
events.record_description: USAF Project SIGN/GRUDGE Incident Summary Sheet — declassified Box 7 file.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Maj. Robert C. Drum, USAF rated pilot, observing from his residence at 2737 Pacific Heights Road, Honolulu, Hawaii. The sighting was corroborated by Mrs. Drum (his wife) and their 8-year-old daughter.

**Sighting:** On 18 October 1948 at approximately 1705-1715 HST (Hawaiian Standard Time), the witnesses observed a bright silver object moving in a northeasterly direction. The object was seen intermittently four times over a 10-minute period, with the longest single observation lasting 10 seconds and another lasting 4 seconds. Due to broken cumulus clouds moving in a southwesterly direction at low altitude, the observer could not determine whether he saw the same disc four times or four different discs.

**Object:** The object appeared bright silver in color, comparable to aluminum aircraft skin, and was circular or elliptical in shape. From the observer's viewpoint, it appeared 4-5 inches in diameter; actual size was estimated at 10-15 feet in diameter. The object was observed at an estimated altitude between 10,000 and 14,000 feet, flying horizontally between two cloud layers (below stratus at 14,000 feet, above cumulus at 3,500 feet). Maj. Drum compared it to a silver dollar held at arm's length at a 45° angle, slightly turned from flat, suggesting the elliptical appearance might have resulted from viewing angle. No vapor trail, exhaust, flame, lights, or sound were observed. The object appeared metallic in construction.

**Tactics:** The object maintained steady horizontal flight on a northeast course at an estimated speed of 200 MPH. Speed was calculated using an estimated 40 MPH factor for the swirling build-up of cumulus clouds as reference. No maneuvering was observed.

**Note:** Maj. Drum stated with certainty that the object was not conventional aircraft. Weather conditions included high broken clouds at 3,500 feet, 3/10 cumulus with bases at 3,500 feet, 2/10 alto cumulus at 14,000 feet, and 5/10 cirrus estimated at 30,000 feet, with visibility of 15 miles. One B-26, one B-17, and one PBM5 were flying in the vicinity during the period 0230Z to 0330Z (approximately 1630-1730 HST).
events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** Robert C. Drum少校，美国空军(USAF)认证飞行员，在其位于夏威夷檀香山太平洋高地路2737号的住所进行观察。目击得到了Drum夫人（其妻子）和他们8岁女儿的证实。

**Sighting:** 1948年10月18日约1705-1715 HST（夏威夷标准时间），目击者观察到一个明亮的银色物体向东北方向移动。该物体在10分钟内断断续续被看到四次，其中最长的单次观察持续10秒，另一次持续4秒。由于低空有碎积云向西南方向移动，观察者无法确定他看到的是同一个圆盘四次还是四个不同的圆盘。

**Object:** 该物体呈现明亮的银色，类似铝制飞机蒙皮，形状为圆形或椭圆形。从观察者的视角看，它直径约4-5英寸；实际尺寸估计直径为10-15英尺。该物体在估计海拔10,000至14,000英尺之间被观察到，在两个云层之间水平飞行（低于14,000英尺的层云，高于3,500英尺的积云）。Drum少校将其比作手臂伸直时呈45°角持握的银币，略微偏离平面，表明椭圆形外观可能是由观察角度造成的。未观察到蒸汽尾迹、排气、火焰、灯光或声音。该物体看起来为金属构造。

**Tactics:** 该物体以估计200 MPH的速度在东北航向上保持稳定的水平飞行。速度是使用积云旋转堆积的估计40 MPH因子作为参照计算得出的。未观察到机动动作。

**Note:** Drum少校确定地表示该物体不是常规飞机。天气状况包括3,500英尺高空有碎云，3,500英尺处有3/10积云，14,000英尺处有2/10高积云，估计30,000英尺处有5/10卷云，能见度为15英里。在0230Z至0330Z期间（约1630-1730 HST），附近有一架B-26、一架B-17和一架PBM5在飞行。

events.title: Incident 179: Pruitt observes mysterious light in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco CA (Oct 1947)
events.record_description: USAF Project SIGN/GRUDGE Incident Summary Sheet — declassified Box 7 file.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** John E. Pruitt, a student at Maj Rockwell School of Aviation, reported an incident from around October 1947. The observer was walking through Golden Gate Park, approximately half a mile from the Great Highway and playgrounds.

**Sighting:** While in the park, Pruitt observed a mysterious light that appeared to illuminate the entire ocean as far as he could see. He felt something described as "like an electric arc" which seemed to have the power to lower his hand "like a sack of shot." The light appeared so close that he felt he could "reach out and touch it." The object appeared to fade. Time in sight, speed, direction, and other specifics were not stated.

**Object:** Details of size, color, shape, luminosity, and apparent construction were not provided beyond the description of a "mysterious light." No sound, exhaust trail, or distinctive flight characteristics were reported.

**Physical Effect:** The witness claimed that where the phenomenon seemed to contact him, he noticed a bruise the following day that had not been present before. He stated he is subject to bruising.

**Note:** The witness delayed reporting for fear of not being believed and did not wish further investigation. Project evaluators assessed the account as "very incoherent" and noted the observer was "apparently not well educated," deeming it "an extremely unreliable account."
events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** John E. Pruitt，罗克韦尔少校航空学校的一名学生，报告了1947年10月左右发生的一起事件。目击者当时正在金门公园(Golden Gate Park)内行走，距离大公路(Great Highway)和游乐场约半英里处。

**Sighting:** 在公园内时，Pruitt观察到一道神秘的光，似乎照亮了他视线所及的整个海面。他感觉到某种被描述为"像电弧一样"的东西，似乎有力量将他的手"像一袋铅弹一样"压低。那道光显得如此接近，以至于他觉得自己"伸手就能触碰到它"。该物体似乎逐渐消失了。目击时长、速度、方向和其他具体细节均未说明。

**Object:** 除了描述为"神秘的光"之外，未提供关于大小、颜色、形状、亮度和明显构造的详细信息。未报告任何声音、尾迹或独特的飞行特征。

**Physical Effect:** 目击者声称，在该现象似乎接触他的地方，他在第二天注意到一处之前没有的瘀伤。他表示自己容易出现瘀伤。

**Note:** 目击者因担心不被相信而推迟了报告，且不希望进一步调查。项目评估人员认为该陈述"非常不连贯"，并指出观察者"显然受教育程度不高"，认为这是"一份极不可靠的报告"。

events.title: Incident 181: Maj Smartt reports teardrop objects from C-47 near Dayton OH (4 Oct 1948)
events.record_description: USAF Project SIGN/GRUDGE Incident Summary Sheet — declassified Box 7 file.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Maj. C. M. Smartt, pilot and ordnance officer with the 2349 AF Ordnance at Hamilton Air Force Base. He and his co-pilot were flying a C-47 transport at 6,000 feet near Dayton, Ohio, on 4 October 1948 at approximately 1430 hours local time.

**Sighting:** Smartt reported observing three or four (initially reported as 15 to 20) silvery white, metallic, teardrop-shaped objects, each approximately 1.5 feet long and 9 inches across. The objects appeared one at a time at intervals of three or four minutes. Visibility was hazy at 15 miles. His attention was drawn to the objects when some came close enough that he and his co-pilot had to duck to avoid what appeared to be an impending collision through the aircraft nose.

**Object:** The objects were described as silver or silvery white teardrops with metallic appearance. They showed a slight tail but no evidence of exhaust. Each object remained in view for only about one second due to their apparent high speed.

**Tactics:** The objects traveled in a straight line in a general easterly direction with a gradual descent, passing from view under the wing of the C-47. No sound was noticed. Smartt compared the sighting to dumping half a gallon of water 200 yards in front of an approaching aircraft about 200 feet above it, with the water taking teardrop shape.

**Note:** Significant discrepancies were noted in Smartt's reports. His first report claimed 15-20 objects, while his later account reduced this to three or four. Initially he stated some objects traveled upward and some downward with no definite course; later he omitted any mention of upward movement. The water-dump analogy suggests a simultaneous group sighting rather than objects appearing singly at intervals, creating ambiguity about what was actually observed.
events.title_ocr_original: Incident 181: Approx 1430 hours local time Near Dayton, Ohio (1948-10-04)
events.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** C. M. Smartt少校，汉密尔顿空军基地(Hamilton Air Force Base)第2349航空军械部队的飞行员兼军械官。1948年10月4日当地时间约1430时，他和副驾驶员驾驶一架C-47运输机在俄亥俄州代顿(Dayton, Ohio)附近6,000英尺高度飞行。

**Sighting:** Smartt报告观察到三或四个（最初报告为15至20个）银白色金属质感的泪滴形物体，每个约1.5英尺长、9英寸宽。这些物体以三到四分钟的间隔逐个出现。当时能见度为15英里，天气朦胧。他注意到这些物体是因为有些物体靠得太近，以至于他和副驾驶员不得不低头躲避看似即将通过机头发生的碰撞。

**Object:** 这些物体被描述为银色或银白色泪滴状，具有金属外观。它们显示出轻微的尾部，但没有排气迹象。由于明显的高速运动，每个物体在视野中仅停留约一秒钟。

**Tactics:** 这些物体沿直线向大致东方移动并逐渐下降，从C-47机翼下方消失在视野中。未注意到任何声音。Smartt将此次目击比作在接近中的飞机前方200码、上方约200英尺处倾倒半加仑水，水呈泪滴状。

**Note:** Smartt的报告中存在明显差异。他的第一份报告声称有15-20个物体，而后来的陈述将数量减少到三或四个。最初他表示一些物体向上移动、一些向下移动且无明确路线；后来他省略了任何关于向上移动的提及。倾倒水的类比暗示的是同时出现的群体目击而非间隔单独出现的物体，这给实际观察到的情况造成了模糊性。

events.title: Incident 183: F-61 radar chase of evasive object near Fukuoka, Japan (15 Oct 1948)
events.record_description: USAF Project SIGN/GRUDGE Incident Summary Sheet — declassified Box 7 file.
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** An F-61 pilot and radar observer operating out of the Fukuoka area conducted multiple intercept attempts of an unidentified aircraft on the night of 15 October 1948. The interception zone spanned the area between Shigamo Shima (33°40'N, 132°00'E) and Fukue Suima (32°45'N, 128°40'E). Sufficient moonlight permitted visual silhouette identification, though no details could be discerned.

**Sighting:** The crew encountered the object(s) six times over the course of the mission, continuing search operations until approximately 0130 hours.
