events.report_summary:
**Document:** Letter from Maxwell Flight Service Center, Maxwell AF Base, AL dated 2 Jan 49, Subject: Unidentified Flying Objects. This is page 2 of a multi-page report (pages 1 and 3+ not shown).

**Sighting:** Object first sighted and reported to Flight Service at Maxwell AF Base at 1735 hours by the Jackson Operations Office. Initial heading was west when first sighted, then changed to southwest when last observed.

**Object Description:** (1) Number: One. (2) Shape: Cigar-shaped with short stubby wings, resembling a rocket; also later reported as resembling a sleeve tow-target. (3) Size: Estimated sixty (60) feet long. (4) Color: Dark blue or black. (5) Speed: Initially estimated as 200 mph, then increasing to 5-600 mph. (6) Maneuverability: Apparently very maneuverable. (7) Altitude: 1500 feet. (8) Sound: Similar to a helicopter. (9) Exhaust trail: None visible.

**Investigation:** Upon receiving the report, an attempt was made to investigate the object by calling all military airfields in the area from which a jet or rocket flight may have originated, or at which the object may have been sighted.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** SECRET report dated 9 December 1948 from Detachment No. 1, 16th Weather Squadron, Chanute Air Force Base, Illinois, reporting information on "Flying Discs" in compliance with 212th Air Weather Group TWX 454 dated 19 November 1948 and letter from Headquarters, United States Air Force of 6 February 1948. File code: WDOUS2. The document is marked SECRET with stamp "5/8/4" and addressed to Commanding General, Air Materiel Command, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Dayton, Ohio.

**Witnesses:** Sgt. James L. Doty and Sgt. Marcus E. Montag, Weather Observers, Det No 1, 16th Weather Squadron, Chanute AFB, Illinois.

**Observation Conditions:** High scattered clouds with visibility of ten miles reported at time of sighting.

**Object Characteristics:** (1) One object sighted; (2) Round shaped; (3) Undetermined size; (4) Bright white color; (5) Two tenths of distant sky covered within two to three seconds; (6) Heading from north east toward south south west; (7) Undetermined maneuverability; (8) Undetermined altitude; (9) No sound; (10) Exhaust trail undetermined.

**General Remarks:** Object sighted to north east moving to south south west resembled a skyrocket or meteor but was moving upward fifteen degrees. Object was described as being about thirty-five degrees above the horizon and traversed across thirty-five degrees of the horizon within three seconds and disappeared.

**Evidence:** No photographs or sketches of objects available.

Capt. George P. Brenner, USAF, Commanding officer, submitted this observation report.

**Sighting:**
The object was sighted during the first leg of a flight from Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, to Kittigazuit, Northwest Territories, Canada. The observation occurred while flying at 7,000 feet MSL on top of an overcast layer. The object was momentarily sighted above a deck of broken status clouds.

**Object:**
The object appeared to be a bright flaming orange object that illuminated the sky momentarily behind it. The witness described it as appearing to be in a shallow dive at the time of observation. The object was at an altitude of approximately 15,000 feet. No sound was reported. The object left an exhaust trail behind it. The maneuverability was described as appearing to be in a shallow dive.

**Document:**
This is page 2 of a "SUBJs Observation of an Object in the Atmosphere" report. The document is stamped "SECRET" at the bottom. It was distributed to Hdqrs.MATS Attn: Dir.of Intelligence (checked) and Cmdr.MATS Attn: Chief, Intelligence Division. The report uses a structured format with numbered items covering maneuverability (7), altitude (8), sound (9), and exhaust trail (10). The document demonstrates official USAF intelligence interest in atmospheric phenomena during this period.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Newark Division Office Memorandum from SAC Newark to the Director, FBI, dated August 13, 1947, titled “Flying Disc Reported at Hackensack, New Jersey, August 3, 1947 – Miscellaneous.” The two rendered pages are consecutive and belong to the same report, continuing from the first page into a second-page letter to Bureau. The text is signed/attributed in narrative form to Special Agents Arthur F. Williams and T. Howard Waldron, with internal file markings and FBI routing stamps visible at the bottom.

**Witness:** Primary witness is Charles Casella, Jr., 287 Euclid Avenue, Hackensack, interviewed by SA Arthur F. Williams. He was with William Truex, Jr., a Fort Dix soldier, and later the report also records statements from Joyce McFarland and Mrs. Winfield S. Booth. Casella is portrayed as a direct eyewitness, though the sighting was brief and at distance; the file also notes corroboration was limited because some nearby people did not see the object.

**Sighting:** The object was seen on Sunday, August 3, 1947, around 7:30-7:45 p.m. near Simons Avenue in Hackensack, roughly two hundred yards above the hill near Summit Avenue and Simons Avenue. Casella and Truex were outside while meeting McFarland; Truex initially thought a child had lost a balloon. Casella saw a round black object moving south-to-north, then northward in a horizontal plane, fast enough to require them to turn their heads to follow it. He estimated it at about 30-40 inches in diameter, with no rays, and said it was too fast to be an ordinary balloon. McFarland described it as round, silver-blue, and revolving, visible for about a minute before disappearing over the horizon. Casella said it seemed to follow a line from the vicinity of Bendix, New Jersey, toward west of Westwood, New Jersey.

**Investigation:** The report records multiple interviews but reaches no firm identification. The witnesses discounted a balloon and said it was not an optical illusion; however, the brief duration, distance, and conflicting impressions (black vs. silver-blue, disc vs. globular) left the event unresolved. The FBI memorandum functions as a factual relay of field interviews rather than a conclusive analytical determination.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI Newark Division Office Memorandum from SAC Newark to the Director, FBI, dated August 13, 1947, titled “Flying Disc Reported at Hackensack, New Jersey, August 3, 1947 – Miscellaneous.” 这两页为连续页，属于同一份报告，内容从第一页延续至发给 Bureau 的第二页信函。正文以叙述形式署名/归于 Special Agents Arthur F. Williams 和 T. Howard Waldron，底部可见内部档案标记和 FBI 流转印章。

**Witness:** 主要证人是 Charles Casella, Jr.，住址为 287 Euclid Avenue, Hackensack，由 SA Arthur F. Williams 进行询问。他当时与 William Truex, Jr.——一名 Fort Dix 士兵——在一起，后来报告还记录了 Joyce McFarland 和 Mrs. Winfield S. Booth 的陈述。Casella 被描述为直接目击者，但目击时间很短且距离较远；档案还指出，由于附近有些人没有看到该物体，因此佐证有限。

**Sighting:** 该物体是在 1947 年 8 月 3 日（星期日）晚上约 7:30-7:45，于 Hackensack 的 Simons Avenue 附近被看到的，地点大约在 Summit Avenue 和 Simons Avenue 附近山丘上方二百码处。Casella 和 Truex 当时在外面，与 McFarland 会面；Truex 起初以为是有孩子放飞的气球。Casella 看到一个黑色圆形物体从南向北移动，随后又以水平轨迹向北飞行，速度快到他们必须转头跟随。Casella 估计其直径约为 30-40 英寸，没有光线，且速度太快，不像普通气球。McFarland 将其描述为圆形、银蓝色、并在旋转，约持续可见一分钟后消失在地平线后方。Casella 说它似乎沿着一条线从 Bendix, New Jersey 一带，朝着 Westwood, New Jersey 以西方向移动。

**Investigation:** 报告记录了多次访谈，但未得出明确认定。证人排除了气球的可能，并表示这不是视觉错觉；然而，由于持续时间短、距离远，以及不同证词之间存在分歧（黑色与银蓝色、圆盘状与球状），这一事件最终仍未被解释清楚。该 FBI 备忘录的作用是对实地访谈作事实性转述，而非作出结论性的分析判断。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Communications Section telemeter, stamped Aug. 8, 1947, file context 62-HQ-83894 Section 2. The page is an urgent field-to-HQ style communication, marked "WASH 9 FROM CGO" and initialed/signed "MC Swain," with later handling stamps showing it was recorded and indexed. The text explicitly says no further inquiry was contemplated.

**Witness:** The report centers on Mrs. Robert Little of 6327 Harper Avenue, Chicago. The telegram notes that she was unavailable for interview when the story was checked. A family contact, her father-in-law Joseph Reiner at the same address, told investigators she was 18 years old and had seen a disc over a month earlier, but the page does not provide a formal statement from her.

**Sighting:** The Chicago Herald-American report relayed that Little said she saw a disc at 3:30 AM "today" sailing above Lake Michigan off Jackson Park Beach. The object is only described as a "disc"; no size, color, altitude, duration, lights, sound, maneuver, or speed are given. The report is therefore thin on observational detail and largely derivative of a newspaper item rather than a direct interview.

**Investigation:** The FBI treated the item as a security matter and logged it through headquarters communications channels, but the text shows no substantive follow-up. Because the witness was unavailable and the only corroborating information came from a relative, the evidentiary value is limited. The page documents an early UFO-era press report from Chicago, not a substantiated field investigation, and it remains an unconfirmed sighting of an unidentified disc over the lakefront.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 报告的中心人物是位于 Chicago 的 6327 Harper Avenue 的 Mrs. Robert Little。电报注明，在核实该消息时她无法接受采访。与该家庭的联系对象、住在同一地址的她的岳父 Joseph Reiner 告诉调查人员，她当时 18 years old，并且在一个多月前曾看到过一个圆盘，但该页并未提供她的正式陈述。

**Sighting:** Chicago Herald-American 的报道转述称，Little 说她于“今天”凌晨 3:30 AM 在 Jackson Park Beach 外、Lake Michigan 上空看见一个圆盘掠过。该物体仅被描述为一个“disc”；未提供大小、颜色、高度、持续时间、灯光、声音、机动动作或速度等信息。因此，这份报告在观察细节方面十分有限，而且主要是转引自一则报纸消息，而非直接采访。

**Investigation:** FBI 将此事视为安全事项，并通过总部通信渠道进行了登记，但正文显示没有任何实质性的后续跟进。由于目击者无法联系，而唯一的佐证信息来自一位亲属，其证据价值有限。该页记录的是芝加哥早期 UFO 时代的一则新闻报道，而非一项得到证实的现场调查；它仍然只是一次未经证实的、关于湖滨上空不明圆盘的目击事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed report headed “Report on Flying Saucers,” dated 7 July 1947 and addressed to the Commanding General, 32d AAF Base Unit, Bolling Field, Washington, D.C. It sits in FBI file 62-HQ-83894 and carries a bottom notation identifying it as an enclosure, signed by John D. Schindler, Jr., Maj., Air Corps, AAF-CAP Liaison Officer. The page appears to be the full report page provided; no continuation or different incident pages are shown here.

**Witnesses:** The report consolidates observations from four witnesses in two aircraft. The first pair was an instructor and a student who had just taken off from Elkhorn Airport. The second pair included Capt. R. J. Southey, Wing Supply Officer, plus a passenger. Their statements were summarized by the liaison officer rather than recorded verbatim.

**Sighting:** Weather was described as CAVU with exceptionally good visibility and scattered altocumulus at 6,000 feet. The first report, at 1145 CST, placed the observers at about 800 feet above ground and the object at 4,000 feet MSL. It was first seen over Koshkonong, Wisconsin, and tracked to Elkhorn, Wisconsin. The second report, at 1430 CST, had observers at 3,500 feet MSL and the object at 2,500 feet, seen from Eagle, Wisconsin to Muskego, Wisconsin.

**Object:** In both accounts the object was called a “saucer” or flying saucer. It allegedly descended vertically through cloud, stopped, assumed a horizontal attitude, and then moved horizontally before disappearing and reappearing. The report calculates extreme speeds—about 6,000 mph in the first case and 3,960 mph in the second—based on witness estimates over only 15–20 seconds.

**Investigation:** This is a contemporary military summary of sightings, not a final analytic determination. The extraordinary speeds and brief observation windows make the estimates highly uncertain, but the report itself records the witnesses’ perceptions as noteworthy and leaves the object unidentified.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 一份打字报告，标题为“Report on Flying Saucers”，日期为 1947年7月7日，收件人为 Commanding General, 32d AAF Base Unit, Bolling Field, Washington, D.C. 该文件收录于 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894，页底注记表明其为随附文件（enclosure），并由 John D. Schindler, Jr., Maj., Air Corps, AAF-CAP Liaison Officer 签署。此页看起来就是所提供的完整报告页；此处未显示后续内容或不同事件页。

**Witnesses:** 报告汇总了来自两架飞机上四名目击者的观察。第一组是一名教官和一名刚从 Elkhorn Airport 起飞的学员。第二组包括 Capt. R. J. Southey，Wing Supply Officer，以及一名乘客。其陈述由联络官整理概述，而非逐字记录。

**Sighting:** 报告称当时天气为 CAVU，能见度极佳，6,000 英尺高空有零散高积云。第一则报告发生于 1145 CST，观察者位于地面上空约 800 英尺处，目标位于 4,000 英尺 MSL。最初在 Wisconsin 的 Koshkonong 上空发现，随后追踪至 Wisconsin 的 Elkhorn。第二则报告发生于 1430 CST，观察者位于 3,500 英尺 MSL，目标位于 2,500 英尺，从 Wisconsin 的 Eagle 一直被看到 Wisconsin 的 Muskego。

**Object:** 在两次叙述中，该物体都被称为“saucer”或 flying saucer。其据称垂直穿云下降，停住后转为水平姿态，随后水平移动，之后消失又重新出现。报告根据目击者估计、且仅持续 15–20 秒的观测，计算出极端速度——第一起约为 6,000 mph，第二起约为 3,960 mph。

**Investigation:** 这是一份当时的军事目击摘要，而非最终分析结论。如此惊人的速度和极短的观察窗口使这些估计高度不确定，但报告本身仍将目击者的感知记录为值得注意，并未对该物体作出 иден定。

**Document:** This page is the tail end of an FBI “Letter to Bureau” dated August 13, 1947, preserved in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2. The document also notes that no nearby police department had brought further information to the Division’s attention.

**Sighting:** TRUEX said the object appeared about two to three feet in diameter and was seen about 200 yards above the ground. It moved rapidly in a steady, straight path toward the north. He first thought it was a child’s balloon, but rejected that explanation when he saw no wind and no strings. The object was observed for roughly 15 to 20 seconds. TRUEX said neither he nor CASELLA had been drinking and that there was enough light to see it clearly.

**Object:** The witnesses could not describe the color or material. TRUEX said it looked like a large, flat child’s cup, oval on top and pointed on the bottom. CASELLA reportedly said, “Maybe it’s a flying saucer.” He added that he had never seen anything move through the air like it and had no idea where it came from.

**Investigation:** The FBI note is essentially a brief follow-up on a local police report, with no corroborating witnesses and no further action by the Hackensack Police Department. The report does not reach a firm analytical conclusion; it simply records an unverified daylight/early-evening observation that the witnesses believed was unlike a balloon and possibly a “flying disc.”

**Document:** FBI Detroit teletype to the Director, marked **URGENT**, dated Aug. 5, 1947 (5:08 PM EST) in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2. The page reports miscellaneous information received from Dow Chemical Company, Midland, Michigan, and records internal Bureau routing/handling notations. The text indicates Dow later examined the material and the FBI treated the account as doubtful, but worth relaying.

**Witness:** Raymond Edward Lane, described as an employee of Dow and a subsidiary since about 1922, is the principal witness. His wife, Laura Lane, was present. According to the report, Raymond brought recovered material to Dow’s physics laboratory on July 10 after the event. Laura was also interviewed, but the report says she was reluctant to talk and her account was less definite.

**Sighting:** On about **5:15 PM, July 9, 1947**, the Lanes were walking in a Dow-owned field about 100 feet from where they stood when they heard a puff/noise and turned to see a **white ball** roughly the size of a **bushel basket** burning about **a foot above the ground**. The flame reportedly went out immediately. Lane later scooped up about a three-inch area of fused sand into a can and took it to the laboratory.

**Object / Investigation:** The lab report summarized in the teletype says the material was **ordinary sand**, **not radioactive**, with a **small silver nugget** that was “almost pure” except for sand. It allegedly gave off **ammonia gas** and the melted sand emitted a slight ammonia odor. The report notes the Dow authorities considered the story “fantastic,” found **marked discrepancies** between the witnesses’ accounts, and saw no evidence of radioactivity or unusual composition beyond fused sand. The page does not support an extraterrestrial conclusion and reads more like a report of a localized burning/fusion event with recovered material.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI teletype/memo dated **August 14, 1947** from **J. Edgar Hoover** to the Communications Section, **SAC, Seattle** (file code shown as **CC-150**; case-file provenance from **62-HQ-83894, Section 2**). The memo responds to a prior telegram (“REURTEL AUGUST TWELVE”) and directs Seattle to reinterview the principals. It is administrative/investigative in nature rather than a fresh field observation report.

**Witness:** The underlying claim centers on **Harold Dahl**, a civilian boat operator, and **Fred Crisman**. The memo also references **Emil Smith** as an interview source, plus “Arnold” in connection with anonymous calls. The report treats Dahl and Crisman as the original storytellers and the key witnesses whose statements were being tested.

**Sighting:** This is the well-known **Maury Island** flying-disc/fragments incident in the **Tacoma / Puget Sound** area. The original alleged event was the discovery and recovery of metal fragments said to be from a flying disc, with the claim later discussed at a conference on **July 31, 1947** and a supposed admission that the story was a hoax on **Saturday night, August 2, 1947**.

**Object:** The alleged object was not a full craft but **“material”/fragments** claimed to be debris from a flying disc. The memo says the story had been repeated to Army intelligence officers and that the fragments were allegedly taken on a fatal flight by **Captain Davidson** and **Lieutenant Brown**.

**Investigation:** Hoover states that, if Emil Smith’s account is correct, Dahl and Crisman had repeated the false story until Dahl admitted it was a hoax. The memo concludes that either Smith or Arnold may have made the anonymous phone calls under the belief the material was real, but that the matter should be cleared up by **reinterviewing Dahl and Crisman**. Once clarified, Hoover says, **no further investigation is necessary**. The document strongly frames the incident as a **hoax**, not a validated UFO sighting.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 1947年**August 14, 1947**日期的FBI电传/备忘录，由**J. Edgar Hoover**致通讯科、**SAC, Seattle**（文件代码标示为**CC-150**；案件档案来源为**62-HQ-83894, Section 2**）。该备忘录回应此前一封电报（“REURTEL AUGUST TWELVE”），并指示Seattle重新询问相关当事人。其性质属于行政/调查性，而非新的现场观察报告。

**Witness:** 其核心主张围绕**Harold Dahl**——一名平民船只操作员——以及**Fred Crisman**。备忘录还提及**Emil Smith**作为一名访谈来源，并在匿名来电的相关内容中提到“Arnold”。报告将Dahl和Crisman视为最初讲述故事的人，也是其陈述正被核实的关键证人。

**Sighting:** 这就是众所周知的**Maury Island**飞碟/碎片事件，发生在**Tacoma / Puget Sound**地区。最初所谓的事件是发现并回收金属碎片，据称这些碎片来自一架飞碟；后来在**July 31, 1947**的一次会议上再次讨论该说法，并据称在**Saturday night, August 2, 1947**承认这一故事是骗局。

**Object:** 所谓对象并非完整飞行器，而是被称作来自飞碟残骸的**“material”/碎片**。备忘录称，该故事曾被转述给陆军情报官员，而这些碎片据称在**Captain Davidson**和**Lieutenant Brown**的一次致命飞行中被带走。

**Investigation:** Hoover表示，如果Emil Smith的说法属实，那么Dahl和Crisman一直在重复这一虚假故事，直到Dahl承认这是骗局。备忘录结论指出，匿名电话可能是Smith或Arnold在相信这些材料真实的情况下拨打的，但此事应通过**重新询问Dahl和Crisman**来澄清。一旦查明，Hoover说，**无需进一步调查**。该文件明确将此事件定性为**骗局**，而非经过证实的UFO目击事件。

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), from SAC, Portland to the Bureau, dated 8-23-47, subject line “Flying Discs / Security Matter - X.” The page carries later FBI file handling stamps and references file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, indicating it is part of the bureau’s 1947 flying-disc correspondence. No continuation page is present in the provided material, so this single page constitutes the full report used here.

**Witness:** Ray Virgil Hatfield of Route 1, Box 195, Roseburg, Oregon, operator of the Tri City Airport at Myrtle Creek. The memo notes that Hatfield was a former U.S. Naval Air Corps lieutenant junior grade, served about 3½ years on Atlantic submarine patrol, and was regarded as a reputable citizen and qualified pilot. His student, Noble Ellison of Myrtle Creek, later corroborated the account.

**Sighting:** On 1947-08-06 at about 6:15 PM, while Hatfield was instructing a student during takeoff at the Myrtle Creek airport, he saw an object east of Myrtle Creek at an estimated 5,000–8,000 feet. The sky was clear with excellent visibility. Hatfield said the object glistened like aluminum sheeting, seemed spherical, and at first appeared to have a darker object on its right side. He took control of the plane, climbed east to pursue it, and estimated the object’s speed at about 1,000 mph. He reported no vapor trail and no sound.

**Object:** Hatfield estimated the sphere at roughly 30 feet in diameter; Ellison later described it as a “silver ball or balloon” and estimated it at 50 feet in diameter. After about 10 minutes of searching, the men returned, took off again, and saw the object in roughly the same position. Ellison said it seemed about 8 miles east of Myrtle Creek, traveling east and climbing very rapidly before vanishing in about 45 seconds.

**Investigation:** The memo says the investigation was conducted at Canyonville and Myrtle Creek, Oregon, on 8-12-47. The report does not offer a firm identification; it records the witnesses’ observations and qualifications without reaching a conclusion, leaving the object unexplained in the file narrative.

**Witness:** Ray Virgil Hatfield，住址为Route 1, Box 195, Roseburg, Oregon，Myrtle Creek的Tri City Airport运营者。备忘录记载，Hatfield曾任美国海军航空队（U.S. Naval Air Corps）少尉（junior grade），在大西洋潜艇巡逻中服役约3½年，被认为是信誉良好的公民和合格飞行员。他的学生Noble Ellison，来自Myrtle Creek，后来证实了这一说法。

**Sighting:** 1947-08-06约下午6:15，Hatfield在Myrtle Creek机场指导一名学生起飞时，看到一个物体位于Myrtle Creek以东，估计高度为5,000–8,000英尺。天空晴朗，能见度极佳。Hatfield称，该物体闪着铝板般的光泽，看上去呈球形，起初似乎在其右侧还有一个较暗的物体。他接管飞机，向东爬升追踪，估计该物体速度约为1,000 mph。他报告称没有看到尾迹，也没有听到任何声音。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Butte teletype to the Director, marked **URGENT** and headed "FLYING DISCS," dated 8-20-47 at 3:22 PM (LB). The page is stamped by the FBI Communications Section / U.S. Department of Justice and sits in file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2. This page appears to be a standalone first page of a longer report; no later page was provided here.

**Witness:** The report says Mr. and Mrs. H. H. Hedstrom, while seated on the front porch at their home on Third Avenue North in Twin Falls, Idaho, were accompanied by Mrs. Henry Schultz. All three are described as direct eyewitnesses; the page does not provide occupations, ages, or any prior special familiarity with aircraft or astronomy.

**Sighting:** Between 9:30 and 9:45 PM on 19 August 1947, the group first saw one object resembling a "flying saucer" moving very rapidly from the southwest to the northeast. About ten minutes later they saw ten similar objects traveling in the same direction in a triangular formation. As the formation neared disappearance in the overcast sky, three objects on the left flank peeled off northward while the rest closed ranks and continued northeast. Three to five minutes later they saw another triangular group of three, then another group of five to six objects, and finally a larger group estimated at 35 to 50 objects moving northeast.

**Object:** The page gives no size, color, altitude, sound, or duration beyond rapid motion and repeated triangular formations. The wording suggests multiple separate groups rather than a single maneuvering craft.

**Investigation:** The FBI page is a relay of a civilian report rather than an on-scene investigation. No follow-up findings, identification, or explanation appear on this page. The multiple adult witnesses and the consistency of the directional description lend some testimonial weight, but the account remains observational only and lacks corroborating physical evidence.

**Sighting:** 1947年8月19日晚上9:30至9:45之间，这一群人首先看到一个类似“飞碟”的物体，以非常快的速度从西南向东北移动。大约十分钟后，他们又看到十个类似物体沿同一方向以三角形队形飞行。随着编队在阴云密布的天空中接近消失，左侧翼上的三个物体向北偏离，其余物体则重新收紧队形，继续向东北飞行。三到五分钟后，他们又看到另一组三个物体的三角形编队，随后又看到一组五到六个物体，最后又看到一大群估计有35到50个物体向东北移动。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, United States Government, from **SAC, Portland** to the **Director**, dated **September 5, 1947**, subject **“Flying Discs / Security Matter - X.”** The page is part of FBI file **62-HQ-83894, Section 2** and is signed/initialed **RJP/es** with later FBI routing stamps and annotations. **Witness:** The primary witness was **John Bartl** of **Agate Beach, Oregon** (initially misidentified in the teletype as **John Bartlett**). The memo says Bartl was later interviewed by **Special Agent Robert J. Pettyjohn** after the Portland office received a July 15 teletype about the report. Bartl was residing in Newport at the time of the interview and was described as having an Agate and Myrtlewood shop in Newport.

**Sighting:** Bartl stated that on **August 7, 1947, about 12:30 A.M.**, while staying at Agate Beach near the ocean, he was awakened by his son and then noticed a **bright glow of light across the sky out over the ocean**. He immediately thought of a flying disc. He said the object appeared to be about **five miles offshore**, was visible for only **15 to 30 seconds**, and moved **much faster than any airplane** he had ever seen. He could not judge its shape or size because of the darkness.

**Object:** Bartl compared the light to **“The Northern Light”** but said it was not nearly as large. He reported that it seemed to **go up and down**, or fluctuate in altitude, as it traveled along, and then **disappeared in the west**, either dropping into the ocean or passing over the horizon.

**Investigation:** The memo records no corroboration or technical analysis, only the witness interview and the agent’s summary. FBI language remains cautious: the object was described as a possible flying disc, but the report offers **no confirmed identification** and no additional evidence beyond Bartl’s observation.

**Document:** FBI 办公备忘录，美国政府文件，**SAC, Portland** 致 **Director**，日期为 **September 5, 1947**，主题为 **“Flying Discs / Security Matter - X.”** 该页属于 FBI 档案 **62-HQ-83894, Section 2**，并带有 **RJP/es** 签署/首字母缩写，后附 FBI 流转印章和批注。此页看起来就是所示事件的完整报告；这里未见单独的续页。

**Witness:** 主要证人是 **John Bartl**，来自 **Agate Beach, Oregon**（在电传中最初误记为 **John Bartlett**）。备忘录称，**Portland** 办公室于 7 月 15 日收到一份关于该报告的电传后，**Special Agent Robert J. Pettyjohn** 随后对 Bartl 进行了采访。采访时 Bartl 住在 Newport，并被描述为在 Newport 经营一家 Agate 和 Myrtlewood 商店。

**Sighting:** Bartl 陈述称，在 **August 7, 1947, about 12:30 A.M.**，他住在临近海洋的 **Agate Beach** 时，先被儿子叫醒，随后注意到**天空中、海面上方横贯而过的一道明亮光芒**。他立刻联想到飞碟。他说，该物体看起来大约在**距海岸五英里**处，仅可见 **15 to 30 seconds**，移动速度**远快于他见过的任何飞机**。由于天色黑暗，他无法判断其形状或大小。

**Object:** Bartl 将这道光比作 **“The Northern Light”**，但表示它远没有那么大。他报告说，这个物体在沿途移动时似乎**上下起伏**，即高度不断变化，随后**在西方消失**，可能是坠入海中，或是飞过了地平线。

**Investigation:** 备忘录未记录任何佐证或技术分析，仅有证人访谈和该特工的总结。FBI 的措辞仍然谨慎：该物体被描述为一种可能的飞碟，但报告**未给出确认身份**，除 Bartl 的目击之外也没有其他证据。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Page two of a typed FBI case-file report in 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, part of the 1947 flying-disc correspondence stream. The page is a continuation of a local sighting narrative and cites Bureau Bulletin No. 42, paragraph B, dated July 30, 1947, showing the report was being handled under early FBI UFO guidance.

**Witness:** The principal civilian source is Mrs. Hedstrom of Twin Falls, described as one of the informants and a reputable citizen. Her account was quickly checked by local law enforcement: Detective Richard Frazier of the Twin Falls Police Department, a next-door neighbor, came to the Hedstrom home with officers M. E. Roundtree and Richard Scott, both also of the Twin Falls PD.

**Sighting:** The witnesses reported objects in a triangular arrangement, then later in groups of three, five, seven, and finally a group of twelve. The objects were seen moving rapidly over Twin Falls in a southwesterly direction. They were described as resembling illuminated flying saucers. The informants said they could not estimate height or speed, heard no sound, and did not see the objects land, arc toward the ground, or appear to be aircraft landing lights or shooting stars.

**Investigation:** The page notes that the FBI investigation was continuing in line with Bureau instructions. The tone is cautious and procedural rather than conclusive: the observers were treated as credible, but the report provides no physical evidence, no recovered objects, and no confirmation of experimental aircraft activity on the page shown. The best-supported conclusion from this page is a multi-witness visual report of lighted aerial objects over Twin Falls, with no immediate explanation established.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 1947年飞碟通信档案流中62-HQ-83894第2部分的一份打字FBI案件档案报告的第2页。该页是对一次本地目击叙述的续写，并引用了1947年7月30日的Bureau Bulletin No. 42，paragraph B，表明该报告是在FBI早期UFO指导下处理的。

**Witness:** 主要的民间信息来源是Twin Falls的Mrs. Hedstrom，被描述为其中一名线人以及一位信誉良好的市民。她的陈述很快由当地执法部门核实：Twin Falls Police Department的侦探Richard Frazier，作为其隔壁邻居，和同属Twin Falls PD的警官M. E. Roundtree与Richard Scott一同前往Hedstrom家中。

**Sighting:** 目击者报告称，这些物体先是以三角形阵列出现，随后又以3个、5个、7个，最后是12个一组出现。这些物体被看到迅速向西南方向飞越Twin Falls。它们被描述为类似于发光的飞碟。线人称他们无法估计其高度或速度，没有听到任何声音，也没有看到这些物体着陆、向地面下坠成弧线，或表现为飞机降落灯或流星。

**Investigation:** 该页注明，FBI调查正按照Bureau的指示继续进行。整体语气谨慎且偏程序性，而非定论性：这些观察者被视为可信，但该报告未提供任何实物证据、未回收任何物体，也未在所示页面上证实有实验性飞机活动。就该页而言，最有根据的结论是：多名目击者报告在Twin Falls上空看到发光的空中物体，但尚未确定任何即时解释。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Handwritten civilian letter addressed to J. Edgar Hoover, FBI, Washington, D.C., dated 8/18/47 and later stamped "RECORDED" 11 SEP 1947 in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2. The page appears to be the sole page of this correspondence; no continuation sheets are shown.

**Witness:** The writer is an unidentified woman whose signature is not legible on the rendered page. She writes in a personal, emotional style and frames the note as a direct appeal to Hoover, saying she is trying to explain the matter in her "own simple way." No rank or official role is indicated.

**Sighting:** She says that "weeks ago" what she and others called a "flying saucer" fell in her front yard, passing only five or six feet from her while she was standing there. She describes the object as coming "straight down out of the skies" at "a terrific speed" and then exploding on impact. The exact date, time, and town are not legible on this page.

**Object:** The description is of a fast-descending object that exploded and left a piece or fragment behind. The letter does not provide dimensions, color, sound, shape, or duration, but the writer treats it as a physical object rather than a distant light.

**Investigation:** She says she turned the piece over to a local chief (name and locality partly illegible), but no technical analysis, chain of custody, or FBI field investigation appears on this page. On its face, the report reads more like an anecdotal civilian claim than a documented airborne craft sighting, and the motion described is consistent with a meteorite or other falling fragment rather than a maneuvering "flying saucer."
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 一封手写的平民来信，致 J. Edgar Hoover，FBI，Washington, D.C.，日期为 8/18/47，后于 11 SEP 1947 在 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894，Section 2 中盖上“RECORDED”印章。该页似乎是这封通信的唯一一页；未显示后续页。

**Witness:** 写信人是一名身份不明的女性，其签名在所示页面上无法辨认。她以个人、情绪化的语气写作，并将此信作为对 Hoover 的直接求助，称自己正试图用她“自己简单的方式”解释此事。文中未表明任何军衔或官方身份。

**Sighting:** 她说“几周前”，她和其他人称之为“飞碟”的东西落在了她家前院，当时她站在那里，它从她身边仅五六英尺处掠过。她描述该物体是以“极快的速度”从“天空中直冲下来”，随后在撞击时爆炸。该页上无法辨认确切日期、时间和城镇。

**Object:** 描述的是一个快速下坠并爆炸、还留下了一块或碎片的物体。信中未提供尺寸、颜色、声音、形状或持续时间，但写信人将其视为一个实体物体，而非远处的光点。

**Investigation:** 她说她把那块碎片交给了一位当地警长（姓名和地点部分无法辨认），但这一页上未见任何技术分析、保管链记录或 FBI 现场调查。就其表面内容来看，这份报告更像是一则平民轶事式的说法，而非有记录的空中飞行器目击；所描述的运动特征与陨石或其他坠落碎片相符，而不像是一架机动飞行的“飞碟”。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Handwritten correspondence in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2 (page p.0073), with a blue FBI received stamp. The page is an undated 1947 letter addressed to “Mrs. Hoover” and appears to be part of the FBI’s flying-disc correspondence cache rather than a formal field report.

**Witness:** The signer is a Florence, Alabama resident, likely “Mrs. W. T. Willi—” (surname partly unclear in the cursive), living at a Stevenson Street address. She writes as an eyewitness/claimant rather than as an investigator.

**Sighting/Claim:** She says something “fell in my yard” and that she did not know “what ever we might call it.” She states she immediately called the police and turned it over to them. Three or four days later, she and a neighbor found more of the material in tall grass nearby, and she also carried that to the police station. No time of day, shape, color, motion, or sound is given, and the page does not describe a visual “disc” sighting so much as the recovery of unknown material.

**Investigation:** The letter asks about a reward and implies local police took possession of the item(s). No FBI analysis or follow-up is shown on this page. Analytically, the account is too thin to support a UFO identification; it is better understood as an unverified report of debris or an unidentified object found on the ground, with the chain of custody resting solely on the witness’s statement.

**Sighting/Claim:** 她说有东西“fell in my yard”，但她不知道“what ever we might call it.” 她表示自己立即报了警，并把它交给了警方。三四天后，她和一位邻居又在附近的高草中发现了更多同样的材料，她也把那些东西带到了警察局。文中没有给出具体时间、形状、颜色、运动方式或声音，且这一页与其说是在描述一次可视的“disc”目击，不如说是在记录对未知材料的回收。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, Standard Form No. 64, from the SAC, Springfield, to the Director, FBI, dated August 20, 1947. The memo references Bureau Bulletin No. 42 (Series 1947), dated July 30, 1947, and carries internal file markings for FBI case 62-0-1445 / SI File 62-0-1445. The second page is the enclosure cover sheet: “Photographs of ‘Flying Disc’ found at Saybrook, Ill. 7-26-47,” indicating six photos enclosed.

**Witness:** Mrs. June Anderson of Saybrook, Illinois, reported the discovery to the Springfield FBI office. The memo gives no indication that she was a trained observer; instead, an agent’s follow-up inquiry notes that her “stability” was questionable, suggesting the reporting circumstances were somewhat unreliable or at least informal.

**Sighting:** The reported event occurred at about 6:00 A.M. on July 26, 1947, when Mrs. Anderson found a “flying disc” in her front yard. The enclosure and memo identify the location only as Saybrook, Illinois.

**Object:** The object was not an aerial craft. Investigation found it to be an old wooden platter with a silver plate, a spark plug, a timer, and pieces of old brass tubing attached. The agent concluded it was apparently assembled from parts gathered by juveniles in the area. The memo explicitly states, “No doubt this was someone’s idea of a prank.”

**Investigation:** Springfield retained the disc pending Bureau guidance, noting that Washington might want to examine it for any novel value. Six photographs were taken and enclosed. The report is therefore best understood as a prank-object recovery case rather than a genuine UFO encounter, despite the contemporary “flying disc” terminology.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI办公室备忘录，Standard Form No. 64，由Springfield的SAC致FBI局长，日期为1947年8月20日。该备忘录提及1947年7月30日的Bureau Bulletin No. 42（Series 1947），并带有FBI案件 62-0-1445 / SI File 62-0-1445 的内部档案标记。第二页为附件封面：“Photographs of ‘Flying Disc’ found at Saybrook, Ill. 7-26-47,”，表明随附6张照片。

**Witness:** 来自Illinois州Saybrook的June Anderson夫人向Springfield的FBI办公室报告了这一发现。备忘录并未表明她是一名受过训练的观察者；相反，一名特工的后续询问记录指出，她的“stability”存疑，这说明当时的报告情况多少有些不可靠，至少也较为非正式。

**Sighting:** 据报事件发生在1947年7月26日早上约6:00 A.M.，当时Anderson夫人在自家前院发现了一个“flying disc”。附件和备忘录仅将地点标为Saybrook, Illinois。

**Object:** 该物体并非空中飞行器。调查发现它是一只旧木制托盘，上面附有一块银板、一个火花塞、一个定时器，以及几段旧黄铜管。特工得出结论，显然是由当地青少年收集零件拼装而成。备忘录明确写道：“No doubt this was someone’s idea of a prank.”

**Investigation:** Springfield在等待局方指示期间保留了该“圆盘”，并指出Washington可能希望对其进行检查，以判断是否具有任何新奇价值。随后拍摄了6张照片并一并附上。因此，尽管当时使用了“flying disc”的术语，这份报告最恰当的理解应是一起恶作剧物件回收案件，而非真正的UFO遭遇事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Standard Form No. 64 office memorandum, dated August 28, 1947, from T. F. Baughman to Mr. R. T. Harbo at FBI Headquarters (case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2; exhibit stamp EX-83). The memo concerns a letter and physical material submitted by Mrs. J. H. Nixon of Estill, South Carolina.

**Witness:** Mrs. J. H. Nixon, a private citizen, is the source of the claim. Her August 14, 1947 letter accompanied the material she said was part of a "flying saucer." No rank, official position, or direct law-enforcement role is indicated.

**Sighting:** The page does not describe a firsthand visual sighting. Instead, it documents a report and sample submission from Estill, South Carolina. The material was received in the Laboratory on August 19, 1947, implying a report date of August 14 and laboratory intake five days later.

**Object:** The alleged saucer fragment was examined and identified as powdered soap stones. The memorandum treats the submission as a possible matter of interest to the Investigative and Security Divisions, but the lab result provides a mundane explanation for the sample.

**Investigation:** Baughman asks Harbo to advise on final disposition of the material and what reply should be sent to Mrs. Nixon. The administrative tone and the laboratory identification strongly indicate no corroborated UFO evidence; the file documents an unsubstantiated civilian claim that was analytically resolved as ordinary material.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI Standard Form No. 64 办公备忘录，日期为 1947年8月28日，由 T. F. Baughman 致 FBI Headquarters 的 R. T. Harbo 先生（案卷 62-HQ-83894，Section 2；证物编号 EX-83）。该备忘录涉及一封信件以及由 South Carolina 的 Estill 的 J. H. Nixon 夫人提交的实物材料。

**Witness:** J. H. Nixon 夫人，普通公民，是该说法的来源。她于 1947年8月14日寄出的信件，随附了她所称属于“飞碟”的材料。未注明任何军衔、官方职务或直接执法职责。

**Sighting:** 该页并未描述亲眼目击经过。相反，它记录的是一份来自 South Carolina 的 Estill 的报告及样本提交。该材料于 1947年8月19日被 Laboratory 收到，这意味着报告日期为 8月14日，而实验室收件是在五天之后。

**Object:** 所称的碟状碎片经检验后被鉴定为粉状皂石。该备忘录将这份提交视为可能值得 Investigative and Security Divisions 关注的事项，但实验室结果为该样本提供了平常的解释。

**Investigation:** Baughman 请求 Harbo 就该材料的最终处理方式以及应向 Nixon 夫人发送何种回复提出意见。该行政性措辞和实验室鉴定结果强烈表明并无经证实的 UFO 证据；此案卷记录的是一项未经证实的平民说法，分析结果将其解释为普通材料。

**Document:** This is page 2 of an FBI UFO-related memorandum in case file 62-1531, initialed "PJM:MB." The excerpt appears to be a continuation page from Section 2 of FBI case-file correspondence.

**Witness:** The report concerns Hatfield and Ellison, identified here as the people who reported the objects. The text frames them as the primary observers; the page itself does not include their full names or ranks, but the context indicates they were pilots or aircrew.

**Sighting:** The witness statement summarized here says he observed no evidence of motion such as vapor trails and heard no noise beyond the sound of his own aircraft. The objects were reported in the vicinity of Myrtle Creek, Oregon. The page excerpt shown does not preserve the original sighting header, so the exact time is not visible on this page alone.

**Investigation:** FBI follow-up in the Myrtle Creek area found no other person who had seen the objects reported by Hatfield and Ellison. The memorandum states that no further investigation is being conducted. The available text indicates no corroborating witnesses, no physical evidence, and no additional leads, leaving the report unverified.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page correspondence on State of Vermont Department of Education letterhead (Orange-Windsor District, South Royalton), addressed to the Federal Bureau of Investigation in Washington, D.C. The page is dated September 17, 1947 and bears FBI file markings, including the case number 62-83894 and recorded/indexed stamps, indicating it was entered into the Bureau's UFO correspondence file.

**Witness:** A. Courtney Parker, Superintendent of Schools, writes in the first person. He presents himself as a careful observer and notes that he owns a six-inch telescope, suggesting some familiarity with sky watching and astronomical comparisons.

**Sighting:** Parker states that at 3:40 P.M. on September 17, 1947, while halfway up Rix Ledges north of Lebanon, New Hampshire, he was watching honey bees near his bee box when he noticed a floating object. He describes the first object as roughly the size of a tennis ball and as white as cotton batting. It approached rapidly and noiselessly from the east.

**Object:** A second object, "in size and shape like a saucer," followed closely behind the first, maintaining a constant angle of inclination and a constant distance. Parker estimated the pair were about five degrees from his eye and remained visible for more than a minute before he lost them in the glare of the sun. In closing, he wrote that if he had seen them at night through his telescope, he would have thought Venus and Saturn had suddenly come together and were traveling at great speed much nearer the earth.

**Assessment:** This page contains the full sighting narrative and no later-page continuation. No FBI conclusion or technical identification appears here; the report preserves the witness's observations and his astronomical analogy only.

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, U.S. Government, from SAC Portland to the Director, dated 9-13-47, subject "Flying Discs / Security Matter - X." The page cites an earlier teletype of 9-4-47 and carries internal file markings including 62-1531 and the main case file 62-HQ-83894. No signer is shown on the page; it is an internal investigative report rather than a public statement.

**Witness:** Mrs. Raymond Dupuis of Oswego, Oregon was interviewed by the Portland office. She had been outside on her lawn with her 7-year-old son and a 10-year-old neighbor child when the incident occurred. The memo presents her as a direct eyewitness, with the children as contemporaneous observers, but no additional corroborating witnesses are named on this page.

**Sighting:** On 9-3-47, around noon, the group noticed approximately two dozen round silver objects high in the sky above Oswego. Mrs. Dupuis said they looked platter-shaped rather than spherical, seemed larger than a nearby cub-type airplane, and appeared to be far away and made of a white metallic material. The objects were grouped in an arc about level with and to the left of the sun. She reported that they held position for roughly 3 to 4 minutes, though some of the larger ones rotated rapidly "in the manner of a wheel." One object separated from the group, descended slowly, and disappeared behind trees on the horizon.

**Investigation:** The memo records that the witness initially thought the objects might be skywriting, but she later abandoned that explanation. She kept watching until glare from the bright sky affected her eyes and then went indoors, unable to say what became of the remaining objects. The page contains no formal analysis or identification, only the witness account transmitted up the FBI chain of command as a "security matter" UFO report.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page FBI Portland teletype/memo in the FBI UFO file (62-HQ-83894, Section 2), marked “URGENT” and “FLYING DISCS,” addressed to the Director. The page is signed by Bobbitt and carries later filing/index stamps and handwritten routing marks, indicating internal Bureau circulation rather than a separate narrative report. File reference visible on the page includes 62-83894-81.

**Witness:** The report attributes the sighting to Leon V. Jenkins, Chief of Police, Portland. Jenkins was reportedly in a police car and observed the object with Patrolman H. C. Raney, the driver; the memo adds that other Portland police officers may also have seen it. Because the witness was the city police chief, the observation is presented as a firsthand law-enforcement account.

**Sighting:** At about 5:15 PM on 11 September 1947, Jenkins observed an object over Portland that was “similar in size to a weather balloon” and appeared to be made of aluminum or another bright metal. It was said to be traveling rapidly from northwest to southeast at an estimated altitude of 10,000 feet. The object then veered south and disappeared in roughly one minute. The memo notes that a short article about the incident appeared in The Oregonian on 12 September 1947.

**Investigation:** The Bureau states that the matter was under investigation. No explanation is offered on this page, and no later continuation page is included here; this single page appears to be the complete record for this specific Portland sighting/report. The document preserves the FBI’s early postwar handling of flying-disc reports, but it does not reach a conclusion beyond noting the observation and ongoing inquiry.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed FBI case-file page headed “Phoenix file 62-213,” appearing as page 2 of the report. The page states that William Albert Rhodes, of 4333 N. 14th Street, Phoenix, Arizona, owned and operated the Panoramic Research Laboratory and Hobby Shop. It also notes that one of the photos from the episode was later submitted to the Bureau as Exhibit II with a letter dated August 4, 1947 from the Office of Assistant Chief of Staff A-2 Intelligence, Hamilton Field, California.

**Witness:** Rhodes was described as technically minded and experienced: he had done experimental work for about ten years, previously worked at the Naval Ordnance Laboratory in Washington, D.C., then at Falcon Field near Phoenix, and said his hobbies included science, physics, radio, electronics, and astronomy. The report adds that his prior experience likely helped him make fairly close estimates of size and distance.

**Sighting:** On the afternoon of July 7, 1947, after a storm in Phoenix with clouds around 5,000 feet and a 15-mph wind, Rhodes was walking from home to his shop when he heard a noise like a P-80 aircraft coming from the west. Looking northeast, he saw an odd-shaped ship, about 20–30 feet in diameter, moving about 100 mph in a small spiral radius and producing a sound that then faded. He hurriedly got a 120 Brownie camera and photographed it twice as it completed circles. He estimated the object at 1,000–2,000 feet altitude when it banked right and disappeared into the clouds.

**Object:** Rhodes said the craft resembled the front-cover image from the May 1947 issue of *Mechanics Illustrated*, except that it appeared to be flying backward. He did not connect it to the “flying discs” reported elsewhere. The report also records that, after a brief interview with newspaper reporters, the published story was “blown up” and Rhodes felt the newspaper version no longer accurately reflected his account.

**Investigation:** This page is a retrospective FBI summary of Rhodes’s statement rather than a first-person narrative. The only documentary provenance visible here is the Phoenix file number and the later A-2 Intelligence submission of one photograph. No analytical conclusion is stated beyond the description of Rhodes’s estimates and his technical background.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** Rhodes 被描述为技术背景深厚且经验丰富：他从事实验工作约十年，先前曾在 Washington, D.C. 的 Naval Ordnance Laboratory 工作，之后在 Phoenix 附近的 Falcon Field 工作，并表示自己的兴趣爱好包括科学、物理、无线电、电子学和天文学。报告补充说，他以往的经验很可能帮助他较为准确地估算了大小和距离。

**Sighting:** 1947 年 7 月 7 日下午，Phoenix 在一场风暴后，云层约在 5,000 英尺高空，风速为 15 mph。Rhodes 正从家里走向自己的商店，这时他听到一阵类似 P-80 aircraft 的声音从西边传来。朝东北望去，他看到一艘外形古怪的飞行器，直径约 20–30 英尺，以约 100 mph 的速度沿小半径螺旋飞行，并发出一种随后逐渐消失的声音。他匆忙取来一台 120 Brownie camera，在它完成几圈时拍了两张照片。他估计该物体在右转并消失进云层时的高度为 1,000–2,000 英尺。

**Object:** Rhodes 说，这个飞行器很像 *Mechanics Illustrated* 1947 年 5 月刊封面的图片，只是看起来像是倒着飞行。他并未将其与其他地方报道的“flying discs”联系起来。报告还记载，在与报社记者进行简短采访后，刊出的报道被“夸大”了，Rhodes 认为报纸上的版本已不再准确反映他的说法。

**Investigation:** 这一页是 FBI 对 Rhodes 陈述的回顾性摘要，而非第一人称叙述。此处可见的唯一文献来源信息，是 Phoenix 案卷编号以及后来由 A-2 Intelligence 提交的一张照片。除对 Rhodes 的估计和其技术背景的描述外，没有给出任何分析结论。

**Document:** FBI Norfolk sent an urgent teletype to the Director in FBI HQ file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, with the page stamped and routed through the Communications Section/Teletype on 13 Sep 1947 at 4:15 PM. **Witness:** The report names Mrs. G. H. Stockton of Ocean View, Virginia, as the original reporter, and states that her son-in-law, Hugh Jennings, also of Ocean View, confirmed the sighting. Jennings is the substantive eyewitness described in the report.

The report is best read as a possible balloon/airborne object sighting rather than a confirmed flying disc event.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, United States Government, Standard Form No. 64, from the SAC, Portland, to the Director, FBI, dated 9-17-47. The subject is **“Reports of Flying Discs / Security Matter - X”** and the text says it refers to a San Francisco letter dated September 4, 1947. The page carries later FBI routing/index stamps and file references including **62-1531** and a copy to **San Francisco (62-2938)**, indicating this is a field-office summary rather than a direct witness statement.

**Witness:** **Fred M. Johnson**, identified as living at the Globe Hotel, 106 NW First Avenue, Portland, and described as a reliable individual who had been a prospector in Montana, Washington, and Oregon for the past forty years.

**Sighting:** Johnson reported that on **June 24, 1947**, while prospecting in the **Cascade Mountains** at about **5,000 feet elevation**, he noticed a reflection and then saw a disc moving in a **southeasterly direction**. He used a telescope immediately and watched the object for about **45 to 60 seconds**. He said he could pick up an object at a distance of ten miles with his telescope.

**Object:** Johnson said the disc was about **30 feet in diameter**, appeared to have a **tail**, made **no noise**, and was seen while **banking in the sun**. He observed **five or six similar objects**, though he focused on one. He estimated they were about **1,000 feet above his position** and said they were not flying in formation.

**Investigation:** The memo notes Johnson stayed in the Cascades for several days, then returned to Portland and saw a newspaper article about a similar Boise, Idaho report. He said he contacted the Army only to bolster the Boise account. The only apparent analytical conclusion in the file is that Johnson was considered a credible informant; no definitive explanation for the discs is given.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** **Fred M. Johnson**，登记住在Portland（波特兰）106 NW First Avenue的Globe Hotel（环球酒店），并被描述为一名可靠人士，过去四十年来一直在Montana、Washington和Oregon从事探矿。

**Sighting:** Johnson报告称，在**June 24, 1947**，他正在**Cascade Mountains**进行探矿，当时大约处于**5,000 feet elevation**，先看到一道反光，随后看见一个圆盘朝**southeasterly direction**移动。他立即使用望远镜观看了该物体约**45 to 60 seconds**。他说，他能用望远镜在十英里外看清一个物体。

**Object:** Johnson说，该圆盘直径约为**30 feet**，看起来有一个**tail**，**no noise**，并且是在**banking in the sun**时被看见的。他观察到**five or six similar objects**，不过注意力主要集中在其中一个。他估计这些物体距离他的位置约**1,000 feet above your position**，并说它们并非以编队飞行。

**Investigation:** 备忘录指出，Johnson在喀斯喀特山脉停留了数日，随后返回Portland，并看到一篇关于Idaho州Boise（博伊西）类似报告的报纸文章。他说自己联系陆军，只是为了为Boise的说法提供佐证。档案中唯一明显的分析结论是，Johnson被认为是一名可信的情报提供者；对这些圆盘并未给出明确解释。

The page is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, and states that the Bureau would be advised after a local inquiry. The text is a secondhand summary drawn from a Salt Lake Tribune item, not a signed witness statement.

**Witness:** The report says that eight different people in Logan, Utah, reported the incident. No names, occupations, or addresses are given on this page, so the witnesses cannot be individually identified from the document.

**Sighting:** According to the teletype, the Logan witnesses said they saw "three different flights of flying discs" between 10:40 and 11:10 PM on Monday, 8 Sep 1947. The page does not describe shape, color, size, altitude, direction, speed, sound, or duration beyond the reference to multiple flights.

**Object:** The objects are only identified as "flying discs," reflecting the 1947 terminology. No physical evidence, photographs, or technical data are mentioned here.

**Investigation:** FBI Salt Lake City notes that an investigation was already being conducted and that headquarters would be informed. Because this page only relays a press report, its evidentiary value is limited; however, it does preserve an early contemporaneous lead involving multiple alleged observers at Logan, Utah, on the night of 8 Sep 1947.

**Document:** This is page three of a typed FBI memorandum in case 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, with handwritten correction marks and a page stamp reading “PAGE THREE.” The visible page continues a longer investigative report; no separate signature block or document date appears on this page.

**Witness/Subjects:** The page centers on Kenneth Arnold (pilot and principal subject of the wider disk-fragment story), along with Dahl, Chrisman, Emil Smith, Ray Palmer, and Ernie Vogel of United Press. It does not record a direct UFO observation on this page; instead, it summarizes telephone contacts and follow-up statements tied to the Arnold-related disc-fragment controversy.

**Incident:** According to the memorandum, on July 31 and August 1 Arnold called Ray Palmer at Evanston, Illinois, and Boise, Idaho, and on August 1 he also called Palmer in Chicago. The page further states that Emil Smith called Roddy in Chicago. It then reports that five anonymous telephone calls were received by a Tacoma Times reporter and a United Press wire man in Tacoma, giving information about a Winthrop Hotel meeting concerning disk fragments and asserting that a B-25 had been shot down or sabotaged, killing Captain Davidson and Lieutenant Brown. The calls implied the plane may have been targeted because intelligence officers were carrying disk fragments.

**Investigation:** Dahl and Chrisman denied making the calls, saying they could only have come from themselves, Smith, or Arnold. The memo says no record could be found of the calls originating from Arnold’s Winthrop Hotel room, and it characterizes Dahl and Chrisman as evasive about what information they provided by phone or letter to Ray Palmer. Overall, the page reads as an FBI attempt to trace rumor sources and phone contacts surrounding the Arnold disk story, rather than as confirmation of any aerial object or confirmed sabotage.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed first-person report headed "CONFIDENTIAL" and "BY KENNETH ARNOLD," preserved in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2. The page is a carbon/copy marked "COPY" and appears to be the opening page of Arnold’s written account. No continuation page was included in the provided set.

**Witness:** Kenneth Arnold, a pilot working for Central Air Service at Chehalis, Washington. He says he had just finished work there and was flying to Yakima when the event occurred. He stresses that his observation was accidental and that he had no prior interest in notoriety.

**Sighting:** On 24 June 1947, shortly after taking off from Chehalis and while flying toward Mt. Rainier, Arnold reports climbing to roughly 9,500 feet and crossing the southwest side of the mountain. After making a sweep near Mineral and returning toward Rainier, he saw a bright flash and then a chain of nine strange aircraft/object shapes north of Mt. Rainier. He estimated they were at about 9,500 feet, traveling rapidly from north to south on a course of about 170 degrees. He initially thought they were jets, but says they appeared unusual, moved in formation, and reflected sunlight brightly off his plane.

**Object:** Nine peculiar-looking objects, later described as having no visible tails, with shapes difficult to discern at first because of distance. He could estimate size and outline more clearly once they approached the snowy mountain backdrop. The page ends as he continues describing watching the formation.

**Investigation/assessment:** The report is notable because Arnold was an experienced civilian pilot observing in clear weather from the air at close to mid-range distance. The document itself contains no FBI conclusion; it is an evidentiary copy of Arnold’s narrative that later became the classic "flying disc" report associated with Mt. Rainier.

**Sighting:** 1947年6月24日，在从 Chehalis 起飞后不久、飞往 Mt. Rainier 的途中，Arnold 说他爬升到大约 9,500 英尺，并越过了山的西南侧。在 Mineral 附近盘旋一圈并返回 Rainier 方向后，他看到一道亮光，随后又看到一串由九个奇怪的飞机/物体轮廓组成的队列，位于 Mt. Rainier 以北。他估计这些物体大约在 9,500 英尺高度，以约 170 度的航向从北向南高速飞行。他起初以为那是喷气式飞机，但他说它们看起来很不寻常，呈编队飞行，并在他的飞机上强烈反射阳光。

**Investigation/assessment:** 这份报告之所以引人注目，是因为 Arnold 是一名经验丰富的民航飞行员，在天气晴朗的空中、以近至中距离进行观察。该文件本身并未包含 FBI 的结论；它只是 Arnold 叙述的证据性副本，后来成为与 Mt. Rainier 相关的经典“飞碟”报告。

**Document:** Confidential copy memo in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, labeled Incident 4AF 1208 I and dated 16 July 1947. It is signed by Frank M. Brown, S/A, CIC 4th AF, and addressed as a memorandum for the officer in charge.

**Witness:** The sole witness discussed on this page is Captain Smith of United Airlines. Brown interviewed him at Boise Municipal Airport, Boise, Idaho, on 12 July 1947 while Smith was passing through on a scheduled flight with a 20-minute stopover.

**Sighting:** Smith repeated the account he had earlier given to the press. He said that in the late evening of 4 July 1947, when his aircraft was about 8 minutes out of Boise on the route to Seattle, Washington, he observed "flying disks." The memo does not preserve further descriptive details on this page, such as size, color, formation, speed, altitude, or direction changes.

**Investigation:** Brown’s note emphasizes that Smith’s standing as an airline captain made him unlikely to make such a claim lightly; in Brown’s view, Smith would need to be strongly convinced that he had actually seen the objects before risking ridicule by reporting them. The page therefore functions as an interview summary rather than a full technical report, preserving the witness’s restated claim and the investigator’s credibility assessment.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Confidential memorandum for the Officer in Charge, Incident 4AF 1208-I, dated 5 August 1947. The report was prepared by James A. Nelson, Special Agent, CIC 4AF, from an interview with Captain William H. Ryherd at the 415th AAF BU, Building 95, Hamilton Field, California. The page is marked confidential and later declassified under NND 90986.

**Witness:** Primary witness was Capt. William H. Ryherd (ASN O-66356), assistant operations officer in the 415th AAF BU and instructor pilot in the 415th Training Unit. He was accompanied by student 1st Lt. Ward L. Stewart during the sighting.

**Sighting:** On 29 July 1947 at about 1450, after landing an AT-6 near the hangar at Hamilton Field, Ryherd looked west over the hangar and saw a P-80 flying southward toward Oakland. Above the P-80, at roughly 8,000 to 10,000 feet, he observed two flying objects moving in the same direction. He estimated them at about 15 to 25 feet in diameter and described them as solid, white, somewhat shiny, and circular, “like a ball on the bottom, but not completely round.” He specifically said they were not airplanes.

**Object:** The first object moved straight and level; the second followed close behind at the same altitude, alternating left-to-right and right-to-left in a way that resembled an aircraft in formation. Ryherd said their speed made the P-80 appear motionless by comparison. The sky was clear, and the objects disappeared in flight, supposedly over Oakland, heading toward the ocean.

**Investigation:** No sound was heard, though the P-80’s noise may have masked it. Ryherd reported no vapor, smoke, or visible trail. He also said he had told no one before because he feared people would think he was crazy. The agent’s note states Ryherd showed extreme sincerity and answered questions with caution and assurance.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 致负责人关于 Incident 4AF 1208-I 的机密备忘录，日期为 1947年8月5日。该报告由 James A. Nelson，CIC 4AF 特别探员，根据在加利福尼亚州 Hamilton Field（汉密尔顿机场）415th AAF BU、95号楼与 William H. Ryherd 上尉的访谈整理而成。该页标注为机密，后依据 NND 90986 解密。

**Witness:** 主要目击者为 William H. Ryherd 上尉（ASN O-66356），他是 415th AAF BU 的作战助理军官，也是 415th Training Unit 的教练飞行员。目击时，他与学员 Ward L. Stewart 少尉一同在场。

**Sighting:** 1947年7月29日约 1450 时，Ryherd 在 Hamilton Field（汉密尔顿机场）机库附近降落一架 AT-6 后，向西越过机库张望，看见一架 P-80 正向南飞往 Oakland（奥克兰）。在 P-80 上方，约 8,000 to 10,000 英尺高度处，他观察到两个飞行物体朝同一方向移动。他估计这两个物体直径约 15 to 25 英尺，并描述它们为实心、白色、略带光泽、呈圆形，“像一个底部是球形的东西，但又不完全是圆的。”他明确表示它们不是飞机。

**Object:** 第一个物体直线且水平飞行；第二个则紧随其后、处于相同高度，以左右交替摆动的方式飞行，类似编队飞行中的飞机。Ryherd 说，它们的速度快到让 P-80 相比之下看起来几乎静止不动。当天天空晴朗，这些物体在飞行中消失，据称是在 Oakland（奥克兰）上空，朝海洋方向飞去。

**Investigation:** 没有听到任何声音，不过 P-80 的噪音可能掩盖了它们的声音。Ryherd 报告说没有看到蒸汽、烟雾或可见尾迹。他还表示此前没有告诉任何人，因为他担心别人会以为他疯了。该探员的记录指出，Ryherd 表现出极高的真诚度，并且回答问题时谨慎而笃定。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page FBI case-file memorandum in 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, built around an attached newspaper clipping dated July 8, 1947. The page records a follow-up interview after Wenyon’s claim had appeared in the press; no later pages in this sequence appear to belong to a different incident.

**Witness:** Horace P. Wenyon (also identified in the clipping as a Rehoboth Beach resident at 123 Rehoboth Avenue) was described as an airplane pilot of about 30 years’ experience. The report notes he first contacted the FBI, then was referred away because the Bureau was “not interested,” after which he notified Eastern Airlines and the Civil Aeronautics Authority. He was later interviewed by an FBI agent.

**Sighting:** Wenyon stated that in September 1946, while flying about 1,000 feet high, two or three miles south of Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, he observed a projectile about 15 inches in diameter crossing his course at right angles, traveling west-to-east. He said several jets of flame were issuing from the object and estimated its speed at 1,000 to 1,200 mph. He further stated that in October 1946 he saw a similar projectile while flying over Rehoboth Beach at 1,400 feet; this one also traveled west-to-east. The newspaper clipping paraphrased his description as a “flying mayonnaise jar.”

**Investigation:** Wenyon told the agent he believed he had seen some kind of test rocket and raised the possibility that such objects could help explain recent airplane crashes. The page reflects a routine Bureau intake: the clipping was logged, the witness was interviewed, and the matter was referred to aviation authorities rather than treated as an active FBI case. No corroborating evidence appears on this page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 62-HQ-83894 第二部分中的一页 FBI 案卷备忘录，围绕一则日期为 1947 年 7 月 8 日的附带报纸剪报展开。该页记录了一次后续访谈，发生在 Wenyon 的说法见诸报端之后；该序列中的后续页面似乎并不属于另一起事件。

**Witness:** Horace P. Wenyon（在剪报中也被描述为一名居住在 123 Rehoboth Avenue 的 Rehoboth Beach 居民）被描述为一名拥有约 30 年飞行经验的飞机驾驶员。报告指出，他首先联系了 FBI，随后因局方“not interested”而被转介，之后他又通知了 Eastern Airlines 和 Civil Aeronautics Authority。后来，他接受了一名 FBI 特工的询问。

**Sighting:** Wenyon 说，1946 年 9 月，他在离海平面约 1,000 英尺的高度飞行时，在 Delaware 的 Rehoboth Beach 以南两到三英里的地方，看到一个直径约 15 英寸的飞行物，以直角穿越其航线，方向为由西向东。他说，该物体喷出数股火焰，估计其速度为 1,000 to 1,200 mph。 他还称，1946 年 10 月，他在飞越 Rehoboth Beach、飞行高度 1,400 英尺时，又看到一个类似的飞行物；这个物体同样由西向东飞行。报纸剪报将他的描述转述为一个“flying mayonnaise jar”。

**Investigation:** Wenyon 告诉该特工，他认为自己看到的是某种试验火箭，并提出这类物体或许有助于解释近期发生的飞机坠毁事件。该页反映的是 FBI 常规受理流程：剪报被登记存档，证人接受询问，案件随后被移交给航空主管机构处理，而不是作为一宗正在积极调查的 FBI 案件来处理。此页未见任何可供佐证的证据。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Newspaper clipping attached to an FBI Baltimore routing sheet in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 2, subject line "FLYING DISCS / MISCELLANEOUS," dated 9/4/47. The clipping is a contemporary press account rather than a Bureau investigative narrative, but it was preserved in the flying-disc file as corroborating correspondence/report material.

**Witness:** Forrest Wenyon of 123 Rehoboth Avenue, Rehoboth Beach, was described as a veteran Delaware pilot with about 30 years' flying experience and as the Rehoboth Airport attendant. That background gives the article some credibility as an aviation observer, though the piece is clearly framed as a sensational newspaper story.

**Sighting:** Wenyon said he first noticed a strange object the previous September while flying around 1,000 feet, and then saw another on June 2, 1947 while piloting a Stinson four-passenger aircraft at about 1,400 feet. He described the craft as looking like a "flying mayonnaise jar" or "jar," moving at tremendous speed, crossing his path from west to east, and disappearing after only a few seconds.

**Object:** The article says Wenyon observed silver flame from the tail, which he believed provided propulsion; the tail also appeared to be a lid with perforations through which the flames escaped. He characterized the motion as guided rather than erratic, and suggested a rocket-like or jet-propelled mechanism. He later speculated that one of these objects might have been involved in the Eastern Airlines crash at Port Deposit, Maryland, on Memorial Day.

**Investigation:** The clipping says Wenyon contacted the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Eastern Airlines, and the Civil Aeronautics Authority, but received no answer. The article embeds his report within a broader roundup of flying-saucer claims nationwide, including references to Harvard Observatory and Army/Navy interest, but it does not record any official identification or Bureau conclusion.

**Document:** This is a single handwritten incoming letter page in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894 (Section 1), stamped with a "G.I.R." mark and an instruction to "KEEP ENVELOPE ATTACHED" / "Anonymous notification," indicating the Bureau wanted the original envelope preserved. No separate continuation page is visible here, and the page appears to be a self-contained report fragment rather than part of a longer multi-page narrative.

**Witness:** The writer is not identified on the visible page. The text is addressed "Dear Mr. ..." and reads like a personal communication to an official or correspondent rather than a formal field report. Because no signature, rank, or occupation is visible, the witness should be treated as an unnamed civilian observer.

**Sighting:** The witness says they "have also seen a flying saucer" on the evening of July 4 at about 10:30 p.m., while sitting on a porch. The object was reportedly "in the air at the same level" as two obvious portions of light in the searchlight beams coming from an air field near Lake St. Clair. The witness notes that there were two clearly outlined beams, with one partly faded, and that the lights/object appeared aligned with the beam level.

**Object:** The description is limited and impressionistic: no definite shape, size, speed, color, or maneuvering is provided beyond the comparison to the searchlight beams. The writer immediately offers a skeptical interpretation, saying that a few trucks with proper equipment could create the same illusion. That comment suggests the observer believed the phenomenon may have been an optical effect or a misread light source rather than a structured craft.

**Investigation:** The page has the hallmarks of FBI file handling rather than an Air Force technical report: administrative stamps, envelope-retention instructions, and a fragmentary civilian narrative. Based on the witness's own wording, the best analytical conclusion is that this is a probable light/beam illusion near a local airfield around Lake St. Clair, not a well-documented aircraft or disc encounter.

**Investigation:** The page appears to be FBI-file correspondence rather than a formal investigative report, with no visible classification stamp or report number beyond the master file code. The document’s analytical value is limited: the writer disputes the "pipe ashes" explanation and offers a tentative, non-UFO possibility of a late July 4 firework. No definitive conclusion is recorded on the page beyond Reibold’s rejection of the earlier identification.

**Document:** One-page FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) dated July 12, 1947, from F. P. Griffee to Mr. Ladd, subject **“Flying discs.”** It references Mr. Howe’s memorandum of July 11 in the same matter and is filed in FBI case 62-HQ-83894, Section 1. The page bears internal routing marks and later file stamps, but no continuation pages are present here, so this single page is the entire event record for this entry.

**Witness:** The primary source is **Sergeant Lonis** of the **Laurel, Maryland Police Department**, reported secondhand through a phone call received by the FBI. Lonis appears to have personally inspected the object. The memorandum also notes follow-up contact with **Captain Calvert**, duty officer at G-2, to whom the information was relayed.

**Sighting:** At **11:55 P.M. on July 11, 1947**, Lonis told the FBI he had examined a so-called “flying disc.” He reported that it was not an aerial object at all, but a device made from a **Gulf Oil sign** and the **top of a garbage can**, both painted with **aluminum paint**. The paint was said to be **fresh and still wet**. Attached to the assembly were a **dry-cell battery, a flashlight bulb, some wires, and a buzzer**.

**Investigation:** Lonis asked whether the Bureau would send anyone to inspect it. Griffee responded that the FBI would not, because the matter had been referred to the **Army**, and suggested that Lonis contact them. Griffee then telephoned Captain Calvert at G-2 and passed along Lonis’s description. The memo strongly indicates the “disc” was a **man-made hoax or improvised prop**, not a genuine unidentified flying object.

The incident is best summarized as a Wisconsin "flying saucer" scare resolved as a circular saw that struck a church lightning rod and fell to the ground.

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 1, from H. B. Fletcher to D. M. Ladd, subject “Flying Discs.” The page carries routine FBI routing/record stamps and handwritten initials, indicating HQ circulation of a field report rather than a standalone investigative memo.

**Witness:** The substantive witness is Mrs. Fred Easterbrook of 215 7th Avenue East, Twin Falls, Idaho. The information reached the FBI through SAC Bannister of the Butte Office, who called at noon on July 11, 1947. Bannister reported that Mrs. Easterbrook was at home when she heard a noise in the back of her house at about 2:45 a.m. Mountain Time and believed a collision may have occurred. The credibility is secondhand in the memorandum, but the report is specific enough to identify the witness, address, and time.

**Sighting:** This is not a conventional aerial sighting; it is a ground recovery report. Mrs. Easterbrook reportedly investigated and found an object in the backyard of the home next door. The object was described as a circular disc about 30½ inches in diameter, shaped like a saucer and “a saucer within a saucer” like cymbals. It had a 14-inch plastic dome attached by eight bolts, another metal dome on the opposite side, three tube-like components visible through the plastic, wiring, a coil-like part marked “Inspected TS,” and signs of burned-off wiring and possible missing parts.

**Investigation:** Bannister said the press was already aware of the incident, that the disc had been taken to the Police Department in Twin Falls, and that local Army authorities were to be notified. The FBI memo records the report without endorsing any explanation; the content suggests a damaged manufactured object or component assembly rather than a verified airborne craft, but no final identification is given in the document.

**Document:** Single-page FBI Office Memorandum, Standard Form No. 64, from Roy E. Wood to Mr. Ladd, dated July 10, 1947, subject "Flying Saucers (DTSCS) Information Concerning." **Witness:** The underlying account is attributed to the Burbank fire chief, conveyed to the FBI through the resident agent at Burbank and SAC Hood. No witness name is given on the page. **Sighting:** At about 11:30 PM on July 9, 1947, a "flying disc" was said to have landed in or near Burbank, California, and to have burst into flame on landing. **Object / Investigation:** Mr. Hood described the recovered item as an aluminum disc about 2 feet in diameter, weighing about 10 pounds, painted with aluminum paint, with some sort of radio tube in the center. The object was in the resident agent's possession and was to be turned over to military authorities (G-2) in Los Angeles that morning. Newspapers had already called; AAF Intelligence reportedly said "we are not interested," prompting concern about press quotes. The memo gives no direct evidence of an aerial craft and reads more like a report of an unusual recovered object than a confirmed flying-saucer observation.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum from the SAC, Los Angeles, to the Director, FBI, dated July 17, 1947, in file 62-HQ-83894 Section 1. The first page is a standard Office Memorandum with subject “Recovery of ‘Flying Disc,’ North Hollywood, California, July 9, 1947”; the second page continues the same memo, so both pages belong to one report. The file copy includes recording/indexing marks, enclosure notation for photos, and later file stamps showing the copies were destroyed in 1964.

**Witness/Report Source:** The initial report came from the North Hollywood area after a “flying disc” was said to have landed near Radford and Magnolia Streets. Battalion Fire Chief Wallace E. Newcomb told FBI Agent SA Richard D. Auerbach that, at about 10:30 p.m., an unknown woman telephoned in an excited state and said the disc had dropped into her garden at 11858 Magnolia Boulevard. She was not named in the memo. The next day, civilian Frank V. Brown of 6552 Teesdale Avenue said he heard neighborhood talk at a service station and believed local students may have been involved in making the object.

**Sighting/Recovery:** The object was reportedly on fire when first found and was extinguished by a fire department truck before being taken to the station and then to the FBI office. The scene attracted newspaper reporters and photographers. The memo frames the event as a recovery rather than a prolonged airborne observation.

**Object:** FBI’s description says the device consisted of two convex steel discs about 2 feet in diameter, fused at the outer edge and joined at the center by a hollow cylindrical connection. It had a vertical galvanized iron fin, a short closed pipe projecting inward from the rim, and what appeared to be a radio tube in the center top, weighing about 20 pounds.

**Investigation/Conclusion:** SA Auerbach arranged photos and forwarded them for Bureau inspection. The object was later turned over to Major Courtney W. Hempstead, A.C., G-2, Fort MacArthur, San Pedro, who reported it was definitely a hoax and could not have flown under its own power. The memo’s overall conclusion is that the North Hollywood “flying disc” was fabricated rather than a genuine aerial craft.

**Witness/Report Source:** 最初报告来自 North Hollywood 一带，当时据称有一个“flying disc”降落在 Radford 和 Magnolia 街附近。消防营长 Wallace E. Newcomb 告诉 FBI 探员 SA Richard D. Auerbach，大约在晚上10:30，一名身份不明的女性在情绪激动的情况下打来电话，说该圆盘落入了她位于 11858 Magnolia Boulevard 的花园里。备忘录中未提及她的姓名。第二天，居住在 6552 Teesdale Avenue 的平民 Frank V. Brown 说，他在一家加油站听到附近居民议论，认为当地学生可能参与了该物体的制作。

**Sighting/Recovery:** 据称该物体在首次发现时正在燃烧，并在被运往消防站之前先由消防车将火扑灭，随后又被送往 FBI 办公室。现场吸引了报社记者和摄影师。备忘录将这一事件表述为一次回收，而非长时间的空中目击。

**Investigation/Conclusion:** SA Auerbach 安排了照片并将其转交 Bureau 审查。该物体随后交给了 Major Courtney W. Hempstead, A.C., G-2, Fort MacArthur, San Pedro；他报告称这显然是一个骗局，不可能依靠自身动力飞行。备忘录的总体结论是，North Hollywood 的“flying disc”是伪造的，并非真正的空中飞行器。

**Document:** This is a Standard Form No. 64 Office Memorandum from D. M. Ladd to Mr. E. A. Tamm, dated July 11, 1947, in FBI file 62-HQ-83894. The page bears later FBI routing/stamp markings, including an EX-56 notation and file handling stamps, showing it was entered into the Bureau’s flying-disc correspondence file. The memo reports secondhand information relayed by the Milwaukee FBI office through SAC Johnson.

**Witness:** The principal named witness is Sig Hanson, identified as the City Engineer at Black River Falls, Wisconsin. His report reached the FBI via Colonel Harry Schafer, a Reserve Officer with the Civilian Air Patrol. Schafer appears to be the immediate source who phoned SAC Johnson; Hanson is the person who allegedly found the object.

**Sighting/Recovery:** At about 3:30 p.m. on July 10, 1947, Hanson reportedly found a large 17-inch disc. The object was described as possibly cardboard painted with silver airplane dope. In the center was a tube and a small motor with a propeller attached to the side. Colonel Schafer expressed the view that the disc would not be able to fly by itself. The memo does not describe anyone seeing the object in flight; it concerns a recovered disc-like item.

**Investigation:** Schafer said the item would be taken to Air Corps Headquarters, but Hanson did not want to release it without FBI approval. Ladd instructed Johnson to tell Schafer the Bureau had no reason to try to secure the material because it was not in FBI custody and the Bureau had no control over it. Ladd also noted that the press was asking about the matter and instructed that no comment be made. Overall, the memorandum treats the item as a likely homemade or non-aerodynamic object rather than a credible flying craft report.

**Witness/Source:** The named source is **Mr. Dave Johnson** of the *Idaho Daily Statesman* (Boise, Idaho), who telephonically contacted the Butte office. Johnson was acting as a newspaper reporter and information conduit, not as an eyewitness to the event itself. He stated that many citizens had reported seeing the discs and that he believed the reports were not imaginary.

**Sighting:** Johnson said the discs were seen on **July 1, 1947**, in the **vicinity of Trail Creek near Sun Valley, Idaho**, by “reputable citizens.” No individual eyewitness names, number of objects, duration, direction of travel, altitude, color, sound, or speed are given on this page.

**Investigation:** The memo says the FBI office told Johnson it was **not making an investigation** and asked whether he had contacted Army and Navy officials; Johnson replied that he was inquiring of those agencies. The page therefore documents a public rumor/report being relayed through a journalist, not a verified FBI investigation. The evidentiary value is limited because the actual witnesses are unnamed and the description is secondhand.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI New Orleans teletype, marked “VERY URGENT,” dated 7-7-47 at 8:02 PM, from the FBI Communications Section to the Director, FBI. The subject line reads “FLYING DISCS, MISCELLANEOUS.” The page contains no continuation marker, so this single page is the full report used here.

**Witness:** F. C. Hairston of 1554 Texas Avenue, Shreveport, Louisiana. He is identified only as a civilian observer, not as a trained aviation or scientific witness. The report says he notified military personnel at Barksdale Field immediately after recovering the object.

**Sighting:** Hairston reported seeing a circular disc at about 6:05 PM on 7 July 1947, coming from the northwest. He said it landed in the 1500 block of Texas Avenue, and that he picked it up at 1554 Texas Avenue. He described the object as whirling in flight, with fire “spouting from sides.” The fire stopped on landing, and smoke appeared a few seconds later. He stated the disc was not hot when recovered.

**Object:** The FBI teletype describes a thin aluminum disc about 16 inches in diameter, with small coils about 2 inches in diameter and 4 inches long at the ends of the diameter. Two copper wires connected the coils to terminals and to a center object about 1 inch in diameter and 2 inches long, likened to a fluorescent-light starter. The center bore the words “MADE IN USA,” and the object reportedly made a sound like a policeman’s whistle. The underside was described as the smooth side facing earth in flight.

**Investigation:** Barksdale Field personnel reportedly took custody of the disc before an FBI Special Agent arrived, and they were making photographs. The message says Barksdale would turn the item over to the FBI if desired, subject to superior instructions, and that the names of all persons who handled it before the agent’s arrival were secured. The report strongly suggests a recovered man-made device or component rather than an unidentified aerial craft, but the document does not record a final technical identification.
