events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Houston teletype(s) to the Director in the Communications Section, file 62-HQ-83894 (Section 5), dated July 4, 1950. The first transmission at 2:35 PM CST reported a “flying disc” said to have been found near Alice, Texas, and noted a reported serial number “X-147A” plus instructions quoted as “do not touch.” A second Houston teletype at 3:50 PM CST follows up with the result of the inquiry.

**Witness:** The principal local source named in the follow-up is Stokes McEnheimer, Chief of Police, Alice, Texas. The report also notes that a resident agent in Corpus Christi had heard local radio commentary suggesting the discovery was a hoax.

**Sighting:** The object was said to have been found on July 4, 1950, in a field about 100 yards northwest of the municipal airport at Alice. Initial descriptions characterized it as a small, elliptical contraption about five feet in diameter, freshly painted, and bearing the markings mentioned in the first teletype.

**Investigation:** McEnheimer advised that the object was built by welding together portions of two airplane wings. It had no motor or means of propulsion, and after examination the police concluded it had been constructed by a group of mechanics at the Alice airport as a practical joke. Air Force officials at Ellington Field were notified, and the Bureau closed the matter with no further inquiry. The page set documents a quickly resolved flying-disc hoax rather than a genuine unexplained aerial incident.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI Office Memorandum from the **SAC, Louisville** to the **Director, FBI**, dated **8/2/50** and filed in **62-HQ-83894** with **3 enclosures**. The memo reports on newspaper coverage of a Louisville flying-saucer photograph and states that copies of the newspaper article and photos were being forwarded to FBI Headquarters. The page is marked with administrative stamps and routing notations, indicating bureau circulation rather than a first-hand field report.

**Witness:** **Alf (Al) Hixenbaugh**, identified as a **Louisville Times** staff photographer. The memo says he was out taking bird photos when he observed the object and later provided the film and account to the newspaper and military personnel.

**Sighting:** On **1950-06-27 about 4:15 p.m.**, at **Longest and Everett Avenues near 2205 Longest, Louisville, Kentucky**, Hixenbaugh reported hearing a big plane (described as a **twin-motored DC-3**) overhead, then looking west of the plant and seeing a **large disk**. The object reportedly had a **slight corona**, appeared **lower than the plane**, remained **motionless for about ten seconds**, then **got smaller** and finally **vanished into the west**.

**Object / interpretation:** The memo quotes the newspaper account as saying the object was a bright flying saucer captured on **16 mm movie film**; Hixenbaugh reportedly shot about **50 feet of film**, and the article said the airplane moved out of frame quickly while the saucer remained visible longer. No official conclusion is stated on this page, but the report notes that military officers at **Godman Field** were notified and flight headquarters at **Wright-Patterson Field** were informed. The memo preserves the incident as a contemporaneous press-and-bureau summary of a photographed UFO sighting rather than a completed investigation.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Confidential memo, DIC/17TD No. 4-50, dated 10 February 1950, subject “Unidentified Phenomena.” The page is numbered 2 and summarizes information from enclosures (1) through (8). It appears in FBI case-file material but describes Navy-origin reports from the Kodiak, Alaska area.

**Witnesses:** The primary witness is Lt. L. T. Smith, USN, patrol plane commander of PV/PBY patrol aircraft with Patrol Squadron One. Additional observers include radar operator G. Skeen, USN; Morgan, FTC, USN aboard USS *Tilamook* (ATA-192); Carver, CN, USN; and later Lt. Causer, Lt. Parco, and plane captain Paulson.

**Sighting:** The page describes several related events around Kodiak on 22-23 January 1950. Smith first reported an unidentified radar contact about 20 miles north of NAS Kodiak, then another contact about 10 miles southeast of the station. During the same period he was also involved in a visual/radar encounter in which an object appeared on the radar scope at about 5 miles, then came directly overhead, reportedly suggesting very high speed. He estimated roughly 1,800 mph and said the object maneuvered too quickly for him to intercept or circle.

**Object:** Descriptions vary by observer but include a very fast-moving red light, a “ball of fire” about one foot in diameter, a blip with a tail-like indication on radar, and an airborne object that seemed to open out, turn left, and come up on the aircraft’s quarter. No sound was detected in the shipboard sighting. The object later departed to the southeast. Another patrol the following day reportedly saw an unidentified object on an ascending westerly course for about ten minutes, but could not close with it at 170 knots.

**Assessment:** The report reflects trained military observers, multiple corroborating sightings, and at least some radar involvement, but the page offers no identification or firm conclusion. The observations are brief, inconsistent in appearance, and partly dependent on radar interpretation; the document itself frames them as unexplained phenomena rather than a solved incident.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 机密备忘录，DIC/17TD No. 4-50，日期为 1950年2月10日，主题为“Unidentified Phenomena.”。该页编号为 2，并汇总了附件（1）至（8）中的信息。其出现在 FBI 案卷材料中，但所述内容为来自 Alaska(阿拉斯加) Kodiak(科迪亚克) 地区的海军报告。

**Witnesses:** 主要目击者为 Lt. L. T. Smith, USN，Patrol Squadron One 的 PV/PBY 巡逻机机长。其他观察者包括雷达操作员 G. Skeen, USN；USS *Tilamook* (ATA-192) 舰上的 Morgan, FTC, USN；Carver, CN, USN；以及后来的 Lt. Causer、Lt. Parco 和机长 Paulson。

**Sighting:** 该页描述了 1950年1月22日至23日围绕 Kodiak(科迪亚克) 发生的几起相关事件。Smith 首先报告称，在 NAS Kodiak(科迪亚克海军航空站) 以北约 20 英里处发现一个不明雷达目标，随后又在该站东南约 10 英里处发现另一个目标。在同一期间，他还参与了一次目视/雷达遭遇：一个物体先在约 5 英里处出现在雷达显示器上，随后直接飞越其上空，据称表明其速度极高。他估计速度约为 1,800 mph，并表示该物体机动过快，无法拦截或绕飞。

**Object:** 不同观察者对其描述不尽相同，包括一个高速移动的红色光点、一个直径约一英尺的“火球”、雷达上带有尾迹样指示的回波，以及一个空中物体，看起来会突然展开、左转并向飞机右后方上升靠近。在舰上目击中未探测到任何声音。该物体随后向东南方向离去。次日的另一次巡逻据称在一个上升的向西航向上观察到一个不明物体，持续约十分钟，但在 170 knots 速度下无法追上它。

**Assessment:** 这份报告反映了经过训练的军事观察员、多个相互印证的目击，以及至少一定程度的雷达参与，但该页并未给出任何确认身份或明确结论。所述观察持续时间短、外观描述不一致，且部分依赖雷达解读；文件本身将其定性为无法解释的现象，而非已解决事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page letter on Walter D. Jones letterhead (36 King Street East, Toronto, Ont.) dated **August 29, 1950**, addressed to the **Federal Bureau of Investigation, Washington, D.C.** The page is part of FBI file **62-HQ-83894, Section 5** and is marked with later FBI handling stamps (“Recorded-90,” “Indexed-90”). No continuation or separate report pages are present in the provided sequence.

**Witness:** The author/signatory is **Walter D. Jones**, who states he was observing his farm near Toronto. He writes as a civilian eyewitness and mentions calling over his “houseman” for corroboration. The houseman watched the object for about ten minutes while Jones continued observing it.

**Sighting:** Jones reports that on **July 19 at 10:30 p.m.** he was looking west over his farm. He says the moon was fairly full and there was a low ceiling of light clouds. Through the clouds he saw a **hazy object of light** approaching the farmhouse at **incredible speed**. It circled before reaching the farmhouse and continued circling; Jones says he could not determine its height, orbit, or shape because it was above the clouds and visible only as a “filter of light.” He adds that it sometimes seemed to slow, then circle in the opposite direction.

**Object:** The object is described only as a bright, hazy light with no discernible structure, beam source, or form. Jones estimates total observation time at about **35 minutes** (10:30 p.m. to 11:05 p.m.), with the object disappearing westward.

**Investigation:** Jones states he is passing the information to the FBI “for what it is worth” and suggests discarding it if unwanted. The letter is a straightforward eyewitness report rather than an FBI investigative memorandum. Based on the text alone, the incident remains **unresolved**, with no corroborating measurements, photos, or physical evidence beyond a second witness’s brief observation.

**Document:** One FBI HQ case-file page, marked 62-83894-242, reproduces a handwritten item titled “New Flying Saucer.” The page itself has no visible date, signature, originating field office, classification stamp, or interview header. The right-hand note leaf is numbered “2,” and the text appears to be an anonymous explanatory claim rather than a formal investigative report.

**Sighting:** The only sighting reference is that a “flying saucer” was “seen over south Chicago last april.” No exact day, time, altitude, duration, witness names, or police/press source is given. For cataloging, the event is placed in the South Chicago area in April 1947, with the exact date unknown.

**Object:** The writer asserts that the object was not a military secret and was not yet owned by any government. It is described as a large, flat fuel or gas tank with “crystal glass wings,” two large jet engines on both sides, and radio control. The note says the wings could not be seen on a clear day, making the craft resemble a saucer in flight and supposedly making it difficult for anti-aircraft gunners to target. The claimed purpose of the large tank was long range for atomic bombing.

**Claims/Analysis:** The note names several alleged private designers or associates, including a Fred with an uncertain surname, Frank Hoechpaw/Hochpaw as an aircraft mechanic, and Carl Eichman/Dickman described as a German World War I ace, and further claims financing by Howard Hughes. **Sighting:** The newspaper account says Hildebrand reported a disc- or saucer-shaped object in the Roscoe, South Dakota area on or about June 27, 1950. The object is described in the usual 1950 press language as a "flying saucer" and appears to have been seen visually and/or photographed. The surviving page does not preserve a precise time, altitude, range, or duration, but the tone suggests a local daylight or near-dusk observation.

**Investigation:** This page is a clipping summary, not a technical analysis. It records provenance through the Roosevelt Times article and subsequent FBI filing, but provides no chain of custody for any photograph and no conclusion beyond archival notice. Based on the page alone, the event is best treated as a civilian flying-saucer claim from rural South Dakota that the FBI retained for reference rather than a substantiated UFO identification.

**Document:** A torn handwritten letter on ruled paper, addressed To the F.B.I. and filed in FBI HQ flying-disc file 62-HQ-83894. **Witness:** The writer is not identified on the surviving page. He describes his truck, going to work, and later pulling out on a trip, so the witness is best treated as an unidentified civilian truck driver/correspondent. He says he is answering an FBI letter and is writing to the best of his memory, indicating a retrospective recollection rather than a contemporaneous official statement.

**Sighting:** The claimed event occurred in Oak Park, Illinois, at about 6:29 a.m. on July 20/50. The witness says his truck was parked under a large ash tree. He states that he ran off, left the truck, and called the Oak Park, Illinois Police.

The witness adds that about a month later, at about 9:30 p.m., he found a note on the truck seat and took it to local police. As he remembered it, the note referred to a piece of paper from the saucer, told him to leave it where the right party could get it, and said the saucer was not meant for him; a second paper allegedly mentioned maps of a big city and an atomic plant. The page provides no corroboration or analytical finding, and the unusual note narrative leaves the report unverified.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), dated October 2, 1950, from the SAC, Philadelphia, to the Director, FBI, attention Mr. Leo Laughlin. Subject line: “Flying Disc Reported at Philadelphia on 9/26/50.” The page carries FBI routing and later handling marks, including a note that the matter was referred to Air Force Intelligence and then to OSI, with no further FBI action taken.

**Witness:** The report is based on two Philadelphia police officers on duty, described as observing the incident firsthand in the late evening hours of September 26, 1950. No individual names are given in this memo, so the witness set is limited to their official role and agency.

**Sighting:** While on Vare Boulevard near 26th Street in Philadelphia, the officers saw a round object about six feet in circumference slowly float down to the ground. It reportedly had the appearance of a parachute and came to rest in a field without depressing the weeds, suggesting it was extremely light. The object was described as lavender in color and “dewy,” “sort of like soap suds,” and it evaporated within 15 to 20 minutes after landing. When touched by the officers, the substance disappeared, leaving only a slight sticky residue.

**Assessment / provenance:** The memo states the report was made to the FBI by the Philadelphia Police and later appeared in the Philadelphia press under the headline “Flying Saucer Just Dissolves.” The language of the report strongly suggests a transient foam-like or soap-suds-like material rather than a conventional metallic craft, and the memo records no definitive identification. The FBI treated it as a field report to be passed to Air Force Intelligence, not as an active FBI investigation.

**Sighting:** 在费城Vare Boulevard靠近26th Street附近，两名警官看到一个周长约六英尺的圆形物体缓慢飘落到地面。据称其外观像一顶降落伞，最终停在一片田地里，但并未压倒杂草，这表明它极其轻盈。该物体被描述为薰衣草色，且“带露水感”， “有点像肥皂泡沫”，并在着陆后15到20分钟内蒸发消失。警官触碰该物质时，它便消失了，只留下少量黏性残留物。

Because the entries are brief and appear to represent several separate observations rather than one continuous craft encounter, the best catalog interpretation is a Camp Hood sightings summary covering multiple transient light events across 6-7 Mar 1949. The document preserves raw observation data but does not establish whether the lights were aircraft, meteors, flares, or another source.

**Document:** Confidential continuation page from the FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 6, titled "Summary of Sightings of Unknown Aerial Phenomena, 17th District OSI (cont)," page 37. The page is a tabular OSI summary rather than a narrative report, and it records several separate UFO sightings in the Albuquerque, New Mexico area. No handwritten signer is visible on this page.

**Witnesses:** The entries list unnamed observers only. The table shows one observer for cases 200-202, four observers for case 203, and eleven observers for case 204. The witnesses are described only as military personnel/observers at Sandia Base and Kirtland AFB; no individual names appear on the page.

**Sightings:** On 21 Mar 1950 at Sandia Base, one observer reported two silver objects moving E to SW at about 45° above the horizon for 10 minutes, no sound, round, dime-sized at arm's length, and "excessive" jet-like speed before fading gradually from view. Another Sandia report that day described a pair of objects, varying from shiny silver to shady gray, moving NE to SE at 40,000-60,000 feet for 30 minutes, round, thumb-tip sized, and disappearing like a jet aircraft. A third Sandia observation at 1315 noted a white round object due east at 75° above the horizon for 5 minutes, smaller than a fist, at an estimated 600-700 mph, vanishing from visual range. At Kirtland AFB, four observers saw a bright silver round object traveling SE to S in a zig-zag up-and-down path for about a minute, while eleven observers later reported a tan-brown flying-wing object moving NW to N at 25,000-30,000 feet for 5-6 seconds.

**Assessment:** The page presents a cluster of short-duration airborne observations with no sound, no trail, and rapid disappearance, recorded by a military intelligence/OSI office. The report style is administrative and comparative, suggesting these were compiled sightings rather than a single coordinated incident. The table's evaluation column indicates these were treated as unexplained/unknown aerial phenomena.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI memorandum dated November 24, 1950, from J. Edgar Hoover, Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, to the Director of Special Investigations, Office of the Inspector General, Department of the Air Force, Pentagon. The page is marked as an FBI file item in case 62-HQ-83894 (red notation and routing stamps), and it summarizes a field report received by the New Haven FBI office.

**Witness:** Aaron L. Hitchens, a chemical engineer in charge of the Chemical and Physical Laboratories at Winchester Repeating Arms Company, reported the event after telling the FBI that he and his wife and daughter observed it from their home at 495 Edgewood Avenue, New Haven. The narrative suggests a credible, professional adult witness, with two family members present as additional observers.

**Sighting:** On Friday, October 20, 1950, at about 6:15 p.m., Hitchens and his family went into the backyard when his young daughter noticed a moving star. Hitchens then saw a sphere-like object directly overhead, giving off a steady golden-orange glow. He estimated it to be very high, between 10,000 and 20,000 feet or possibly higher. The glow did not blink or flicker, and the whole sphere appeared to glow with the same steadiness. He watched it for about 20 seconds as it moved westward toward New York City, then veered southward as if crossing Long Island, before disappearing behind trees.

**Object:** Hitchens compared its apparent size to roughly ten times the diameter of Venus, which he said was shining brightly that night. He noted a clear sky with twinkling stars, but the object itself did not twinkle and did not seem to shrink as it moved away, maintaining about the same apparent size.

**Investigation:** The page contains no resolution or identification of the object; it is a forwarded incident summary from the New Haven FBI office to the Air Force. Based on the report alone, the object remained unidentified and was described in classic early-1950 UFO terms as a luminous, starlike sphere with steady light and unusual movement.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** Aaron L. Hitchens（艾伦·L·希琴斯），Winchester Repeating Arms Company 的化学工程师，负责该公司的化学与物理实验室。他在向FBI说明自己与妻子、女儿从位于 New Haven 的 495 Edgewood Avenue 的家中目睹了该事件后，报告了这一情况。叙述显示，他是一名可信、专业的成年目击者，另有两名家庭成员作为补充观察者在场。

**Sighting:** 1950年10月20日星期五，约下午6:15，Hitchens 与家人走到后院时，他年幼的女儿先注意到一颗移动的星星。随后，Hitchens 看见一个类似球体的物体正位于头顶正上方，发出稳定的金橙色光芒。他估计其高度很高，在 10,000 到 20,000 英尺之间，甚至可能更高。该光芒没有闪烁或明灭不定，整个球体看起来都以同样稳定的方式发光。他观察了大约 20 秒，看到它向西移动，朝 New York City（纽约市）方向飞去，随后又像是穿过 Long Island（长岛）般转向南方，之后消失在树后。

**Object:** Hitchens 将其表观大小比作大约是 Venus（金星）直径的 10 倍；他还说当晚金星非常明亮。他注意到天空晴朗、群星闪烁，但该物体本身并不闪烁，也没有在远离时显得缩小，而是始终保持着大致相同的表观大小。

**Investigation:** 该页未包含对该物体的结论或识别结果；它只是纽黑文FBI办公室转交给空军的一份事件摘要。仅根据这份报告，该物体仍未被确认身份，并以20世纪50年代初典型的UFO术语被描述为一个发光、类似星体的球状物，具有稳定的光亮和异常的运动方式。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Communications Section teletype from SAC, Knoxville, to the Director, FBI, marked **URGENT** and dated Oct. 13, 1950. The page is part of FBI file **62-HQ-83894, Section 6**, with the report signed off **ROBEY** and routed for acknowledgement and hold. The text describes a radar incident over Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and is the only page needed for this event.

**Witness:** The report is based on **USAF radar installation personnel** at Knoxville, whose track was later checked by Air Force and AEC personnel. No individual witness names appear on the page; the reporting channel is the Knoxville FBI office, relaying military radar observations to headquarters.

**Sighting:** At **11:25 PM EST on Oct. 12, 1950**, the radar station near Knoxville picked up indications of **11 objects, and perhaps more**, moving across the controlled area of the Atomic Energy installation at Oak Ridge. The objects were reported at **1,000 to 5,000 feet altitude**, on courses **from south-southeast to southeast**, with radar-derived size estimates comparable to a **C-47** and speeds of **100 to 125 mph**. A fighter plane attempted interception within minutes; radar contact was briefly reflected, but the pilot reported **no object visible visually or on his radar screen**. An **AEC patrol** was also alerted, but no objects were seen.

**Investigation / assessment:** The teletype states that **OSI and Eastern Air Defense Forces** had been advised and were checking the incident. It emphasizes that the radar operators were experienced personnel and that the radar set was in **perfect operating condition**, yet **no reasonable explanation** for the radar readings had been developed at the time of reporting. The document is therefore a contemporaneous, unexplained radar-track report rather than a confirmed visual sighting.

**Document:** FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 6, in a typed memo headed “Letter to the Director” and dated 11/9/50. This page is the continuation of a report on a flying-disc sighting; no later page shown here appears to describe a different incident.

**Witness:** Mr. Hitchens, described by the Bureau as a chemical engineer with 15 years of research and development experience. He said he was not a pilot but had considerable flying experience and had read technical material on flying saucers and discs. The Bureau noted that he appeared reliable, sincere, and technically knowledgeable.

**Sighting:** Hitchens reported seeing a complete circular ball with no attachments or projections. He said it left no trail and had no odors associated with it. He could not determine the propulsion method, but observed that when it changed direction it appeared to back up and go forward two or three times. He estimated its speed at roughly 400 to 700 mph, depending on height, and said it may have been about ten times the diameter of Venus as seen in the sky. No clouds were present to obscure the view, and he could not say whether the object went through or around clouds.

**Witnesses/Context:** Hitchens said his wife and daughter also saw the object. His wife ran to neighbors in the same house, but by the time they got outside the object had disappeared.

**Investigation:** The Bureau advised Hitchens that the information would be passed to another agency, with his approval, and he specifically requested no public announcement or comment. The report does not identify the object and offers no analytical conclusion beyond noting Hitchens’ apparent credibility and the technical detail of his account.

**Sighting:** Hitchens报告称，他看到一个完整的圆球，没有任何附属物或突起。他说它没有留下尾迹，也没有任何相关气味。他无法确定其推进方式，但观察到当它改变方向时，似乎会向后退一下，再向前移动两到三次。他估计其速度约为400 to 700 mph，具体取决于高度，并称它可能大约是空中所见Venus直径的十倍。当时没有云层遮挡视线，他也无法判断该物体是穿过云层还是绕过云层飞行。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI-file newspaper clipping from the Denver Post, headed “(Saucer),” with later file stamps including 62-HQ-83894 / 162-83894. The clipping says Robinson sent the paper a copy of a mimeographed AEC form he used to report the object; it also notes that the AEC had standardized forms for “reports of unidentified aerial objects at Los Alamos.”

**Witness:** Lee Robinson, described as a Denver construction worker employed by Armex Construction Company at Los Alamos, NM. He is presented as the principal observer; the article adds that eight other Armex employees also saw the object.

**Sighting:** Robinson said the sighting occurred on Sept. 12, 1950, while he and the others were eating lunch in the Los Alamos area over a highly restricted part of the atomic-energy project. He reported an unidentified aerial object passing over the site. He stated it was not a balloon or a conventional aircraft, estimated it at about 20,000 feet, and said it alternated between bright and black at roughly two-second intervals. The object remained visible for about 3 minutes and 40 seconds.

**Assessment:** The page contains no separate investigative conclusion beyond the reported witness statement. Its value is mainly documentary: it shows that Los Alamos/AEC maintained a formal reporting system for unidentified aerial objects and that the FBI file preserved a contemporaneous press account of one such report.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Communications Section teletype from Washington, D.C., to the SAC in Knoxville, marked **URGENT** and signed **HOOVER**. The page is dated 12-5-50, 4:47 PM, and carries FBI file references including 62-HQ-83894 / 162-83894. It orders immediate follow-up on a reported incident affecting a sensitive national-defense area.

**Witness:** No individual witness is named on this page. The message refers generally to an incident at/near Oak Ridge, implying reporting from local radar or installation personnel connected with the area’s protection of vital installations.

**Sighting:** HQ refers to a prior report from **December 4** concerning possible **radar jamming** at Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and to the **detection of unidentified objects over the Oak Ridge area**. The teletype asks whether an incident **northeast of Oliver Springs, Tennessee** could be related. No object shape, color, altitude, duration, or motion details are provided here.

**Investigation:** The Bureau directed Knoxville to obtain all facts concerning possible radar jamming, including whether the effect could have been caused by **ionization of particles in the atmosphere**. The document shows that FBI headquarters treated the matter as potentially serious because of Oak Ridge’s importance, but it does not state any final conclusion or identify the objects. This page is the operative event record; no additional pages were provided for this incident.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This single page is an FBI transmittal memorandum from the Special Agent in Charge, Knoxville, to the Director, FBI, dated November 4, 1950. It is filed under the Oak Ridge matter in case file 62-HQ-83894 (stamped on the page) and concerns “Detection of Unidentified Objects at Oak Ridge, October 20, 23, 24, 26, 1950” under the heading “Protection of Vital Installations.” The page is a cover sheet only; it states that enclosed are copies of CIC reports and that additional information would be forwarded as received. Handwritten and stamp annotations include “Flying Saucers,” later file-control marks, and an “original copy filed” stamp.

**Witness:** No named civilian witness appears on this page. The only source identified is CIC reporting from Oak Ridge personnel/observers, implying military counterintelligence observation at or near the Oak Ridge installation.

**Sighting:** The memo lists multiple dates of observation—October 20, 23, 24, and 26, 1950—at Oak Ridge, Tennessee, but gives no times, bearings, altitude, duration, or object description on this page. Because the document refers to “unidentified objects” rather than a single event, the safest interpretation is a clustered series of sightings at the same secure site over several nights.

**Object:** No physical or visual characteristics are described here beyond the generic label “unidentified objects.” The page does not state whether the reports involved lights, discs, aircraft-like shapes, or radar returns.

**Investigation:** The FBI Knoxville office was acting as a conduit for CIC material concerning a vital-installations security issue. This page alone does not permit a substantive technical assessment, but it shows that the Oak Ridge sightings were considered serious enough for Bureau handling and follow-up. The likely analytical significance is the association with a sensitive atomic-energy installation rather than any conclusion about the objects themselves.

**Sighting:** On **24 Feb 1950 at 1400**, the witness reported an object near **Albuquerque, New Mexico**, seen about **20° above the horizon** and moving **east by southeast**. The listed course field is otherwise blank. The object was seen for **20–30 seconds**.

**Object:** The table describes a **bright white, round** object with **no trail/trail-like train**, **no sound**, and **very slow** apparent speed. The only analytical clue given by the compiler is the weather-balloon size comparison; the table does not state a firm identification or conclusion.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum No. 64, from the SAC, Chicago (file 100-18999) to the Director, FBI (62-83894), dated March 21, 1952, subject “Flying Discs – Karl Nyquist, Informant.” The page is stamped declassified and bears routing/record stamps showing it was recorded and indexed in the Bureau’s files. The memorandum was written by SA Myron H. Treter (MHT:BJB) after speaking with the witness and forwarding the report and sketch to the local Office of Special Investigations.

**Witness:** Karl Nyquist, identified as an artist living at 2417 North Burling Street, Chicago, Illinois, told SA Treter on March 11, 1952 about a sighting he said occurred at 9:00 AM on March 6, 1952. He is described as a civilian informant, not a trained observer, but he gave a detailed narrative and produced a sketch.

**Sighting:** Nyquist said he was looking south from a window in his home when he saw a flying disc approximately 7,000 feet above Fullerton Avenue, with an elevation angle of about 45 degrees. He reported the object emerged from a cloud in the east, paused motionless for a split second, then flew due south at great speed and vanished in about three seconds. He estimated the speed at 600–700 mph or more.

**Object:** The disc was described as circular, about six feet in diameter, white with a bluish tinge, and appearing to be made of a metal similar to aluminum. Nyquist reported no exhaust, no lights, and no sound. He also said nothing was visible to explain how it maintained flight and believed it may have been radio controlled. When it disappeared, he said it was about the size of a golf ball on the southern horizon.

**Investigation:** The memo preserves the report as received; it does not record a Bureau conclusion, but it notes that Nyquist’s sketch and information were furnished to the local Office of Special Investigations.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI办公室备忘录第64号，由芝加哥(SAC, Chicago)办公室（file 100-18999）致FBI局长（62-83894），日期为1952年3月21日，主题为“Flying Discs – Karl Nyquist, Informant.” 该页盖有解密印章，并带有传阅/登记印记，显示其已被记录并编入局档案。该备忘录由特工SA Myron H. Treter（MHT:BJB）在与目击者交谈后撰写，并将报告和草图转送至当地的特别调查办公室(Office of Special Investigations)。

**Witness:** Karl Nyquist，被确认是一名居住在伊利诺伊州芝加哥(Chicago, Illinois)2417 North Burling Street的艺术家，他于1952年3月11日告诉SA Treter，自己于1952年3月6日上午9:00曾目击到一起事件。他被描述为一名平民线人，并非受过训练的观察者，但他提供了详细叙述并绘制了草图。

**Sighting:** Nyquist称，当时他正从家中的一扇窗户向南望去，看见一个飞碟位于Fullerton Avenue上空约7,000英尺处，仰角约45度。他报告称，该物体从东边的一朵云中出现，静止了不到一瞬间，随后以极快速度正向南飞去，并在约三秒内消失。他估计其速度为600–700 mph或更快。

**Object:** 该圆盘被描述为圆形，直径约六英尺，呈白色并带有淡蓝色调，看上去像由类似铝的金属制成。Nyquist称未看到任何尾气、灯光或声音。他还表示，看不出它如何维持飞行，并认为它可能是无线电控制的。它消失时，他说其在南部地平线上看起来只有高尔夫球大小。

**Investigation:** 这份备忘录如实保存了收到的报告；其中未记录局方结论，但注明Nyquist的草图和信息已提供给当地的特别调查办公室(Office of Special Investigations)。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), from SAC Memphis (62-0) to the Director, FBI, dated 4-3-52, subject line "Unknown Subject; Flying Objects, Nashville, Tennessee" / "Information Concerning Flying Discs." The page records an oral report given to SA Charles J. Honetor of the Nashville Resident Agency and forwarded for information only; the memo states that no action was contemplated unless otherwise directed.

**Witness:** Lt. Commander Melvin Michael Kuhn, U.S. Navy, temporarily residing at 1900 Graybar Lane, Nashville, Tennessee. His position and service background make him a comparatively credible observer, though the report is still a single-witness sighting with no corroborating witnesses mentioned.

**Sighting:** On March 13, 1952, at about 10:20 p.m., while standing in the backyard of 1900 Graybar Lane and looking toward the moon in the southwest sky, Kuhn saw an object about 20 degrees above the horizon. He said it was circular, roughly half the size of the moon, and deep bright blue or very vivid blue, with a slight reddish fringe at the aft end. He estimated it moved from northwest to southeast, remained visible no more than three seconds, and made no sound. He noted clear skies, stars out, and a full moon.

**Assessment:** Kuhn compared the appearance to a very high-powered spotlight on a cloud, but rejected that explanation because he saw no spotlight or strong search lights in the area that evening. The memo contains no technical analysis, only a transmittal of the witness account to FBI headquarters. Based on the text, the incident remains unidentified and undocumented beyond the witness narrative.

**Witness:** U.S. Navy少尉指挥官（Lt. Commander）Melvin Michael Kuhn，暂住于1900 Graybar Lane, Nashville, Tennessee。其职位和服役背景使其相对而言属于较为可信的目击者，但该报告仍是一份单一目击者陈述，未提及任何可相互印证的目击者。

**Sighting:** 1952年3月13日晚上约10:20，Kuhn站在1900 Graybar Lane的后院，朝向西南天空中的月亮望去时，看到一个位于地平线以上约20度的物体。他称其为圆形，大小约为月亮的一半，呈深亮蓝色或非常鲜艳的蓝色，在其后端带有一圈轻微的红色边缘。他估计该物体从西北向东南移动，持续可见不超过3秒，且没有任何声音。他还注明当时天空晴朗、群星可见，并且是一轮满月。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Savannah sent an **urgent teletype** to the Director, FBI, on **May 12, 1952** (Communications Section; file context in **62-HQ-83894, Section 6**). The page is stamped “TELETYPE” and appears to be **page one** of the report. No later page from the same incident was provided here.

**Witness:** The report names **four last employees of DuPont Co.** working on the **Savannah River Plant near Ellenton, S.C.** as the observers. The source is indirect, relayed through FBI Savannah, but the account is presented as an employee sighting rather than rumor.

**Sighting:** At about **10:45 PM on May 10, 1952**, the employees saw **four disc-shaped objects** approaching the **Four Hundred Area from the south** and disappearing to the north. Around **11:05 PM**, they reportedly saw **two similar objects** approach from the south and leave northward. At about **11:10 PM**, one similar object came from the northeast and disappeared toward the southwest. Another object was seen at about **11:15 PM** traveling south to north.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed FBI case-file continuation page from 62-HQ-83894, Section 6, p. 2. The page is mid-report and does not show the original heading or report date, but it clearly continues a single witness statement about a 1947 flying-object sighting. No separate later incident appears on this page.

**Witness:** Mr. Hitchens is described as a chemical engineer with about fifteen years of research-and-development experience. He was not a pilot, but had done considerable flying and had also read technical material on flying saucers and discs. He told investigators he was familiar with astronomy and did not confuse the object with Venus.

**Sighting:** Hitchens reported a bright orange object seen directly overhead and then over New York City. He said the glow stayed steady the entire time, the object made no sound, and there were no visible attachments, projections, odors, or trail. He described it as a complete circular ball. He believed it was far enough away that he would have lost sight of it shortly once it moved behind nearby trees.

**Object / motion:** He estimated the object’s speed at roughly 400–700 mph, depending on altitude, which he could not measure precisely. He said it appeared to change direction, possibly over New York City, and seemed to back up and move forward two or three times while doing so. He also compared its apparent size to Venus, estimating it as about ten times Venus’s diameter.

**Investigation:** Hitchens said his wife and daughter also saw it, but neighbors whom his wife summoned did not get outside in time. The page contains no analytical conclusion beyond the witness’s own estimate and the interviewer’s transcription; the FBI record preserves the account as a civilian sighting report rather than a confirmed identification.

**Object / motion:** 他估计该物体的速度约为 400–700 mph，具体取决于高度，而这一点他无法精确测量。他说该物体似乎改变了方向，可能是在 New York City 上空，并且在此过程中看起来向后退又向前移动了两到三次。他还将其表观大小与 Venus 作比较，估计其直径大约是 Venus 的十倍。

**Investigation:** Hitchens 说他的妻子和女儿也看到了它，但他妻子叫来的邻居没能及时到外面来看。除证人本人的估计和采访者的记录外，该页没有其他分析性结论；FBI 记录将这一说法保留为一份民间目击报告，而非已证实的识别结果。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 6. The first page is an Office Memorandum from the SAC, Indianapolis (62-0), to the Director, FBI, dated July 31, 1952. The following page is the same report recopied as a letter dated August 11, 1952 from J. Edgar Hoover to Mr. Glenn H. Bethel, c/o the Commissioner, Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Ottawa. Both pages describe the same incident and should be treated as one event record.

**Witness:** Dr. R. E. McIndoo of 820 West Walnut Street, Kokomo, Indiana, reported the sighting on July 30, 1952 to Special Agent John F. Gerdis. His account was considered credible enough to be forwarded; the memo notes he was referred to the FBI by Donald D. Smith, president of the First National Bank of Kokomo, who said McIndoo had a good reputation.

**Sighting:** On July 27, 1952, at about 10:00 A.M., while fishing in the back waters of Thessalon Lake, Ontario, Canada, McIndoo said he saw a formation of 16 to 20 "bombing planes" in two groups flying south at an estimated height of four or five miles. As the planes passed over the lake, they suddenly dropped objects he first thought were parachutes. He said the objects fell straight down briefly, then emitted vapor and sped off to the southwest.

**Object:** McIndoo could not identify the nationality of the planes. He said the aircraft carried twin trails of bluish smoke, while the dropped objects had a single trail of bluish smoke. He also noted that Paul Gaddis of Kokomo accompanied him on the fishing trip but had no further details.

**Investigation:** The FBI recorded and indexed the matter and stated that no further action would be taken. The report was forwarded for Bureau information in case the Air Force wished to contact the witness. The file is cataloged under the classic early UFO correspondence heading "Flying Saucer(s) Seen Near Thessalon Lake, Ontario, Canada, July 27, 1952."
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 来自 Indiana 州 Kokomo 市 West Walnut Street 820 号的 Dr. R. E. McIndoo 于 1952年7月30日向 Special Agent John F. Gerdis 报告了这一目击。他的陈述被认为足够可信，因而被上报；备忘录注明，他是由 First National Bank of Kokomo 行长 Donald D. Smith 转介给 FBI 的，Smith 说 McIndoo 信誉良好。

**Sighting:** 1952年7月27日，大约上午 10:00，McIndoo 在 Canada, Ontario 的 Thessalon Lake 后湖区钓鱼时称，他看到一队由 16 到 20 架“轰炸机”组成的编队，分成两组，正以估计四到五英里的高度向南飞行。当这些飞机掠过湖面上空时，它们突然投下了他起初以为是降落伞的物体。他说，这些物体先是笔直下坠了一小段，随后冒出蒸汽，并迅速向西南方向飞去。

**Object:** McIndoo 无法辨认这些飞机的国籍。他说，这些飞行器拖着两道蓝灰色烟迹，而投下的物体则只有一道蓝灰色烟迹。他还提到，Kokomo 的 Paul Gaddis 与他一同参加了这次钓鱼，但没有提供更多细节。

**Investigation:** FBI 对此事进行了记录和索引，并表示不会采取进一步行动。该报告已转交供 Bureau 备查，以便 Air Force 如有需要可联系该目击者。该档案归入早期经典 UFO 通信标题“Flying Saucer(s) Seen Near Thessalon Lake, Ontario, Canada, July 27, 1952.” 下。

**Investigation/Disposition:** The FBI memorandum states that Bureau indices contained no information identifiable with Winchester. No corroborating evidence is mentioned, and the case was simply marked “Action: File.” The overall handling suggests the Bureau treated it as an unverified complaint rather than a substantiated UFO incident, with the most likely explanation being storm-related lightning or another natural electrical phenomenon, possibly compounded by the witness’s condition and newspaper influence.

**Witness:** 本页未列出主要证人姓名。措辞表明这是一位能够判断**速度和高度**的证人，说明其可能是机组成员，或其他能够清楚观察天空的目击者。

**Sighting:** 缺失的第一页很可能包含一则关于空中物体事件报告的开头细节。在本页中，对目击者陈述的概述称，这些物体**“似乎保持着总体航向”**，并且由于其速度和高度，**仅在几秒钟内可见**。这些措辞暗示的是**多个不明空中物体**，而非单一目标。

**Investigation:** 此处未给出任何识别或解释，本页也未显示 Savannah office 进行过正式的本地调查。该报告似乎是作为行政情报转交至 FBI 总部，而非作为正在积极处理的案件。由于仅能看到第二页，具体事件日期及证人身份无法仅凭此图像还原。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Page 0178 is a press-clipping page in FBI HQ file 62-HQ-83894, Section 6. The UFO item is a Sunday Graphic article dated July 6, 1952, by Antony Terry from Berlin, headlined “50 Yards Away I Saw Two Men Take Off in a ‘Flying Saucer.’” No FBI investigative memorandum, classification stamp, or Bureau analytical conclusion is visible on this page; it preserves a newspaper account of a sworn statement being reviewed by Western/West Berlin officials.

**Witness:** The principal witness is Oskar Linke, described as a 48-year-old ex-mayor from Gleimershausen near Meiningen who had escaped from the Russian zone with his wife and six children. The article says Linke and his 11-year-old stepdaughter Gabriele gave a solemn affidavit before a judge, increasing the reported evidentiary value of the account.

**Sighting:** Linke stated that on June 17, 1950, while riding a motorcycle with Gabriele as passenger near Hasselbach, a tire problem caused them to stop. In the half-light Gabriele pointed out something roughly 150 yards away. Linke first thought it was a deer, then approached to about 60 yards and eventually to about 30 feet behind a ridge.

**Object:** Linke reported two human-like figures wearing a shimmering metallic substance, bending near a large oval object he compared to a “warming pan.” He estimated it at roughly 40–50 feet across, with rows of holes along the sides and a black cylindrical “conning tower” about 10 feet high. When Gabriele called out, the figures hurried into the object. Linke said the craft emitted changing green-to-red light and a humming sound, the conning tower retracted, and the object rose and departed toward Stockheim.

**Investigation:** The article says other local people later reported seeing what they thought was a comet-like object, and Linke claimed he found a fresh circular depression where the craft had stood. A sidebar quoted Vickers aircraft designer George Edwards as saying the described machine did not resemble known conventional aircraft, though vertical takeoff was conceptually possible. The page presents the case as possible evidence of a secret Soviet “flying saucer,” but contains no FBI finding validating the report.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 第0178页是 FBI HQ 文件 62-HQ-83894 第6部分中的一页新闻剪报。该 UFO 条目为一篇刊登于 1952年7月6日《Sunday Graphic》的文章，作者 Antony Terry，发自 Berlin，标题为“50 Yards Away I Saw Two Men Take Off in a ‘Flying Saucer.’”。该页未显示任何 FBI 调查备忘录、分类印章或局方分析结论；其内容保留了一则关于一份宣誓陈述正在由 Western/West Berlin 官员审阅的报纸报道。

**Witness:** 主要证人为 Oskar Linke，文中称其为来自 Meiningen 附近 Gleimershausen 的48岁前市长，他与妻子及六个孩子已从 Russian zone 逃出。文章称，Linke 及其11岁的继女 Gabriele 在法官面前作了正式宣誓书，从而提高了该说法所述证据的分量。

**Sighting:** Linke 说，1950年6月17日，他骑摩托车载着 Gabriele 经过 Hasselbach 附近时，因轮胎出问题而停下。在微光中，Gabriele 指出约150 yards外的一个东西。Linke 起初以为那是一头鹿，随后走近到约60 yards，最后又前进到一道山脊后方约30 feet处。

**Object:** Linke 报告称，有两个类似人形的身影穿着闪亮的金属物质，弯身站在一个大型椭圆形物体旁，他将其比作一个“warming pan”。他估计该物体直径约40–50 feet，侧面排列着一行行孔洞，并有一个约10 feet高的黑色圆柱形“conning tower”。当 Gabriele 喊叫时，这两个身影迅速进入该物体。Linke 说，这个飞行器发出由绿转红的变换光芒和嗡嗡声，conning tower 便缩回，物体随后升空并朝 Stockheim 方向离去。

**Investigation:** 文章称，后来其他当地人也报告看见过他们以为是彗星般的物体，而 Linke 则声称他在飞行器停放处发现了一个新鲜的圆形凹痕。侧栏引用 Vickers 飞机设计师 George Edwards 的话称，所描述的机器并不像已知的常规飞机，不过从概念上讲，垂直起飞是可能的。该页将此案呈现为某种秘密 Soviet “flying saucer” 的可能证据，但未包含任何验证该报告的 FBI 结论。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page typewritten letter dated **Portland, Oregon, August 20, 1947**, preserved in FBI file **62-HQ-83894, Section 3** and stamped **CONFIDENTIAL**. It is addressed to **Lt. Col. Donald L. Springer, Assistant Staff**. The page bears a later **A TRUE COPY** endorsement signed by Springer, indicating this is a retained file copy rather than the original outgoing letter.

**Witness:** The author identifies himself as **F. M. Johnson**, a **prospector** living at **106 No. West 1st Ave, Portland, Oregon**. He says he was in the **Mt. Adams district** on **June 24, 1947**, the same day Kenneth Arnold reported his now-famous sighting near the Cascade range.

**Sighting:** Johnson states he saw “the same flying objects” at about the same time Arnold did. He says he used a **telescope** and is certain the objects were real. He reports they passed **very high** overhead, probably around **1,000 feet** above him, making no sound like an airplane. He describes them as **round**, about **30 feet in diameter**, tapering sharply to a point, with an **oval shape** and a **bright top surface**. The rear or tail end allegedly looked like “a big hand of a clock shifting from side to side like a big magnet.” He says their speed seemed greater than anything he had ever seen and that the last view showed them “standing on edge” while **banking in a cloud**.

**Assessment:** This is a contemporaneous eyewitness letter tying the observation to the **Kenneth Arnold** wave of 1947 reports. The account is detailed but subjective, with no supporting witnesses or measurements beyond the observer’s estimate. The page appears to be the complete report for this incident; no later page in the provided sequence indicates a different event.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 一封单页打字信件，日期为 **Portland, Oregon, August 20, 1947**，存于 FBI 档案 **62-HQ-83894, Section 3**，并盖有 **CONFIDENTIAL** 印章。收信人为 **Lt. Col. Donald L. Springer, Assistant Staff**。该页后附有 **A TRUE COPY** 的较晚期背书，并由 Springer 签名，表明这是一份留存的档案副本，而非原始发出的信件。

**Witness:** 作者自称为 **F. M. Johnson**，是一名居住在 **106 No. West 1st Ave, Portland, Oregon** 的 **prospector**。他表示自己于 **June 24, 1947** 在 **Mt. Adams district**，也就是 Kenneth Arnold 报告其如今广为人知的目击事件的同一天，当时地点靠近喀斯喀特山脉（Cascade range）。

**Sighting:** Johnson 说他在与 Arnold 大致相同的时间看到了“相同的飞行物”。他称自己使用了 **telescope**，并确信这些物体是真实存在的。他报告说，这些物体从他头顶 **very high** 地方飞过，大约在他上方 **1,000 feet** 处，发出的声音不像飞机。他将其描述为 **round**，直径约 **30 feet**，并且迅速收尖成一点，呈 **oval shape**，顶部表面 **bright top surface**。据称，其后部或尾端看起来像“一个大钟表的时针在左右摆动，就像一个大磁铁一样”。他表示，这些物体的速度似乎超过他所见过的任何东西，最后看到它们时，它们正 **standing on edge**，并在 **banking in a cloud**。

**Assessment:** 这是一封与 **Kenneth Arnold** 1947 年目击事件浪潮相关的同时代目击者信件。该叙述细节丰富，但带有主观性，除观察者的估计外，没有其他支持性证人或测量数据。此页似乎就是该事件的完整报告；所提供的后续页面序列中没有显示不同事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Confidential memo labeled "LAF-1205-I" and dated 9 September 1947, headed "Memorandum for the Officer in Charge" and signed by Leslie S. Hubbard, S/A, CIC ADC LAF. The page records an interview conducted 8 September 1947 at Stewart’s workplace, the Hearst Mining Building, University of California, Berkeley.

**Witness:** Ward L. Stewart, 1242 Milvia Street, Berkeley, stated he was a 1st lieutenant in the Reserve and a former U.S. Army Air Forces officer with considerable flying experience, including service as a B-29 pilot. The agent noted that Stewart did not appear to be the type to imagine sightings and had no apparent desire for publicity.

**Sighting:** Stewart reported that on 29 July 1947, shortly after 12 noon, he was with Captain William H. Ryherd of the 415th AAF BU (RT) after a routine training flight. As they landed and were on preliminary approach to Hamilton Field, Ryherd pointed out an unidentified flying object trailing a P-80 aircraft. Stewart estimated the P-80 was flying about 250 mph and said the object was moving at roughly three to four times that speed. A second object then appeared and moved in a course resembling a fighter’s maneuver when accompanying heavier aircraft, a left-to-right motion over the first object.

**Object:** Stewart said the objects were milky white, unlike any conventional aircraft he had seen. He estimated the action lasted about 15 seconds, the course covered about 120 degrees, and the objects remained beyond 6,000 feet; he could not estimate their size or actual altitude. He added that the objects were not Navy "flapjacks".

**Investigation:** The report is an intelligence-style interview summary rather than a full technical analysis. The file preserves the witness’s account and the agent’s credibility assessment, but it offers no definitive identification or conclusion beyond documenting the observation near Hamilton Field.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 标注为“LAF-1205-I”的机密备忘录，日期为1947年9月9日，标题为“Memorandum for the Officer in Charge”，由Leslie S. Hubbard，S/A，CIC ADC LAF签署。该页记录了1947年9月8日在Stewart的工作地点——加州大学伯克利分校的Hearst Mining Building——进行的一次访谈。

**Witness:** Ward L. Stewart，地址1242 Milvia Street，Berkeley，称自己是预备役1st lieutenant，曾是U.S. Army Air Forces军官，具有相当丰富的飞行经验，包括担任B-29飞行员服役。该探员注明，Stewart看起来不像会凭空捏造目击事件的人，而且显然也无意引起公众注意。

**Sighting:** Stewart报告称，1947年7月29日中午12点刚过不久，他与第415 AAF BU (RT) 的William H. Ryherd上尉在一次例行训练飞行后同行。就在他们着陆并以Hamilton Field为初始进近时，Ryherd指出有一个不明飞行物尾随一架P-80飞机。Stewart估计P-80的飞行速度约为250 mph，并表示该物体的移动速度大约是其三到四倍。随后又出现了第二个物体，其运动轨迹类似于战斗机在伴飞较重型飞机时的机动动作，即在第一个物体上方从左向右移动。

**Object:** Stewart表示，这些物体呈乳白色，与他见过的任何常规飞机都不同。他估计整个过程持续约15 seconds，航迹覆盖约120 degrees，而且这些物体始终保持在6,000 feet以上；他无法估计其大小或实际高度。他还补充说，这些物体不是Navy的“flapjacks”。

**Investigation:** 该报告属于情报式访谈摘要，而非完整的技术分析。文件保留了目击者的陈述和探员对其可信度的评估，但除记录在Hamilton Field附近的这一观察外，并未给出明确的识别结果或结论。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Confidential FBI-file page titled *Report on a "Flying Saucer"*, filed in FBI case 62-HQ-83894 Section 3. The page is a one-page narrative report, signed at bottom by **R. J. Madden, Division Plant Engr., The Pac. Tel. & Tel. Co.** The page is marked **CONFIDENTIAL** at top and bottom, and no continuation or separate incident page is present here.

**Witness:** The account describes three occupants of a sedan: **Steve Herrmann** (driver), **K. J. "Bob" Madden** (front-seat passenger), and **Karl Herrmann** (rear-seat passenger). Karl is the principal observer because he first called out the sighting and pointed to the object; Steve then slowed and stopped the car while all three watched.

**Sighting:** At about **12:00 p.m. on 29 July 1947**, while traveling northwest on the road from **Canyon Ferry to York, Montana**, approximately 25 miles northeast of Helena, Karl said, "See it! See it there! It's a flying saucer!" About ten seconds later, after the car stopped, the men saw a bright disc directly ahead to the northwest, estimated at **2 to 3 miles distance** and about **3,000 feet above ground**. The object appeared to hover and flutter, then rose and fell through roughly **50 to 100 feet** for about five seconds before suddenly shooting northeast at tremendous speed and vanishing into clear air.

**Object:** The witness description says the object looked **circular**, about **5 feet in diameter** as observed, and **3 to 4 inches thick**, with a surface that shone like **highly polished nickel** in bright sunlight. The report notes that the visible size estimate was likely distorted by distance and that the true dimensions were probably greater.

**Investigation / assessment:** After the object disappeared, the car continued northwest, and the observers reported **no evidence of a trail or other physical trace** along the road. The report is presented as a straightforward witness narrative rather than an analytical finding; its main value is the detailed contemporaneous description and the fact that it was formally preserved in an FBI case file under confidential cover.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 机密 FBI 档案中的一页，标题为 *Report on a "Flying Saucer"*，归入 FBI 案卷 62-HQ-83894 第 3 部分。该页为单页叙述报告，底部签署为 **R. J. Madden, Division Plant Engr., The Pac. Tel. & Tel. Co.**。该页顶部和底部均标注 **CONFIDENTIAL**，此处未附有续页或单独的事件页。

**Witness:** 记述中提到一辆轿车内的三名乘员：**Steve Herrmann**（司机）、**K. J. "Bob" Madden**（前排乘客）和 **Karl Herrmann**（后排乘客）。Karl 是主要目击者，因为是他首先喊出所见并指向该物体；随后 Steve 放慢并停下汽车，三人一起观察。

**Sighting:** 大约在 **1947年7月29日中午12:00**，当他们沿着从 **Canyon Ferry 到 York, Montana** 的道路向西北行驶时，地点约在 Helena 东北方 25 英里处，Karl 说：“看！看那里！那是飞碟！” 大约十秒后，汽车停下，几人看到正前方西北方向有一个明亮的盘状物，估计距离为 **2 to 3 miles**，离地约 **3,000 feet**。该物体似乎悬停并轻微摆动，随后在大约五秒内上下起伏约 **50 to 100 feet**，接着突然以极快速度向东北疾飞而去，消失在晴空中。

**Object:** 证人的描述称，该物体看上去是 **圆形** 的，目测直径约 **5 feet**，厚度约 **3 to 4 inches**，其表面在明亮阳光下闪耀，宛如 **highly polished nickel**。报告指出，所见尺寸估计可能因距离而失真，实际尺寸很可能更大。

**Investigation / assessment:** 物体消失后，汽车继续向西北行驶，目击者报告称沿路 **no evidence of a trail or other physical trace**。该报告呈现的是一份直接的目击叙述，而非分析性结论；其主要价值在于详细的当时描述，以及该记录作为机密材料被正式保存在 FBI 案卷中。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) was sent from the SAC, San Francisco to the Director, FBI, dated August 28, 1947, subject “Reports of Flying Discs.” It references follow-up on an earlier A-2 report dated August 4, 1947 and notes that three photographic prints alleged to have been taken by Rhoads were being enclosed for the Phoenix Field Division. The memo was routed with Airmail Special Delivery and marked for internal FBI handling under file 62-2938 / 62-83894-related indexing.

**Witness:** The principal witness named is William Rhoads of Phoenix, Arizona. The memo does not give a formal occupation, but it treats him as the person who reported the sighting and as the alleged photographer of the objects.

**Sighting:** According to the memo, on July 7, 1947, Rhoads said he saw what he believed were “flying discs.” No detailed visual description of the objects appears on this page beyond that term. The report was significant enough that A-2 personnel wanted Rhoads “completely interviewed,” and the FBI was advised to obtain the photographic evidence and an interview if one had not already occurred.

**Investigation:** The memo originated with Lt. Col. Donald Springer, A-2, Fourth Air Force, Hamilton Field, California, and mentions that FBI agent George F. Fugate, Jr. would soon be in Phoenix and could assist. In accordance with Bureau Bulletin No. 42, Series 1947, the Phoenix Field Division was instructed to interview Rhoads at 4333 North 14th Street, Phoenix. This page is therefore best understood as an investigative referral and coordination note, not a first-hand sighting narrative. The page supports the existence of photographs and a formal interagency inquiry, but it does not itself establish any conclusion about the objects.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这份 FBI Office Memorandum（Standard Form No. 64）由位于 San Francisco 的 SAC, San Francisco 发给 Director, FBI，日期为 1947年8月28日，主题为“Reports of Flying Discs.”。其中提及对先前一份日期为 1947年8月4日的 A-2 报告的后续跟进，并说明据称由 Rhoads 拍摄的三张照片印刷件将一并寄送给 Phoenix Field Division。该备忘录通过 Airmail Special Delivery 转送，并标注为供 FBI 内部处理，按 file 62-2938 / 62-83894 相关索引归档。

**Witness:** 记名的主要目击者是来自 Arizona 的 Phoenix 的 William Rhoads。备忘录未注明其正式职业，但将其视为报告该次目击的人，也是这些物体的据称摄影者。

**Sighting:** 根据备忘录，1947年7月7日，Rhoads 说他看见了他认为是“flying discs”的东西。除这一术语外，本页未对这些物体作出进一步的详细视觉描述。该报告的重要性足以使 A-2 人员希望对 Rhoads 进行“completely interviewed”，并建议 FBI 获取相关照片证据；若尚未进行访谈，则应安排一次访谈。

**Investigation:** 该备忘录源自位于 California 的 Hamilton Field 的 Fourth Air Force 的 A-2 中校 Donald Springer，并提到 FBI 探员 George F. Fugate, Jr. 不久将前往 Phoenix，届时可提供协助。根据 Bureau Bulletin No. 42, Series 1947，已指示 Phoenix Field Division 在 Phoenix 的 4333 North 14th Street 采访 Rhoads。因此，本页最适合被理解为一份调查转介与协调记录，而非第一手目击叙述。该页支持存在照片以及正式的跨机构调查，但其本身并未对这些物体作出任何结论。

**Document:** One-page FBI Headquarters teletype in the 62-HQ-83894 UFO/Flying-Disc file, routed through the FBI Communications Section and sent from Portland FBI to the Director, FBI. The page is headed "Flying Discs - Security Matter Dash X" and dated Aug. 15, 1947, with later handling stamps/notations but no continuation pages in this extract. The message is signed/initialed "Bobbitt" and states Bartlett was to be interviewed.

**Witness:** Mr. John Bartlett, identified only as a civilian resident of Agate Beach, Oregon. The record does not give his occupation or prior reliability, but the report treats him as a firsthand observer whose statement was important enough to forward to FBI Headquarters for follow-up.

**Sighting:** Bartlett reported that on the evening of August 7, 1947, at about 11:30 PM, he saw what he believed was a disc. The object was described only as bright in color. He was able to observe it for only a short time because of its speed. No size, altitude, sound, heading, maneuvers, or duration beyond the brief observation are given on this page.

**Investigation:** This is a preliminary field report rather than a completed case summary. The FBI note indicates Bartlett was to be interviewed, but no interview results appear on the provided page set. With only one teletype page available, the event remains uncorroborated here and the object characteristics are too sparse for a stronger identification; the report captures an early postwar "flying disc" inquiry rather than a resolved analysis.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** Mr. John Bartlett，仅被标识为居住在 Oregon州 Agate Beach 的一名平民。记录未说明其职业或既往可信度，但该报告将其视为一名直接目击者，其陈述重要到足以转呈 FBI Headquarters 以供后续跟进。

**Sighting:** Bartlett 报告称，在 1947年8月7日晚上约 11:30 PM，他看到了一个他认为是圆盘的物体。该物体仅被描述为颜色明亮。由于其速度很快，他只能短暂观察到它。此页未给出大小、飞行高度、声音、航向、机动动作或除短暂观察之外的持续时间。

**Investigation:** 这是初步的现场报告，而非已完成的案件总结。FBI 备忘指出将对 Bartlett 进行访谈，但在所提供的页面中未见访谈结果。由于这里只能获得一页电传稿，该事件在此仍未得到证实，而且对该物体特征的描述过于稀少，无法作出更有力的识别；该报告记录的是战后早期一次“飞碟”调查，而非已解决的分析。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed FBI case-file page labeled “Page 5” from 62-HQ-83894, Section 3, a UFO/flying-disc correspondence file. The page is a continuation of an undated report/statement and is part of the long Kenneth Arnold narrative compiled in the FBI’s 1947 flying-disc material. No other page from a different incident is needed here; the references to later sightings are cited as corroboration, not as the primary event.

**Witness:** Kenneth A. Arnold, a civilian pilot from Boise, Idaho, speaks in the first person and describes his own judgment of the objects’ appearance and behavior. His account is treated as a direct eyewitness statement from a competent air observer, although he explicitly contrasts air observation with less reliable ground descriptions.

**Sighting:** Arnold says that when the objects were flying “approximately straight and level,” they looked like a “black thin line,” and that he could judge their size only when they flipped. He reports that they held an almost constant elevation and did not appear to be climbing or descending like rockets or artillery shells. The page reflects his belief that the objects were some type of airplane, though not a conventional one.

**Object:** He characterizes the craft as “saucer-like discs” and argues that ground observers would have difficulty making accurate descriptions unless the objects were at great altitude. He notes the possibility that atmospheric moisture and dust near the ground could distort vision, while stating that air observers would be more accurate. This is consistent with the classic flying-disc description rather than a conventional aircraft identification.

**Investigation/Context:** Arnold cites multiple allegedly similar reports from observers across the United States, including Western Air Lines employees in Cedar City, Utah; a pilot from Oklahoma City; a locomotive engineer in Illinois; John Corlett of United Press in Boise; Dave Johnson of the Boise Daily Statesman; and United Air Lines personnel Captain Smith, co-pilot Stevens, Marty Morrow, Captain Charles F. Gabian, and Jack Harvey. He also says he has letters from people in the United States and Europe. The page’s analytical thrust is that many sightings may be of the same phenomenon, but no definite identification is made.

**Witness:** 来自 Idaho 的 Boise 的民航飞行员 Kenneth A. Arnold 以第一人称叙述，并描述他自己对这些物体外观和行为的判断。他的说法被视为一份来自合格空中观察者的直接目击陈述，不过他明确将空中观察与较不可靠的地面描述作了对比。

**Sighting:** Arnold 说，当这些物体以“approximately straight and level”方式飞行时，看起来像一条“black thin line”，而且只有在它们翻转时，他才能判断其大小。他报告称，这些物体几乎始终保持恒定高度，看上去并不像火箭或炮弹那样上升或下降。该页反映了他认为这些物体是某种飞机，但不是传统意义上的飞机。

**Object:** 他将这些飞行器形容为“saucer-like discs”，并认为除非物体处于很高的高度，否则地面观察者很难做出准确描述。他指出，地面附近的空气湿度和尘埃可能会扭曲视觉，而空中观察者则会更准确。这与经典的 flying-disc 描述一致，而不是对常规飞机的辨认。

**Investigation/Context:** Arnold 引用了美国各地多名观察者据称相似的报告，包括 Utah 的 Cedar City 的 Western Air Lines 员工；来自 Oklahoma City 的一名飞行员；Illinois 的一名机车工程师；Boise 的 United Press 的 John Corlett；Boise Daily Statesman 的 Dave Johnson；以及 United Air Lines 的人员 Captain Smith、co-pilot Stevens、Marty Morrow、Captain Charles F. Gabian 和 Jack Harvey。他还说自己收到了来自美国和欧洲的来信。该页的分析重点在于，许多目击可能属于同一种现象，但并未作出明确鉴定。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI case-file page BT 65-480 from 62-HQ-83894, Section 3. The page is a typed continuation sheet (page 2) with internal initials "RJG:FO'S" and enclosure notation "Enc. (2)". It compiles statements gathered by Special Agents from local newspaper and witness interviews, including Times-News reporter John Brosnan.

**Witness:** The primary on-page witness is Mr. Urie, a sober, middle-aged canyon resident; his sons Keith (8) and Billy (10) also witnessed the event. Brosnan, who first passed the story to Special Agents, said Urie appeared completely sincere. A second corroborating account came from J. H. Brown, interviewed instead of L. W. Hawkins because Brown had been present with Hawkins at the time.

**Sighting:** Urie reported a "machine" flying down the canyon from east to west, following the terrain contour. As it passed the Urie place, it flew almost directly over Mormon poplars; Urie said the trees did not merely bend in the wind but "spun around on top as if they were in a vacuum." Keith saw it first, Billy almost immediately, and both lost sight of it behind a tree after moments. They then told their father, who said he had seen it too. Brown said he and Hawkins heard a roar, looked up, and saw two high-flying objects, possibly 4,000-6,000 feet up, though he could not judge their true size or distance.

**Investigation:** The memo emphasizes sincerity and sobriety of the witnesses and notes that neither the Urie family nor Brown/Hawkins had previously seen "one of the discos." Brown and Hawkins were reportedly fishing at Salmon Dam. The report does not identify the objects conclusively; the file leaves them as an ambiguous, possibly aircraft-like but unconfirmed aerial sighting.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI案卷页 BT 65-480，来自62-HQ-83894，第3节。该页为打字的续页（第2页），带有内部首字母标注“RJG:FO'S”和附页标记“Enc. (2)”。其中汇编了特别探员从当地报纸和目击者访谈中收集到的陈述，包括Times-News记者John Brosnan。

**Witness:** 页面上的主要证人为Urie先生，一位清醒、年纪中等的峡谷居民；他的儿子Keith（8）和Billy（10）也目击了这一事件。首先将这一故事转告特别探员的Brosnan表示，Urie看起来完全真诚。第二份相互印证的陈述来自J. H. Brown，对其进行访谈是代替L. W. Hawkins，因为事发时Brown与Hawkins在一起。

**Sighting:** Urie报告说，一架“机器”从东向西沿着峡谷地形轮廓低飞而下。它飞过Urie家附近时，几乎正从摩门杨树的上方掠过；Urie说，这些树并不是单纯被风吹弯，而是“像在真空中一样在顶部旋转”。Keith最先看到它，Billy几乎立刻也看到了，两人仅过了片刻就因一棵树挡住视线而失去了它的踪影。随后他们告诉了父亲，父亲说他也看见了。Brown说，他和Hawkins听到一阵轰鸣，抬头看见两个高空飞行物，可能在4,000-6,000英尺高空，尽管他无法判断其真实大小或距离。

**Investigation:** 备忘录强调了目击者的真诚与清醒，并指出Urie一家以及Brown/Hawkins此前都未曾见过“one of the discos”。据称Brown和Hawkins当时正在Salmon Dam钓鱼。报告并未对这些物体作出确证；卷宗将其保留为一次含糊的、可能类似飞机但未经证实的空中目击事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Seattle urgent teletype to the Director, marked "Internal Security-X" and dated Aug. 14, 1947, 5:21 PM, in the UFO/Flying-Disc correspondence file (62-HQ-83894, Section 3). The page relays a Seattle Post-Intelligencer article and then summarizes an FBI interview with the witness. No formal FBI conclusion appears on the page.

**Witness:** Sidney Decker of Redmond, Washington (box 296) was interviewed; L. R. Brummett of Redmond (box 254) is identified as the other observer. Brummett said he called Decker’s attention to the objects and also pointed them out to Mrs. Mamie English.

**Sighting:** Around 9:00 AM on Aug. 13, 1947, Decker said he was standing near the Redmond Post Office when he saw two very bright objects moving at extreme speed northeast over Redmond, Washington. They traveled with one slightly behind and a little above the other, maintained equal speed for about eight seconds, and then disappeared from view. Decker said they were higher than a plane generally travels.

**Object:** Decker described the objects as noiseless, wingless, tailless, tapered at both ends, and resembling a "belly tank." Brummett independently reported seeing two objects flying northeast at a 45-degree angle. The report is consistent with a brief daytime double-object sighting, but the page provides no identification, physical recovery, or corroborating technical analysis beyond the witness descriptions.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI西雅图致局长的紧急电报，标注为“Internal Security-X”，日期为1947年8月14日，下午5:21，收录于UFO/飞碟往来文件（62-HQ-83894，第3部分）中。该页转述了一篇《Seattle Post-Intelligencer》报纸文章，并随后总结了FBI对证人的访谈。页面上没有出现正式的FBI结论。

**Witness:** 受访者为华盛顿州Redmond（Redmond，邮政信箱296）的Sidney Decker；L. R. Brummett（Redmond，邮政信箱254）被认定为另一名目击者。Brummett称，是他提醒Decker注意到这些物体，并且他也将它们指给了Mamie English夫人看。

**Sighting:** 1947年8月13日约上午9:00，Decker说，他当时站在Redmond邮局附近，看见两个非常明亮的物体以极快速度向东北方向飞越华盛顿州Redmond（Redmond）。它们飞行时一前一后，后者略微落后并稍高一些，速度大致相同地持续了约八秒，然后消失在视野中。Decker说，它们飞行高度比通常飞机的飞行高度更高。

**Object:** Decker将这些物体描述为无声、无翼、无尾，两端渐尖，看起来像一个“belly tank”。Brummett则独立报告称，看见两个物体以45度角向东北飞行。该报告与一次短暂的白天双物体目击事件相符，但页面未提供任何身份确认、实物回收，或除证人描述之外的可供验证的技术分析。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from SAC, Philadelphia, to the Director, FBI, dated September 18, 1947. Subject line: "Flying object reported over Philadelphia August 6, 1947" with "sabotage" typed beneath. This page appears to be the complete visible report excerpt for the incident; no continuation page is shown. The file context is FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 3, and the page bears later indexing/recording stamps and marginal handwritten notes typical of UFO-era file handling.

**Witness:** The first and primary account is from Miss Eleanor Naddle, 2114 Hobart Street, Philadelphia, employed by the George R. Greenwald Manufacturing Company. Secondary corroborating statements follow from Miss Cecelia Fine, 5617 Arlington Street, employed by Pressman & Gutman Company, Inc., and John Snyder, 1440 Vankirk Street, an insurance agent and former B-24 pilot in the Army Air Corps.

**Sighting:** Naddle said that between 10:30 and 10:45 p.m. on August 6, 1947, while sitting on her front steps with Fine, she saw a large white object moving very fast to the south. She reported a buzzing sound and a thin grayish smoke trail. Fine said she did not actually see the object, but noticed Naddle become frightened and heard a slight buzzing sound.

**Object:** Snyder, viewing the same general event around 10:45 p.m. with his wife and neighbors, described a bluish-white flame or object traveling quickly from northeast to southwest. Using his aviation experience, he estimated it at 1,000-3,000 feet altitude and 400-500 mph, leaving smoke or a condensation trail for about two seconds and making a hissing sound less loud than a rocket ship.

**Investigation:** The memorandum is a straight factual relay from the Philadelphia field office; no identification or final explanation is stated on this page. The combined descriptions emphasize a fast-moving luminous object with sound and a short-lived trail, but the record here stops short of concluding what it was.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI办公室备忘录（标准表格第64号），由费城（Philadelphia）SAC致FBI局长，日期为1947年9月18日。主题行：“1947年8月6日费城上空报告有飞行物”，其下方打印有“sabotage”。此页似乎就是该事件完整可见的报告摘录；未显示后续页。文件背景为FBI案件卷宗62-HQ-83894，第3部分，该页带有后来的索引/登记戳记以及边栏手写备注，这些都很典型，属于UFO时代档案处理方式。

**Witness:** 第一位也是主要的陈述来自Eleanor Naddle小姐，住址为2114 Hobart Street, Philadelphia，就职于George R. Greenwald Manufacturing Company。随后是补充印证陈述，来自Cecelia Fine小姐，住址为5617 Arlington Street，就职于Pressman & Gutman Company, Inc.，以及John Snyder，住址为1440 Vankirk Street，是一名保险代理人，曾任陆军航空队（Army Air Corps）B-24飞行员。

**Sighting:** Naddle称，1947年8月6日晚10:30至10:45之间，她与Fine坐在前门台阶上时，看见一个大型白色物体以很快的速度向南移动。她报告听到一种嗡嗡声，并看到一条淡灰色的烟迹。Fine说她并没有真正看见该物体，但注意到Naddle变得惊慌，并听到轻微的嗡嗡声。

**Object:** Snyder与妻子及邻居在大约晚上10:45看到同一总体事件时，描述为一团蓝白色火焰或物体，从东北向西南快速飞行。凭借其航空经验，他估计其高度为1,000-3,000英尺，速度为400-500 mph，留下烟迹或凝结尾迹约两秒，并发出嘶嘶声，音量比火箭船（rocket ship）更低。

**Investigation:** 该备忘录只是来自费城（Philadelphia）外勤办公室的直接事实转述；本页未给出任何确认或最终解释。综合描述强调的是一个高速移动、发光并伴有声音且尾迹短暂的物体，但这里的记录并未进一步下结论说明它究竟是什么。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum on Standard Form No. 64, from SAC Anchorage to the Director, FBI, dated 17 Sep 1947. The page references Bureau Bulletin No. 42 (30 Jul 1947) and bears file markings for 62-HQ-83894, Section 3. The page is a forwarded intelligence report rather than a field interview transcript; no exact sighting date appears on the page, so the memorandum date is the only explicit date visible.

**Witness:** Two Army officers assigned to the Office of the Director of Intelligence, Headquarters Alaskan Department, Fort Richardson, Alaska. The memo does not identify them by name, but presents them as trained military observers. A weather group at a nearby station also contributed altitude context.

**Sighting:** The officers reported seeing an airborne object pass through the sky at a tremendous speed. The first officer said it drew his attention, then he pointed it out to the second officer. The object was visible for about 15–20 seconds, traveling due south and apparently below scattered clouds that were reported above 10,000 feet.

**Object:** The witnesses did not describe a classic “saucer.” The first officer said it looked spherical, about 2–3 feet in diameter, with no vapor trail. He thought it was metallic and silver like an airplane. The second officer estimated it at about 10 feet in diameter, compared it to half the size of a full moon, and said it showed no spinning motion or reflection; he described it as having a dull metal finish and estimated its altitude at roughly 3,000–4,000 feet.

**Investigation:** The FBI report records the observations without drawing a firm conclusion. The object’s speed was described as greater than any plane seen by the witnesses, but the narrative offers no identification, only the eyewitness characteristics and the conflicting size estimates.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI关于标准表格第64号的办公室备忘录，由阿拉斯加安克雷奇（Anchorage）驻点负责人SAC致FBI局长，日期为1947年9月17日。该页引用了局方公告第42号（1947年7月30日），并带有62-HQ-83894、Section 3的档案标记。此页是一份转交的情报报告，而非现场访谈记录；页面上未出现确切的目击日期，因此备忘录日期是唯一明确可见的日期。

**Witness:** 两名陆军军官，隶属于阿拉斯加领地总部（Headquarters Alaskan Department）迪内利局长情报办公室，驻地为阿拉斯加理查森堡（Fort Richardson, Alaska）。备忘录未注明他们的姓名，但将其描述为受过训练的军事观察员。附近一处气象站的一个气象小组也提供了高度方面的背景信息。

**Sighting:** 这两名军官报告称，看到一个空中物体以极快速度穿过天空。第一名军官说，是它先吸引了他的注意，然后他把它指给第二名军官看。该物体大约持续可见15–20秒，沿正南方向飞行，且看起来是在零散云层下方通过；据报告，云层高度在10,000英尺以上。

**Object:** 目击者并未将其描述为典型的“飞碟”。第一名军官说它看起来是球形，直径约2–3英尺，没有尾迹。他认为它是金属材质，呈银色，像一架飞机。第二名军官估计其直径约10英尺，把它比作满月的一半大小，并称其没有旋转动作或反光；他形容它具有暗淡的金属表面，并估计其高度约为3,000–4,000英尺。

**Investigation:** FBI报告仅记录了这些观察情况，并未作出明确结论。该物体的速度被描述为快过目击者所见过的任何飞机，但叙述中没有给出身份确认，只提供了目击者特征以及相互矛盾的尺寸估计。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, sent from the Butte field office to the Director, FBI, dated September 27, 1947, in file 62-HQ-83894, Section 3. The page is an internal UFO/flying-disc report with routing references to Seattle and the 4th Air Force (S-2, McChord Field). It carries Bureau notation, file stamps, and initials indicating internal review and indexing.

**Witness:** The report centers on Warden John Henry of Montana State Prison, Deer Lodge, Montana, who relayed the account to the FBI writer. His account was corroborated by Melbourne M. Hill, identified as a convict chauffeur, and Mrs. Henry. The memorandum notes that Henry delayed reporting because he had already seen extensive newspaper coverage of the disc stories and initially thought the matter might be dismissed as "seeing things."

**Sighting:** On May 5, 1947, at about 3:30 P.M., while driving between Ellensburg and Seattle, Washington, Henry and the two other observers saw a silver object streak across the sky. He said it entered a nose dive and appeared likely to crash, but before reaching the earth it disintegrated, leaving a long smoky or gaseous pillar hanging high in the air. The object reportedly retained its form until breakup and did not blow away immediately.

**Object:** Henry described the target as moving at an extremely high speed with erratic motion at first, causing him to think it might be a jet-propelled plane, though he could not identify it. The memo emphasizes that the smoky pillar remained suspended and that the object was still far from the ground when it came apart.

**Investigation:** The Butte office concluded no further action was warranted because of the delay between the sighting and the report. The Seattle office was asked to advise H. R. Peterson of the 4th Air Force, but the case file page itself presents no technical analysis or identification beyond the witness descriptions.

**Witness:** 报告的核心人物是 Montana State Prison（Montana州立监狱）狱长 John Henry，Deer Lodge, Montana（蒙大拿州 Deer Lodge），他将这一经过转述给了 FBI 撰写人员。其说法得到了 Melbourne M. Hill（被认定为一名囚犯司机）以及 Mrs. Henry 的印证。备忘录指出，Henry 之所以延迟报告，是因为他已经看到大量有关飞碟故事的报纸报道，起初还以为此事可能会被当作“看花了眼”而草草带过。

**Sighting:** 1947年5月5日约下午3:30，当 Henry 与另外两名目击者在 Washington（华盛顿州）Ellensburg 和 Seattle 之间驾车行驶时，他们看到一个银色物体划过天空。Henry 说它以俯冲姿态急速下坠，看起来很可能会坠毁，但在接触地面之前便解体了，在空中留下了一道长长的烟状或气体状柱体高悬不散。据称，该物体在分裂前一直保持其形状，并未立刻消散。

**Object:** Henry 将该目标描述为以极高速度移动，起初轨迹还带有不规则的摆动，这使他一度以为那可能是一架喷气推进飞机，但他无法识别其真实身份。备忘录强调，那道烟状柱体一直悬浮空中，而该物体在解体时距离地面仍然很远。

**Investigation:** Butte 办公室认为，由于目击与报告之间间隔过久，无需进一步采取行动。Seattle 办公室被要求向第4空军的 H. R. Peterson 通报此事，但该案卷页本身除目击者叙述外，并未提供任何技术分析或身份认定。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Seattle SAC memorandum to the Director, dated Sept. 12, 1947, in file 62-HQ-83894, “Security Matter X,” subject “FLYING DISKS Reported by BRUCE ARMSTRONG and M. A. NICHOLS, Seattle, Washington, August 12, 1947.” The second page is a direct continuation of the same report (header “FLYING DISKS, Report of 8/26/47”), so both rendered pages belong to one case file item.

**Witness:** The primary witness was Bruce Armstrong, identified as an electronics technician at the Boeing Aircraft plant. The report also names M. A. Nichols of Seattle as a second sighting witness, with additional corroboration from Ray Stanley, George and Mrs. Krogstad, and Boeing Field personnel.

**Sighting:** Armstrong stated that about 2:20 p.m. on August 12, 1947, while standing in front of Section D of the Boeing Aircraft Plant with about ten other research engineers, he saw a small black object about 200 feet high moving south over the Boeing Field runway. He described it as triangular, fluttering “like a leaf,” and estimated its speed at about 15 mph. The engineers’ consensus was that it resembled a black leaf or tar paper. Later, report text notes another sighting by Nichols at about 4 p.m., who said he saw an object over his home moving southwest at a much higher altitude, with observers describing it as a white, cylindrical object reflecting sunlight with a purplish tinge.

**Investigation:** The Seattle office interviewed control-tower operator Ken Grant and Boeing Field weather-bureau personnel. Grant suggested the low object may have been a piece of burnt paper blown across the field; weather personnel noted that balloons were released every six hours from Boeing Field, were white in color, and could reflect sunlight at altitude. The report concludes that the observed object was probably a balloon or other debris and states that no further investigation would be conducted.

**Witness:** 主要证人为Bruce Armstrong，报告将其身份注明为Boeing Aircraft工厂的电子技术员。报告还提到来自Seattle的M. A. Nichols为第二名目击证人，并由Ray Stanley、George和Mrs. Krogstad以及Boeing Field工作人员提供进一步印证。

**Sighting:** Armstrong称，1947年8月12日下午约2:20，当他与约十名其他研究工程师站在Boeing Aircraft Plant的D区前方时，看见一个约200英尺高的小黑色物体沿Boeing Field跑道上空向南飞行。他形容该物体呈三角形，像“叶子一样”飘动，并估计其速度约为15 mph。工程师们一致认为它看起来像一片黑色的叶子或沥青纸。后续报告文字提到Nichols于下午约4点另一次目击，他称自己在家上空看见一个物体向西南方向移动，飞行高度更高；目击者形容该物体为白色、圆柱形，在阳光下反射出带紫色的光泽。

**Investigation:** Seattle办公室采访了控制塔操作员Ken Grant以及Boeing Field气象局工作人员。Grant推测，这个低空物体可能是一张被烧过的纸，被风吹过场地；气象人员指出，Boeing Field每六小时会放飞一次气球，这些气球呈白色，在高空可能反射阳光。报告最终结论认为，所见物体很可能是气球或其他碎片，并说明不会继续展开调查。

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum from the SAC, Salt Lake City, to the Director, FBI, dated September 15, 1947, subject "Flying Discs," in Section 3 of case file 62-HQ-83894. The report is a field summary of local interviews and newspaper references; it carries office initials (SMK:LMS) and closes with the conclusion that no further investigation would be conducted. The two rendered pages are consecutive parts of the same report, with page 0170 continuing the narrative from page 0169.

**Witnesses:** The principal named observers were Mr. and Mrs. Richard Anderson of Logan, who were interviewed by an FBI agent. The memo also references Mr. and Mrs. Gaylon Caldwell, Mr. and Mrs. Fred Thunell, Mr. and Mrs. Norman Hall, Keith Hughes, Joan Crookston, and others. Some names appeared in a newspaper account but later denied observing the objects because they had not had the opportunity; this suggests the local press report was at least partly inaccurate.

**Sighting:** The sightings occurred in Logan, Utah, on the evening of September 8, 1947, mainly between about 10:30 and 11:10 p.m. One account said approximately a dozen objects moved in group formation at 2,000-3,000 feet, were small like pigeons, white and illuminated, showed no wing movement, and disappeared to the north after circling the city for about 1-2 minutes. Another account described five groups of 35-60 small yellowish-white objects circling at high speed. A separate account said the objects traveled clockwise and looked like a group of moving stars.

**Investigation:** The memo treats the event as a composite of local reports rather than a single verified track. The varied descriptions, uncertainty about size and nature, and the possibility that some witnesses could have been seeing birds or lights are noted in the text. The final determination was that the information remained indefinite, and the Salt Lake City office ended active inquiry while informing military intelligence at Fort Douglas of the results.

**Witnesses:** 主要点名的目击者是来自 Logan 的 Richard Anderson 先生和夫人，他们接受了一名 FBI 特工的询问。备忘录还提到 Gaylon Caldwell 先生和夫人、Fred Thunell 先生和夫人、Norman Hall 先生、Keith Hughes、Joan Crookston 等人。部分姓名曾出现在报纸报道中，但后来否认曾看到这些物体，因为他们并没有机会目睹；这表明当地媒体报道至少有一部分不准确。

**Sighting:** 这些目击事件发生在 Utah 州 Logan，时间为 1947年9月8日晚，主要在晚上约 10:30 至 11:10 之间。一则说法称，大约十几件物体以编队方式移动，飞行高度为 2,000-3,000 英尺，体型像鸽子一样小，呈白色并发光，没有翅膀摆动迹象，在绕城约 1-2 分钟后向北消失。另一则说法描述有五组 35-60 个小型黄白色物体高速盘旋。另一个说法称这些物体按顺时针方向移动，看上去像一群移动的星星。

**Investigation:** 该备忘录将这一事件视为当地多份报告的综合，而非单一、经证实的轨迹。文中提到，各种描述彼此不同，对物体大小和性质也存在不确定性，而且有些目击者也可能看到的是鸟或灯光。最终认定信息仍然不明确，Salt Lake City 办公室在将结果告知 Fort Douglas 的军事情报部门后，结束了主动调查。

**Witness:** The named witness is Mr. A. Courtney Parker of South Royalton, Vermont. In the memo he is treated as an informant/resident witness rather than an official observer. An agent had contacted him at his residence, and Parker reiterated that the information he had concerning the flying discs was already contained in his earlier letter to the Bureau.

**Sighting:** Parker stated that, as far as he knew, no one else in South Royalton saw the discs. He believed he saw them because he had unusually good eyesight and could see bees and similar objects farther than other people. He also suggested that the discs may have been beyond the range of normal vision. The memo does not preserve a time of day, direction of travel, duration, or a detailed visual description beyond the phrase “flying discs.”

**Investigation:** The Albany office asked Parker to send any additional information directly to the Air Forces, since they were handling matters of this type. The memo concludes that no further action would be taken by the FBI. The overall record is a brief follow-up on an uncorroborated civilian report, with no physical evidence and no independent witnesses noted.
