events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from the SAC, Portland to the Director, FBI, dated October 9, 1947, subject "Flying Discs – Security Matter - X." The memo cites a Portland teletype dated September 13, 1947 and summarizes Portland Police Department dispatcher logs and officer statements. The page is marked in the FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, with internal recording stamps, but it is a single, self-contained report page.

**Witness:** Primary eyewitness Robert D. Adair, 4325 S.E. Madison Ave., Portland, described himself as one of two officers on duty in District 18 on September 11, 1947. His partner was J. R. Caldwell, 7652 S.E. Lincoln St., who supplied a corroborating statement. The memo also notes a report from Chief of Police Jenkins and radio-dispatch records from the Portland Police Department.

**Sighting:** Police logs first placed notice of unidentified objects over Portland at 5:21 P.M., with a request at 5:23 P.M. to District 14 to help locate and identify them; Jenkins reported seeing some objects at 5:24 P.M., while District 14 saw nothing unusual at 5:27 P.M. Adair said that near N.E. 25th Avenue and Saratoga Court he saw a very bright sun-glint on an object apparently made of silvery metal. It came from the east, made a wide turn over the city, and disappeared to the south after about two minutes. He estimated about 150 mph and 5,000 feet altitude, noted steady flight with no oscillation, and concluded it was probably an ordinary airplane reflecting sunlight.

**Object:** Caldwell said the object appeared to follow the same course, was difficult to judge in size/speed/height, seemed about three miles away and two miles high when first seen, looked larger and faster than a conventional airplane, and appeared elliptical and very bright silver/aluminum. Overall, the FBI file preserves a police-observed daylight “flying disc” report, but the principal witness analysis leaned toward a conventional aircraft caught in intense sun reflection.

**Witness:** The principal witness is Jack Peck, a pilot employed by Al Jones Flying Company at Bethel, Alaska. The memo says his co-pilot, Vince Daly, also observed the object. The report notes that Peck’s account had previously been relayed to Military Intelligence.

**Sighting:** Peck said the sighting occurred on a July night in 1947 when the sky was completely clear and the “entire night” was in daylight conditions. He placed the time at about 10:00 PM, with the sun just below the horizon, while he and Daly were approaching Bethel Airport in a DC-3.

**Object:** Peck said the object was immediately to his left and both men tried to maneuver to avoid it because they could not tell its direction of travel. He reported no propellers, no jet exhaust, no vapor trails, and no radio interference. He characterized it as dark with a definite, concise outline. At first glance he thought it might be a vapor trail, but the white streak never changed shape or direction. He judged it faster than any airplane he had seen high enough to leave a vapor trail. He described it as resembling a streamlined train in the sky and said it rose high enough to disappear from view while still far above the horizon. In a postscript, he said the object was traveling east to west and may have passed over Denver. No corroborating witnesses or investigation findings are included on this page.

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum from H.B. Fletcher to D.M. Ladd, subject “Flying Discs,” dated December 28, 1948. The page is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, and carries later file stamps (including 162-83894-149 and a Jan. 4, 1949 routing mark). It records a telephone report from SAC Willis in Houston and subsequent instructions from FBI Headquarters.

**Witness:** The primary eyewitness is Lonnie Noack of the Humboldt Oil Company, Houston, Texas. According to the memo, Noack was flying as a passenger with a friend in a private aircraft from California to Houston when the incident occurred. A Houston businessman, Fuller Blackwell, had furnished photographs reportedly taken by Noack.

**Sighting:** About 30 miles east of Lone Pine, California, Noack and the pilot saw an object on the ground that produced a very strong bright reflection. They landed to inspect it. The object was described as roughly 8 feet in diameter, with wings about 4 feet long, about 1 foot thick, and something in the center that “appears to be some type of gyroscope.” The wings were said to have some kind of jet propulsion arrangement. No identifying marks were found, and photographs were taken.

**Investigation:** SAC Willis said he had already informed Lt. Robert Fleming of the Army Air Forces at Ellington Field and Capt. Bush, the Army representative in Houston. Noack was to be interviewed the next morning with Lt. Fleming present, and an Army Air Forces examination of the object was anticipated. Fletcher instructed Willis to send full details and a copy of the photograph by air mail special delivery and to ensure a Bureau agent was present when the object was examined in California. The memo reflects active FBI coordination with the Army Air Forces rather than a completed technical conclusion.

Tester, P.M.).” No later pages are provided, and this page appears to be the full report/complaint.

**Witness:** The writer is Mrs. Mary C. Tester, identified as P.M. (likely postmaster/postmistress) in Port Allegany. She writes not as an eyewitness to a disc itself, but as a local citizen relaying what she was told in conversation by Dr. H. E. Cromwell, a local practicing dentist.

**Sighting/Claim:** Tester reports that following the appearance in town on November 6, 1947, of Mr. Joe Lippincott, Director of the Eastern Area, Red Cross, Pittsburgh, as the “speaker of the evening” at the annual local Red Cross dinner, Dr. Cromwell said Lippincott told him that the “saucers” reported in various parts of the country were actually from Spain. Cromwell further related that Lippincott had been in Europe and knew conditions there.

**Object/Content:** The alleged object is not described from direct observation. The only claim is a second-hand assertion that flying saucers originated from Spain. Tester says the rumor could spread easily because Cromwell is active in the Methodist church and local Protestant men’s club, and because Lippincott’s Red Cross role could lend the statement credibility.

**Investigation/Assessment:** Tester asks the FBI to check with Mr. Lippincott or his organization, questioning the advisability of an accredited Red Cross representative distributing such information “off the record.” The page reflects rumor transmission and concern over authority, not a verified UFO observation. No physical description, flight behavior, or independent corroboration is provided.

**Document:** This is page two of a typed FBI memorandum in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4. The page records handling of “Noack” films received in Houston and routed through FBI/OSI channels. It includes references to SA Robert Fleming (OSI, Ellington Field, Texas), SAC R. B. Hood, and Bureau instructions regarding field coordination. No page-one context is shown here, so the page is summarized as a standalone continuation of the same report.

**Witness:** The only named source on this page is Noack of Houston, apparently the person who mailed or held the film. The document does not give a first name or a separate eyewitness narrative; it describes the film as evidence received by mail and later shown to investigators.

**Sighting/Object:** The film is said to show a disk approximately seven feet in diameter, about two feet thick at the center with a feathered rim, and with four-foot wings on both sides resembling conventional airplane wings. The object is described as having no markings, no radio, and appearing to have landed at great speed. It is also said to be in comparatively good condition. Small aluminum cylinders were attached to the wing ends, apparently for jet propulsion; one cylinder was retained by Noack as a souvenir and one was then in Bureau possession.

**Investigation:** The page states that Fleming at Ellington Field was notified on Dec. 27, and on Dec. 28 he advised the Fifth OSI District at Wright Field, Dayton, Ohio. SAC Hood was told to keep in touch with R. C. Person so Bureau agents could assist OSI in observing and retrieving the flying disk, per Bureau instructions. The memo also notes that Houston had no facilities for reproducing the movie film, though still shots could be developed elsewhere. The page asserts the film “shows disk in all positions and are authentic,” but it does not independently identify the object’s origin.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这是联邦调查局（FBI）备忘录第2页，属于案件档案 62-HQ-83894，第4节。该页记录了在 Houston（休斯敦）收到并通过 FBI/OSI 渠道转送的 “Noack” 胶片的处理情况。其中提及了 SA Robert Fleming（OSI，Ellington Field, Texas）、SAC R. B. Hood，以及有关外勤协调的局方指示。此处未显示第1页的上下文，因此本页作为同一报告的独立续页进行概述。

**Witness:** 本页唯一点名的来源是 Houston 的 Noack，显然是寄送或持有该胶片的人。该文件未提供其名字，也没有单独的目击者叙述；它将该胶片描述为通过邮件收到、随后展示给调查人员的证据。

**Sighting/Object:** 据称，胶片显示一个直径约 seven feet 的圆盘，中心厚度约 two feet，边缘呈羽状，并且在两侧各有 four-foot 的翼，外形类似传统飞机机翼。该物体被描述为没有标记、没有无线电设备，并且看起来是以很高速度着陆的。还提到它整体状况相对良好。翼端连接着小型铝制圆筒，显然用于喷气推进；其中一个圆筒由 Noack 保留作纪念品，另一个当时已归联邦调查局（Bureau）保管。

**Investigation:** 本页称，Ellington Field 的 Fleming 已于 Dec. 27 接到通知，并在 Dec. 28 向位于 Dayton, Ohio 的 Wright Field 第五 OSI 区报告。按照局方指示，SAC Hood 被告知要与 R. C. Person 保持联系，以便局方探员在观察并取回飞行圆盘时协助 OSI。备忘录还指出，Houston 没有复制电影胶片的设备，但静态照片可以在其他地方冲印。该页断言该胶片“shows disk in all positions and are authentic”，但并未独立确认该物体的来源。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Director correspondence marked “Re: Flying Disc” with file code “HO 12/28/48,” this page being the continuation page (“-2-”) of a Houston case file entry. The text states that two copies of a signed statement taken from Mr. Noack, dated Houston, Texas, 12/28/48, were attached for the Bureau; copies were also routed to the Los Angeles Office, the Cincinnati Division, and the FBI Laboratory, with the original retained in the Houston file. The matter was being handled in coordination with O.S.I. (Office of Special Investigations) personnel at Ellington Field and Wright Field.

**Witness:** The page identifies Mr. Noack as the person who observed the object and later surrendered a detached aluminum cylinder, but it also says the Bureau should first confer with Mr. R.C. Person, who was named as the individual who initially discovered the flying disc and would know its present whereabouts. The available page does not give Noack’s first name or Person’s rank; both appear to be civilian witnesses or handlers associated with the Ellington Field report.

**Sighting/Object:** The object is described only as a “flying disc.” Noack reportedly saw an aluminum cylinder become detached from one wing tip and brought it back as a souvenir; the memo notes it could conceivably function as a rudder, rocket housing, or fuel-tank attachment. The page provides no independent technical conclusion, only that the cylinder was initial evidence and was surrendered for examination.

**Investigation:** Initial information was telephoned to Inspector Howard Fletcher at the Bureau at 9 A.M. on 12/28/48, who requested a summary by teletype and said the Bureau should remain actively involved while cooperating with O.S.I. representatives. The District Commander of the 5th O.S.I. District at Wright Field, Dayton, Ohio, was notified, and the note suggests O.S.I. in California might also handle the inquiry. No final determination is made on this page; it is an administrative evidence-forwarding memo supporting an ongoing investigation centered on Ellington Field, Houston.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 本页将Mr. Noack列为目击该物体并随后交出一个分离的铝制圆筒的人，但同时又说明Bureau应首先与Mr. R.C. Person联系，因为他被指为最初发现该飞碟的人，并且会知道其目前下落。现有页面未给出Noack的名字，也未注明Person的军衔；二人似乎都是与Ellington Field报告相关的平民证人或经手人。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum from the SAC, Houston, to the Director, dated 12/28/48, subject line "Flying Disc — Lonnie Edward Noack, Complainant." The page is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, with routing to Assistant Director D.M. Ladd and internal file/index stamps at the bottom.

**Witness:** The primary witness is Lonnie Edward Noack, identified as a machinist employed by the Humble Oil and Refining Company in Houston. He is described as the source of the information and the holder of the film. Attorney Fuller Blackwell acted as the intermediary, telephoning the Houston Office on 12/27/48 to relay Noack’s account and to determine which authorities should be contacted.

**Sighting:** Blackwell reported that Noack had observed an object at a desert location near Las Vegas, Nevada. The object was described as approximately eight feet in diameter, with a tail and wings, and as apparently equipped for jet propulsion. Noack allegedly took motion-picture footage of the object; the memo states that he had a 50-foot roll of 8mm film, with about fifteen feet relating exclusively to the disc images.

**Investigation:** On receipt of the call, the FBI arranged for Noack to bring the film to the Houston Office for a showing at 2:00 P.M. on 12/27/48. The viewing took place with Captain Harold Bush (MID), Mr. Robert B. Fleming (O.S.I.), Special Agent Graham W. Kitchel, Noack, and the writer observing. Noack then returned the morning of 12/28/48 to provide a written account and surrendered the film. The memo reflects referral of the matter to O.S.I. and military intelligence, but it gives no independent FBI conclusion about the object’s nature.

**Sighting:** Blackwell 报告称，Noack 在 Nevada 的 Las Vegas 附近一处沙漠地点观察到一个物体。该物体被描述为直径约八英尺，带有尾翼和机翼，并且似乎配备喷气推进装置。Noack 据称对该物体拍摄了电影胶片；备忘录称他持有一卷50英尺长的8mm胶片，其中约十五英尺专门拍摄了该飞碟影像。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a typed continuation from FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, a UFO/flying-disc correspondence file. No page header or signer is visible on this excerpt, but the text is clearly part of a first-person statement describing a disc encounter, subsequent photography, and later circulation of the film.

**Witness:** The narrator is an unnamed Humble Oil & Refining Company employee in Houston who traveled in California. He refers to coworkers and acquaintances who later viewed the developed film, suggesting he was a civilian observer rather than a trained investigator. Because the name is not visible on this page, the witness cannot be identified more precisely from the excerpt alone.

**Sighting:** The witness states that he and others finished observing and photographing the object at about 5:30 or 6:00 P.M. on 7 December 1948. He says that after the observation they returned to Pasadena, California that evening and reached Hollywood about 9:00–9:30 P.M. The exact observation site is not named, but Pasadena is the clearest geographic anchor in the narrative.

**Object:** The object is described only as a “disc or saucer.” A question from Mr. Fleming about radio equipment is answered negatively: “there was no radio equipment noted on the object in any fashion or form.” The witness also says Mr. Person intended to obtain a truck and haul the object to his shop, implying the object may have been tangible and nearby, though the witness cannot confirm whether that happened.

**Investigation / disposition:** The witness says he later took additional photos in Hollywood, had the roll developed by Eastman Kodak in Los Angeles, and received the prints in Houston on 23 December 1948. He then showed the film to multiple Humble Oil coworkers and to a brother-in-law in Pasadena, Texas, and mentions that a young Southern Pacific employee who was interested in photography may have helped cause newspaper contact. The page offers no technical evidence beyond the witness’s account and does not establish the object’s nature; the report remains anecdotal and unverified.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 本页是 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894 第 4 部分中一份关于 UFO/飞碟往来的文件的打字续页。该摘录上未显示页眉或签署人，但文本显然属于一份第一人称陈述，内容描述了一次飞碟遭遇、随后拍摄以及胶片后来被传播的经过。

**Witness:** 叙述者是一名未具名的 Humble Oil & Refining Company 员工，常驻 Houston，并曾在 California 旅行。他提到后来查看冲洗后胶片的同事和熟人，说明他更像是一名平民目击者，而非受过训练的调查人员。由于本页未显示姓名，仅凭该摘录无法进一步确定该证人的身份。

**Sighting:** 证人称，他和其他人在 1948 年 12 月 7 日约下午 5:30 或 6:00 完成了对该物体的观察和拍摄。他说在观察结束后，他们当晚返回 Pasadena, California，并于晚上约 9:00–9:30 抵达 Hollywood。确切的观察地点未被提及，但 Pasadena 是叙述中最明确的地理锚点。

**Object:** 该物体仅被描述为“disc or saucer”。Fleming 先生关于无线电设备的提问得到了否定回答：“there was no radio equipment noted on the object in any fashion or form.” 证人还说 Person 先生打算弄来一辆卡车，把该物体运到他的工坊，这暗示该物体可能是实物且就在附近，不过证人无法确认此事是否真的发生。

**Investigation / disposition:** 证人说他后来在 Hollywood 又拍了几张照片，胶卷由 Los Angeles 的 Eastman Kodak 冲洗，照片于 1948 年 12 月 23 日寄到 Houston。随后他把胶片给多名 Humble Oil 同事以及一位住在 Pasadena, Texas 的妹夫/姐夫看过，并提到一名对摄影感兴趣的 Southern Pacific 年轻雇员可能曾促成与报社的联系。此页除证人陈述外没有提供任何技术性证据，也未能确定该物体的性质；该报告仍属轶事性陈述，未经证实。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed statement dated Houston, Texas, Dec. 28, 1948, signed by Lonnie Edward Noack of 2921 Chicago Street, Houston 17, Texas, and given to Special Agents Robert B. Fleming and Christopher R. Bradley (Office of Special Investigation, Ellington Field) and FBI Special Agents Graham W. Kitchall and Galen N. Willis. The pages shown are consecutive pages 1–2 of the same statement in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4.

**Witness:** Noack says he was traveling with R.C. Person, Nathan Smith, C.A. Toce, Robert Broussard, and one other unidentified man. He describes the information as partly firsthand and partly relayed by Person and Smith. The statement reads like an interview/affidavit rather than an independent field report, but it includes Noack’s own observation of the object and the photos/film taken at the scene.

**Sighting:** On Dec. 6, 1948, the group dined at the Old Virginia Inn in Los Angeles and then returned to Smith’s electrical manufacturing company. Person reportedly described a flying disc and arranged for the group to leave the next day with cameras. Because Person was delayed at a private airfield, they did not depart until about 2 P.M. on Dec. 7. They then drove to the reported location, which Noack describes as flat, desert, and desolate, roughly 150 miles from Pasadena and east/northeast of the city.

**Object:** At the site they found a “disc, or flying wing” on the ground in a semi-vertical position at about a 45-degree angle, with the left wing imbedded in the ground. Noack says it had apparently struck with considerable force and slid 300–400 feet. He estimates the diameter at about seven feet, with wings about four feet by twenty inches and three inches thick, mounted on an axle through the disc and on ball bearings. The object was dented but generally intact.

**Investigation:** Nathan Smith shot about 10 feet of 16 mm film; Person took five or six Speed Graphic stills, though Noack notes the first three may have been underexposed. The report contains no formal FBI conclusion, but the physical description strongly suggests a man-made flying wing or experimental device rather than an unexplained aerial object.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 打字稿，日期为 1948 年 12 月 28 日，地点为德克萨斯州休斯敦（Houston, Texas），由居住在 Texas 州 Houston 17, 2921 Chicago Street 的 Lonnie Edward Noack 签署，并提交给 Special Agents Robert B. Fleming 和 Christopher R. Bradley（Office of Special Investigation, Ellington Field）以及 FBI Special Agents Graham W. Kitchall 和 Galen N. Willis。所示页面为 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894，第 4 部分中同一声明连续的第 1–2 页。

**Witness:** Noack 说，他当时与 R.C. Person、Nathan Smith、C.A. Toce、Robert Broussard 以及另一名身份不明的男子同行。他表示，相关信息一部分是亲眼所见，一部分由 Person 和 Smith 转述。这份陈述更像是一份访谈/宣誓证词，而非独立的现场报告，但其中包含了 Noack 对该物体的亲眼观察，以及在现场拍摄的照片/胶片。

**Sighting:** 1948 年 12 月 6 日，该小组在洛杉矶（Los Angeles）的 Old Virginia Inn 共进晚餐，随后返回 Smith 的电气制造公司。Person 据称描述了一个飞碟，并安排小组次日携带相机出发。由于 Person 在一处私人机场（private airfield）耽搁，他们直到 12 月 7 日下午约 2 点才启程。随后他们驾车前往据称的地点，Noack 将其描述为平坦、荒凉、沙漠地带，距 Pasadena 约 150 英里，位于该市的东偏东北方向。

**Object:** 在现场，他们发现地面上有一个“disc, or flying wing（圆盘，或飞翼）”，呈半直立状态，约成 45 度角，左翼嵌入地面。Noack 说，它显然是以相当大的力量撞击后又滑行了 300–400 英尺。他估计其直径约为七英尺，机翼约四英尺长、二十英寸宽、三英寸厚，通过贯穿圆盘的一根轴并由滚珠轴承支撑。该物体有凹痕，但整体上基本完好。

**Investigation:** Nathan Smith 拍摄了约 10 英尺的 16 mm 胶片；Person 拍摄了五到六张 Speed Graphic 静态照片，不过 Noack 指出前三张可能曝光不足。报告中没有正式的 FBI 结论，但该物体的物理描述强烈表明，它更像是一种人造飞翼或实验装置，而不是无法解释的空中物体。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Form No. 1 case report in file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, file no. 105-445, case originating at Houston and reported from Los Angeles by Special Agent W. Nathan Provinse on 3/30/49. The case is marked as an Internal Security matter. Page 0123 is a duplicate continuation/copy of the same report and adds no new substantive facts.

**Witness:** Lonnie Edward Noack is named as complainant and the principal source of the report. The object was also seen with R. C. Person and Mr. and Mrs. Nathan Smith of South Pasadena. Special Agent Edward Olsen later noted that R. C. Person of Vasco Manufacturing Company was traveling in Arizona and unavailable for interview.

**Sighting:** On or about 1948-12-27, Noack reported finding an object in the desert near Helendale, California, which he believed might be a flying disc. The report situates the find roughly 150 miles northeast of Pasadena.

**Object:** FBI follow-up concluded the item was not a mysterious disc but a model tow target or kite that had been abandoned after unsuccessful tests. Henry T. Rice of Los Angeles, described as the manufacturer and former financial backer, positively identified portions of the object as belonging to that target/kite.

**Investigation:** The report cites teletype traffic from Houston and Los Angeles to the Director dated 12/28/48 and 12/29/48. The final analytical conclusion is dismissive of a UFO interpretation: the purported flying disc was explained as discarded test equipment rather than an unexplained aerial object.

**Document:** FBI Salt Lake City sent an urgent Communications Section teletype to the Director on 5 Apr 1949, stamped "FBI SALT LAKE CITY" and "TELETYPE," with later routing/handling marks and the file context of FBI case 62-HQ-83894, Section 4. The page is a single-page report (p.0126) and appears to be the primary record for this incident.

**Witness:** The initial account was relayed from Logan, Utah, based on what an unnamed guard at the Army General Supply Depot in Ogden said he saw at about 9:00 AM. Additional contemporaneous observers included Lt. Ron Hatfield of the Logan Police Department, Utah Highway Patrolman L. N. Jeppson at Mantua, and several residents at Trenton. Because the report is a teletype summary rather than a signed field interview, the first-hand chain is somewhat indirect, but the sightings were reportedly corroborated by multiple local witnesses.

**Sighting:** Witnesses described a silver-colored object, a flash of light/fire, and what looked like an airborne explosion followed by a falling object west of Ogden/Logan, near Taylor, Sardine Canyon, and west of Trenton. One report mentions two puffs of smoke high in the air; another says the object appeared to explode as it neared the mountain. The timing clustered around 9:00-9:20 AM on 5 Apr 1949.

**Investigation:** The report says the information was immediately furnished to OSI at Hill Field, Utah. Hill Field then advised that the phenomena were probably caused by two B-29s from Wendover Field practice-bombing in the desert west of Logan at extremely high altitude, producing vapor trails that could have been misread as aerial explosions or a falling disc. The document therefore records a UFO-style sighting but ends with a conventional military explanation rather than a confirmed unknown."

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from the SAC, Little Rock, to the Director, FBI, dated 22 Apr 1949. The subject line reads “Unknown Subjects; Wade H. Harrison - Informant; Flying Discs; Fort Smith, Arkansas (4-16-49).” The page is marked with FBI exhibit/file notations including EX-118 and recorded/indexed stamps, indicating this is an internal investigative UFO report.

**Witness:** Wade H. Harrison of Fort Smith, Arkansas, whose residence is listed as Route 1, Box 293. He was employed as a Special Delivery messenger by the Fort Smith Post Office Department. The memo treats him as the principal civilian eyewitness, with no indication that he had prior involvement beyond providing the account.

**Sighting:** Harrison said that at about 5:25 p.m. on Saturday, 16 Apr 1949, while stopped at a traffic light at North Eleventh Street and Grand Avenue, he looked up and saw a “brilliant object” moving in a southeasterly direction. He estimated it was about 2 miles high and followed it for about 3 to 4 miles until trees blocked his view. He reported clear weather, good visibility, and no clouds near the object.

**Object:** The object made no audible noise. Harrison initially thought it might be a reflector on an airplane, but he could not locate or hear any aircraft. He also noted that other motorists nearby could have seen it when he pointed it out.

**Investigation:** After the sighting, Harrison later spoke with an Army officer wearing major or lieutenant colonel insignia at the 1400 block of North “C” Street. The officer said his wife had seen a similar flying object the day before while traveling from Oklahoma City toward Fort Smith, and that he had seen it too. The memo does not identify a final explanation, leaving the incident unresolved as a “flying discs” report rather than a confirmed aircraft or astronomical event.

It is marked “RE: FLYING DISCS,” stamped “CONFIDENTIAL BY SPECIAL MESSENGER,” and bears FBI file markings including “62-HQ-83894-167” and a “RECORDED - 128” notation. The page also shows a May 3, 1949 communications-section stamp and routing/approval initials, indicating internal FBI handling rather than a field investigation.

**Witness:** The memo does not name the actual observers. It says a reliable confidential source told the FBI that Mr. C. A. Atkins of 4312 Los Feliz, Hollywood, California, had reported the account. Atkins in turn said that three employees of the Department of Recreation in Parks in the city of Los Angeles had seen objects in the sky that appeared to be flying discs. Because the observers are unnamed and the report is secondhand, witness credibility is limited to the confidential-source chain.

**Sighting:** The sighting occurred during the first part of April 1949 in Los Angeles, California. No precise time, direction, duration, altitude, number of objects, color, shape, speed, or maneuvering details are provided. The only description is that the objects in the sky “appeared to be flying discs.”

**Investigation:** The FBI explicitly states that the information is being furnished to the Air Force for any action desired and that “no investigation is being conducted” by the Bureau. Analytically, this is a brief referral, not a substantive case report: it preserves an early civilian UFO-style tip, but the page contains no corroboration, no technical description, and no follow-up findings.

**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), from the SAC, San Antonio, to the Director, FBI, dated April 4, 1949, marked "Air Mail / Special Delivery" and filed under Bureau file 65-48300 (with local notation 100-7545). The memo references an earlier San Antonio letter to the Bureau dated March 22, 1949 concerning "unconventional aircraft" and records a follow-up inquiry from G-2, 4th Army on April 4, 1949 asking whether the FBI had information to substantiate or discredit Walter Winchell’s remarks about "flying discs."

**Witness:** The principal observer was 1st Lt. Frederick W. Davis, who was in charge of a platoon in Company C, 12th Armored Infantry Battalion, part of the alert force ("Force Abel") assigned from Camp Hood to protect Killeen Base. The report presents him as a trained military officer on duty near the installation, which gives the account some operational credibility, though the narrative remains secondhand within the FBI memo.

**Sighting:** At about 11:50 P.M. on March 31, 1949, Lt. Davis reportedly saw a lighted object about the size of a basketball, reddish-white in color and trailing fire, southwest of Killeen Base adjacent to Camp Hood, Texas. He estimated it at about 6,000 feet altitude. The object traveled parallel to the ground, passed directly over him at rapid speed, remained visible for 10 to 15 seconds, and then suddenly disappeared high in the sky without descending. He reported no sound or odor, and the night was clear with good visibility. The object passed almost directly over the air strip at Killeen Base.

**Investigation:** Immediately after the sighting, Lt. Davis tried to telephone headquarters but heard static or electrical interference on the line, which he considered possibly radio interference. The memo further notes that G-2 reported other unidentified lights on March 6, 7, 8, and 17, 1949, seen by military personnel about 1,000 yards east of the fence surrounding Killeen Base, but states the March 31 object was different in nature from those earlier lights. No FBI analytic conclusion is recorded on this page; the document functions as a relay of military observations and a request for Bureau input amid public discussion of "flying discs."

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from SAC, New Orleans to the Director, FBI, dated June 2, 1949, subject line “FLYING DISCS.” The memo references SAC Letter 38 of March 25, 1949 and carries Bureau routing/receipt stamps. It is an internal FBI intelligence note, not a field interview, and states that all three incidents had been investigated by Army Intelligence.

**Witness:** The underlying sightings were reported through the Office of Naval Intelligence, New Orleans, and involved two unnamed witnesses for at least one observation. The memo notes that the witnesses were outdoors and did not wear glasses. No personal names, occupations, or ranks are provided on this page.

**Sighting:** The Bureau was advised that three flying-disc sightings occurred in the City of New Orleans within the previous ten days, on May 18, 19, and 23, 1949. The objects were described as single discs in straight flight, generally northbound in the late afternoon, about the size of an observation plane but shaped like a saucer. The Navy further reported that two witnesses said the object appeared to be traveling end over end.

**Investigation:** Weather was reportedly good at the times of the sightings. Naval Intelligence considered the possibility that the objects were weather balloons, but noted that weather balloons were launched from only one airport, typically an hour before sighting times, and would usually be out of view within minutes. The memo does not reach a definitive conclusion, but it preserves the Navy’s tentative balloon explanation and the fact that Army Intelligence had already looked into the three cases. The event is therefore best catalogued as a New Orleans multi-sighting UFO/flying-disc report rather than a confirmed aircraft or astronomical identification.

Instead, it reports a remembered account that "there were thousands of them" and that "they were supposed to be the rocket type." No color, shape, flight behavior, speed, sound, or duration is provided.

**Assessment:** Because the page is hearsay rather than a direct observation, it is best treated as a correspondence lead, not a substantiated sighting. The document’s value lies in showing how civilians near the Texas-Mexico border interpreted earlier rocket rumors through the 1947 flying-saucer lens. The page offers no corroboration, no investigative findings, and no technical analysis beyond the writer’s belief that such "flying saucers could be more dangerous than we think."

The article says they told their story after arriving at Atlanta Municipal Airport. Chiles is the named pilot in the headline photo caption, with Whitted as the second witness.

**Object:** Described as having a fiery comet-like tail 25 to 50 feet long, an estimated 100-foot fuselage, and two rows of brightly lit square windows. The article says no crew was seen aboard. **Investigation:** This page is a newspaper account rather than a formal investigative report, so it provides no corroboration, radar data, or chain-of-custody evidence. In the FBI file it serves as press documentation of the famous Alabama/Eastern Air Lines “wingless aircraft” event, with the sighting date clearly preceding the newspaper date by one day.

**Document:** This is page 2 of an FBI Los Angeles file item marked "LA 100-2442" in Section 4 of the 62-HQ-83894 UFO file. The page is a continuation of a typed report/letter and closes with "The above is being furnished for the information of the Bureau," indicating a field-office transmission rather than a standalone public statement.

**Witness:** The principal witness is identified only as Mr. Parrott, a major in the Active USAF Reserve. The report says he qualified as a pilot in August 1941 and had approximately 2,200 hours of flying time, with substantial night-flying experience during World War II. Those details were included to support his credibility as an experienced observer.

**Sighting:** Parrott stated that he first heard the object about 10 seconds before seeing it and then watched it for about 35 seconds from his home area. He described a dull-surfaced, light-colored metal object moving very slowly west or northwest, then passing beyond the house and making an estimated 90-degree left turn before heading south or southwest. He said the object came to appear directly overhead before disappearing.

**Object:** The witness reported a continuous clicking sound, likened to the beaters of an improperly meshed home mixer. He denied any whistle, roar, flame, exhaust trail, or steady lights, though he saw brief reflections twice. He believed the underside may have been curved because of the streetlights behind him about half a block away. His dog also reacted to the object’s path, which he noted as a possible indicator of sound frequencies not obvious to him.

**Investigation:** The report says no other witnesses were located through the local newspaper or area inquiry. Mr. Bremer indicated he would clear the matter with headquarters and likely conduct an investigation. No final explanation is offered on this page, but the report preserves a seemingly credible, short-duration observation of a metallic, noisy object with unusual maneuvering and no visible propulsion.

**Investigation:** The Richmond office states it had **no information other than the news items** and that those items appeared to contain the **best available information**. In analytical terms, this page documents a **media-reported UFO allegation** with **no corroborated FBI inquiry** and no assessed conclusion beyond referral consideration.

**Witness:** The most detailed quoted witness on this page is Mrs. W. R. Delk of 914 Hemphill Ave., N.W., Atlanta. She compares the object to Halley’s Comet but says it looked nothing like what she had seen before. The article also summarizes accounts from other unnamed Atlantans, a newspaperman, and references prior reports by Eastern Air Lines pilots near Montgomery.

Some accounts mention a long purple tail; others describe a fiery-red front end with square sections trailing behind.

**Object:** The object was consistently described as intensely luminous, fiery, and fast-moving, with a tail or trailing sections. No size, distance, or altitude was established beyond estimates and comparisons. The article presents the object as an unknown aerial phenomenon, not identified on the page.

**Investigation:** The page is a newspaper summary of public sightings, not a Bureau conclusion. The article suggests widespread curiosity and multiple corroborating witnesses, but it offers no definitive explanation. Based on the descriptions, a meteor/bolide would be a plausible mundane candidate, though the report itself leaves the object unidentified.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI enclosure, stamped **FBI - Richmond, May 16 1949**, filed as **62-83894-178**. The clipped article is from the **Radford News Journal** (handwritten on the cover as **Radford, Va., 4/13/49**) and is a local newspaper roundup of a widely reported nighttime object. No separate FBI memorandum or follow-up report appears on this page; the Bureau retained the clipping as correspondence/evidence in the UFO file.

**Witnesses:** The newspaper quotes several unnamed or named civilians, including a Radford man who asked not to be identified, **Mrs. Alfred Tolley**, **Miss Joe Stewart** of Radford College, **Fred W. Hurt**, **Mrs. James D. Heinlein**, **Miss Dody Jones**, and **L. B. Graybeal** (a former Air Force pilot from Christiansburg). Their accounts were gathered by reporter **Wells Caldwell**.

**Sighting:** The object was seen **just after sundown** on the evening before the paper date, moving **from the southwest toward the east** over Radford and the surrounding region. Witnesses said it came from the direction of **Pulaski**, passed near or over **Blacksburg**, and was also reported from **Christiansburg**, **Bedford**, and even **Kingsport, Tenn.**

**Object:** Descriptions varied but were broadly similar: a **long black cigar/stick-like object** with a **bright light or fire at the front**, trailing **vapor, smoke, or long streaks of fire**. Several witnesses compared it to a **comet or meteor**; one thought it resembled an airplane’s exhaust, while another heard a faint sound or “roaring” as it passed. No clear structure, landing, or impact was reported.

**Investigation:** The article itself offers no identification and no FBI conclusion. Based on the many comet/meteor comparisons, the lack of a consistent mechanical profile, and the luminous trail described by multiple observers, the incident reads most like a **bright bolide/meteor-like phenomenon** rather than a conventional aircraft, though the newspaper left it unresolved.

**Document:** FBI Form No. 1, file no. 62-2542 VFH, case originated at Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. This one-page report was made at Philadelphia on 15 Jun 1949 by James L. Kirkland for the period ending 20 May 1949. The title on the form reads “Unknown Subject Fire, Scranton, Pennsylvania, Unknown Date,” with George Kington listed as complainant. The report is administrative/miscellaneous in character rather than a formal UFO sighting report.

**Witness:** The principal named individual in the narrative is Frederick Marquardt, who submitted ash residue to the Philadelphia Fire Marshal’s Office for chemical analysis. Captain Michael Hannan of the Fire Marshal’s Office is the other key source, describing the correspondence and follow-up efforts. The file notes that Marquardt had at one time worked for the Atomic Energy Commission.

**Sighting/Incident:** The underlying event is an unexplained fire in Scranton, Pennsylvania. In the transmittal letter, Marquardt reportedly stated that the fire continued to burn for twelve hours after water was first applied. He also claimed that an object had entered the roof of the building, caused an explosion, and threw people out of bed. No direct visual description of a “flying disc” appears on this page, but Marquardt’s opinion was that the fire may have been caused by a military flare or a “flying saucer.”

**Investigation:** The Philadelphia Fire Marshal’s Office received an ash sample by mail on 21 Apr 1949 and requested chemical analysis. The office examined the original letter, confirmed the unusual claims, and attempted to locate Marquardt at 127 South 16th Street without success. A building manager said Marquardt had been employed by the Atomic Energy Commission. The FBI report does not reach a scientific conclusion; it simply records the Fire Marshal’s inquiry and the speculative UFO-related remark, leaving the incident unresolved on this page.

**Document:** FBI Philadelphia memo page 2 (file mark **PH 62-2542**) in 62-HQ-83894, Section 4. The page is an internal interview summary mentioning Acting Chief **George Kington**, Dr. **Edward Burke** (City Chemist), and an ash analysis forwarded through the office. It is undated on the page itself and appears to be a continuation of a longer report.

**Witness:** **Frederic Marquardt** of the H. A. Kuljian Company, Philadelphia, was interviewed at his business. He said he was not present at the fire and had received the ash sample from a friend, **Woody Shaeffer** of Lake Ariel, Wayne County, by mail. His information is therefore secondhand, relaying Shaeffer's letter and sample rather than a direct observation.

**Sighting/incident:** Marquardt reported that Shaeffer's house, near **Lake Ariel** about one mile south of South Canaan, burned about six months earlier during a nighttime storm. According to Shaeffer's account, a **large object struck the roof** and ignited the house, which burned to the ground in less than an hour. Marquardt said the ash residue remained ignited for about twelve hours and that a quantity of ash was still on Shaeffer's premises.

**Object/analysis:** Kington furnished results of a city-laboratory analysis by Dr. Burke. The ash was said to contain **magnesium, aluminum, iron, calcium, silicates, sulphur, and carbonates**. Marquardt speculated it might have been part of a **military flare** or a **"flying saucer"**, but also noted he had been advised that some flares burn for a long period and thought the loud noise could have come from vacuum effects when the object struck the roof.

**Investigation:** The report says the Marshal's Office withdrew on a question of jurisdiction and advised that any further action be referred to **State Police** authorities. No definitive conclusion is given; the page records an unverified, indirect account of a house fire attributed by the witness to an unidentified object.

**Object/analysis:** Kington 提供了由 Dr. Burke 所做的市实验室分析结果。称该灰烬含有 **magnesium, aluminum, iron, calcium, silicates, sulphur, and carbonates**。Marquardt 推测这可能是某种 **military flare** 或 **"flying saucer"** 的一部分，但也指出，有人告诉他某些照明弹可以燃烧很长时间，并认为巨大的声响可能来自该物体撞击屋顶时产生的真空效应。

**Investigation:** 报告称，因管辖权问题，Marshal's Office 已退出，并建议将任何后续行动移交给 **State Police** 方面处理。文中未给出明确结论；该页记录的是一则未经核实的间接说法，即一场房屋火灾被证人归因于一个身份不明的物体。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typewritten “TRUE COPY” letter from Jackson, Minnesota, dated Aug. 2, 1952, addressed to J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Washington, D.C., and signed “/s/ Wm Hoffmeyer.” It appears in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7, among UFO/flying-disc correspondence. No classification marking is visible on the page.

**Witness:** Hoffmeyer writes on behalf of his family, describing what his uncle and a neighbor’s wife observed. The page does not identify the uncle by name, but Hoffmeyer is the sender and primary correspondent. The letter is informal and speculative, not a formal incident report.

**Sighting:** The event appears to have occurred on Sunday morning, 27 Jul 1952, at a pasture near Jackson, Minnesota. A neighbor’s wife reportedly got up to get water and saw a “steady white Light circling their farm,” though she did not initially consider it important. Later that same morning, Hoffmeyer’s uncle went to get the cows and found an unidentified substance in the pasture.

**Object/trace:** The material was described as “something that looks like tinsel,” found in a round pile. Beneath it, the clover “looked as tho the clover was burned,” and there were “3 similar patches” burned in a triangle formation. Hoffmeyer argues it could not have been dropped from a plane because it was loose, not in a container, and the nearest road was about a half-mile away.

**Investigation:** The letter explicitly asks the FBI to analyze the sample and identify it. No technical findings or FBI conclusion are included on this page, only the request for examination and the sender’s observations connecting the light, burn marks, and strange metallic-looking debris.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), dated 29 Aug. 1952, from D. J. Parsons to Mr. Harbo, subject “Unidentified Flying Object allegedly cited by Mr. D. S. Desvergers, West Palm Beach, Florida.” The memo says the Air Force, by letter of 26 Aug. 1952, asked the FBI to examine Desvergers’ cap for possible residues and to provide an oral report the same night. Internal routing initials and file stamps show it was handled at FBI Headquarters / Laboratory level.

**Witness:** Mr. D. S. Desvergers, identified here as a scoutmaster in West Palm Beach, claimed he was in a desolate area when he observed an unidentified flying object. He reported that the object was about 30 feet in diameter, hovered over his head, and shot a “red blob” that caused him to lose consciousness. He also said the hair on his arms was singed and his cap was burned.

**Investigation:** FBI examination of the cap found no residue that would identify the material responsible for the burns. The memo notes one small burned area that was likely caused by a small hot ember rather than deliberate ignition, and says the singeing was not uniform as would be expected from a single flash of flame. The front edge of the bill was more severely singed than other portions, a pattern the lab said would not be expected if the source were directly overhead. The memo further observes that the fold in the blue cloth showed no singeing underneath, suggesting the cap may not have been worn when the burning occurred. Recommendation: orally advise the Air Force/Colonel Free of these findings rather than attributing the damage to an identified aerial substance.

**Witness:** D. S. Desvergers先生，此处身份标注为West Palm Beach的一名童子军领队，声称他当时身处一处荒凉地带，看到一个不明飞行物。他报告称，该物体直径约30 feet，悬停在他头顶上方，并发射出一个“red blob”，导致他失去知觉。他还说，手臂上的毛发被烧焦，帽子也被烧伤。

**Investigation:** FBI对该帽子的检验未发现任何能识别造成烧痕材料的残留物。备忘录指出，有一处小的烧灼区域，可能是由一小块灼热的火星造成，而非故意点燃；并称烧焦痕迹并不均匀，这与单次火焰闪灼时应有的情况不符。帽檐前缘的烧焦程度比其他部位更严重，实验室认为，如果热源正位于正上方，则不应出现这种分布。备忘录进一步指出，蓝色布料的折痕处下方没有烧焦痕迹，这表明帽子在燃烧发生时可能并未被戴在头上。建议：将上述发现口头告知空军/Free上校，而不要将损坏归因于已确认的空中物质。

**Witness:** No firsthand witness statement appears on this page. The only named field contact is ASAC Plaxico of the Butte FBI office, who was asked about the reports. He is the source for the local-office status of the matter, not the observer of the object.

**Sighting:** According to the memo, a strange white object was reportedly seen on September 19, 1952, streaking across the sky of Montana for about 100 miles. The document does not provide a precise time, altitude, speed, direction, or description beyond “strange white object.” The event is described as a statewide/long-distance aerial track rather than a single-point sighting.

**Object:** The only physical characterization given is that it was white and moved rapidly enough to be described as “streaked across the sky.” No shape, sound, breakup, trail, or landing is noted on this page.

**Investigation:** Hennrich states that while a report of the object had been received at the Butte Office, no investigation was conducted and none was contemplated. This page therefore records administrative awareness rather than a substantive field investigation. For cataloging purposes, the event scope is limited to this single page; no continuation page or separate incident is indicated here.

**Document:** FBI Newark Office Memorandum, Standard Form No. 64, dated 3 Oct 1952 and marked "Security Information Confidential," addressed to the Director, FBI. The memo is filed under Newark division file 100-36998 and references the broader UFO correspondence chain (including USAF Inspector General / 2nd District Office of Special Investigations and later routing to OSI). It concerns background checks on two New Jersey civilians connected to alleged UFO photographs.

**Witness:** George J. Stock of 221 Brooks Avenue, Passaic, N.J., is identified as the photographer who allegedly captured the object. John R. Riley of 571 Main Street, Paterson, N.J., is described as the person who witnessed the incident and developed/printed the exposed film.

**Sighting:** The underlying event occurred on 31 Jul 1952. The memo does not give an exact observation point, but ties the matter to the Passaic/Paterson, New Jersey area. The report says Stock "did photograph an allegedly unidentified aerial object" and Riley witnessed the incident.

**Object:** No physical description of the object appears in this memo beyond its identification as an "unidentified aerial object". The exposed film was later forwarded to the 5th OSI District, Air Technical Intelligence Center, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, by Charles Gregg, staff writer for *The Herald News* (Passaic, N.J.).

**Investigation:** At USAF request, Newark FBI conducted credit checks, criminal checks, and discreet neighborhood inquiries on both men. The office found no criminal records and no indication either man had a history of fraud. The memo states no local investigation was made into the authenticity of the photographs beyond forwarding the results to the local OSI office in New York City, and no further investigations were made by Newark. The FBI’s conclusion was limited to witness reliability/background, not a technical judgment on the image itself.

No shape, motion, size, altitude, sound, or duration is described; the only attribute is that it appears as a spot or blemish on the image.

**Investigation:** The letter is essentially a request for consideration rather than a confirmed sighting report. Because the witnesses saw nothing unusual in real time and the evidence is limited to a photographic mark, the analytical value is weak and the most plausible explanations include dust, emulsion defect, or other photographic artifact. The document preserves the case only as a civilian-submitted UFO-related photograph claim from Washington, D.C.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page printed article excerpt preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7. No FBI routing slip, memo header, classification stamp, or signer is visible on this rendered page; the page is a secondary source narrative rather than a first-hand incident report. Because the sheet also mentions unrelated later sightings, only the Kenneth Arnold incident is treated as the primary event for cataloging.

**Witness:** Kenneth Arnold, described as a businessman on a trip for a Boise, Idaho, fire-control equipment firm, was flying his private plane from Chehalis, Washington, to Yakima, Washington. The article presents him as the inaugural modern “saucer” witness and quotes him directly, suggesting a credible adult observer with aviation experience and a clear view from the cockpit.

**Sighting:** On the afternoon of 1947-06-24, Arnold reported a bright flash reflected from one wing, then observed what he believed were nine tailless aircraft at roughly 20 miles distance, moving toward Mount Rainier. He said the objects flew very close to the mountain tops, in a diagonal chainlike line, and were flat, shiny, and mirror-like. The article states he watched them for about three minutes and estimated their speed at about 1,200 miles per hour.

**Object:** Nine saucer-like, silvery, tailless objects, described as flat and highly reflective. Arnold likened their motion to geese in formation and later to a linked chain of saucerlike things. The piece emphasizes their apparent speed and unusual flight behavior, while noting that Air Force technicians and skeptical newspaper accounts argued the objects would have been invisible at that distance.

**Investigation / assessment:** The article frames the event as the first major U.S. flying-saucer incident and then contrasts it with later explanations applied to other sightings on the same page. It also notes that Arnold later wrote articles about the experience for Fate magazine. As presented here, the page is informative but not an investigative finding; no contemporaneous FBI conclusion about this specific sighting appears on the page itself.

**Witness:** Kenneth Arnold，被描述为一家位于 Idaho 州 Boise 的火控设备公司的商务出差人员，当时正驾驶其私人飞机从 Washington 州 Chehalis 飞往 Washington 州 Yakima。文章将他呈现为现代“飞碟”现象的首位目击者，并直接引用了他的话，表明他是一名可信的成年观察者，具备航空经验，并且从驾驶舱拥有清晰视野。

**Sighting:** 在 1947-06-24 下午，Arnold 报告称看到一道明亮闪光从一侧机翼反射出来，随后观察到他认为是 9 架无尾飞机，距离约 20 miles，正朝 Mount Rainier 方向飞行。他说这些物体飞得非常接近山顶，沿着一条斜向链状队列前进，外形平扁、发亮，像镜面一样。文章称他大约观察了 3 分钟，并估计其速度约为 1,200 miles per hour。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Undated clipping page preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7, the bureau’s UFO-related correspondence/report file. The scanned page (FBI page 0079) is a newspaper/magazine excerpt rather than a formal field report, and it carries no visible letterhead or signature on this page.

**Witness:** The principal witness is Lt. George F. Gorman, described as a North Dakota National Guard pilot flying an F-51 on a routine patrol. The article presents him as a trained airman with enough experience to identify other aircraft in the area and to report the encounter directly to the Fargo tower and later investigators.

**Sighting:** The encounter is described as occurring over Fargo, North Dakota, on 1 Oct 1948. Gorman first saw what looked like another aircraft’s tail light about 1,000 yards away while approaching the Fargo Municipal Airport. Tower personnel reportedly told him the only other aircraft in the area was a Piper Cub, which he could see below him. Gorman described the light as round, clear white, about six to eight inches across in apparent size, with fuzzy edges and an on-and-off blinking pattern. He said that when he moved toward it, the light became steady, banked sharply left, later turned right, and at one point came straight at his aircraft. He dived, climbed, and pursued it from roughly 7,000 to 14,000 feet before it disappeared to the northwest.

**Investigation:** The clipping explicitly discusses Project Saucer’s later skepticism and notes that Fargo weather station had released a lighted balloon about ten minutes before Gorman’s patrol ended. The behavior described on the page, especially the steady, nearly vertical climb and lack of exhaust or sound, is framed as consistent with a balloon rather than a structured craft. On this page, the most plausible analytical conclusion is that the incident was likely a weather-balloon misidentification, not a conventional aircraft or confirmed UFO.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 主要目击者是 George F. Gorman 中尉，他被描述为一名北达科他州国民警卫队飞行员，驾驶 F-51 执行例行巡逻。文章将他呈现为一名受过训练的飞行员，具有足够经验来识别该地区的其他飞机，并将这次遭遇直接报告给 Fargo 塔台以及后来的调查人员。

**Sighting:** 这次遭遇据称发生于 1948 年 10 月 1 日，在 Fargo, North Dakota 上空。Gorman 在接近 Fargo Municipal Airport 时，首先看到约 1,000 码外有一个看起来像是另一架飞机尾灯的光点。塔台人员据称告诉他，当时该区域内唯一的另一架飞机是一架 Piper Cub，而他也能在自己下方看到它。Gorman 将那道光描述为圆形、清晰的白色，按表观大小约有六到八英寸宽，边缘模糊，并呈现断续闪烁的模式。他说，当他朝它飞去时，那道光变得稳定，突然大幅向左倾斜，随后向右转，并且在某一时刻直冲他的飞机而来。他进行了俯冲、爬升，并在大约 7,000 到 14,000 英尺的高度范围内追逐它，直到它向西北方向消失。

**Investigation:** 这段剪报明确提到 Project Saucer 后来持怀疑态度，并指出 Fargo 气象站在 Gorman 的巡逻结束前约十分钟放出过一个带灯的气球。页面所描述的行为，尤其是稳定、近乎垂直的爬升以及没有排气或声音，被认为与气球相符，而不像是有结构的飞行器。在这一页中，最可能的分析结论是，这起事件很可能是将气象气球误认成了其他物体，而非传统飞机或已证实的 UFO。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a secondary-source newspaper/magazine clipping preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7. No FBI memo header, classification stamp, or signer is visible on the page itself; the material is a narrative excerpt about the Washington, D.C. radar UFO incidents, with unrelated advertisements in the left column.

**Witness:** The principal named witness in the excerpt is Barnes, described in context as the radar/controller source for the Washington air-traffic facility. He is quoted at length describing what he saw on the radarscope and rejecting ordinary explanations. Other witnesses mentioned include a commercial pilot, additional nearby pilots, and Air Force interceptor pilots.

**Sighting:** Barnes reports that for six hours on the morning of 20 July 1952 there were at least ten unidentifiable objects moving above Washington. The text then shifts to a related follow-up on 26 July 1952 at 9:08 P.M., when the Air Route Traffic Control Center and Andrews AFB radar again showed unidentified targets over the capital. Two jet interceptors were sent from New Castle, Delaware, toward the objects; one pilot later reported four lights roughly ten miles ahead and slightly above his aircraft, and another saw a steady white light before it vanished.

**Object:** The objects are described as radar pips and lights, not ordinary aircraft. Barnes says they were not aircraft and that he could not attribute them to natural phenomena, shooting stars, electrical disturbances, or clouds. Visual descriptions are sparse but include multiple lights, horizontal motion, and abrupt disappearance.

**Investigation:** The excerpt states that Air Force spokesmen denied evidence that the objects were flying saucers, while also admitting they had no evidence they were not. The incidents triggered intense public reaction, with the Air Force receiving large numbers of letters, calls, and telegrams and airlines being asked to photograph any saucers encountered. The overall analytic takeaway on the page is that the Washington radar cases remained unexplained in the source narrative, even as official caution persisted.

**Witness:** 摘录中提到的主要具名证人是 Barnes，他在上下文中被描述为华盛顿空中交通设施的雷达/管制员消息来源。他被大段引用，描述自己在雷达屏幕上看到的情况，并否定了普通解释。文中还提到其他证人，包括一名商业飞行员、其他附近飞行员以及空军拦截机飞行员。

**Sighting:** Barnes 报告称，在 1952 年 7 月 20 日上午长达六个小时的时间里，华盛顿上空至少有十个无法识别的物体移动。随后，文本转到 1952 年 7 月 26 日晚 9:08 的一个相关后续事件，当时 Air Route Traffic Control Center 和 Andrews AFB 雷达再次在首都上空显示出不明目标。两架喷气式拦截机从 Delaware 的 New Castle 起飞，前往接近这些目标；其中一名飞行员后来报告称，在其飞机前方约十英里处、略高的位置看到了四个灯光，另一名飞行员则看到一个稳定的白光，随后它便消失了。

**Object:** 这些物体被描述为雷达上的光点和灯光，而非普通飞机。Barnes 说它们不是飞机，并且他无法将其归因于自然现象、流星、电气扰动或云层。视觉描述较少，但包括多个灯光、水平移动以及突然消失。

**Investigation:** 摘录称，空军发言人否认这些物体是飞碟的证据，但同时也承认他们没有证据证明它们不是飞碟。这些事件引发了强烈的公众反应，空军收到大量信件、电话和电报，并要求航空公司对遇到的任何飞碟进行拍照。页面上的总体分析结论是，尽管官方保持谨慎态度，华盛顿雷达案例在来源叙述中仍然没有得到解释。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is from *SPACE REVIEW*, page 10, under the heading “SAUCER SIGHTINGS BY IFSB MEMBERS,” with the subhead “Exclusive! From Franklin, Indiana and Surrounding Towns.” The primary incident on the page is “Sighting No. 4,” compiled from a police report turned in by Capt. Lee Sloan, Patrolman Jack W. Moore, and Patrolman Kenneth Rund of the Franklin, Indiana Police Department. The page states that the objects were also witnessed by civilian authorities and members of the U.S. Army, and that after authorities were notified no definite action was taken by the Army or otherwise.

**Witness:** The reporting witnesses were Franklin police officers—Capt. Lee Sloan, Patrolman Jack W. Moore, and Patrolman Kenneth Rund. Because the account is framed as a police report and references multiple corroborating observers, it reads as a multi-witness civilian/official observation rather than a lone sighting. However, the page is a later UFO-periodical summary, not the original police incident report itself.

**Sighting:** On the morning of July 28, 1952, at about 6:00 a.m., three strange objects were seen in the skies southeast of and at times directly over Franklin, Indiana. One object was larger and brighter than the other two; it cast a white-yellow light and appeared to follow the smaller craft. The two smaller objects had their own lights, one orange and one reddish. The report says they flew in a “dog fight” pattern, making barrel rolls, loops, spins, 90-degree and 45-degree turns, and even appearing to move up and down like a giant yo-yo.

**Object:** The observers estimated the objects at about 15,000 feet altitude and varying from 1,500 to 10,000 mph. Even with binoculars, the witnesses could not determine an exact shape beyond “round and flat as a saucer.” The objects were reportedly visible for 4 hours and 15 minutes, with daylight not changing their appearance. At 5:11 a.m. the smaller objects disappeared above the larger one, first the orange and then the red; the larger object then moved west and vanished. The report emphasizes the apparent coordinated maneuvers, but the speed and altitude estimates are likely subjective and should be treated cautiously.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a *Space Review* clipping, page 3, carrying an article titled “Sutton, West Virginia Monster May Be ‘Collier’s’ Rocket!” by Rev. S. L. Daw, Washington, D.C., listed as a Representative of the IFSB. The page is a composite newsletter page; the lower half begins a separate item about New Zealand saucer contacts and is not part of this event.

**Witness:** The article does not name individual observers. It refers generically to “the West Virginia people” who claimed to have seen the object at Sutton, and it cites secondary testimony about a police officer burned by a similar object in Wheeling, with Daw’s cousin described as the treating doctor.

**Sighting:** The Sutton incident is described as a “monster” or object seen in the Sutton/Flatwoods area of Braxton County, West Virginia. Daw summarizes the reported appearance as a large object “in the shape of a man,” estimated at about 10 feet tall and four feet wide at the bottom, with two flashing lights, a sound like gas escaping, and a sharp, sickening odor.

**Object / interpretation:** Daw argues the reported creature may have been a rocket or test article rather than a biological being. He connects the event to a *Collier’s* magazine piece describing a future moon rocket: a sphere-headed, wide-bottomed, tank-bellied craft that would emit burning hydrazine and nitric acid and could, in reflection, be mistaken for a small person or “monster.”

**Investigation / conclusion:** This is not a field report from law enforcement or the military; it is a speculative popular-press interpretation reprinted in a civilian UFO newsletter. The author concludes that the United States may be experimenting with secret rocket technology and that the public is being kept uninformed, suggesting the age of rocket ships is near.

**Document:** This page is a clipped article from *Space Review* titled “Excerpts from a Summary of a Five-Year Flying Saucer Investigation,” by George D. Fawcett (International Council, IFSB). It appears in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7, but it is not an FBI-originated investigative memo. No classification marking is visible on the page.

**Witness:** Fawcett presents himself as a private flying-saucer researcher who had spent a little over five years collecting reports, interviewing astronomers, scientists, pilots, guided-missile experts, and other eyewitnesses. He says he also wrote a pamphlet and lectured on the subject. His own sighting is described as the event that most increased his interest.

**Sighting:** Fawcett states that his first personal encounter was an “orange disk like globe” that hovered for about four minutes over the Lynchburg College administration building in Lynchburg, Virginia, on the morning of 6 July 1951. He does not provide an exact time, weather conditions, or corroborating witnesses on this page.

**Object:** The object is described only as orange, disk-like, and globe-shaped, with a brief hover. No sound, lighting behavior, size estimate, maneuver details, or physical evidence are reported here.

**Investigation:** The rest of the page is a general summary of his five-year UFO research and speculation. Fawcett argues that the accumulated reports suggest the phenomenon may involve grouped sightings, long-duration observations, and possibly controlled or satellite-like activity. He further suggests the U.S. government may know more than it says, but offers no concrete evidence in this excerpt. The page ends with an editorial note and unrelated club notice.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, United States Government, dated March 10, 1953. It was addressed to A. H. Belmont and signed by L. H. Martin. Subject line: “FLYING SAUCERS / JOHN BAILEY, INFORMANT.” The file context and routing show this was an internal FBI HQ memo, not a standalone field interview report.

**Witness:** John Bailey, identified only as an informant. The memo says he called from Bowie, Maryland, at 9:05 P.M. on 3/9/53. He was not cooperative: he was vague about where he was calling from and about his residence, and he did not provide identifying details.

**Sighting:** Bailey stated that he had “just seen a flying saucer near that city,” meaning near Bowie, Maryland. No description of the object’s shape, size, color, motion, altitude, duration, sound, or direction of travel was recorded. The memo does not confirm whether the object was observed directly, photographed, or independently verified.

**Investigation:** When asked where he planned to stay that night so the Air Force could interview him if advisable, Bailey replied that “the writer wanted to know too much” and disconnected. The memo concludes that because no specific information was furnished and the call may have been a prank, the Air Force was not advised. It also notes that no identifying information was obtained and no attempt was made to check Bureau records. Overall, this is best characterized as an unsubstantiated, low-detail UFO claim rather than a corroborated sighting report.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from the SAC, San Juan (65-330) to the Director, FBI, dated 4/28/53. The subject line reads "UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECT OBSERVED 11:30 AM, APRIL 8, 1953, FORT BUCHANAN, PUERTO RICO; MISCELLANEOUS." The page bears handwritten office markings and a blue pencil note reading "flying saucers." The memo states it was prepared after a report was received on 4/27/53 from Major Bradford P. Shuman, Wing Intelligence Officer, Ramey Air Force Base, Puerto Rico.

**Witness:** Five persons at Fort Buchanan reportedly observed the object, including three captains and a sergeant of the U.S. Army, plus one civilian. Their statements were summarized by the Air Force intelligence office; the memo does not identify the individuals by name. The sighting was therefore secondhand to the FBI, coming through military intelligence channels.

**Sighting:** The event occurred at 11:30 AM on 4/8/53 at Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico. The witnesses described the object only generally, as either a "bright star" or a "bright ball of fire" at a great height, moving rapidly while observed. No size, shape, maneuvering details, sound, or duration are provided.

**Investigation:** The memorandum notes that all witnesses also observed one RB-36 aircraft in the area at the time. The Wing Intelligence Officer reported two RB-36 aircraft were operating nearby, at 12,000 and 21,000 feet respectively. None of the witnesses could accurately describe the object beyond the brief comparison above. The memo says the matter was being reported to the Bureau for information purposes and is marked "CLOSED." The file code at the bottom reads FDO 'B:MD, and the page is stamped/recorded in FBI indexing traces. Overall, the report records an unexplained daytime aerial observation, but the contemporaneous military context and the lack of detailed description prevented any firm identification.

**Document:** Single-page handwritten civilian letter preserved in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7 (1947 UFO/flying-disc correspondence). The page bears FBI handling stamps and routing marks, but no formal investigative memorandum or interview notes. The letter is signed by Mrs. Robert W. Harrison.

**Witness:** Mrs. Harrison writes as a private citizen in Watertown, Massachusetts. Her tone suggests a contemporaneous complaint to federal authorities after she was unable to get a response from local channels. She asks for the matter to be reported to the proper authorities and for guidance on whom citizens should contact in such cases.

**Sighting:** She says that when she arrived home she spent about half an hour calling Civil Defense and Air Force ground operations, then called the Watertown police when no one answered. She describes the thing only as an “unknown object” and says she had never seen anything like it before. The page does not preserve any details about shape, size, color, motion, altitude, noise, or duration beyond her statement that it was unfamiliar.

**Investigation:** No identification, corroboration, or technical analysis appears on this page. Instead, the letter reflects the early 1947 UFO reporting environment: a civilian trying to find an official channel for a suspected aerial anomaly and urging local Civil Defense to maintain a duty contact. The record provides provenance for the complaint but not enough observational detail to assess the object beyond “unknown.”

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page letter on Grand Hotel, Mackinac Island, Michigan stationery, dated June 30, 1953, addressed to the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Washington, D.C. The page is marked with FBI handling stamps and notations including “RECORDED,” “INDEXED,” and file references, indicating it was retained as correspondence in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7. The text is the only page shown, so the event scope is limited to this single report.

**Witness:** The described observer is a respected farmer near Circleville, Ohio, identified in the letter only as “Mr. Stevenson.” The author says a relative in Circleville relayed the account. No first name appears on the page.

**Sighting:** The farmer reportedly saw “a lighted object” dancing around and flying in the air late at night in a pasture or field near Circleville. The object was described in the local retelling as a “flying saucer.” The letter states the sighting occurred “two years ago” relative to the document date, placing it at approximately mid-1951.

**Investigation / provenance:** The writer claims the story became known in the community and later appeared in the Circleville newspaper. The letter further alleges that FBI representatives later visited the farmer, showed him pictures of various flying saucers or space ships said to have been recovered by the government, and that he identified one as matching what he had seen. Those claims are presented as secondhand rumor (“so it is said”) rather than direct observation. The letter also repeats a sensational claim that the identified craft was said to be from Mars and that a Martian captive was being taught English in California; this appears clearly folkloric and not corroborated by the document. No official FBI findings are included on the page, and the best reading is that this is an unsolicited civilian letter recounting a local UFO rumor rather than a formal investigative report.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI Atlanta teletype to the Director, marked urgent, dated 8 Jul 1953 at 11:02 AM, filed under the Bureau’s “Flying Saucers” correspondence. The page is stamped as FBI Communications Section material and carries routing/initials marks and the file notation from the 62-HQ-83894 UFO section.

**Witness:** The account was not observed directly by FBI personnel. Atlanta Constitution reporter Tom McRae is named as the complainant, but the event originates with Edward E. Waters of 1855 Peachtree Rd. NE (telephone ELgin 9562), who telephoned McRae at 3:45 AM. Waters said he and two companions were traveling in a car near Mableton, Georgia.

**Sighting:** Waters reported that the party encountered three small animals on or near Bankhead Highway about Mableton. He believed the animals had landed from a flying saucer. As they approached, the three objects/animals began moving back toward what Waters thought was the saucer; two allegedly escaped into it, while the third was struck and killed by the automobile. Waters then brought the specimen to McRae at the newspaper office.

**Object:** McRae said the animal did not resemble anything he had seen before, though it looked like it belonged to the monkey family. It was measured at approximately 21 inches long, with a rather pointed head, large ears, and pinkish skin. The teletype adds that McRae could not locate a scientist early that morning, but a leading city veterinarian did examine the animal.

**Assessment:** The report is a secondhand, sensational early-morning account transmitted through a newspaper reporter and relayed to FBI headquarters. The description strongly suggests a misidentified animal or specimen rather than a confirmed aerial craft event. No follow-up findings are contained on this page.

**Document:** FBI case-file cable/page from **62-HQ-83894, Section 7** (UFO/Flying-Disc-related correspondence), signed **CARSON** and cc’d to **Mr. Belmont** and the **Supervisor, Domestic Intelligence Division**. The page says the matter was **referred to OSI** at 9:00 AM EST and that **no investigation** was being conducted by that office. It also notes **“Atlanta indices negative on Waters.”**

**Witness/Source:** The narrative is attributed to **McRae**, who relayed what a veterinarian said after examining an animal brought in by **Waters**. McRae appears to be the principal human source describing the specimen and the surrounding circumstances.

**Sighting/Report:** This is not a classic flying-disc sighting; it is a report about a **hairless, monkey-family animal carcass** that Waters presented amid what McRae suspected might be a **publicity gag**. McRae said the veterinarian would not fully commit to an identification, but pointed out he had never seen an animal in the monkey family without hair like this one, nor a dead animal that did not turn pale at death.

**Object:** The animal reportedly **had a tail, but it was missing**, possibly cut off accidentally. McRae also noted **blood around the mouth**, described as resembling human blood. He believed Waters may have been trying to exploit recent newspaper stories, though he also suggested the timing was poor for a stunt because the paper could print after midnight.

**Assessment:** The memo treats the matter as a likely **publicity/hoax lead rather than an authentic UFO event**. The FBI did not open a local investigation, and the only recorded action was referral upward to OSI for awareness.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a newspaper clipping preserved in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7, with the enclosure stamp "62-83894-334" and source code "7/8--N53P." It appears to be a press item forwarded to the Bureau rather than a direct field report. No continuation page is shown, and nothing on this page indicates a separate second incident.

**Witness:** The principal claimant is Edward Watters, a 28-year-old barber in Atlanta. His companions were Arnold Payne, a butcher, and Thomas Wilson, another barber. The article says all three gave the same account. Their credibility is weakened by the fact that the report itself notes they had consumed "one beer apiece" before the event.

**Sighting:** The men said that about midnight, while driving on a highway near Atlanta, they struck or ran into a glowing object in the middle of the road. Watters described it as "glowing red all over," about waist high and roughly half as wide as the road. He claimed it resembled a flying-saucer image he had seen in a science magazine. He further asserted that three small men were running toward it, that two escaped, and that he hit the third, after which the machine/object "rose into the air and zoomed away."

**Object / investigation:** The men produced a 21-inch-long "creature" the next day to support their story. Dr. W. A. Mickle, anatomy professor at Emory University, examined it and concluded it was an animal victim of an automobile accident, most likely a member of the rhesus monkey family, although hairless. He rejected the extraterrestrial interpretation with a dismissive remark that, if it were from outer space, "they haven't invented anything news." Watters reportedly planned to freeze the specimen with dry ice and put it on display. Overall, the clipping records a sensational UFO claim that was immediately contradicted by a medical/animal identification and was likely treated by the FBI as a press curiosity rather than corroborated evidence of a flying-saucer event.

**Document:** 这是一页报纸剪报，保存在 FBI 案卷 62-HQ-83894、Section 7 中，附有封存编号“62-83894-334”和来源代码“7/8--N53P。”。看起来这是转交给 Bureau 的新闻报道，而不是直接的现场报告。页面上没有显示续页，且本页内容也未表明另有单独的第二起事件。

**Witness:** 主要当事人是 Edward Watters，亚特兰大(Atlanta)的一名28岁理发师。他的同伴是 Arnold Payne，一名屠夫，以及 Thomas Wilson，另一名理发师。文章称三人所作陈述完全一致。但报告本身提到，他们在事发前都各喝了“一杯啤酒”，这削弱了他们的可信度。

**Sighting:** 这几名男子说，大约在午夜时分，他们驾车行驶在亚特兰大(Atlanta)附近的一条公路上时，撞上了或开进了道路中央一个发光物体。Watters 将其描述为“全身发红发亮”，大约有腰部那么高，宽度约为道路的一半。他声称，这东西看起来像他在一本科学杂志上见过的飞碟图像。他进一步称，有三个小个子男人正朝它跑去，其中两人逃脱了，而他击中了第三个，随后那台机器/物体“升入空中并疾速飞走”。

**Object / investigation:** 第二天，这几名男子拿出一个长21英寸的“生物”来支持他们的说法。Emory University 的解剖学教授 W. A. Mickle 博士对其进行了检查，并得出结论：它是汽车事故中的动物受害者，最可能属于恒河猴(rhesus monkey)一类，尽管没有毛发。他以一种轻蔑的评论否定了外星生物的解释，说如果它来自外太空，“那他们还没发明什么新鲜玩意儿呢。” 据报道，Watters 计划用干冰把这个标本冷冻起来并公开展示。总体而言，这份剪报记录了一起耸人听闻的 UFO 声称，但很快就被医学/动物鉴定所推翻；FBI 很可能只是把它当作一则新闻奇闻，而非经过证实的飞碟事件证据。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single typed Spanish letter dated Valparaíso, Chile, 4 Mar 1953, addressed to the Director of the FBI in Washington and included in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7. The page is headed as a reference to a person with possible involvement in "Discos Voladores". No sender name is visible on the page.

**Witness:** The author appears to be an unnamed correspondent in Valparaíso rather than a firsthand UFO witness. The page compiles reported newspaper material and draws inferences from it.

**Sighting:** The letter does not describe one direct observation by the writer. Instead, it cites three published anecdotes: (1) the 1950 London detention/escape of Dr. Julius Linke, during which police allegedly encountered a sudden blackout, stopped elevators, dead telephones, and failed flashlights; (2) a Berlin incident shortly before the fall of the city in which car and truck engines allegedly stopped for about an hour before restarting; and (3) a local newspaper/AP account from roughly three months earlier in which an officer and companion pursued a flying disc that performed maneuvers, rose to great height, hovered over their airplane, and allegedly stalled the aircraft’s engines.

**Object:** The object is described as a "disco volador" (flying disc) with unusual maneuverability and the apparent ability to interfere with electrical or mechanical systems.

**Investigation:** The writer’s central theory is speculative: if the London/Kent incidents involved a person’s "interference" with electrical systems, then Dr. Linke might also explain the Berlin engine stoppage and the aircraft encounter. The page reads as analytical correspondence, not as an official FBI field investigation or a verified sighting report.

**Witness:** 作者似乎是Valparaíso（瓦尔帕莱索）的一名匿名通信者，而非亲历UFO目击者。该页汇编了已报道的报纸材料，并据此作出推断。

**Sighting:** 这封信并未描述作者本人的一次直接观察。相反，它引用了三则已发表的轶事：（1）1950年London（伦敦）对Dr. Julius Linke（朱利叶斯·林克博士）的拘留/逃脱事件，据称警方当时遭遇了突发停电、电梯停运、电话失灵以及手电筒不亮；（2）Berlin（柏林）在城市陷落前不久的一起事件，据称汽车和卡车发动机曾停止运转约一小时，随后才重新启动；（3）大约三个月前的一则当地报纸/AP报道，其中一名警官及其同伴追逐一个飞行碟，该物体进行了机动动作，升至很高高度，悬停在他们的飞机上方，并据称使该飞机发动机熄火。

**Object:** 该物体被描述为一个“disco volador”（飞碟），具有不同寻常的机动性，并似乎能够干扰电气或机械系统。

**Investigation:** 作者的核心理论带有推测性质：如果London（伦敦）/Kent（肯特）事件涉及某人对电气系统的“干扰”，那么Dr. Linke（朱利叶斯·林克博士）或许也能解释Berlin（柏林）的发动机停转事件以及那次与飞行器的遭遇。该页更像是一封分析性通信，而不是正式的FBI现场调查或经过核实的目击报告。
