events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from the SAC, Cincinnati, to the Director, FBI, dated July 15, 1953, with internal notations including ReBulet dated 7-9-53 and file markings (DOE:VD, AMSD). The subject line names “Mr. W. S. Woodfill, President, Grand Hotel, Mackinac Island, Michigan,” but the body of the memo is about a separate Ohio flying-saucer inquiry.

**Witness:** Bruce Stevenson, Rural Route 2, Circleville, Ohio, was the principal civilian witness. The memo also cites Sheriff Charles Radcliff of Circleville as a local law-enforcement source who knew Stevenson personally and characterized him as a prosperous, well-respected farmer who was considered trustworthy.

**Sighting:** Stevenson reportedly said a saucer-shaped object had landed on his farm “some time ago,” with the report later reaching local newspapers. The memo does not give a precise sighting date; it places the matter in June 1953 and notes an FBI interview on 7-14-53 after the case received publicity.

**Object:** The object is described only as “saucer-shaped.” No size, color, sound, duration, occupants, or landing traces are recorded in this memo.

**Investigation:** According to Sheriff Radcliff, an individual discussed the report with Stevenson in June 1953 and claimed no official government connection. Stevenson identified the visitor as Jack W. Grant, Post Office Box 512, Tri-Village Station, Columbus, Ohio, who said he sold television antennas, had spent over six years investigating flying-saucer reports, had no official government tie, and had once been “checked” by the FBI. Stevenson also said Grant showed him flying-saucer pictures and said he was writing a book. FBI Cincinnati then searched its indices and found no identifiable information on either Bruce Stevenson or Jack W. Grant. The memo reflects a routine field check and does not reach a substantive conclusion on the alleged landing beyond negative index results and local credibility notes.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is an FBI Headquarters reply from J. Edgar Hoover, dated July 24, 1953, to Mr. W. S. Woodfill, President of the Grand Hotel, Mackinac Island, Michigan. It bears the file context 62-HQ-83894 (Section 7), a red cross-reference number 62-83894-335, and routing/classification markings including “RECORDED-34.” The page is mainly a follow-up note rather than a field sighting memo.

**Witness:** The only named alleged witness is Bruce Stevenson, a farmer on Rural Route 2 near Circleville, Ohio. Hoover’s letter says Woodfill had asked about a report that Stevenson had seen a “flying saucer” and had been interviewed by the FBI.

**Sighting:** No direct first-hand observation details are provided on this page. The document does not describe the object’s appearance, movement, duration, sound, altitude, or number of witnesses. The underlying date of the claimed sighting is not given; the earliest referenced event is Woodfill’s June 30, 1953 inquiry about the rumor.

**Investigation:** Hoover states the matter was outside the FBI’s investigative jurisdiction and that no FBI representative conducted the interview Woodfill referenced. A note appended to the page says FBI Cincinnati was asked to determine the rumor’s basis; its July 15, 1953 response reported that Stevenson was interviewed on July 14 and said he had been interviewed by Jack W. Grant of Columbus, Ohio, who claimed to have been “checked” by the FBI. Cincinnati files reportedly showed no prior FBI interview with Stevenson. Overall, the page documents rumor verification and administrative clarification, not a substantiated UFO case.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 唯一被点名的所谓目击者是Bruce Stevenson，一名居住在俄亥俄州Circleville附近Rural Route 2的农民。Hoover的信中说，Woodfill曾询问一则传闻：Stevenson看见了一个“flying saucer”，并且还接受了FBI的采访。

**Sighting:** 这一页没有提供任何直接的一手目击细节。文件未描述该物体的外形、运动方式、持续时间、声音、高度或目击者人数。所称目击事件的原始日期也未给出；最早提到的相关事件是Woodfill于1953年6月30日就该传闻提出询问。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Newspaper clipping from *The Cincinnati Post* dated 1954-10-11, preserved in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8. This page is a press clipping rather than an FBI-authored memo; no FBI signatory, routing stamp, or classification marking is visible on the page itself.

**Witness:** The article’s latest Cincinnati report is attributed to Keith Wildeson, identified as a WLW announcer, who relayed the incident to Leonard H. Stringfield of 7017 Britton Avenue, Madison Place. Stringfield is described as the director of civilian research on “interplanetary flying objects,” and the story also names neighbor John H. Sundstrom of 7010 Britton Avenue as another local observer.

**Sighting:** The clipping says “mysterious aircraft” — described as orange-red, silent, disc-shaped, and about 60 feet in diameter — were reported hovering roughly 300 feet over Cincinnati on Monday at 5 a.m. It adds that this was the fifth similar report within a week, with the objects allegedly appearing in threes. A separate Cincinnati sighting attributed to Sundstrom is said to have occurred Sunday at 5 p.m., when he saw a formation of three discs.

**Investigation:** Stringfield is quoted as saying the reports “seem to indicate a pattern” and speculating that Cincinnati may lie on a magnetic fault line where the saucers might “recharge.” The clipping then switches to a separate German “little men” saucer story, which is clearly unrelated and not part of the Cincinnati event. No independent FBI evaluation, follow-up report, or corroborating field investigation is shown on this page; the record here is a newspaper account of multiple civilian sightings in and around Cincinnati.

events.date_raw: Between the hours of 10:35 and 11:15 P.M., 9/5/54 (document page -7-; no separate document date shown)
events.title: Rockford, IL amateur astronomers report luminous object near Moon, 5 Sep 1954
events.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a mixed newsletter-style case-file page preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8. It includes an unrelated write-up on the Cincinnati paint incident and, under **CASE FILE REVIEW**, a separate Rockford, Illinois observation coded “C-22, Rockford, Ill.. 9/5/54).” The page is numbered “-7-” and cites a prior article by Edward S. Schultz in B.S.R.A.’s *Round Robin*; the editorial note is signed by Meade Layne.

**Witness:** Amateur astronomers Peter Bartkus and Theodore McColm were watching the Moon through a telescope. Bartkus is the principal narrator in the quoted report.

**Sighting:** Between 10:35 and 11:15 P.M. on 5 September 1954, Bartkus reported observing “the most unusual phenomena” he had ever witnessed. The Moon was in first quarter, with an apparent diameter of 29 feet 30 inches. Using a 6-inch casigranian reflector telescope with secondary mirror, over 100 inches focal length, and 150x and 200x eyepieces, the pair saw a spherical object rising from the northern section of Mare Humboldtianum.

**Object:** The object was described as not glowing or brilliant, but more like a dull reflected light from a planet. Its estimated apparent size was about that of the craters Pitiscus or Vlaco. By the time it disappeared at 11:15 P.M. it had traversed more than the Moon’s apparent diameter in roughly 40 minutes.

**Investigation / conclusion:** The witnesses checked for atmospheric diffraction and optical artifacts by moving the telescope and changing eyepieces, but found no explanation. Bartkus concluded the object was a powered body because the Moon was descending at about 1,081 mph while the object appeared to rise and did not follow a true orbit. His final assessment was that it was “definitely in space” and in the same field as, or near, the Moon. The page records no formal FBI analysis beyond preserving the report in the case file.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 本页是保存在 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894、Section 8 中的一页混合式通讯稿风格案件档案页。其内容包括一则与辛辛那提油漆事件无关的报道，以及在 **CASE FILE REVIEW** 标题下的一条独立的伊利诺伊州 Rockford（罗克福德）观测记录，编号为“C-22, Rockford, Ill.. 9/5/54).” 本页编号为“-7-”，并引用了 Edward S. Schultz 先前发表于 B.S.R.A. 的 *Round Robin* 中的一篇文章；编辑注记署名 Meade Layne。

**Witness:** 业余天文学家 Peter Bartkus 和 Theodore McColm 当时正通过望远镜观察月球。Bartkus 是引文报告中的主要叙述者。

**Sighting:** 1954年9月5日晚上 10:35 至 11:15 之间，Bartkus 报告称他观察到了自己“所见过的最不寻常的现象”。当时月球处于上弦月，其视直径为 29 feet 30 inches。两人使用一台带副镜的 6-inch casigranian 反射望远镜，焦距超过 100 inches，并配合 150x 和 200x 目镜，看到一个球形物体从 Mare Humboldtianum 的北部区域升起。

**Object:** 该物体被描述为并不发光或明亮，更像是来自行星的暗淡反射光。其估计视大小大约与 Pitiscus 或 Vlaco 两个陨石坑相当。到晚上 11:15 它消失时，它在大约 40 分钟内穿越了超过月球视直径的距离。

**Investigation / conclusion:** 目击者通过移动望远镜和更换目镜，检查了大气衍射和光学伪影的可能性，但未能找到解释。Bartkus 认为该物体是一个由动力驱动的天体，因为月球正以约 1,081 mph 的速度下沉，而该物体却似乎在上升，并且没有遵循真实轨道。他的最终判断是，它“绝对在太空中”，并且与月球处于同一视场，或位于月球附近。该页仅记录了将这份报告保存在案件档案中，并未包含任何正式的 FBI 分析。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single newspaper clipping preserved in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8, enclosure 62-83894-357. The clipping is from the *Rome Daily American* and carries a United Press story datelined Rovigo, Italy, Oct. 16, published in the Sunday, Oct. 17, 1954 edition.

**Witness:** The account does not name an individual witness. It attributes the sighting to several score of unnamed villagers from nearby Po di Gnocca, with police serving as the secondary source for their statements.

**Sighting:** The article says the villagers saw a silver disc or “flying saucer” approach at great speed over the Po River marshlands, land gently in the marshes a few miles away, then after a short pause rise vertically and depart toward the east. Police reportedly found a shallow 20-foot crater and scorched popular trees at the alleged landing site.

**Investigation:** The clipping presents the event as one of many contemporaneous Italian “flying saucer” reports. It notes that the Italian Air Ministry said no such objects had been registered on its radar network. No FBI narrative, interview report, or follow-up analysis appears on this page, so the preserved evidence is limited to a press account of an alleged landing rather than a verified investigation.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI 案卷 62-HQ-83894 第 8 节、附件 62-83894-357 中保存的一张报纸剪报。该剪报来自 *Rome Daily American*，刊载了一则美联社（United Press）报道，报道日期为意大利 Rovigo，10 月 16 日，发表在 1954 年 10 月 17 日星期日版。

**Witness:** 该记述未点名任何具体目击者。它将此次目击归于来自附近 Po di Gnocca 的数十名未具名村民，并由警方作为其陈述的第二手来源。

**Sighting:** 文章称，村民们看到一个银色圆盘或“飞碟”以极快速度掠过波河（Po River）沼泽地带，在几英里外的沼泽中轻轻降落，随后短暂停顿，又垂直升起，向东飞去。据报道，警方在所谓的降落地点发现了一个浅浅的 20 英尺弹坑，以及被烧焦的杨树。

**Investigation:** 这则剪报将该事件呈现为当时意大利众多“飞碟”报道之一。文中提到，意大利空军部（Italian Air Ministry）表示，其雷达网络上并未记录到此类物体。此页未见 FBI 的叙述、访谈报告或后续分析，因此所保存的证据仅限于一则关于所谓降落事件的新闻报道，而非经过核实的调查。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum from SAC, Cincinnati (62-0) to the Director, dated 8/2/54, in FBI file 62-HQ-83894 (Section 8). The page is an incoming UFO/flying-saucer report and notes that the matter was to be referred to the appropriate United States Air Force officials. It records the report as having been received through Colonel J. M. Smith, Deputy Director of Civilian Defense for Greater Cincinnati and Hamilton County, Ohio.

**Witness:** The principal witness was Carl R. Keyser of Route 1, Milford, Ohio. According to the memo, Smith spoke with Keyser after receiving the initial complaint, and Keyser said he could be reached at his residence about two miles east of Milford on U.S. Highway 28. The report is based on Keyser's account and is secondhand to the FBI through Smith.

**Sighting:** Keyser stated that he and his wife observed the object at approximately 2:40 p.m. on 7/23/54. The object was described as a silver, circular or spherical shape in the sky, located to the southeast of their residence and about 45 degrees above the horizon. The memo does not record any estimated size, motion, sound, duration, or trail, and it provides no indication of a landing or close approach.

**Investigation:** The Cincinnati office advised Smith that the report would be forwarded to the proper U.S. Air Force authorities. The document contains no follow-up findings, and no analytical conclusion beyond referral is stated. Because the file page is a brief administrative summary rather than a full interview, the evidence here is limited to a single civilian observation relayed through local civil defense channels.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 来自 Cincinnati (62-0) 的 SAC 致 Director 的 FBI 办公备忘录，日期为 8/2/54，收录于 FBI 文件 62-HQ-83894（Section 8）。该页是一份入报的 UFO/flying-saucer 报告，并注明此事将转交给适当的 United States Air Force 官员处理。报告记录称，该信息是通过 Colonel J. M. Smith 传来的，他是 Ohio 州 Greater Cincinnati 和 Hamilton County 的 Civilian Defense 副主任。

**Witness:** 主要目击者为 Carl R. Keyser，住址为 Milford, Ohio 的 Route 1。根据备忘录，Smith 在收到最初投诉后与 Keyser 进行了交谈，Keyser 表示可在其住所联系到他，该住所位于 Milford 以东约两英里，靠近 U.S. Highway 28。该报告依据 Keyser 的叙述而成，通过 Smith 转述给 FBI，因此属于间接信息。

**Sighting:** Keyser 称，他与妻子于 7/23/54 下午约 2:40 观察到该物体。该物体被描述为天空中的银色、圆形或球形物体，位于其住所的东南方向，且约在地平线以上 45 度处。备忘录未记录其估计大小、运动情况、声音、持续时间或尾迹，也未表明其有着陆或近距离接近的迹象。

**Investigation:** Cincinnati 办公室通知 Smith，该报告将转交给适当的 U.S. Air Force 当局。该文件未包含后续调查结果，也未给出除转交之外的分析结论。由于该档案页仅是简短的行政摘要，而非完整访谈，因此这里的证据仅限于通过地方民防渠道转述的一次普通民众目击。

events.title: Piedmont windshield “cancer” epidemic, 1954
events.report_summary:
**Document:** Single newspaper clipping pasted to FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8, enclosure 351, from the *Rome Daily American* dated Tuesday, September 28, 1954. This page is a press excerpt only; no FBI memo, interview report, or follow-up sheet appears on the page.

**Witness:** The article’s named individual is Dr. Martino Farinetti of Modena, who was driving to a clinic when his windshield allegedly burst. The clip also references unnamed motorists in the Italian Piedmont, Rome, and Genoa who experienced the same phenomenon.

**Sighting:** The reported event is not a conventional flying-object observation but a wave of unexplained windshield breakages described as a "windshield ‘cancer’ epidemic." According to the article, the trouble first appeared in the Italian Piedmont in June 1954, then moved east and south to Rome, later to Genoa, and most recently to Modena. Drivers reportedly had no warning before the glass suddenly shattered.

**Object:** No aircraft, disc, or physical object is described. The "phenomenon" consisted of windshields exploding into thousands of pieces, injuring occupants and nearly causing accidents. The article says the episodes occurred day or night and seemed unrelated to weather, speed, or vehicle age; Italians reportedly called it "cancer of the windshield."

**Investigation:** The clipping says the mystery had left authorities puzzled. It offers no technical explanation and no evidence tying the incidents to a UFO or other airborne object. In the FBI file, it functions as a retained news clipping about an unexplained public-safety anomaly in Italy rather than a formal investigative report.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 剪自 *Rome Daily American*（《罗马每日美国人报》）1954年9月28日星期二的一则报纸剪报，粘贴于FBI案件档案 62-HQ-83894，第8节，附件 351。此页仅为新闻摘录；页面上没有出现FBI备忘录、访谈报告或后续记录表。

**Witness:** 文章中提到的当事人是来自Modena（摩德纳）的Dr. Martino Farinetti，他当时正驾车前往一家诊所，声称挡风玻璃突然炸裂。该剪报还提到意大利Piedmont（皮埃蒙特）、Rome（罗马）和Genoa（热那亚）一些未具名的驾车者也经历了同样现象。

**Sighting:** 所报告的事件并不是常规的飞行物目击，而是一波无法解释的挡风玻璃破裂事件，被形容为一种“挡风玻璃‘癌症’流行”。据文章称，这一麻烦最初于1954年6月出现在意大利Piedmont（皮埃蒙特），随后向东和向南蔓延至Rome（罗马），之后又到了Genoa（热那亚），最近则出现在Modena（摩德纳）。据称，驾驶员在玻璃突然碎裂之前毫无预警。

**Object:** 文中没有描述飞机、圆盘或任何实体物体。所谓“现象”表现为挡风玻璃爆裂成成千上万的碎片，伤及车内人员，并几乎引发事故。文章称，这些事件无论白天黑夜都会发生，且似乎与天气、车速或车龄无关；意大利人据称将其称为“挡风玻璃癌症”。

**Investigation:** 这则剪报称，这一谜团已使当局困惑不已。文中没有提供技术解释，也没有证据将这些事件与UFO或其他空中物体联系起来。在FBI档案中，它仅作为一则保留的新闻剪报，内容涉及意大利一项无法解释的公共安全异常事件，而非正式的调查报告。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, Standard Form No. 64, from SAC Kansas City (66-2995) to Director, FBI, dated 1/18/55, file subject “C. W. Cheek / Flying Saucer / Misc. - Information Concerning.” The page carries FBI handling stamps and later redactions, but the text is legible enough to reconstruct the report.

**Witness:** C. W. Cheek, telephone AT 6747, Kansas City, Kansas, who told an FBI agent on 13 Jan 1955 that he was employed as an aeronautical engineer at the Ford Aircraft Plant in Claycomo, Missouri. He said he had obtained the agent’s name from a prior FBI investigation connected to a sabotage case at the plant about a year earlier.

**Report:** Cheek stated that he and two other engineers had perfected plans for a “flying saucer type aircraft.” He claimed they had been negotiating for several months with the U.S. Air Force and the CIA regarding sale of the plans to the Air Force. He further said that Jack Stampler, identified as Chief of the Defense Department in Washington, D.C., was fully aware of the aircraft plans and had advised him not to discuss them with anyone except FBI agents or high-ranking U.S. Air Force officers.

**Investigation / Conclusion:** This page records a tip/interview rather than an observed aerial event. No actual sighting, object description, flight path, or corroborating witness testimony is given on the page. The FBI memorandum is essentially a notice of Cheek’s claims about a proposed aircraft design, not a confirmed UFO incident. No follow-up findings or technical validation appear on this page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI办公室备忘录，标准表格第64号，由堪萨斯城SAC（66-2995）致FBI局长，日期为1/18/55，案卷主题为“C. W. Cheek / Flying Saucer / Misc. - Information Concerning.” 该页带有FBI处理印章及后来的删改痕迹，但文字仍清晰到足以还原报告内容。

**Witness:** C. W. Cheek，电话 AT 6747，Kansas City, Kansas（堪萨斯州堪萨斯城），他于1955年1月13日向一名FBI特工表示，他受雇于Missouri（密苏里州）Claycomo的Ford Aircraft Plant（福特飞机厂），担任航空工程师。他说，他是从先前一次与该工厂破坏案件有关的FBI调查中得知这位特工姓名的，该案件大约发生在一年前。

**Report:** Cheek称，他与另外两名工程师已完善了一种“flying saucer type aircraft（飞碟型飞机）”的设计方案。他声称，数月来他们一直在与U.S. Air Force和CIA就将该方案出售给空军一事进行谈判。他还说，Jack Stampler，被认定为Washington, D.C.（华盛顿特区）国防部负责人，完全知晓该飞机方案，并建议他除FBI特工或高级别U.S. Air Force军官外，不要向任何人谈论此事。

**Investigation / Conclusion:** 这一页记录的是一次线索/访谈，而非一次实际观察到的空中事件。页面未给出任何真实目击、物体描述、飞行路线或可相互印证的证人证词。该FBI备忘录本质上只是对Cheek关于一项拟议飞机设计之说法的记录，并非已证实的UFO事件。此页未见后续调查结果或技术验证。

events.title: Frances Swan 'outer space' contact claims, Ottawa area, 27 May 1954
events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Headquarters memorandum in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8, continuing across pages 3-4 of the report. The pages carry the standard FBI distribution list at the bottom (Tolson, Boardman, Nichols, Belmont, Harbo, Mohr, Parsons, Rosen, Tamm, Sizoo, Winterrowd, Tele. Room, Holloman, Gandy) and conclude that the information is being furnished to USAF Office of Special Investigations, Army G-2, and Naval Intelligence, with no further Bureau action.

**Witness:** Mrs. Frances Swan is described by Hutson as a very simple-minded, religious, middle-class woman with at most a high school education. Her husband, Guy Swan, and their daughter, Dawlyn, also reportedly heard a buzzing in their ears, though they did not receive the “messages.”

**Sighting/Claim:** This is not a conventional visual UFO sighting but a reported telepathic/contactee case. Mrs. Swan complained that a painful buzzing sound had been occurring since May 27, 1954, often at night, and that it was disrupting her sleep. A schedule was arranged for messages at 8:00 a.m., noon, and 6:00 p.m. daily so the messages would not interfere with sleep.

**Object/Content:** The report says the transmissions concerned flying saucers, why they were here, life on other planets, life hereafter, and Bible prophecies. Mrs. Swan allegedly identified two principal ships, M-4 and L-11, measuring 150 miles wide by 200 miles long and 100 miles deep, plus about 5,000 smaller mother ships. Their commanders were named as “Affa” (from Uranus) and “Ponnar” (from Hatann). The alleged purpose was to protect Earth from atomic/hydrogen-bomb destruction and to preserve the universe by repairing “fault lines.”

**Investigation:** Hutson stated that he and Smith were seeking proof and wanted to know whether they could contact the “man from outer space.” Mrs. Swan allegedly said contact could be made on any frequency if they first advised her of the frequency used. The report also says Smith planned to try contact on Sunday, August 1, 1954, and that the ship would come within 100 miles of Ottawa, Canada. The memorandum treats the claims as extraordinary and unsupported, but records them for referral rather than endorsement.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI总部备忘录，载于案卷62-HQ-83894，第8节，续见报告第3-4页。各页底部列有标准的FBI分发名单（Tolson, Boardman, Nichols, Belmont, Harbo, Mohr, Parsons, Rosen, Tamm, Sizoo, Winterrowd, Tele. Room, Holloman, Gandy），并注明相关信息已转交USAF Special Investigations办公室、Army G-2和Naval Intelligence，FBI不再采取进一步行动。

**Witness:** Hutson将Frances Swan夫人描述为一位非常单纯、虔诚的中产阶级女性，受教育程度最高不过高中。她的丈夫Guy Swan以及他们的女儿Dawlyn，据称也听到耳中有嗡嗡声，不过他们并没有接收到这些“信息”。

**Sighting/Claim:** 这并非传统意义上的目击UFO事件，而是一宗据称通过心灵感应/接触者方式发生的案件。Swan夫人称，自1954年5月27日起，她一直受到一种刺耳且令人痛苦的嗡嗡声困扰，且常在夜间出现，严重影响她的睡眠。后来安排了每天上午8:00、中午和下午6:00接收“信息”的时间表，以免这些信息干扰睡眠。

**Object/Content:** 报告称，这些传输内容涉及飞碟、它们为何来此、其他行星上的生命、来世以及《圣经》预言。Swan夫人据称确认了两艘主要飞船，分别为M-4和L-11，尺寸为宽150英里、长200英里、深100英里，另有约5,000艘较小的母舰。其指挥官被称为“Affa”（来自Uranus）和“Ponnar”（来自Hatann）。据称其目的在于防止地球遭受原子弹/氢弹毁灭，并通过修复“断层线”来维持宇宙的稳定。

**Investigation:** Hutson表示，他和Smith正在寻求证据，并想知道他们是否能够联系到“来自外太空的人”。据称Swan夫人说，只要先告知她所使用的频率，就可以在任何频率上建立联系。报告还称，Smith计划在1954年8月1日星期日尝试联系，而那艘飞船将会到达加拿大Ottawa以外100英里范围内。该备忘录将这些说法视为非同寻常且缺乏证据，但仍予以记录，供转交参考，而非表示认可。

events.title: Billy Thomas Gambill: bright yellow light over Oxford, PA, 4 May 1956
events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI memo EX-109, dated May 11, 1956, from John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation, to the Director of Special Investigations, Office of the Inspector General, Department of the Air Force (Building Tempo E, Washington, D.C.). File markings on the page reference FBI file 62-HQ-83894 and the subject line reads "FLYING DISC OBSERVED, OXFORD, PENNSYLVANIA, MAY 4, 1956" with the classification/case notation "MISCELLANEOUS - INFORMATION CONCERNING (ESPIONAGE)." The page is stamped "BY COURIER SERVICE" and appears to be a single-page report; no later page on this image set indicates a separate incident.

**Witness:** The reporting party first identified himself to the FBI as Thomas Gamble of 102 Center Street, Oxford, Pennsylvania, then later corrected his identity to Billy Thomas Gambill of 419 South Broad Street, Kennett Square, Pennsylvania. He was a civilian driver traveling by car at the time of the sighting.

**Sighting:** At 11:35 p.m. on May 4, 1956, Gambill reported seeing a bright light in the air over Oxford, Pennsylvania, traveling toward Baltimore, Maryland at an estimated altitude of about 2,000 feet. He said the object was a solid, bright yellow light visible from all directions, roughly twice as bright and twice as large as an automobile headlight, and about twice as bright as the evening star. He reported no sound and said the light initially appeared to match his car's speed before accelerating; despite driving 80 mph, he could not keep up. He also stated that two friends, Cecil Pew and Raymond Dixon, had also observed the object.

**Investigation:** The memo is a brief relay from FBI Director Hoover to the Air Force, with no detailed scientific evaluation on the page. Based on the description, the event is recorded as an unexplained bright light rather than a structured aircraft identification. The page provides no follow-up determination, triangulation, or corroborating technical data beyond the witness account and the later correction of his true name and address.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI 备忘录 EX-109，日期为 1956年5月11日，发自 Federal Bureau of Investigation 局长 John Edgar Hoover，致 Department of the Air Force 监察长办公室特别调查主任（Building Tempo E, Washington, D.C.）。页面上的档案标记注明 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894，主题栏写有“FLYING DISC OBSERVED, OXFORD, PENNSYLVANIA, MAY 4, 1956”，分类/案件标注为“MISCELLANEOUS - INFORMATION CONCERNING (ESPIONAGE)”。该页盖有“BY COURIER SERVICE”印章，且看起来是一份单页报告；在这组图像中未见更后续的页面表明这是另一起独立事件。

**Witness:** 报告人最初向 FBI 自称为 Thomas Gamble，地址为 Pennsylvania 州 Oxford 的 102 Center Street，随后又更正其身份为 Billy Thomas Gambill，地址为 Pennsylvania 州 Kennett Square 的 419 South Broad Street。事发时，他是一名乘车行驶的平民司机。

**Sighting:** 1956年5月4日晚上 11:35，Gambill 报告称他在 Pennsylvania 州 Oxford 上空看到一束明亮的光，朝 Maryland 州 Baltimore 方向飞行，估计高度约为 2,000 英尺。他说，该物体是一团实体、明亮的黄色光，从各个方向都可见，亮度大约是汽车前灯的两倍、大小也约为两倍，且约为傍晚时分金星亮度的两倍。他报告称没有听到任何声音，并表示这束光起初看起来与他汽车的速度相当，随后加速；尽管他驾驶速度达到 80 mph，仍无法追上。他还称，两位朋友 Cecil Pew 和 Raymond Dixon 也曾观察到该物体。

**Investigation:** 这份备忘录只是 FBI 局长 Hoover 向空军进行的一次简短转交，页面上没有详细的科学评估。根据描述，该事件被记录为一束无法解释的明亮光，而非经过结构化识别的飞行器。除目击者陈述及其后对真实姓名和地址的更正外，该页未提供后续结论、三角测量结果或可佐证的技术数据。

events.title: Sylvia L. Richards near Henderson NC: blue spinning disc, 6 Apr 1956
events.report_summary:
**Document:** These three consecutive pages are one event file chain for FBI case 62-HQ-83894, Section 8. Page 133 is an internal memo from W. G. Eames to Mr. Nichols dated 4-10-56; page 132 is a follow-up memo from A. H. Belmont to L. V. Boardman dated April 13, 1956; page 134 is Director J. Edgar Hoover’s cover memo dated April 16, 1956 to the Air Force Inspector General, Director of Special Investigations. All three describe the same reported sighting by Sylvia L. Richards and are clearly part of the same incident/report, not separate events.

**Witness:** Sylvia L. Richards, a GS-5 employee in the FBI Name Check Unit, reported the incident while traveling with her fiancé, Joseph L. Morris, Jr., an employee of the National Security Agency. The memo from Eames notes she is “one of our best employees” and that she had previously placed little credence in flying-saucer stories, which the file uses to support her credibility.

**Sighting:** On about 5:00 a.m. on April 6, 1956, while driving on Route 1 north of Henderson, North Carolina, Richards and Morris saw an unusual low-flying object approach their car from ahead/on the driver’s side. She described it as round or oval, spinning, very bright, light blue, and apparently containing a zig-zag or series of lights. It flew very low, appeared at least as wide as the highway, and was estimated to be only 2 to 4 feet thick and less than 25 feet above the ground. It made no sound, passed over the car, then appeared to accelerate and veer out of sight. She later noted that daylight was breaking, the sky was cloudy, and rain began about 30 minutes afterward.

**Investigation:** The FBI’s summary states that both Richards and Morris felt they had seen something unusual that was difficult to explain and that it did not seem to be an optical illusion. The case was routed within FBI Headquarters and then referred by Hoover to the Air Force for possible further handling. The file does not resolve the object’s identity; the closest analytical note is that an optical illusion was considered but not favored by the witnesses or the reviewing agents.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这三页连续的材料构成了 FBI 案件 62-HQ-83894、第 8 节中的一条事件文件链。第 133 页是一份 W. G. Eames 于 4-10-56 致 Mr. Nichols 的内部备忘录；第 132 页是一份 A. H. Belmont 于 1956 年 4 月 13 日致 L. V. Boardman 的后续备忘录；第 134 页是 Director J. Edgar Hoover 于 1956 年 4 月 16 日致 Air Force Inspector General, Director of Special Investigations 的附函备忘录。这三份文件都描述了 Sylvia L. Richards 报告的同一次目击事件，显然属于同一事件/报告链，而不是彼此独立的事件。

**Witness:** Sylvia L. Richards 是 FBI Name Check Unit 的一名 GS-5 员工，她是在与未婚夫 Joseph L. Morris, Jr. 一同旅行时报告了这一事件；Joseph L. Morris, Jr. 是 National Security Agency 的一名员工。Eames 的备忘录指出，她是“我们最优秀的员工之一”，而且她此前对飞碟传闻并不太相信，文件据此用来支持她的可信度。

**Sighting:** 1956 年 4 月 6 日约凌晨 5:00，当 Richards 和 Morris 驾车行驶在北卡罗来纳州 Henderson 以北的 Route 1 上时，他们看到一个异常的低空飞行物从前方/驾驶员一侧向他们的车接近。她将其描述为圆形或椭圆形、旋转、非常明亮、浅蓝色，并且似乎内部有锯齿状或一系列灯光。该物体飞行得很低，看起来至少和公路一样宽，估计只有 2 到 4 英尺 厚，且离地面不足 25 英尺。它没有发出任何声音，从汽车上方掠过，随后似乎加速并转向飞离视线。她后来补充说，当时天色已开始发亮，天空多云，大约 30 分钟后开始下雨。

**Investigation:** FBI 的摘要称，Richards 和 Morris 都认为他们看到了某种难以解释的异常现象，而且这并不像是视觉错觉。该案随后在 FBI Headquarters 内部流转，之后由 Hoover 转交给 Air Force 以便视情况进一步处理。文件并未最终确认该物体的身份；最接近的分析性说明是，曾考虑过视觉错觉的可能，但目击者和审阅该案的特工都不倾向于这一解释。

Damon Eckles of the Air Information Service.

Sauter reportedly believed the account was "utterly ridiculous" but needed to comply with orders. events.title: John Stuart Martin UFO report, Great Meadows NJ, 12 Mar 1957
events.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI Headquarters office memorandum (Standard Form 64) from L. B. Nichols to Mr. Tolson, dated March 15, 1957, in file 62-HQ-83894 (Section 8). The page is heavily annotated and cross-referenced, with cc lines to Boardman and Belmont and later recording/index stamps. It is an internal FBI summary of a civilian telephone call, not a field investigation report.

**Witness:** John Stuart Martin, age 56, of Great Meadows, New Jersey, telephone Mercury 7-2683. Nichols identifies him as one of the original founders of *Time* magazine, formerly associated with Louis de Rochemont's *House on 92nd Street* and editor of *March of Time*; the memo also notes he is married to Mary Gilbert and has one arm. Martin is portrayed as a credible, well-connected civilian source who believed his information had not been handled properly by military channels.

**Sighting:** Martin phoned his home at 12:52 p.m. on March 14, 1957, and said that "two days ago" he had encountered a situation involving an unidentified flying object observed in the Great Meadows vicinity, implying a sighting date of about March 12, 1957. The memo does not preserve any physical description of the object, only that it was an "unidentified flying object." Martin said he had already made a formal written report to military authorities and to two civilian groups interested in the matter, one of which was connected with Gen. Wedemeyer.

**Investigation:** Martin wanted an FBI Agent to visit so his information could be evaluated, but he also acknowledged that "flying saucers" were outside FBI interest and jurisdiction. Nichols notes the usual FBI response would be to refer such matters to the proper military authority. The page contains no independent corroboration, and no analytical conclusion about the object is offered beyond the jurisdictional referral.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Communications Section teletype from SAC, New York, to the Director, dated Nov. 7, 1957 at 12:41 AM, filed in 62-HQ-83894 (Section 8). The page is an internal bureau relay of a local UFO complaint; it includes routine routing marks, stamps, and initials, but no follow-up report on this page beyond the initial field summary.

**Witness:** The principal named source is James Colyer of the incorporated village of Old Brookville police department, who relayed the reports. He said several residents and a member of the police department had seen the phenomenon, and that he passed the information to Mitchell AFB and Roslyn Airfield.

**Sighting:** On the evening of Nov. 6, 1957, over Old Brookville, Long Island, New York, observers reported two red lights hovering in the air over the vicinity. The lights were described as an even distance apart and at one point appeared to be joined together. Colyer also reported that the lights lit up and seemed to cast a red dust or fog into the surrounding air.

**Investigation:** The teletype notes that Mitchell AFB and Roslyn Airfield both reported receiving numerous similar calls; Roslyn Air Field said aircraft were investigating the matter. The report also says the information was broadcast on WINS radio. No identification is offered on the page, and the FBI appears to be forwarding the local police/airfield reports rather than drawing a conclusion.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), from the SAC, Kansas City (file 66-2995) to the Director, FBI, dated 1957-11-08, subject “Flying Discs – Information Concerning.” The page is an internal lead report, with a recommendation that the Dallas Office locate and interview the witness and obtain film for transmittal to the Bureau.

**Witness:** The reporting source was Mr. Donald Keith Gash, 3012 Blueridge, Kansas City, Missouri, who told SA Walter S. Pond about his uncle, Leland Jesse Gash (also written Jesse Leland Gash). The uncle was described as employed by an aircraft concern and residing in Fort Worth, Texas.

**Sighting:** According to Donald Keith Gash, his uncle saw an unidentified object in the sky near his home in Fort Worth about two years earlier. The uncle used his movie camera to take pictures of the object. No size, shape, color, flight pattern, duration, or performance details are given in this memo beyond the fact that the object was unidentified and photographed on film.

**Evidence:** About 18 months before the memo, the uncle visited Kansas City and showed the film. The film was described as being about 15 feet long and “very good.” The memo does not indicate whether the Bureau had yet reviewed it.

**Investigation:** Gash said he and his uncle felt “foolish” about discussing the matter and therefore never reported it, but later decided the Government should have the information because of international developments. The memo suggests the Bureau, after reviewing the film, advise the USAF Office of Special Investigations of any pertinent information. This page appears to be the complete report for this lead.

events.title: Sen. Richard B. Russell: glowing ball from train near Butte, Montana
events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Headquarters memorandum to the Director of Central Intelligence, subject “Sightings of Flying Saucers or Unconventional Aircraft,” file 62-HQ-83894 / enclosure 62-83894-361 (copy 6 of 10). The page states that all four participants had been debriefed and gives a consolidated summary of their observations.

**Witness:** The primary witness was Senator Richard B. Russell, traveling by rail with three companions, including Colonel Hathaway and Mr. Green (a fourth participant is referenced later in the text but the name is partly unclear on this page). The report portrays Russell as a cooperative, credible observer who was simply resting in his compartment when the first object appeared.

**Sighting:** While the party was traveling by train from Butte, Montana, at about 1910 hours, Russell saw a small greenish-yellow glowing ball rise rapidly after darkness had already fallen. He alerted the others, who then observed a second object a few minutes later. One observer described only two lights “resembling eyes,” while Colonel Hathaway saw a shadowy body with a single light near the top and projecting lights at the base. The objects were estimated variously as rocket-sized or about the size of a U.S. jet fighter.

**Object:** The observers agreed that the object(s) seemed to rotate or whirl during a steep initial ascent, and some thought the flight path changed sharply to horizontal flight. No trail was seen behind the luminous ball. Mr. Green also reported a third ground-level object with three lights near a searchlight, but the others did not confirm ground objects.

**Investigation:** The memo’s own conclusion is cautious: based on the testimony, only Colonel Hathaway’s account meaningfully supported the possibility of an unidentified unconventional aircraft; the other accounts were less definitive. The page is thus a debrief summary rather than a confirmed identification, and it preserves the FBI’s skepticism about whether the sighting was an actual flying saucer or a misinterpreted aircraft/light phenomenon.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI总部致中央情报局局长的备忘录，主题为“飞碟或非常规飞机的目击”，卷宗 62-HQ-83894 / 附件 62-83894-361（第 6 份，共 10 份）。该页说明四名参与者均已接受询问，并对他们的观察作了汇总摘要。

**Witness:** 主要目击者是参议员 Richard B. Russell，他与三名同伴一同乘火车旅行，其中包括 Hathaway 上校和 Mr. Green（文中后面还提到第四名参与者，但此页上姓名部分不清楚）。报告将 Russell 描述为一位配合、可信的观察者；当第一个物体出现时，他只是在车厢内休息。

**Sighting:** 当一行人乘火车从 Butte, Montana 出发、约在 1910 hours 时，天色已经完全黑下来，Russell 看见一个小小的黄绿色发光球体迅速升起。他随即提醒其他人，几分钟后他们又观察到第二个物体。一名观察者只描述看到两个“像眼睛一样”的灯光，而 Hathaway 上校则看见一个模糊的主体，顶部附近有一盏灯，底部有向外投射的灯光。对这些物体的估计不一，有人认为其大小如火箭，也有人认为大约相当于一架 U.S. 战斗机。

**Object:** 观察者一致认为，该物体（或这些物体）在最初陡直上升时似乎发生了旋转或翻滚，部分人认为其飞行轨迹随后突然转为水平飞行。发光球体后方未见任何尾迹。Mr. Green 还报告称地面上另有第三个物体，附近有三盏灯和一盏探照灯，但其他人并未确认存在地面物体。

**Investigation:** 该备忘录本身的结论较为审慎：根据证词，只有 Hathaway 上校的叙述在实质上支持“存在不明非常规飞机”的可能性；其他叙述则不够明确。因此，这一页更像是一份询问后总结，而非已确认的识别结果，并且保留了 FBI 对该目击事件究竟是实际的飞碟，还是被误解的飞机/光学现象的怀疑态度。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Decoded FBI teletype/copy in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8, marked "DEFERRED" and routed "TO DIRECTOR" from **SAC, Springfield** (file/traffic no. 072245). The page is a single incident report with no continuation page shown. It is stamped/processed through FBI radio and coding channels and marked for information bureau use.

**Witness:** The report is secondhand to the FBI through **Assistant Chief Walter A. Eichen, Illinois State Police**, who relayed the account of ISP officers **Calvin Showers** and **John Matulis** of **District Ten**. Because the report comes through police channels rather than directly from the observers, it is a law-enforcement report with moderate corroborative value, but still hearsay at the FBI level.

**Sighting:** Officers reported that at about **9:00 PM on 7 Nov 1957** they saw a **bright white light** flying through the air in a **southwesterly direction from Danville, Illinois**. They attempted to follow it by car and drove generally southwest for about **20 miles** before losing sight. During the chase the object reportedly appeared **bright white, amber, and orange**. The report says there was **no indication it dipped to the ground** or that it affected their car.

**Object / Effects:** For a few seconds it was said to affect both the **receiver and transmitter of their FM two-way radio**. No shape, size, altitude, or maneuvers beyond directional flight were documented. The narrative does not indicate a landing, crash, or debris.

**Investigation:** The teletype notes that **International News Service** representatives inquired and the office made **no comment**. The report was furnished "for information bureau." On the basis of the text alone, the case documents an unexplained light/possible aircraft or electrical interference episode, but provides insufficient detail for a firm identification.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 该报告并非直接来自 FBI，而是由 **Assistant Chief Walter A. Eichen, Illinois State Police** 转述，后者又转达了 **District Ten** 的 ISP 警员 **Calvin Showers** 和 **John Matulis** 的陈述。由于该报告经由警方渠道而非直接来自目击者，因此在执法层面属于一份具有中等佐证价值的报告，但在 FBI 层面仍属传闻证据。

**Sighting:** 警员报告称，大约在 **7 Nov 1957 晚上 9:00**，他们看到一个**明亮的白色光体**以**自 Danville, Illinois 向西南方向**在空中飞行。他们试图驾车追踪，整体向西南行驶了约 **20 miles** 后失去视线。在追逐过程中，该物体据称曾呈现**明亮白色、琥珀色和橙色**。报告称**没有迹象表明它降到地面**，也没有影响他们的车辆。

It is a Bureau-originated summary, not a direct witness affidavit.

**Witness:** Mrs. Donald Blevins of 1235 Shawnee, Houston, Texas, reported that an object fell into her yard on October 24. Her son recovered it and brought it to a science teacher, who recommended that authorities be notified. The report is therefore second-hand at the Bureau level, but it preserves the woman’s first description of the event and the object.

**Sighting/Object:** The object was described as being between the size of a golf ball and a fist, "of metallic ash of some kind," and "bright and hot when it fell." No movement, trajectory, or sound was recorded in the memo. The event is framed as a falling object that landed near a home rather than a distant aerial observation.

**Investigation:** Information was furnished to the FBI by OSI at Ellington AFB, which had conducted an investigation. A press inquiry was answered by stating that the report had been received and relayed to military authorities. OSI’s conclusion, as quoted in the memo, was that the object was part of an ordinary flare and of no significance. The Bureau’s treatment of the matter is consistent with a non-UFO explanation, and the file entry serves mainly as a documented referral and closure note.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Detroit 31, Michigan memorandum dated November 7, 1957, in file 62-83894-384, under the heading "UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS." The page bears an unclassified stamp and red handwritten routing/approval notations. These two pages are a single continuous report; page 2 is explicitly marked "-2-" and continues the same interview narrative.

**Witness:** Wladyslav Krasuski, a Polish displaced person and former prisoner of war living in Detroit, was interviewed at the request of the federal government after writing to Robert Cutler, special assistant to President Dwight D. Eisenhower, saying he might know something about "the rocket in Texas." At the time of the interview he was employed at Gobel Brewery in Detroit.

**Sighting:** Krasuski said that in 1944, while walking to work near Gut Alt Golssen, about 30 miles east of Berlin, he experienced a tractor-engine stall in a swampy road area. He later observed an alleged circular vehicle in an otherwise deserted zone guarded by German SS personnel. He placed the vehicle at roughly 500 feet, describing it as circular, 75-100 yards across, about 14 feet high, with dark gray top and bottom sections and a three-foot middle section that appeared as a rapidly moving blurred band around the circumference. He also described a whine or generator-like noise.

**Investigation:** The account says an SS guard spoke with the tractor driver, waited several minutes, and the noise stopped, after which the tractor restarted normally. On a later visit, Krasuski said he saw a circular enclosure screened by a ~50-foot tarpaulin wall, a vertical rise of the object, and uninsulated metal cables running underground between the enclosure and a small concrete column-like structure. He reported that the cables were removed after the war and the area later flooded. The memo also notes he had not been in contact since 1945 with other POW laborers who had discussed the incident, except for remembering one man, Francizek Grabowski. The report is a retrospective wartime recollection, not a contemporaneous airborne sighting, and the source is a single civilian witness with no corroboration in the file excerpt.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** Wladyslav Krasuski，一名波兰流离失所者、前战俘，居住在 Detroit；他是在联邦政府的要求下接受采访的。此前，他曾写信给 Robert Cutler（Dwight D. Eisenhower 总统的特别助理），称自己可能知道“the rocket in Texas.” 的一些情况。接受采访时，他在 Detroit 的 Gobel Brewery 工作。

**Sighting:** Krasuski 说，1944 年，在前往工作途中、靠近 Gut Alt Golssen（Berlin 以东约 30 英里）时，他在一处泥泞道路地带遇到拖拉机引擎熄火。后来，他在一片原本空无一人的区域里，看到一个据称的圆形飞行器，该区域由 German SS 人员看守。他将该飞行器的位置估计在约 500 英尺处，并描述其为圆形，直径 75-100 码，高约 14 英尺，顶部和底部为深灰色，中间有一段约 3 英尺的区域，看上去像一道沿周边快速移动的模糊带。他还描述听到一种尖啸声或类似发电机的噪音。

**Investigation:** 该叙述称，一名 SS 警卫与拖拉机司机交谈了几分钟，随后噪音停止，拖拉机也随即恢复正常并重新启动。后来再次前往时，Krasuski 说他看见一个圆形围栏，外围由约 50 英尺高的防水油布墙遮挡，随后又看到该物体竖直上升，并有未绝缘的金属电缆从围栏与一个小型混凝土柱状结构之间穿过地下。他报告说，这些电缆在战后被拆除，而该地区后来被洪水淹没。备忘录还指出，自 1945 年以来，他未再与其他曾讨论此事件的战俘劳工保持联系，只记得其中一人名叫 Francizek Grabowski。该报告属于对战时经历的事后回忆，并非当时的空中目击；在所引文件片段中，也只有这一名平民证人，且没有任何旁证。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Standard Form 64 memorandum from the Legal Attaché in Havana, Cuba, addressed to the Director, FBI, dated **November 20, 1957**. Subject line: **“REPORTS OF FLYING DISCS / FOREIGN MISCELLANEOUS.”** The memo states the information is submitted “as of interest to the Bureau” and adds that no other corroborating reports were received and no inquiry was made by that office. File markings and stamps indicate routine Bureau handling and indexing of the report.

**Witness:** The sighting is attributed to **José María Nieto** and **Carmelo Guzmán**, described in the memo only as men who had just arrived in town from the **Matahambre Mines** area in Pinar del Río Province. The report does not identify them as trained observers, but it presents their account as a newspaper-cited civilian report.

**Sighting:** According to the Havana newspaper **Diario de la Marina** (Nov. 12, 1957), in a dispatch datelined **Nov. 11, 1957** from **Pinar del Río, Cuba**, the two men said they saw a **flying disc in the shape of a man’s hat** hovering over the general area of **Matahambre** for several minutes. They reportedly judged it larger than ordinary airplanes seen locally, said it was **completely silent**, and stated that it departed at **very high speed toward the sea**.

**Investigation:** The FBI memo gives no technical analysis and no follow-up findings. It merely relays the newspaper account, notes that Matahambre is about 90 miles west of Havana, and records that the Legal Attaché had received no corroboration. No direct witness interview appears on this page; the incident is captured as a foreign press item forwarded for reference.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 载于古巴哈瓦那的法律专员致 FBI 局长的一份 FBI 标准表格64备忘录，日期为 **November 20, 1957**。主题行：**“REPORTS OF FLYING DISCS / FOREIGN MISCELLANEOUS.”** 备忘录称，所提供信息“系因其对 Bureau 具有参考价值”而提交，并补充说，该办公室未收到其他可佐证的报告，也未进行任何调查。案卷标记和印章表明，该报告仅按 Bureau 的常规程序进行处理和归档。

**Witness:** 这起目击事件归因于 **José María Nieto** 和 **Carmelo Guzmán**。备忘录中仅将二人描述为刚从 **Matahambre Mines** 地区来到 **Pinar del Río Province** 镇上的两名男子。报告并未将他们认定为受过训练的观察者，但将其说法作为一则被报纸引用的平民报告予以转述。

**Sighting:** 据哈瓦那报纸 **Diario de la Marina**（1957年11月12日）报道，在一则署名日期为 **Nov. 11, 1957**、发自 **Pinar del Río, Cuba** 的通讯中，这两名男子称，他们看到一个**形状像一顶人帽的飞碟**在 **Matahambre** 一带上空悬停了数分钟。据称，他们判断其体积比当地常见的普通飞机更大，并表示它**完全没有声音**，随后又称它以**极高速度向海上飞去**。

**Investigation:** FBI 备忘录未作任何技术分析，也没有后续调查结果。它只是转述了报纸报道，注明 Matahambre 距 Havana 西约 90 英里，并记录法律专员未收到任何佐证材料。此页未见对目击者的直接访谈；该事件仅作为转供参考的外国媒体报道被收录。

**Document:** Handwritten first-person narrative on lined paper retained in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9. The page is date-stamped Mar. 10, 1958 and carries FBI handling marks (including REG-92). No accompanying formal memorandum or conclusion appears on this page; it reads as a citizen-submitted story about an alleged UFO encounter.

**Witness:** The writer identifies herself only indirectly as a married woman living with her husband and three daughters on a farm in Michigan. She says her oldest daughter worked nights as a waitress at a country club about seven miles away, and the witness regularly drove to pick her up after midnight. The account is firsthand but retrospective, written roughly 5 or 6 years after the event, which reduces precision on date and place.

**Sighting:** One night, shortly after leaving the highway on the return trip from the country club, the witness saw a moving object ahead of her along the side of the road. She says it had tiny lights that were going on and off; when the lights were off she could make out a dark moving shape. She emphasizes that there was absolutely no noise and states that she immediately believed human beings were guiding it. The remainder of the report continues beyond this page.

**Assessment:** On the evidence visible here, the event is too vague to geolocate more precisely than rural Michigan. The report is a personal anecdote rather than an official field investigation, with no measurements, witnesses, or physical evidence recorded on this page. The most reliable take-away is that the writer described a silent, low-level moving object with intermittent lights, seen from a car on a dark road near a country club.
events.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 这名作者只间接表明自己的身份：她是一位已婚女性，与丈夫和三个女儿住在 Michigan（密歇根州）的一处农场里。她说，长女在大约七英里外的一家乡村俱乐部做夜班女服务员，而她自己经常在午夜后开车去接女儿。这个叙述属于第一手经历，但带有回忆性质，写于事件发生后大约 5 或 6 年，因此在日期和地点上不够精确。

**Sighting:** 某个夜晚，在从乡村俱乐部返程、刚驶离公路后不久，目击者看到前方路边有一个移动的物体。她说它带着微小的灯光，灯光忽明忽灭；当灯光熄灭时，她能看出一个黑暗的移动轮廓。她强调现场绝对没有任何噪音，并表示她立刻认为是有人在操控它。报告其余部分在本页之后继续。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** This is a later FBI Headquarters memorandum dated 18 Nov 1958 from G. A. Nease to Mr. Tolson, summarizing a Phoenix Office matter in file **62-HQ-83894, Sec. 9** (with later stamps such as **EX-135** and **REC-15**). It is not the original 1947 field report, but a retrospective recap prompted by an Arizona Republic inquiry about Rhodes and his negatives. The page is the only one in the provided sequence and no later page indicates a separate incident.

**Witness:** The named individual is **William Albert Rhodes**, a civilian who told the Phoenix Office that he had photographed what he believed were flying discs. The memo does not give a rank or employer, and it provides no first-hand observation details beyond Rhodes’ claim.

**Sighting:** On **30 Apr 1947**, Rhodes reportedly told the Phoenix Office that he had taken photographs of alleged flying discs. The memo does not specify the exact observation location or the time of the photographs themselves, only that the report was made to the Phoenix Office in Phoenix, Arizona.

**Object:** The objects were described only as “flying discs” / later “flying saucers.” No shape, color, size, motion, altitude, or number is given on this page. The key item discussed is the **photographic negatives**, which Rhodes initially did not have with him, then brought in on **30 Aug 1947**.

**Investigation:** According to the memo, Rhodes was told in 1947 that the negatives were being accepted for **FBI/Air Force intelligence** and that their return was doubtful. The negatives were then turned over to **George Fugate, Jr.**, military representative. In 1950 Rhodes asked for their return and was referred to the Air Force Office of Special Investigations in San Francisco. In 1958, SAC McMahon reported that Rhodes told the Arizona Republic the FBI had borrowed the negatives but never returned them; HQ instructed that the paper be told the negatives had been received with the understanding they would go to Air Force intelligence and might not be returned. The page reflects administrative handling of the material rather than independent confirmation of the sighting.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这是一份较晚的 FBI 总部备忘录，日期为 1958 年 11 月 18 日，由 G. A. Nease 致 Mr. Tolson，概述了档案 **62-HQ-83894, Sec. 9** 中凤凰城办公室的一项事项（后附有诸如 **EX-135** 和 **REC-15** 等印章）。它并非 1947 年的原始外勤报告，而是针对 Arizona Republic 就 Rhodes 及其底片所作询问而形成的事后回顾。本页是所提供序列中的唯一一页，且后续页面未显示另有独立事件。

**Witness:** 文中所指个人为 **William Albert Rhodes**，一名平民，他向凤凰城办公室称自己拍摄到了他认为是飞碟的物体。备忘录未给出其职务或雇主，也未提供除 Rhodes 声称之外的第一手目击细节。

**Sighting:** 据称在 **30 Apr 1947**，Rhodes 向凤凰城办公室报告说，他拍摄了所谓飞碟的照片。备忘录并未说明具体的观测地点或拍摄时间，只提到该报告是向亚利桑那州 Phoenix 的凤凰城办公室作出的。

**Object:** 这些物体仅被描述为“flying discs”/后来的“flying saucers”。本页未给出形状、颜色、大小、运动方式、飞行高度或数量。文中讨论的关键物品是 **photographic negatives**（摄影底片），Rhodes 起初并未随身携带，随后在 **30 Aug 1947** 将其带来。

**Investigation:** 根据备忘录，Rhodes 在 1947 年被告知，这些底片将移交给 **FBI/Air Force intelligence**，且其返还的可能性不大。随后，底片被交给了 **George Fugate, Jr.**，即军方代表。1950 年，Rhodes 请求归还底片，并被转介至旧金山的 Air Force Office of Special Investigations。1958 年，SAC McMahon 报告称，Rhodes 告诉 Arizona Republic，FBI 借走了这些底片却从未归还；总部指示应告知该报，这些底片是在同意将其交给空军情报部门的前提下接收的，且可能不会归还。该页反映的是对相关材料的行政处理，而非对该目击事件的独立确认。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Detroit memorandum dated March 9, 1960, headed "Re: Unidentified Flying Object; Joseph Perry, Grand Blanc, Michigan – Complaint." It is a narrative report in Bureau correspondence style, produced in response to Perry’s request. The page is part of FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9.

**Witness:** Joseph Perry of 3079 Edwards Street, Grand Blanc, Michigan, said he operated a pizza house at 3075 Edwards Street and had been a professional photographer for about thirty years. Agents contacted him at his request on March 5, 1960.

**Sighting:** Perry reported that at about 1:00 a.m. on February 21, 1960, while photographing the moon through a home-made telescope, he took a set of moon photographs. After developing them and viewing the images, he said that one photograph showed what appeared to be a flying object somewhere between the end of the telescope and the surface of the moon.

**Object:** Perry described the object as flat on the bottom when enlarged, oval-shaped, with a fluorescent glow around the entire object and a vapor trail behind it. He believed it was actually moving. He said he had taken over 1,000 moon pictures and had never seen anything resembling it. Based on his photographic experience, he stated he was sure the image was not a camera malfunction, not a blur from the telescope, and not an artifact of film development.

**Investigation:** Perry said he took about twenty moon pictures that night, found most underexposed, cut out the two that appeared properly exposed, destroyed the rest, and furnished both selected pictures to the FBI. The page contains Perry’s statement only and does not record any final Bureau conclusion about the image.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI Detroit 备忘录，日期为 1960 年 3 月 9 日，标题为 “Re: Unidentified Flying Object; Joseph Perry, Grand Blanc, Michigan – Complaint.” 这是一份采用局内函件风格撰写的叙述性报告，为回应 Perry 的请求而制作。该页属于 FBI 案卷 62-HQ-83894，第 9 节。

**Witness:** 来自 Michigan（密歇根州）Grand Blanc（格兰布兰克）3079 Edwards Street 的 Joseph Perry 说，他在 3075 Edwards Street 经营一家比萨店，并且已经做了大约三十年的职业摄影师。探员于 1960 年 3 月 5 日应其要求与他取得联系。

**Sighting:** Perry 报告称，1960 年 2 月 21 日凌晨约 1:00，他用自制望远镜拍摄月亮时，拍了一组月球照片。冲洗并查看这些照片后，他说其中一张照片显示出一个看起来像飞行物的东西，位置大约在望远镜末端与月球表面之间。

**Object:** Perry 将该物体描述为：放大后底部平坦、呈椭圆形，整个物体周围带有荧光般的光晕，后方还有一条蒸汽尾迹。他认为它实际上正在移动。他说自己拍过 1,000 多张月球照片，从未见过类似的东西。根据他的摄影经验，他表示自己确信这张影像不是相机故障，不是望远镜造成的模糊，也不是胶片冲洗过程中的伪影。

**Investigation:** Perry 说，当晚他拍了大约二十张月球照片，发现大多数曝光不足，便剪下了两张看起来曝光正常的照片，销毁了其余照片，并将这两张选中的照片交给了 FBI。该页仅包含 Perry 的陈述，并未记录 FBI 对该影像的最终结论。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Handwritten page 6 from FBI HQ file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9, a flying-disc correspondence file from 1947. No typed header is visible on this page; the text is a first-person account and reads like a private letter or statement submitted to the Bureau. The writer closes by saying she has “no proof” but wanted to see whether the government believed any of it.

**Witness:** An unnamed adult woman, apparently a widow. She says her husband died two years earlier, that she rented out the farm, and that she and her daughters now live in Elkhart, Indiana. Her account is therefore secondhand only in the sense that she is narrating from memory, but she presents herself as an ordinary rural resident with direct observation of the object.

**Sighting:** She states that on the morning she found a newspaper she went upstairs and looked down across the orchard toward the river, where she saw “the flying saucer.” The exact calendar date and exact farm location are not stated on this page. The sighting location is only described as a farm/orchard with a river view in the Elkhart area.

**Object:** She describes a transparent, glass-like, dome-shaped craft “like an eskimo hut.” Inside was a large ring “like a napkin ring,” but enormous, with everything apparently inside that ring. As she watched, the whole ring lit up in colors and the interior could no longer be seen. The object rose straight up, was plainly visible against the trees, and then—after climbing above the treetops—looked “just like a star.”

**Assessment:** The writer offers speculation rather than certainty, suggesting pilots may have seen similar objects many times without realizing what they were, and that the craft may have been used for travel within Earth rather than outer space. No corroborating investigation, identification, or FBI conclusion appears on this page.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI HQ 文件 62-HQ-83894 第 9 节中的第 6 页手写页，该文件是一份 1947 年关于飞碟往来通信的档案。本页未显示打字页眉；正文以第一人称叙述，读起来像是提交给局方的一封私人信件或陈述。作者最后说她“没有证据”，但想看看政府是否相信其中任何内容。

**Witness:** 一名未具名的成年女性，显然是一位寡妇。她说她的丈夫两年前去世，她把农场租了出去，如今她和女儿们住在 Indiana（印第安纳州）的 Elkhart（埃尔克哈特）。因此，她的叙述只是转述记忆中的内容，但她将自己呈现为一位普通的乡村居民，并声称对该物体有直接观察。

**Sighting:** 她说，在她发现一份报纸的那天早晨，她上到楼上，俯视果园另一侧通向河流的方向，看见了“飞碟”。本页没有注明确切的日历日期和确切的农场位置。目击地点只被描述为 Elkhart 一带一处能看到河景的农场/果园。

**Object:** 她将其描述为一个透明、玻璃般、圆顶形的飞行器，“像爱斯基摩人的小屋”。里面有一个巨大的环，“像餐巾环”，但大得多，所有东西似乎都在那个环内。她注视时，整个环发出彩色光芒，内部再也看不见了。该物体直直上升，在树木映衬下清晰可见，然后——在升到树梢以上后——看起来“就像一颗星星”。

**Assessment:** 作者提出的是推测而非定论，认为飞行员可能曾多次见到类似物体，却没有意识到它们是什么，而且这种飞行器也许是用于地球内部旅行，而不是外太空。本页未见任何佐证调查、身份确认或 FBI 结论。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Detroit memorandum dated **May 20, 1960** (file **62-HQ-83894**, Section 9), subject **“Unidentified Flying Object; Joseph Perry, Grand Blanc, Michigan – Complainant.”** The page is marked with later archival stamps including **“ALL INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN IS UNCLASSIFIED”** and **“COPIES DESTROYED.”** It is an FBI report containing no recommendation or conclusion.

**Witness:** The principal named individual is **Joseph Perry of Grand Blanc, Michigan**. The report also cites **Jerry Chiappetta** of the *Detroit Times* and **Dave Downey**, identified as District Director of the **Aerial Phenomenon Investigation Society**. Downey is described as the source of the account relayed to the newspaper and then to the FBI.

**Sighting:** Downey said Perry had received a slide from **Selfridge Air Force Base, Mt. Clemens, Michigan, on May 3, 1960**. Perry reportedly claimed the slide showed a photograph of the Moon and that it also showed what appeared to be a flying object near the Moon. The incident is therefore a photographic UFO claim rather than a direct visual sighting, and the exact time of the original exposure is not given on this page.

**Object:** The alleged object is described only as a **flying object** or **UFO** appearing in the vicinity of the Moon on the slide. No size, shape, motion, color, or altitude is provided. The report notes that the Air Force returned the photograph with a letter explaining that the apparent object was **actually part of the negative that was not properly developed**.

**Investigation:** Downey reportedly did **not** accept the Air Force explanation, saying he knew Perry was careful in developing pictures and that the slide likely did contain a real flying object. He intended to obtain the slide and forward it to **Eastman Kodak Company** for further analysis. The FBI memo itself records these competing views without resolving them. This page appears to be the only page in the event scope shown here.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI Detroit备忘录，日期为 **May 20, 1960**（档案 **62-HQ-83894**，Section 9），主题为 **“Unidentified Flying Object; Joseph Perry, Grand Blanc, Michigan – Complainant.”** 该页带有后来的档案戳记，包括 **“ALL INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN IS UNCLASSIFIED”** 和 **“COPIES DESTROYED.”** 这是一份FBI报告，不包含任何建议或结论。

**Witness:** 主要提及的个人是 **Joseph Perry of Grand Blanc, Michigan**。报告还提到了《*Detroit Times*》的 **Jerry Chiappetta**，以及被认定为 **Aerial Phenomenon Investigation Society** 地区主任的 **Dave Downey**。Downey被描述为该说法的来源，此说法先转述给报纸，随后又传到FBI。

**Sighting:** Downey称，Perry曾在 **May 3, 1960** 从 **Selfridge Air Force Base, Mt. Clemens, Michigan** 收到一张幻灯片。Perry据称表示，这张幻灯片显示的是月球的照片，而且还显示出月球附近似乎有一个飞行物。因此，这一事件属于照片式UFO声称，而非直接目击；原始曝光的准确时间未在此页中注明。

**Object:** 所称物体仅被描述为出现在幻灯片上月球附近的 **flying object** 或 **UFO**。未提供其大小、形状、运动、颜色或高度。报告指出，空军将照片连同一封信退还，信中解释说，所见的物体 **actually part of the negative that was not properly developed**。

**Investigation:** 据称，Downey并 **不** 接受空军的解释，他表示自己知道Perry在显影照片时非常仔细，而且这张幻灯片很可能确实包含了一个真实的飞行物。他打算取得这张幻灯片，并将其转交给 **Eastman Kodak Company** 进行进一步分析。FBI备忘录本身只是记录了这些相互对立的观点，并未作出裁定。此页似乎是这里所示事件范围内的唯一一页。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Denver memorandum on letterhead of the U.S. Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation, dated April 26, 1960. The page is marked “Property of FBI” and is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9. No separate continuation page is present, so the report scope is limited to this single page.

**Witness/Event:** On April 17, 1960, George W. Van Tassel gave a public lecture at Philips Auditorium in City Park, Denver, Colorado. The event was advertised as a lecture, movie film, and discussion of unidentified flying objects and was sponsored by Denver-area unidentified flying objects investigative societies.

**Sighting/Program:** The audience was described as mostly older and mostly female, with few young people apart from some family groups. The program included a 45-minute film with shots said to be flying saucers and interviews with people recounting UFO sightings. After the film, Van Tassel delivered a talk that the writer characterized as more religious-economic than specifically about UFOs.

**Object/Claims:** Van Tassel stated that he had been in the “flying saucer” field for over 30 years and operated a privately owned Civil Aeronautics Authority-approved airfield in California. He claimed personal observation of many sightings, conversations with hundreds of witnesses, and contact with beings from outer space. He presented his work as a crusade to bring these claims to the American public.

**Investigation/Assessment:** The memorandum is descriptive and does not document an independent FBI observation of a UFO. Its value is primarily as a record of a public contactee-style UFO lecture and the speaker’s self-reported background and beliefs, rather than as evidence of a specific aerial incident.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI Denver 备忘录，抬头为美国司法部、联邦调查局，日期为 1960年4月26日。该页标注有“Property of FBI”，并属于 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894，第9部分。由于没有单独的续页，报告范围仅限于这一页。

**Witness/Event:** 1960年4月17日，George W. Van Tassel 在 Colorado 的 Denver，City Park 内的 Philips Auditorium 举行了一场公开演讲。该活动被宣传为关于不明飞行物的讲座、电影放映和讨论，并由 Denver 地区的不明飞行物调查协会赞助。

**Sighting/Program:** 观众被描述为以年长女性为主，年轻人很少，只有一些家庭群体中的成员例外。节目包括一部45分钟的影片，片中据称有飞碟镜头以及对讲述 UFO 目击经历者的采访。影片结束后，Van Tassel 发表了讲话，撰写者认为其内容与宗教和经济方面更相关，而非专门讨论 UFO。

**Object/Claims:** Van Tassel 表示，他在“飞碟”领域已从事30多年，并在 California 经营着一个由 Civil Aeronautics Authority 批准、私人拥有的机场。他声称自己亲眼目睹过许多目击事件，与数百名证人交谈过，并且与来自外太空的生命体有过接触。他将自己的工作描述为一场向美国公众传播这些说法的使命。

**Investigation/Assessment:** 这份备忘录属于描述性材料，并未记录 FBI 对某个 UFO 的独立目击。其价值主要在于作为一场面向公众的“接触者”式 UFO 讲座及演讲者自述背景和信念的记录，而非某一具体空中事件的证据。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Cincinnati memorandum/letter dated October 17, 1961, file no. 100-11671, with the subject line "Civilian Research, Interplanetary Flying Objects, Leonard H. Stringfield, Director, Cincinnati, Ohio." The page bears a loan stamp indicating it was circulated by the FBI.

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield was identified as an advertising manager for DuBois Chemical Company, Inc., and as a well-known civilian UFO researcher. The letter notes that he lived at 4412 Grove Avenue, Mariemont, Cincinnati, Ohio, had published a UFO bulletin, and had worked with the Air Defense Command on matters involving unidentified flying objects.

**Event:** Stringfield said he appeared on the television program *Impact News* on WCPO-TV, Cincinnati, on Sunday, September 10, 1961. He reported that at approximately 9:00 A.M. on September 25, 1961, he received an anonymous telephone call from a male caller whose voice he described as firm, clear, and speaking good English. The caller said he had very important information to relate to Stringfield about unidentified flying objects and asked for Stringfield by name.

**Investigation:** This page is an FBI record of Stringfield’s account, not a UFO observation report with object characteristics. The extant text ends mid-narrative, and no corroboration, analysis, or conclusion appears on this page. The report mainly documents Stringfield’s background, his media appearance, and the anonymous UFO-related contact he received.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Declassified FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9, typed continuation page marked “-2-” (page 0189). This page contains the second half of an FBI memorandum/report; no signature or report date is visible on the page shown, but it is clearly part of an FBI file concerning UFO-related correspondence and calls.

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield, identified here as a public UFO researcher and adviser to the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP). He also stated that he was authorized to report unidentified-object sightings to Air Defense Command headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, which the report uses to explain why he may receive such calls.

**Sighting/Claim:** Stringfield described a telephone call from an unidentified male who refused to identify himself but, according to Stringfield, spoke intelligently and did not sound like a prankster. The caller told him to expect “the biggest flurry of unidentified flying objects sightings” as a result of Russian nuclear explosions “in the one hundred megaton range.” He advised that confusion would begin with these sightings and said, “Mark these dates, October 15 to October 19,” adding that this would be the greatest UFO incident “over the years.” The caller reportedly said he would remain in touch and call back after the nineteenth.

**Assessment:** Stringfield told the FBI he was concerned because the caller seemed serious and because, if true, such a claim could cause public panic. He emphasized that anonymous UFO-related calls were not unusual for him due to his public role. The page records no confirmed visual observation, only an anonymous prediction/warning; the available text does not support any verified UFO event and reads more like an unverified tip or hoax warning than a substantiated sighting.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 解密的 FBI 案卷 62-HQ-83894，第 9 部分，打字续页，标注为“-2-”（第 0189 页）。本页包含一份 FBI 备忘录/报告的后半部分；所示页面上看不到签名或报告日期，但它显然是 FBI 案卷的一部分，内容涉及与 UFO 相关的通信和来电。

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield，此处被认定为一名公开的 UFO 研究者，并担任 National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena（NICAP）的顾问。他还表示自己获授权将不明物体目击报告转报至俄亥俄州哥伦布的 Air Defense Command 总部，报告据此解释他为何可能接到此类电话。

**Sighting/Claim:** Stringfield 讲述了一个来自身份不明男性的电话，对方拒绝透露姓名，但据 Stringfield 说，此人言谈机智，听起来不像恶作剧者。来电者告诉他，要预期“最大规模的一波不明飞行物目击潮”，这是由于俄国进行的“百万吨级”的核爆炸所致。他建议说，混乱将从这些目击开始，并表示：“记下这些日期，10 月 15 日到 10 月 19 日，”还补充说，这将是“多年来最重大的 UFO 事件”。据称，来电者还说他会保持联系，并在 19 日之后再打来。

**Assessment:** Stringfield 告诉 FBI，他感到担忧，因为来电者似乎很认真，而且如果此事属实，这种说法可能引发公众恐慌。他强调，由于自己的公开身份，接到匿名的 UFO 相关电话对他来说并不罕见。该页未记录任何经证实的目击，只记录了一则匿名的预测/警告；现有文本并不支持任何已核实的 UFO 事件，更像是一则未经证实的线索或恶作剧式警告，而不是有根据的目击报告。

The records include high-profile incident accounts, photographic evidence from sites like Oak Ridge, TN, and technical proposals regarding potential propulsion systems. Additional topics include convention programs, researcher accounts, and extensive media coverage from the period.  This file is partially posted on FBI vault with more redactions and some pages missing.  Included here is the complete case file with several newly declassified pages and only minor redactions.
events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Communications Section teletype from **Albuquerque 62-1028 3P** to the Director, stamped **Apr 27 1964**, with the matter captioned **“Unidentified Flying Object, Socorro, N.M., April twentyfour sixtyfour”**. The page is marked **END PAGE ONE** and carries routing/initialing notations, indicating it was a bureau relay of a field report rather than a direct witness statement.

**Witness / source chain:** The teletype says **OSI, Albuquerque** advised the incident was not known to be connected with military activity or **Operation Cloud Gap**. It then adds a second, separate incident reported at **La Madera, N.M.**. For that follow-up, **Capt. Martin Vigil, NMSP, Espanola** is quoted as having interviewed the only known witness, **Orlando Gallegos**, age 35, described as sober and frightened while visiting his father **Frank Gallegos**.

**Sighting:** The La Madera account places the event at about **1:00 AM on April 26, 1964**, about 70 miles north of Santa Fe. Gallegos reportedly went out to tend noisy horses and saw an object about **300 feet from the house**. The object was described as **“something shaped like a butane tank,”** possibly **12 to 14 feet high**, and **“long as a telephone pole.”** The page is cut off mid-sentence after saying it was apparently on the ground and surrounded with something, so the final details on appearance or behavior are not preserved here.

**Investigation / assessment:** The report’s language is cautious and administrative, with no definitive identification of the object. The page suggests the FBI was collecting and forwarding local law-enforcement and Air Force-related information while explicitly noting no known military explanation at that stage. Because the page also references a prior **Socorro** report from **April 24, 1964**, it likely serves as a combined bureau summary linking the better-known Socorro UFO matter with a separate northern New Mexico sighting.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI 通讯处电传，从 **Albuquerque 62-1028 3P** 发给局长，盖有 **Apr 27 1964** 印章，主题标题为 **“Unidentified Flying Object, Socorro, N.M., April twentyfour sixtyfour”**。该页标注 **END PAGE ONE**，并带有传递/签注记录，表明这是一份由地方报告转发的局内转递件，而非直接的目击者陈述。

**Witness / source chain:** 电传称 **OSI, Albuquerque** 表示，该事件据悉与军事活动或 **Operation Cloud Gap** 无关。随后又补充了在 **La Madera, N.M.** 报告的另一起独立事件。对于这起后续事件，文中引用 **Capt. Martin Vigil, NMSP, Espanola** 的说法：他曾采访唯一已知目击者 **Orlando Gallegos**，35岁，被描述为清醒但十分惊恐，当时正在探访其父亲 **Frank Gallegos**。

**Sighting:** 关于 La Madera 的记述将事件时间定在 **1964年4月26日凌晨1:00左右**，地点在 Santa Fe 以北约 70 英里处。据称 Gallegos 外出安抚嘈杂的马匹时，看见一个物体，距离房屋约 **300 feet**。该物体被描述为 **“something shaped like a butane tank,”** 可能高 **12 to 14 feet**，并且 **“long as a telephone pole.”** 这一页在说到它似乎在地面上、并被某种东西包围之后于句中截断，因此关于其外观或行为的最终细节在此并未保留下来。

**Investigation / assessment:** 报告措辞谨慎、偏行政性，并未对该物体作出明确认定。该页显示，FBI 当时正在收集并转发当地执法部门及空军相关信息，同时明确指出在那一阶段并无已知的军事解释。由于该页还提及此前 **April 24, 1964** 的 **Socorro** 报告，因此它很可能是一份合并性的局内摘要，将更为人熟知的 Socorro UFO 事件与新墨西哥北部的另一目击事件联系在一起。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Typed FBI case-file page from 62-HQ-83894, Section 9, on UFO/flying-disc correspondence. The rendered page is numbered "-2-" and continues a report begun on the preceding page (not provided). No signer is visible on this page.

**Witness:** Mr. Leonard H. Stringfield, described as publicly known for his interest in unidentified flying objects, an advisor to the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP), and someone authorized to relay sightings to Air Defense Command headquarters in Columbus, Ohio.

**Sighting/Call:** The report concerns an anonymous telephone call placed to Stringfield's workplace. The caller refused to identify himself but spoke, in Stringfield's view, intelligently and seriously. The caller said, in effect, that "we are calling all key and responsible people on this matter" and warned Stringfield to expect "the biggest flurry of unidentified flying objects sightings" as a result of Russian nuclear explosions "in the one hundred megaton range." He also urged him to be prepared for confusion and stated that the sightings would occur between October 15 and October 19, which he called the greatest UFO incident "over the years." The caller said he would remain in touch and call back after the nineteenth.

**Object/Claim:** No object was seen by Stringfield on this page; the event is a warning report about future alleged UFO activity. Stringfield said there was no indication the call was a joke or prank, but he was concerned that if any such sightings occurred they might panic the public.

**Investigation/Assessment:** The FBI record preserves Stringfield's account only. The page provides no corroborating observation, no named caller, and no technical evidence. It reads as an unverified, possibly hoax-like or speculative warning rather than a documented UFO encounter.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 62-HQ-83894 第9节中关于 UFO/飞碟通信的打字 FBI 案卷页。该页编号为“-2-”，并延续了前一页（未提供）开始的一份报告。本页未见签署人。

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield 先生，被描述为因对不明飞行物的兴趣而广为人知，担任 National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP) 的顾问，并被授权将目击报告转交给位于 Ohio 州 Columbus 的 Air Defense Command 总部。

**Sighting/Call:** 报告涉及一次打到 Stringfield 工作地点的匿名电话。来电者拒绝表明身份，但在 Stringfield 看来，其言谈理智而严肃。来电者大意是说，“我们正在就此事联系所有关键且负责任的人”，并警告 Stringfield，要准备好迎接“最大规模的不明飞行物目击潮”，这将是俄国在“1亿吨级（one hundred megaton range）”核爆炸之后的结果。他还敦促 Stringfield 为可能出现的混乱做好准备，并表示这些目击将发生在 10 月 15 日至 10 月 19 日之间，他称这将是“多年来”最大的一次 UFO 事件。来电者说他会保持联系，并在 19 日之后再打来电话。

**Object/Claim:** 在本页中，Stringfield 并未看到任何物体；这一事件是一份关于未来据称 UFO 活动的警告报告。Stringfield 说，没有迹象表明这通电话是玩笑或恶作剧，但他担心如果真的出现此类目击事件，可能会引发公众恐慌。

**Investigation/Assessment:** FBI 记录仅保留了 Stringfield 的陈述。本页没有提供任何可佐证的观察结果、具名来电者，也没有技术证据。其内容更像是一则未经证实、可能带有恶作剧性质或纯属推测的警告，而不是一次有据可查的 UFO 事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI UFO case-file page 2 from 62-HQ-83894, Section 9. The page is a typed continuation marked “PAGE TWO / END PAGE TWO” and ends with a referral to the proper military authorities at Kirtland AFB, Albuquerque.

**Witness:** The initial observer is identified only as Orlando, a civilian local resident. On this page he appears to have been dismissed by his father when he first reported the event. A New Mexico State Police officer, Captain Vigil, later inspected the site and provided physical observations.

**Sighting:** Orlando reportedly saw a blue-white flame that appeared to come from “port holes” on a stationary, silent object. He watched for about one minute until the flame went out. He then went into the house, told his father, and returned the next morning to find a smoldering area at the site.

**Object / Ground Effects:** Captain Vigil said he checked the site at about 7:30 PM on April 26. He noted a scorched circular area roughly 30–40 feet in diameter, one rectangular/V-shaped indentation in the ground about 8 by 12 inches and 3–4 inches deep, and three more similar indentations reported by another officer. He also saw several smooth circular prints on the ground about 3.5 inches across.

**Investigation:** The excerpt names no other witnesses and provides no identification of the object. The physical traces make the report more substantial than a simple visual sighting, but the file fragment does not establish a cause. The event remains unresolved in this excerpt; possibilities could include a landing or burn event, but no firm conclusion is documented here.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI UFO 案件档案第 2 页，来自 62-HQ-83894，Section 9。该页为打字续页，标注“PAGE TWO / END PAGE TWO”，并在末尾提及移交给 Kirtland AFB, Albuquerque 的适当军事当局。

**Witness:** 最初的目击者仅被识别为 Orlando，一名当地平民居民。在这一页中，他似乎在首次报告事件时被其父亲斥退。随后，新墨西哥州警官 Captain Vigil 勘查了现场并提供了实地观察。

**Sighting:** 据称，Orlando 看见一道蓝白色火焰，似乎来自一个静止、无声物体上的“port holes”。他观察了大约一分钟，直到火焰熄灭。随后他进入屋内告诉了父亲，并于次日清晨返回现场，发现该处有一片阴燃区域。

**Object / Ground Effects:** Captain Vigil 说他于 4 月 26 日约晚上 7:30 检查了现场。他注意到一处被烧焦的圆形区域，直径约 30–40 英尺；地面上还有一个矩形/V 形凹痕，尺寸约为 8 by 12 英寸、深 3–4 英寸；另有另一名警官报告了三处类似的凹痕。他还看到地面上有几个光滑的圆形印痕，直径约 3.5 英寸。

**Investigation:** 该摘录未提及其他证人，也未提供对该物体的身份识别。物理痕迹使这份报告比单纯的视觉目击更为实质，但档案片段并未确定成因。在此摘录中，该事件仍未解决；可能包括降落或燃烧事件，但这里没有记录任何明确结论。

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield, a publicly known UFO researcher and advisor to the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP), was reached at his workplace, listed with telephone GA 1-5100. Stringfield told the FBI that he routinely received calls about unidentified objects because of his public interest and his ability to pass sightings to Air Defense Command in Columbus, Ohio.

**Sighting/Prediction:** The caller would not identify himself, but told Stringfield to expect 'the biggest flury of unidentified flying objects sightings' allegedly caused by Russian nuclear explosions in the 'one hundred megaton range.' The caller said the activity would occur between October 15 and October 19 and that this would be the greatest incident in UFO activity 'over the years.' He also said he would remain in touch and call back after the nineteenth.

**Assessment:** Stringfield reported that the caller seemed intelligent and serious, with no indication that the message was a joke or prank. He expressed concern that if any such sightings were real they could create public panic. The page records only the warning call and Stringfield’s reaction; it does not corroborate any actual UFO sighting or nuclear event.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这是联邦调查局总部（FBI Headquarters）文件 62-HQ-83894 第 9 节中一份打字报告的第 2 页。该摘录未显示签名栏或密级标记，但叙述显然是对收到的一通匿名电话的报告的延续，该电话由 Mr. Stringfield 接听。

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield，一位广为人知的 UFO 研究者，也是国家空中现象调查委员会（National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena，NICAP）的顾问，在其工作地点接到联系；电话簿中登记的号码为 GA 1-5100。Stringfield 向 FBI 说明，由于他公开关注不明物体，并且能够将目击报告转交给位于俄亥俄州哥伦布的空防司令部（Air Defense Command），因此他经常接到有关不明物体的来电。

**Sighting/Prediction:** 来电者拒绝透露身份，但告诉 Stringfield 要准备迎接“有史以来最大的一波不明飞行物目击潮”，并声称这是由俄罗斯在“1 亿吨级”范围内进行的核爆炸所引起的。来电者表示，这一活动将发生在 10 月 15 日至 10 月 19 日之间，而且这将是“多年来”UFO 活动中最严重的一次事件。他还说自己会保持联系，并在 19 日之后再打电话回来。

**Assessment:** Stringfield 报告称，来电者听起来聪明而认真，没有迹象表明这通电话是玩笑或恶作剧。他表示担忧：如果这些目击情况属实，可能会引发公众恐慌。该页只记录了这通警告电话以及 Stringfield 的反应；并未证实任何实际的 UFO 目击事件或核事件。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** These three consecutive pages are one FBI event packet for the Socorro, New Mexico UFO case, filed under Albuquerque file **62-1028** and cross-referenced in HQ file **62-HQ-83894, Section 9**. Page p.0232 is an HQ airtel dated 4/28/64 from the Director, FBI, to SAC Albuquerque; p.0233 is the Albuquerque airtel response dated 4/28/64; and p.0234 is continuation page 2 of the same report. The subject line is "UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECT, SOCORRO, NEW MEXICO, APRIL 24, 1964" with a "miscellaneous - information concerning" classification note. The matter was handled in ordinary FBI administrative traffic and routed for liaison with the Air Force.

**Witness:** The principal witness is Socorro police officer **Lonnie Zamora**. The file repeatedly emphasizes his credibility, describing him as sober, dependable, mature, and not given to fantasy; later field officers said they were impressed by his sincerity and that he was "perfectly sober and thoroughly frightened."

**Sighting:** Zamora reported an oval-shaped object, about 20 feet long, with a red insignia, which rose from the ground with a roar, emitted bluish and orange flames, and disappeared over a distant mountain. The pages do not preserve an exact time, but the sighting date is 24 Apr 1964.

**Investigation:** Local law enforcement and Air Force personnel inspected the scene. The report says investigators found four small irregular smouldering/burned areas and four regular depressed areas, but no clear "blast" effects; unburned brown range grass remained between the spots. Lt. Col. L. B. King, OSI at Kirtland AFB, could not explain Zamora's observations. Major William R. Conner and T/Sgt. D. N. Moody also could not account for the event, though Conner suggested debris or a paint can might have caught fire; the file notes no supporting evidence for that theory. The FBI treated the case as unresolved, with the Air Force already cognizant and the Albuquerque office maintaining liaison.
events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这三页连续页面是有关新墨西哥州 Socorro（索科罗）UFO 案件的一份 FBI 事件资料包，归档于 Albuquerque 档案 **62-1028**，并在 HQ 档案 **62-HQ-83894, Section 9** 中交叉引用。第 p.0232 页为一份 HQ airtel，日期为 4/28/64，由 FBI 局长致 SAC Albuquerque；第 p.0233 页为 4/28/64 的 Albuquerque airtel 回复；第 p.0234 页为同一报告的第 2 页续页。主题栏写着“UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECT, SOCORRO, NEW MEXICO, APRIL 24, 1964”，并附有“miscellaneous - information concerning”分类说明。此事按 FBI 常规行政往来处理，并转交与空军联络。

**Witness:** 主要目击者是 Socorro 警官 **Lonnie Zamora**。文件多次强调他的可信度，称其为清醒、可靠、成熟且不爱幻想；后来的外勤人员表示，他们对他的真诚印象深刻，并称他“完全清醒，而且极度惊恐”。

**Sighting:** Zamora 报告称，一个椭圆形物体，约 20 feet 长，带有红色标志，从地面伴随轰鸣升起，喷出蓝色和橙色火焰，并飞越远处的一座山后消失。页面未保留确切时间，但目击日期为 24 Apr 1964。

**Investigation:** 地方执法人员和空军人员对现场进行了勘查。报告称，调查人员发现了四处小型、不规则的阴燃/烧灼区域，以及四处规则的凹陷区域，但没有明显的“爆炸”痕迹；各处之间仍保留着未烧毁的棕色牧草。驻 Kirtland AFB 的 OSI 中校 **L. B. King** 无法解释 Zamora 的所见所闻。**William R. Conner** 少校和 **D. N. Moody** 士官长（T/Sgt.）也无法说明该事件，不过 Conner 推测碎片或一个油漆罐可能曾起火；文件指出，这一理论没有任何支持性证据。FBI 将此案视为未解决案件，空军方面已知悉此事，且 Albuquerque 办公室一直保持联络。
